title: The Case For And Against The Ravens Trading Ronnie Stanley
full_text:
The Ravens need to get real about their years of failure and how far they have fallen from being close to a contending team.
They need to be willing to embrace a way of thinking they have long avoided – really since Ozzie Newsome tore down their last Super Bowl winner 15 years ago – and start repositioning themselves for the future and riding a wave of youth. They kept 10 of their 11 draft picks on this team, best start finding out what they can do, because many of the highest-paid starters are not replacement-level performers themselves.
Left tackle Ronnie Stanley, who spent his entire distinguished career in Baltimore, must be one of the players the Ravens strongly market this week in hopes of getting back a midround pick in return. He is not playing particularly well but has a real pedigree and is also being further exposed by the lack of talent around him and a rookie offensive player caller who is getting exposed.
He was one of the players who longtime Ravens coordinator Wink Martindale urged to show more fight and leadership when he joined “The Daily Flock Show” last week. “They got a left tackle that's been paid a [crap] ton of money who needs to step up and be a leader, you know, with Ronnie. And I love Ronnie but …”
On a roster loaded with salary dumps, Stanley is actually one of the more interesting trade candidates and I would move him for a mid-round pick in a heartbeat, especially after failed GM Eric DeCosta just wasted a 2028 second-round pick on struggling offensive lineman Cam Jurgens.
Here is the case for and against it (oh and Derrick Henry absolutely needs to be available for trade as well).
Nobody fetishsizes comp picks more than DeCosta (yet he is virtually incapable of turning those picks into real football players). But Stanley is signed for 20287 at about $1M per game, that’s not going to make sense for this team whether two-time MVP Lamar Jackson is back or not (if he plays with an $84M cap hit the Ravens are pinching pennies everywhere) and anyone who studies this team could see them drafting a left tackle in the first round.
So you don’t get a comp if you cut a guy and Stanley might want to hang ‘em up anyway at the end of the season. He gutted through a toe injury, he has a very deep injury history and though he might retire years ago, and after going through all of this, he might be cool with going to a contender to try to get a ring. Either way, it’s Baltimore’s call.
I asked a few people about his worth, including longtime NFL GM Marty Hurney on “The Daily Flock Show,” and given the need for tackles (hello Kansas City), they believe he could bring back maybe a fourth-round pick in return. “He’s making the vet minimum, right?” said one exec whose team is not looking for tackle help but is deep in trade talks as a buyer. “That’s huge for them.”
Indeed, the acquiring team has virtually no cap or salary risk ($650,000-ish) and none of his 2027 salary is guaranteed so it could be a pure rental and if it works out, $16M for a starting left tackle for a Super Bowl contender is not extreme.
Furthermore, without having to worry about protecting Jackson’s blindside anymore, sorry to be crass, but you can afford to take some liberties at tackle in the name of player development. Carson Vinson has some promise and it would be silly to head into the 2027 draft having seen precious little of Vinson in games that count in the standing.
It’s time to play the kids, right, Marty?
“You have to,” Hurney said. “You're right. You're right. You have to. You really do. That's where they are right now.”
Yeah, um, I don’t have much here. Not buying he is integral to whatever culture they have. He is definitely a declining player and perhaps rapidly. It’s not like they don’t have other options and if you don’t trade him now you damn well he isn’t getting benched making this money until maybe with just a few games left … and what are you really going to find out then?
Hurney explained some of the obstacles involved … but ultimately he was with me that this is guy they really need to try to maximize return on.
“These are decisions the whole organization's got to be behind,” he pointed out, “because it affects the whole organization. It affects the business side. I mean, you're letting go of names that fans have known for years …
"You're just not talking about trading a player now. You're really talking about a whole rebuild direction that is happening right now … And that's the right thing to do. That's the right thing to do. But it is very hard sometimes, especially for coaches whose job is, you know, they are evaluated by the number of wins next to them, right? So it it's a hard thing to do, especially when everything happens this fast.”
It’s also hard for fans to watch a team that is far too old in vital areas of the starting roster and far too young in too many other spots and has no chance of doing anything in 2026. And that has even less chance of making a move in 2027 without using this window to explore the depths of what they have under contract.
If Stanley is still here next Wednesday, that’s another huge fail for a failure front office.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The Ravens Announce Starting QB for Thursday Night Against Jacksonville
full_text:
The Ravens are going to start their third quarterback of the Jesse Minter era Thursday night against Super Bowl hopeful Jacksonville, in what could be their fourth-straight defeat.
When the Ravens kept undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano after a tryout at rookie camp many were surprised and when he made it deep into training camp it was a major upset and when he played quite well after veteran third-QB Skylar Thompson got hurt it was a major surprise and when he made the opening day roster, it was a complete shocker.
Now, he will be making his first NFL start, in primetime, with Lamar Jackson (thumb) almost assuredly having made his last appearance of the season (and perhaps of his Ravens career ) and with veteran backup Snoop Huntley (toe) out as well. All three quarterbacks got hurt in the opening half of Sunday’s disgraceful, 36-10 loss at Buffalo , and even Fagnano has been limited this week with an ankle injury, but he is the best option for this game.
The Ravens signed Austin Reed, who was with them briefly this summer, to serve as the backup and they signed Kedon Slovis from the Packers practice squad for depth. Many NFL executives have suggested to me they expect the Ravens to secure veteran Jacoby Brissett , who has started the last two years at Arizona before losing that job Sunday.
Fagnano had been serving as the emergency third-QB before Sunday, when he had to enter the game behind a terrible offensive line in the second quarter and he, too, was immediately under fire with the Bills generating pressure on 65% of Baltimore’s dropbacks
Fagnano spoke about the support he has received from future Hall of Famers like Calais Campbell and Derrick Henry – both of whom should be deal by the trade deadline next Tuesday if this organization is capable of doing the right thing – and is trying to prepare as best he can in such a short week for an opportunity that many never thought would materialize.
“It’s special,” the rookie said. “That’s really the only way I can think about it. You work a lot to get to this position. It’s unfortunate to see what happened to Lamar and Snoop, especially being two guys I look up to … That part’s tough, but I’ve had talks with them and it’s truly a next-man up mentality, and my job now is just to play to the best of my ability.”
Fagnano was getting his ankle taped shortly after entering the game and was beaten up by Buffalo’s defense with rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle failing to run the ball enough or max protect. Baltimore has had no run game since Jackson suffered his high-ankle sprain in the first half in Week 4, with Henry running more than anyone in the NFL this year but averaging just 4.0 yards per carry (it was 5.5 the last two years). Doyle must get many people involved in the run game – including rookie Adam Randall coming back from IR – because at age 32, behind this line, Henry is getting crushed at or behind the line of scrimmage .
Volume in the run game will be imperative. Fagnano said he has been doing walk throughs and mock practices with his wife to try to prepare for the biggest moment of his professional life, but the Jaguars defense is quite good and balanced, they reached the playoffs last season, enjoyed a bye in Week 7 and had the Colts put to bed Sunday well before halftime (42-7) so they will be fresher and healthier than Baltimore in the short week.
Fagnano tried to downplay his health (“Every game you’ve got bumps and bruises,” Fagnano said), but the reality is the Ravens were not certain he was going to be able to play in this game, and this will be a very tall ask.
“You always go into each game with the same preparation,” Fagnano said, “because you always know, as we’ve seen, your number can be called at any moment … Just keeping the preparation the same.”
The Jaguars (5-2)  are second in the NFL in scoring defense, allowing just 16 points per game, and the Ravens are likely to be underdogs with regularity the rest of the year no matter what they do at the trade deadline.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The Ravens Most Likely Trade Deadline Moves: Who Has To Go Now
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens are not who they pretend to be.
They are not a Super Bowl contender, or anything close to it, and haven’t carried that sort of talent since their loss in the 2023 AFC Championship Game. They are not an ascending team. They do not have a roster anyone that in the NFL envies, or wants takes seriously, or would ever want to duplicate. And the saddest part of all is that they employ next to nothing that actual contending teams want anything to do with ahead of next Tuesday’s trade deadline.
The truth is, checked-out billionaire owner Steve Bisciotti picked the wrong people to re-empower, he failed to see an obvious window of contention closing, he ran an unnecessarily bloated $370M payroll with the bulk of it tied to aged and injured and descending players who were paid too much for too long by general manager Eric DeCosta – who should have been fired with head coach John Harbaugh and can’t return to oversee the impending rebuild in 2027.
The dirty secret is DeCosta’s horribly flawed teams are exposed whenever they don’t have a should-be three-time MVP quarterback he inherited from mentor Ozzie Newsome, Lamar Jackson. They are 7-14 when he doesn’t start and Jackson has quite possibly played his last snap in Baltimore because DeCosta has been unable to convince why he should resign with this failing operation .
This will be a second-straight losing season, and, like the Orioles, it’s not the injuries, it’s because the front office is woefully inept and painfully stubborn and fueled by a hubris that has no backing in reality. Their “culture” that they can’t stop hyping because they think it helps them sell tickets is that a guy who went 0-16 as the Browns GM oversees their building on a daily basis (Sashi Brown), with an egomaniacal failed negotiator and evaluator under him.
Their brand? Biggest chokers in the NFL.
Here’s what the entire NFL knows (and like Marvin Lewis explained to me so well on “The Daily Flock” ) and what Bisciotti must accept: When you go from a potential Hall of Fame coach on a veteran staff to an inside job process to hire a novice head coach, and you refuse to stack that staff with any former NFL head coaches , you are rebuilding. When you hire guys with an inherently steep learning curve throughout literally that entire staff, and keep 20 percent of your opening roster as guys who have never played a snap in the – you are rebuilding.
When those coaches get overmatched and overrun and outclassed in the second half of literally almost every game you play, and they can’t execute basic football fundamentals to try to have at least one QB on your current roster healthy enough to host a prime time game Thursday – you are rebuild. When another season is over at Halloween – you are rebuilding.
You can pay as many bad football players like they are All-Pros up and down your roster – and you are – but you are still a rebuilding football team with a GM who has accomplished nothing (it was Ozzie!), and coaches who have accomplished even less. You have no winning culture and haven’t for years and it’s going to take you a long time to establish one … and that will be almost exclusively with players who aren’t starting for you now.
You didn’t listen to me when I told you it was an absolute must to wipe out DeCosta and Brown and get a new football operations staff (one that’s hungry and determined, and infinitely less entitled) when you fired all the coaches. Best heed the path espoused here and get ahead of some of the massive roster gutting that’s on the horizon, whether you want to admit it or not. Stop compounding your mistakes.
We wrote back in the spring that this team would be desperately trying to peddle their highest-paid corner and left tackle and alleged starting receiver at the deadline to rebuild for the future (from way back on April 13 when we just got started here). Get it done.
The Ravens have the ability to make, maybe, three football trades given how brutal their contracts are, and they should he executing a minimum of three salary dumps (and probably more). With guys like Joe Fagnano or Snoop Huntley or Jacoby Brissett or Tyson Bagent playing out the string, it’s silly not to also find out literally all you can about all those draft selections you insisted on using yet again, and all those rookies who absolutely had to make this team.
Derrick Henry: Why make him play out the final year of his deal, at age 32, already asked to lead the league in rushes on a team going nowhere when he doesn’t fit with this OL or any QB here except for Jackson? He could get you a midround/midround-is pick in return and after lighting your 2028 second-round pick on fire for Cam Jurgens ( what a desperate trade no true “steward” of a franchise ever would for a concussed player) you better can back whatever you can.
Next-man Up: Adam Randall/Rasheen Ali/Make a smart waiver or practice squad singing for once before you all hopefully get fired
Ronnie Stanley: He’s not a good left tackle anymore, but he has a resume and while no one  besides DeCosta would give him a real contract a few years back because of the extreme medicals; as a half-season rental with a pedigree, someone will bite. The state of OL play is brutal around the NFL (but trust me it’s as bad as it gets in Baltimore) and landing a new left tackle should have been up there with getting Jackson extended as top priorities last year. They always talk up Carson Vinson – he needs a runway before the draft to see what he can do.
Calais Campbell: Even his overwhelmingly special leadership skills couldn’t make a dent in the Ravens’ culture of extreme failure. Give him a chance at age 40 to finally get a ring. Let him pick the team if he wants. He deserves everything and anything. On a pitch count in a functioning defense he has something to offer and there is a reason he is always in demand. The King of the Ring loves to talk about all the trades he wasn’t ballsy enough to execute (like landing Campbell and Henry years before he did). A lot of smart evaluators I know r eally liked late-round pick Rayshaun Benny - of course these guys probably have no idea what he is, but get him off the practice squad and on the field.
Rashod Bateman: It’s not a salary dump because he’s only due like $3.5M for the rest of the year. One of DeCosta’s favorites – and another brutal draft miss – he has never clicked with Lamar, he is a blocker/deep threat decoy, and he is set to make $13M next year (non-guaranteed) and even DeCosta wouldn’t sign off on that (probably). You want a real culture? Get the guys the GM plays favorites with out now.
Next-man Up : Devontez Walker
Mark Andrews: They may have to package a pick with him, and, honestly, the horribly contract basically means he is getting $35M between last Dec and the end of 2027. They’re stuck with this, but another guy who should go to send a message to the team about mistakes of the pass and made men not being so made anymore. Shoulda been benched weeks ago.
Next-Men Up : Matthew Hibner and Josh Cuevas must out-snap Andrews by a wide margin the rest of the way
Roquan Smith : This contract is, honestly, probably the single most egregious overpay in the NFL for two years running at $20M a year for an inside LB who doesn’t impact a football game. The amount of salary they would have to eat to move him (absorb $5M to shed $5M, maybe?) means this is probably impossible, too. But having a guy with a cap hit $14M higher than anyone else at his position in the league on your bench is awkward, too.
Next-Men Up : Trenton Simpson/Teddye Buchanan. Ain’t no way Smith is back; making no attempt to lower his cap # always told you that. This is a massive need for 2027 and if Minter can fix this defense – that’s a big if – having someone wearing the dot who has already been here a while and played in the system would be ideal. Bench him now so both get a look; we wrote in May that he needed to he on the sidelines in dime (but what do we know?).
Marlon…

title: Ravens GM Eric DeCosta Should be Fired For Sunday's Offensive Line Atrocity
full_text:
The reasons for firing Ravens failing general manager Eric DeCosta go far beyond the reasons for keeping him.
A clear-eyed billionaire who wanted to win badly would have dismissed him when he fired former head coach John Harbaugh in January, but that’s not what we get in Baltimore. There were a litany of reasons to accept that the entire culture in Owings Mills was warped as the 2025 campaign came undone, but Steve Bisciotti chose sides instead and absolved DeCosta of blame and absurdly claimed he “bats .800” on the job and is some kind of a savant; that’s farcical given his pathetic record in the draft, free agency, the trade market and, worst of all, in negotiating contracts including the one with Lamar Jackson that trumps all else.
Everybody in the NFL sees it – boy does Eagles GM Howie Roseman who just undressed him in the Cam Jurgens trade – but unfortunately, the only person that matters can’t bring himself to do the hard work of rebooting an entire front office that has been living off the regulation of genius Ozzie Newsome for nearly a decade now. But that Jurgens trade – a second round pick in 2028 that could end up in the top 40 overall selections – while making an terrible line demonstrably worse as he replaced rookie Vega Ioane at center, that should be the end.
The case for ending this charade regime, led by the most overhyped and under-delivering GM in recent NFL history – the kind who inherits Jackson on a rookie deal on the cusp of his first MVP season (he should have three) and wastes his 20s - is deep. Leave it to DeCosta to make the pass protection demonstrably worse year after year, while failing to get the QB signed in a reasonable manner year after year.
If for no other reason than this dynamic, DeCosta would be fired on the spot if there was actual accountability and if this owner really cared, with the 2026 season already worse than last year and the team getting DeCosta-ed (blowing a double-digit lead in the second half to lose) or blown out every week.
Three quarterbacks getting hurt in one half doesn’t happen in professional football, for whatever reason, and the lack of adjustments from a scheme-and-personnel standpoint were staggering to NFL execs who watched the film. Lamar Jackson being lost likely for the season and back-up Snoop Huntley being immediately jumped behind the line and abused on the blitz was ugly;trying to have undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, with no reps since preseason, drop back repeatedly against that was far below grade.
“That can’t happen,” one GM said. “What the (heck) was the OC doing? They didn’t do nearly enough to help that kid. They threw him to the wolves ... That was hard to watch, man.”
Another GM said: "I don't know what the hell they were thinking. That's karma when you do what they did to Maxx," referring to DeCosta's cowardly act pulling out of a trade for star Maxx Crosby in March.
With a coaching staff full of novices getting outclassed after halftime every week, that’s all on DeCosta. He wanted puppets. Boy, did he get them.
Ravens QBs dropped back 17 times in the first half; they were hit nine times and sacked four times and hurried four times. Both tackles – Ronnie Stanley and Roger Rosengarten - proved they were no match for Greg Rousseau (that’s what a real passer rusher looks like, DeCosta, but he’s no Oweh!). But they didn’t get nearly enough help from the backs and tight ends. Somehow rookie coordinator Declan “Genius” Doyle thought this was a good day to run 11 personnel nearly 66% of the time (three receivers and one back) while his quarterbacks got dismembered.
Happy Halloween! Trick or Treat!
The Bills had an astonishing pressure rate of 64.5%, and a sack rate of 13.3%. Simple twists and stunts were totally befuddling to this offensive line. They had complete and utter disrespect for Doyle and this line (and by default the failure GM behind them both) as well they should – how about blitzing on two of every three plays for the entire game?
Yeah, that happened. Ravens QBs completed nine passes on 20 dropbacks against the blitz for 69 yards. Overmatched rookie head coach Jesse Minter almost tried to laugh off the atrocity after the game, pretending he’d have to look at the film first, and even Monday he failed to speak stringently enough to the extent of the problem (of course this team is walking all over him, and it's time to sell at the deadline).
“There’s a lot of things we still need to improve on,” Minter said, “in particular with the offensive line - pass protection, the run game. We’re chasing improvement and we’re chasing continuity, which we haven’t quite had.”
Of course, trying to squeeze a few more years out of Ronnie Stanley, who thought his career was over years ago with chronic ankle/lower leg issues , was always silly. When he came back to DeCosta at the combine a few years on a soft market, that was the time to walk away not extend (we said repeatedly on the radio at the time). Right tackle Roger Rosengarten is a replacement level guy at best far more comfortable running than trying to hold up against a real pass rusher.
The interior OL has been a cruel joke on any and all Ravens QBs just waiting to land since DeCosta chose a fringy edge defender with limited pass rush in the second round (Zion Young, a profile he has misevaluated with staggering consistency ) instead of any center in the draft after letting Tyler Linderbaum be among his massive exodus of young talent in March. Pretending Danny Pinter or Jovaughn Gwyn could play was cute (our guy Brian Baldinger and a legion of execs said it had no chance ).
They couldn’t even realize that rookie Vega Ioane was the solution at center despite him faring quite well, and Jurgens has led the team to two of its worst yards before contract games for Baltimore running backs (0.75 and 0.30) in recent history since coming out of concussion protocol to move back to a position he hadn’t been playing in Philly …. where he was about to get benched. DeCosta lit $10M on fire giving it to John Simpson.
It’s the stuff that ends a charade of a GM career in places serious about winning. But Bisciotti couldn’t be bothered to take part in almost all of his own head coaching search; DeCosta has sucked up to him for years, Bisciotti speaks about him like David Rubenstein speaks about baseball fraud Mike Elias) so don’t hold your breath waiting for anything to change in Owings Mills. The press conference hyping DeCosta when they fired Harbaugh was shameful in realtime and looks like a weak Vaudeville routine now with the passing of just a few months.
The Castle and The Warehouse are one in the same: Reality doesn’t matter, accountability only extends to coaches/managers and the joke’s always on the paying customer.
Thursday night should be a doozie. Wonder if DeCosta will break out the sunglasses at night in primetime again? In a real organization, he'd be reading his termination papers through them by now.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The Ravens Will Have A New Starting QB and Kicker Thursday Night. They Just Don't Know Which Ones
full_text:
The Ravens do not know who will start at quarterback on Thursday night in a must-win game against the Jaguars, according to head coach Jesse Minter, while second-year kicker Tyler Loop could be heading to Injured Reserve..
In an atrocious combination of roster-construction failure and misevaluation by their crack front office – and gross negligence by rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle – the Ravens got three quarterbacks hurt behind the line of scrimmage in Sunday’s, 36-10 debacle in Buffalo. They ran 11 personnel – three receivers, not heavy packages designed for max protection – over 65% of the time, they didn’t do enough to help failing tackles and called way too many pass plays in a game that was basically done by halftime, behind failure GM Eric DeCosta’s greatest offensive line malfeasance yet (set Derrick Henry free from this mess before the deadline, like a real org).
Superstar Lamar Jackson was lost, likely for the season , with a mostly free runner smashing his hand on the first dropback of the game in his first game back from a three-week, high-ankle sprain. Backup Snoop Huntley (toe) was quickly ambushed behind this line himself, and he will not be able to play Thursday, according to Minter, and undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano was beat up and getting treatment on his foot and ankle throughout the game.
“I think we’ll figure that out in the next day or two,” Minter said of his starter. At 4-4, losing three straight games, scoring three points in the second half total in those games and allowing the most points in the NFL in the second half with the worst scoring differential, it probably doesn’t really matter at this point.
Baltimore has two AFC wins (Colts and Jaguars) and its playoff hopes are nil without Jackson. Whether it’s Fagnano trying to gut it out – “To Joe’s credit he’s kind of fighting through some things … we expect him to have a chance on Thursday,” Minter offered – or Austin Reed who was just brought back to the practice squad this week after a brief cameo in the preseason, this is going to be rough. The Ravens are trying to acquire a veteran with ties to this system – Chicago’s Tyson Bagent was the top objective, league sources said, but won’t come cheaply if at all – and are expected to make a play for former Arizona starter Jacoby Brissett.
Mintner said the team could have more clarity on the timetable for Jackson later this week – he was scheduled for a procedure the coach said Sunday – but the reality is the Ravens are virtually certain to be out of the mix whenever Jackson could come back, and with a fake contract for 2027 that essentially cedes all leverage to him , playing him would be ridiculous even by DeCosta’s standards.
As for Loop, he sent the opening kickoff out of bounds and missed another chip-shot field goal and Minter and DeCosta have had him on notice for weeks. Minter was nebulous about the nature of the injury and when exactly it occurred (“He was dealing with something small that kind of became something more,” is what we’re going with here). Whatever it is, he could be bound for IR and Jake Moody will be elevated from the practice squad for Thursday’s game.
The Ravens are going to raise eyebrows with Loop having "something" going on - we didn't get a lower-body or upp-er-body cop out here, and the nebulous timetime given he has never shown up on any injury report, but has struggled with consistency. Hmm.
Moody has kicked for three teams previously and is yet to establish himself after being a second-round pick of the 49ers. Loop was drafted in 2025 to replace scorned and despised former kicker Justin Tucker, who accepted a lengthy suspension from the NFL for sweeping and credible accusations of predatory sexual behavior from throughout his tenure in Baltimore. He was never condemned in any way by anyone in this organization, even when finally terminated, and mostly praised even on the way out.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The Overwhelming Case For The Ravens Trading Derrick Henry At The NFL Deadline
full_text:
The Ravens need to get real about the Frankenstein roster that feckless general manager Eric DeCosta constructed yet again.
They need to get real – as they scramble to find second-and-third-string QBs (we have the names) to prop up another lost season after getting three quarterbacks hurt Sunday (a 36-10 defeat that frankly flatters DeCosta and wannabe head coach Jesse Minter ). It's time to acknowledge what a nightmare front office they are and what a pathetic offensive line they have constructed, again. Having blown years of opportunities to get two-time MVP Lamar Jackson extended and instead ending up with him in a potential walk year,  and now on Injured Reserve and potentially having played his last snap as a Raven (the only one he completed Sunday; ambushed immediately by DeCosta's OL and "genius" Delan Doyle's playbook), it’s time to get real.
Checked-out billionaire Steve Bisciotti is running a $370M waste of payroll with DeCosta and team president Sashi Brown doling out ridiculous contracts to their buddies and building a roster with no heart, no soul, no leadership and precious few blue-chip performers. He already gave away a 2028 second-round pick that could end up in the top 10 of that round for a concussed and soon-to-be-benched offensive lineman. DeCosta needs to do right by some of these players and do right by the fanbase and start playing youngsters and eradicating some of the problems that are standing in their way.
Problem is, they aren’t getting anything in return for DeCosta’s guys – astonishingly overpaid vets like Mark Andrews, Marlon Humphrey, Roquan Smith, Trey Hendrickson, John Simpson – and they would have to include draft capital with them to incentivize any contending team with a teal GM to take them on. They are broken; they are done and the league already knew (they couldn't get anything for Andrews after the 2024 season(.
However, first-ballot Hall of Famer Derrick Henry, in a running back market that is already getting heated up for Jonathan Taylor (Colts) and Tony Pollard (Titans), could bring back decent return now and with so few other options, the rebuild should begin with him. Maybe they get a half decent pick for struggling left tackle Ronnie Stanley and they could get a lil something for 40-year-old defensive lineman Calais Campbell, who could help a good defense in their rotation but is wasting the likely final season of his Hall of Fame career here, too.
Let’s be clear, the Ravens trying desperately to get Bears back-up Tyson Bagent or demoted Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett isn’t to save the season … it is literally to just be able to field a team with two QBs for a stretch of time. The Ravens will not have quality QB play this season, and if Jackson leaves, who knows when they will ever again (somebody ask DeCosta about Kyle Boller if you can find him; he’s cowering behind Sashi last I heard).
The only way, at age 32, with a terrible offensive line, this was going to have a chance to work was if Jackson was performing like the best player in football and drawing loads of attention from the defense with his legs and opening up space for Henry to get a head of steam before contact. DeCosta trade fail Cam Jurgens has made the run blocking worse (0.30 yards before contact for RBs in his first start; 0.75 in his second), Jackson is on IR and we are looking at having a backup QB from outside the building potentially start Thursday, or undrafted, beat-up rookie Joe Fagnano.
It’s over for Henry here. It has no shot to be even slightly below functional, let alone league average.
Doyle, the rookie offensive coordinator, is horribly out of his depth without the real genius, Jackson, on the field. And they are wasting what’s left of Henry's remarkable career, at the age where virtually all RB careers die ( we told you in the spring ). Yet  Doyle is running Henry more than any back in the NFL and it's not getting better .
He is getting crushed at or behind the line of scrimmage, there is no under-center rush attack without Vega Ioane at center (he was out with a knee injury and they pushed him back to guard after the desperate ploy for Jurgens ). Henry leads the NFL with 158 carries  - this is ridiculous; a winning team with a team with a real offense could get way more out of him with less load – and ranks 29th at 4.0 yards per carry.
The last five weeks Henry is 33rd in the NFL at 3.6 yards/carry. That's the reality without Jackson.
For the season, Henry is 36th in the NFL at 0.87 yards before contact – that ain’t gonna work and it will get worse as Jurgens, a major medical red flag, gets beatdown in the  second half of the season and with Simpson a waste of $10M and with the tackles getting exposed, too. How can I be 100% sure this will be an unmitigated disaster run game without Jackson? Here’s the breakdown for Henry:
With Jackson : 75 rush – 340 yards – 7 TDs (4.5/carry); 20 1st Downs, 1.12 Yds B4Contact
16% rushes 0 or Neg Yards, 42.7% Success Rate, 6.7% Explosive Rate
Without Jackson : 83 – 292 – 1 (3.5/carry); 12 1st Downs, 0.65 Yds B4Contract
23% rushes 0 or Neg Yds, 33.7% Success, 2.4% Explosive Rate
Check please. Let the selfish GM who is never at fault and always shuns accountability do right by this man and move the remaining $6M of his deal and get back some picks.
He doesn’t want to leave. For whatever reason, he is dead against it.
He doesn’t owe them anything, this isn’t what DeCosta sold him and running him into the ground with below-grade QBs and a failure offensive line serves no one. Give rookie “Joker” Adam Randall carries , run Wild Cat with Justice Hill. Empty out that playbook from the genius OC you hired when he was 29 years old (who comes from a coaching family tree of almost nothing but acute play-calling failures) .
How about this for the mooks in the front office who haven’t worked hard in years and operate like made men who have jobs for life and peacock around like they’ve accomplished something:
FIND A REAL FOOTBALL PLAYER ON WAIVERS. GET OFF YOUR ASS ON A TUESDAY AND STEAL SOMEONE OFF A PRACTICE SQUAD LIKE THE RAIDERS STOLE DARREN WALLER FROM YOU. BACK UP FOR YOUR BS FOR JUST ONCE. PLEASE. SHOW HOW SMART YOU ARE AND FIND A DECENT BACK TO PLAY OUT THE STRING.
They are losers and have managed to be losers, even with Jackson producing what should have been three MVP seasons. And they are fat and lazy and entitled, because the owner always fired assistant coaches and never asked real questions of personnel (him claiming DeCosta essentially "hits on 80% of his transactions" back in January told you how little Mostly Silent Steve pays attention anymore ).
I’ve known it forever, the league has known it for years and despite getting most of the Baltimore corporate media sucking from their thumb, the fans see DeCosta and Brown for the frauds they are now, too.  (And longtime Ravens coordinator Wink Martindale breaks it down below).
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Ravens Have Initiated Trade Talks For This QB With Lamar Jackson Possibly Out For The Season
full_text:
The Ravens are in a dire situation with the quarterback position, getting three passers injured in an ugly loss to Buffalo Sunday including losing Lamar Jackson, possibly for the year, with a serious thumb injury. And they are trying desperately to line up a quarterback to be in uniform ahead of Thursday’s game against Jacksonville, according to league sources.
Jackson was hurt on his first dropback of the game in what became a third-straight ugly defeat (36-10, this time), getting hit in the hand by pass rusher Greg Rousseau, who destroyed Baltimore’s pathetic offensive line all game. Jackson is headed to Injured Reserve and rookie head coach Jesse Minter acknowledged after the game it could be season-ending, With the way this season is going, even a four-week absence would probably end the season as Jackson doesn’t have a viable contract for 2027 and has GM Eric DeCosta by the throat in contract leverage and could want out next season; he won’t be playing in garbage games or quasi-garbage games.
Backup Snoop Huntley left the game with a toe injury that will likely keep him from being able to start Thursday and possibly to play at all. And rookie emergency QB Joe Fagnano, an undrafted rookie forced into action, was getting treatment on his ankle/foot throughout the second half and his status for Week 9 is in question as well with such a quick turnaround.
“We'll do everything in our power to keep rolling, to keep this thing going, to get it back on the right side,” Minter said after the game, alluding to the QB issue. “Again, with whatever that looks like, and whoever that's playing. If it's Joe, we have a lot of belief in Joe, whoever it is. But that's what we'll do."
The Ravens had to begin reaching out to other front offices, immediately Sunday, as relying on free agency to fly someone in, work them out, make sure they can pass a physical and get them signed in time to play Thursday is a stretch. A trade would be ideal and while there are few options in that vein who already have an understanding of the system rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle is operating.
The Ravens top pursuit is Bears back-up quarterback Tyson Bagent, according to multiple high-ranking NFL personnel execs. They have reached out to Chicago, but are in a desperate position, DeCosta already got fleeced trading a second-round pick for a concussed and suspect offensive lineman . Multiple league sources told me through the summer that the Bears were rebuffing all overtures for Badgent (who makes $4M this year and $4M next year), who they believe can be a valuable back-up in Ben Johnson’s system.
“Chicago doesn’t have to trade him,” one NFL GM told me. “They like him … Wonder how hard they squeeze DeCosta?”
The Bears signed Bagent to a contract extension in part because of that upside; he has great athleticism and the ability to run option plays and try to generate something for a Baltimore run game that is going nowhere (32-year-old back Derrick Henry is getting swallowed up at the line of scrimmage in the traditional run game).
Bagent, 26, was signed as an un-drafted free agent in 2023 out of tiny Shepherd College and was rushed into starting duty. When Johnson arrived last year (with Doyle on staff) they took a liking to him. Bagent played in three games this season with Caleb Williams was out, completing 66% of his passes for 6.4 yards/attempt and a 63.9 rating. The Bears play at Seattle on Monday night, which also complicates things.
He is well-versed in the offense, his legs can help sustain things but he is not one to push the ball downfield. The Bears are carrying three QBs, including veteran Case Keenum. Broncos third QB Sam Ehlinger – the Broncos offense is similar to Baltimore’s with Denver coach Sean Payton Doyle’s primary mentor, could be another option. Ehlinger was inactive for Denver's game Sunday.
A high-ranking official from another NFLclub also suggested Jacoby Brissett as a viable option for the Ravens. "That's the other name I heard they are interested in, besides the back-up in Chicago," he told me. It's unclear at this point if the Ravens have contacted the Cardinals but this would also make sense.
Brissett had a career year in 2026, but carries a very manageable $1.5M base salary and the Cardinals want to get a look at rookie Carson Beck, and the rebuilding team benched Brissett for journeyman Gardner Minshew Sunday in a comeback win over Dallas. Execs around the NFL expect the Cardinals, in a rebuild, to move veterans before the trade deadline.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Bills-Eagles Trade Proposal Would Land Buffalo Perfect Deadline Addition
full_text:
We are less than one week from the NFL trade deadline and some big moves have already happened. As of yet, however, the Buffalo Bills have been rather quiet .
Despite seeing contenders such as the San Francisco 49ers, Chicago Bears, and Seattle Seahawks all bolster their rosters, Buffalo general manager Brandon Beane hasn’t made any moves. That’s frustrating given the state of the defense, which is currently ranked 24th in points surrendered (and that number was helped tremendously by the fact that they faced a Baltimore Ravens team that had to rely on Joe Fagnano for most of the game).
If Beane did decide to look for defensive help, Cody Williams of FanSided has an intriguing name to keep an eye on. Williams says the perfect deadline target for Buffalo would be Zack Baun , a versatile linebacker who currently plays for the Philadelphia Eagles.
"At some point, we need to see the Buffalo Bills and general manager Brandon Beane give Josh Allen more help on the opposite side of the ball. Against the best teams on their schedule, the Bills are set up to need to put a huge number on the scoreboard," Williams wrote.
"They're capable, but the level of difficulty shouldn't be that high. The Eagles' huge downturn could make Zack Baun available, and the versatile linebacker is the all-angles presence that the Bills defense lacks in the middle right now."
Originally a third-round pick of the New Orleans Saints in 2020, Baun broke out with the Eagles in 2024 after signing a one-year deal in free agency. He made the Pro Bowl after recording 151 tackles, 3.5 sacks, and one interception. Baun then signed a three-year, $51 million deal in 2025 , keeping him under contract through the 2027 season.
There’s no denying that Baun would instantly improve the Buffalo defense. He’s currently the sixth-highest rated linebacker in the NFL, according to PFF, with an overall grade of 79.7 . He’s also incredibly well-rounded, proving to be capable against the run as well as in coverage.
The question is whether the Eagles really would be willing to make a move. Unfortunately, the answer is probably no.
While this is a lost season for the Eagles due to injuries, they know they have a championship-caliber team when healthy. Perhaps if Baun were a free agent in 2027 they would be willing to move on, but since he’s signed for another season, they’re far more likely to keep him around and hope they can contend next season when fully healthy.
That said, Beane would be doing his team a disservice if he didn’t look for an upgrade at linebacker and that should include at least seeing if the Eagles are open to a discussion.

title: Bills' Practice Squad Player Essentially Forced CJ Gardner-Johnson Out Door
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills apparently had enough of the Chauncey Gardner-Johnson experiment.
Much like he did with the Philadelphia Eagles, Detroit Lions, Houston Texans and Chicago Bears, all within the span of four seasons, Gardner-Johnson has worn out his welcome sooner than later in Orchard Park.
Required to make a roster move by Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET as Gardner-Johnson's one-game NFL-imposed suspension expired, the Bills chose not to tinker with the combination that performed so well in the combustible defensive back's absence.
Rather than cutting someone to open a roster spot for Gardner-Johnson, Buffalo sent the obnoxious, saliva-spewing safety packing .
Notably, the Bills decided to keep practice squad promotion Te'Cory Couch on their 53-man roster following his eye-opening performance against the Baltimore Ravens on November 1.
After appearing twice as a practice squad elevation this season, Couch signed to the active roster when Gardner-Johnson's suspension created a one-week vacancy.
There was an initial thought that Couch would serve only as a stop gap for the Week 8 home game against Baltimore. After providing nickel cornerback/safety insurance, Buffalo would release Couch with the hope of getting him back on the practice squad.
As it turns out, Couch isn't going anywhere. In fact, the 27-year-old versatile defensive back may have played his way into the Bills' long-term plans. At least, he's earned another chance to show what he can do.
While some of it has to do with the combustible Gardner-Johnson's subpar performance, particularly when it comes to on-field communication, Couch's opportunity is just as much a result of his progress in Jim Leonhard's defense.
"Te'Cory Couch had a great game," said Leonhard. "He went in there and executed really at a high level, communication and just winning some one-on-ones."
Seemingly acing his assignments, Couch totaled five tackles in the 36-10 win over Baltimore.
The Bills signed Couch as an undrafted rookie free agent out of Miami in 2024.
Following back-to-back seasons on Buffalo's practice squad , Couch finally made his NFL debut as a practice squad elevation against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 3. He was active on game day again in Week 4, but subsequently missed practice time as a result of being banged up.
Couch, who saw only special teams snaps in his first two appearances, was needed on defense with the secondary missing Gardner-Johnson and injured starting slot cornerback Dee Alford .
“He's been injured. Now he's coming back. Hey, what's the Dee Alford situation going to be? Boom, you're up," said head coach Joe Brady. "Being able to make plays on the football, critical tackles, the involvement he has on special teams. And so it's going to be like that moving forward."
Couch appeared to come into his own this past summer during training camp. His willingness and ability to move around in Leonhard's defense helped him get noticed.
"TC, man, that's a dude who truly had to learn every position on this defense to get opportunities like today, and he did it, and he executed so well," said veteran Damar Hamlin , who started at safety in place of Gardner-Johnson .
Playing multiple roles during an August 22 preseason game against the Cleveland Browns, Couch made an interception as a safety. Playing in all three exhibition contest, he totaled six tackles on defense and added two more on special teams.
On Sunday against the Ravens, he played 71 percent of defensive snaps. His efforts were key to holding Ravens' wide receiver Zay Flowers without a catch.
"He was out there communicating. He was out there playing just lights out, if you ask me. So shoutout to him," said Hamlin. "He's been waiting on the opportunity for years, and it finally came his way, and I think he made the most of it."
The excellent communication represented a noticeable improvement over what Gardner-Johnson showed over the first six weeks.

title: Bills, Budda Baker Rumors Give Buffalo Hope for Deadline Trade With Cardinals
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills ' need at the safety position just became more dire when it was reported on Tuesday that the Bills are going to release safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson.
The decision to cut ties with Gardner-Johnson comes following him serving a one-game suspension for spitting on a Las Vegas Raiders player. Despite that disgusting act, it's still at least a bit surprising the Bills are cutting him, as head coach Joe Brady previously said Gardner-Johnson wasn't going anywhere .
NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe reported that Gardner-Johnson's "inconsistency in play" was what led to his release and "not as much the spitting incident."
Nevertheless, adding to the safety position just became more important because the Bills don't have much they can rely on there.
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler touched on Budda Baker's potential availability on Wednesday morning.
Fowler says Baker is on his radar as a trade candidate, and while Baker "would be hard to trade" because of his status as an Arizona Cardinals "lifer," he is also hearing that all of the losing in Arizona has "weighed on him."
In addition to all that, Fowler also said "teams such as Buffalo or Jacksonville could try to take advantage of that."
"Also on the Arizona front, safety Budda Baker remains on my radar, though he has been a Cardinals lifer and would be hard to trade. But my sense is the consistent losing has weighed on him, and teams such as Buffalo or Jacksonville could try to take advantage of that," Fowler said.
Fowler isn't the first one to surmise that Baker's career-long stint in Arizona might have him standing pat. ESPN's Adam Schefter recently said the same thing.
"That guy has been such a stud I don't know that Budda Baker is gonna be traded," Schefter said . "I don't think Arizona wants to move on from a guy that has meant so much to that franchise. (Baker) is such a baller."
It might be true that the Cardinals don't want to trade Baker, but if he wants to be moved because he is indeed sick of all the losing that isn't likely to end in the next few years with the Cardinals rebuilding, Arizona could oblige out of respect for him.
An eight-time Pro Bowler and four-time All-Pro, Baker has been one of the better safeties in the NFL during his career.
The veteran is an excellent box safety who is both strong against the run and as a pass-rusher. Baker's 73.8 Pro Football Focus run defense grade ranks 33rd at the position, and he's top five in run stops, also. As a pass-rusher, Baker sports a 72.6 grade, ranked 14th, and he has 3.5 sacks in eight games.
The Bills could really use a boost in coverage given the fact that they have the third-worst pass defense in the league, and Baker has been strong in that area with a 48.1% completion rate surrendered and a passer rating against of 94.2.
When it comes to compensation, we could see Baker going for a fourth-round pick.
The Bills are well-stocked with draft capital to be able to afford that, and what makes this potential trade even better is that Baker's contract runs through 2027.
If Baker can be had, general manager Brandon Beane shouldn't hesitate to go get him.

title: Former NFL Player Questions Bills' Decision to Cut C.J. Gardner-Johnson
full_text:
On Tuesday, the Buffalo Bills decided to move on from C.J. Gardner-Johnson , releasing the veteran safety after he served his one-game suspension for spitting at Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers.
On the surface, it looks as though Buffalo made the right call. Gardner-Johnson joined the team with a questionable resume, which included being released by the Houston Texans after just three games last season.
What was worse is Gardner-Johnson showed no remorse whatsoever following the incident. He refused to admit he spit at Bowers , even making the ridiculous claim that it was a sign of his competitiveness.
Not everyone agrees, however, as former NFL linebacker Emmanuel Acho questioned the decision. Acho said the Bills might struggle to win without Gardner-Johnson, who he says was an enforcer on their defense.
"I don't know if I agree because you might need Chauncey to win. Like I think you need an enforcer. The Bills do not have an enforcer on that defense," Acho said.
BREAKING: Chauncey Gardner-Johnson was released by the Buffalo Bills 😳 My immediate reaction! Let me know if y’all agree— pic.twitter.com/wkSldUPdHk
"Terrell Bernard, good player, not an enforcer. Dorian Williams, good player, not an enforcer. You usually find your enforcers at linebacker. Um, sometimes Seattle Seahawks, you can find them outside at cornerback, but you need a freakazoid like Devin Witherspoon, but you don't have an enforcer up front, Ed Oliver is here today, gone tomorrow. Greg Rousseau having a phenomenal season. He's a good player, but he's not an enforcer."
Acho went on to say that without him being on the defense, he's torn. "The Bills, Where's your enforcer now on defense? ... The Bills lost their enforcer, so I'm torn."
Acho discussed some of the recent championship teams and pointed out the enforcers on their defense. He mentioned the Philadelphia Eagles who won a title in 2024 with Gardner-Johnson as their defensive enforcer.
There's truth to that after Gardner-Johnson recorded six interceptions for the Eagles that season, but that wasn't the same player Buffalo had in Gardner-Johnson. This season, he was a liability in the secondary, posting a 55.2 overall according to PFF . He also had nine missed tackles in just six games, two of which were in the first half against the Raiders before being ejected.
Gardner-Johnson might have been an enforcer at one point in his career, but he doesn't fall into that category now. Throw in the distraction he became with his antics and the decision to move on was one of the easiest the Bills have made in recent years.

title: Jim Leonhard's Bye Week Adjustment Pays Off for Bills' Defense, Becomes New M.O.
full_text:
There's an idea that this adjustment will help Buffalo Bills ' defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard when making in-game adjustments.
Leonhard, a former NFL safety in his first season at the helm of Buffalo's defense, decided to change his physical location on game days .
Prior to the Week 7 bye, Leonhard spent the first six games calling the defensive alignments from the Bills' sideline . When Buffalo hosted the Baltimore Ravens, however, Leonhard relocated from field level up to the coaches' booth.
"It was something I've kicked around for a few weeks. Again, going into the bye, and having a little bit more time to sit back, I just felt like it was going to give me the best opportunity to call a clean game," said Leonhard in the aftermath of a 36-10 victory.
During the preseason, Leonhard tested both locations before settling on the field level perspective for Week 1.
"I see the benefits of both. There's definitely some benefits of being up in the box, but feel more comfortable being on the sideline. Being able to have direct communication with the players, with the coaches, and kind of feel the energy and the excitement on the sideline, I think that helps me call plays," said Leonhard this past summer.
Whether a correlation between Leonhard's location and the unit's success exists, or not, the Bills' defense enjoyed its most productive performance yet this season in Week 8 against the Ravens. Buffalo, which gave up at least 348 yards in each of its first six games, limited the Ravens to a minuscule 144 yards of total offense.
For perspective, Leonhard's predecessor, Bobby Babich, operated from the coaches' booth during games. In 2023, after Leslie Frazier's departure and before Babich's promotion, ex-head coach Sean McDermott called the defense from the sideline.
In an example of a defensive coordinator going in the opposite direction of Leonhard, Patrick Graham, who is in his first year with the Pittsburgh Steelers , opened the season in the coaches' box. In Week 5, Graham moved down to the field, apparently in an attempt to improve communication.
Although it was not at the NFL level, Leonhard, who has mentioned the effect of on-field energy, was on the sidelines during his tenure as Wisconsin's interim head coach and defensive coordinator.
Although he must sacrifice the face-to-face interaction, Leonhard recognizes the advantages of an elevated view.
"I can sit up there and just kind of get in the lab and get my thoughts rolling, get ahead of things. I know what I'm looking for from a substitution standpoint and different areas of the field," said Leonhard.
As for the communication, the former 10-year NFL veteran is willing to rely on the players and his fellow coaches to get it done.
"Trust our coaches. We have emotionally a pretty stable group of coaches, and emotionally a pretty mature group of players. So the more I got to see that over the first six weeks of the season, seven weeks of the season, it trusts me to go get away from it and not have to feel like I got to lead and be face to face with guys," said Leonhard.
According to first-year head coach Joe Brady, who called the offensive plays from the booth in his 2.5 seasons as a Bills' coordinator, the operation was impressive against the Ravens.
"I felt like the communication from upstairs and downstairs was elite yesterday. I thought he [Leonhard] had a great understanding of what they were trying to do. I think sometimes when you're up there, I think it makes life a little easier," said Brady.
The expectation is for Leonhard to remain upstairs throughout the rest of the season.
"It'd be hard to change, I think, at this point," said Leonhard. "It obviously worked. It was helpful for me. I feel the benefits outweigh being on the field right now, so I think that will continue."
Between the "elite" communication, Leonhard's play calls and the players flying around on the field, the adjustment seems to be just what the doctor ordered for a defense that had been struggling.

title: Top NFL Trade Options to Replace Safety CJ Gardner-Johnson After Bills Cut Ties
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills ' safeties arguably enjoyed their best performance of the season this past Sunday.
And they did it without the erratic safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson in the lineup.
Suspended one game by the NFL for spitting at an opponent on October 18 in Las Vegas, Gardner-Johnson was unavailable in Week 8 against the Baltimore Ravens.
Apparently comfortable enough with what they saw from veterans Damar Hamlin and Geno Stone in Sunday's 36-10 win, the Bills decided to release Gardner-Johnson rather than re-add him to the 53-man roster.
Even with Hamlin and Stone proving capable, one has to think Buffalo is going to seriously consider directly replacing Gardner-Johnson via the trade market. After all, Stone is still on the practice squad, and the Bills have only three true safeties on their active roster with Hamlin, Cole Bishop and fifth-round rookie Jalon Kilgore, who was a healthy scratch against the Ravens.
Whether they simply want veteran insurance or a bona fide starter, the Bills have multiple sensible options for general manager Brandon Beane to target. While On SI's Colin Richey, prior to Gardner-Johnson's dismissal, suggested four "salary-cap-friendly" safeties for the Bills to target, we considered three bigger names below.
With the last-place Titans (1-7) clearly sellers heading toward the NFL trade deadline , Hooker may be the most realistic option.
Furthermore, his $11.9 million salary cap hit (per Spotrac) is low enough where the Bills could make him fit by exercising some creative cap gymnastics. With the season nearly half over, that number is already down to under $7 million, and the Bills reportedly have approximately $4 million in room.
The 28-year-old Hooker, who intercepted Cincinnati Bengals' quarterback Joe Burrow three times in Week 8, has 103 career appearances under his belt. The 2019 fourth-round pick has spent his entire career with Tennessee, totaling 74 starts and 17 interceptions over seven-plus seasons.
His versatility makes him an even more attractive option. Hooker has shown the ability to play effectively in the box and out in centerfield. He also has experience as a nickel defensive back.
While the Bills will surely love to get him, it seems like a difficult task to convince the Arizona Cardinals to trade away an eight-time Pro Bowl selection.
Still, it's worth at least making a phone call on Baker. Although the 30-year-old may have lost a half-step from his prime years, he remains an important piece of Arizona's defense. Baker has 51 tackles, 3.5 sacks and one interception over eight starts this season.
Still, the Cardinals, although competitive, are in a rebuilding phase, and they could look to stock draft capital. Would a third-round pick be enough?
The winless Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) would likely be willing to flip James for a Day 2 draft pick, but the safety's recent injury complicates matters.
James, who signed a three-year contract extension reportedly worth $76 million this past offseason, went onto Injured Reserve last week due to a hamstring issue. The good news is the NFL changes its rules in 2018, permitting teams to trade IR players prior to the deadline.
The 30-year-old James, a 2018 first-round draft pick, has spent his entire NFL tenure with the Chargers. He has 101 career starts and 12 interceptions. Capable of manning both safety spots, the versatile James has totaled 705 tackles and 19.0 sacks.
The Sporting News columnist Vinnie Iyer listed a James-to-the-Bills move as one of 12 best potential deadline deals for playoff contenders.

title: Bills Make Smart Call With C.J. Gardner-Johnson Release Following Suspension
full_text:
During the victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected for spitting at tight end Brock Bowers and was suspended for one game afterward . With his suspension officially over, the Buffalo Bills decided to make the smart call and move on.
According to Jordan Schultz, the Bills are officially releasing Gardner-Johnson after he appeared in just six games for the franchise.
This marks the second time in as many years that Gardner-Johnson was released early in the season by a new team. In 2025, he was traded to the Houston Texans but was released after just three games. Gardner-Johnson struggled to play within the scheme with Houston and was reportedly frustrated with his role.
Eventually, head coach DeMeco Ryans decided he had enough and moved on. Gardner-Johnson then spent time with the Baltimore Ravens practice squad before finishing the season with the Chicago Bears.
He signed a one-year deal with the Bills this offseason, a move that was seen as risky given the issues Gardner-Johnson has had in the past. Still, their need for a difference-maker at the safety position led to the role of the dice.
In six games, Gardner-Johnson flashed some of his talent, finishing with 26 tackles, two pass breakups, and an interception against the Los Angeles Chargers which helped seal the win. Unfortunately, he also had missed assignments in coverage and struggled with tackling. Gardner-Johnson had two missed tackles in his final game alone before being ejected.
It's already concerning that Gardner-Johnson decided to spit at an opponent, but what was even worse was the fact that he genuinely acted as though he did nothing wrong. Gardner-Johnson, who appealed the suspension but lost , never admitted to spitting at Bowers.
Gardner-Johnson also gave one of the worst apologies ever, saying there was "nothing to it" when discussing his act. He even tried to claim it was just an example of being competitive .
"I gotta just control my emotions. There was nothing to it; it's competitive. Like I said, heat of the moment. Everybody saw what was going on. It wasn't nothing egregious against nobody. Like I said, we just competed in the game. A call was made. A flag was made. We went to chirping. And I guess, you know, just being competitive. Like I said, nothing towards Brock and nothing towards the team," Gardner-Johnson said.
Buffalo is coming off one of its best defensive showings of the season  against the Baltimore Ravens. They were aided by the fact that Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley were both hurt during the game, but still showed enough in the secondary to give them the confidence to do what needed to be done and say goodbye to Gardner-Johnson.

title: Josh Allen Is Latest Victim of Despicable Act From Roquan Smith During Bills-Ravens Game
full_text:
There is an alarming trend with Baltimore Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith and we saw it first hand with Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen in Week 8.
During the contest on Sunday , Allen was attempting to score at the goal line on a QB sneak when Smith can clearly be seen grabbing Allen's facemask.
As if that wasn't bad enough, Smith turns Allen's entire helmet in what absolutely looks like a malicious play from the Ravens linebacker.
Check out video of the play below.
Is Josh Allen part owl? Roquan Smith twisted his neck nearly 180 degrees on his touchdown run. #BillsMafia @BuffaloPlus pic.twitter.com/92orE2nEeJ
Incredibly, even with all of the focus squarely on the play, no flag was thrown by the officials.
We would like to think that was an accident, but we've seen Smith do this at least once more this season, and twice more since last season, so the veteran defender doesn't get the benefit of the doubt.
Back in Week 2, he did something similar to New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough. Smith ended up getting hit with a fine from the NFL, but he was not flagged during the game, either.
"The NFL fined Ravens LB Roquan Smith $11,941 for grabbing Saints QB Tyler Shough’s facemask on this play last week," The Ringer's Tom Pelissero wrote. "No flag was thrown, but officials ruled Shough scored a TD and it stood upon review."
Refs miss a face mask on this Saints tush push. Tyler Shough gets his head pulled all the way back and the refs didn't see it pic.twitter.com/EPC9KNpfAa
There's also video of Smith doing a similar thing to Los Angeles Rams tight end Davis Allen in 2025. There might be even more instances if we dig, but you get the point. This isn't a one-off situation here.
These plays are extremely dangerous and could cause a serious injury. There is no excuse for what Smith did in either instance.
"I didn't know anything about it in game. Had I know, I probably would have impacted some of the QB sneaks later in the game," head coach Joe Brady said . "Whether it was intentional or not, that's obviously not something you want to see in football."
"I'm surprised something didn't get called from there, but obviously not my place," Brady added.
The NFL will likely fine him again, but at this point the league should suspend Smith to drive home the point that this is unacceptable.
What will it take for the league to take action outside of just a simple fine that Smith can easily afford with his $100 million contract?
As for Smith, he needs to do some serious soul-searching before he seriously injures someone, or worse.

title: Week 9 NFL Power Rankings Roundup: Bills Are Mid-Season Kings of NFL
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills won easily this weekend against the Baltimore Ravens, although they know that game got out of hand in a hurry . Lamar Jackson was injured on Baltimore's first offensive snap and Tyler Huntley went down later in the first half.
That left the Ravens with Joe Fagnano under center and the Bills capitalized by winning 36-10. It was their most lopsided victory of the season and while some might shrug off the performance due to the injuries, Buffalo did what good teams are supposed to do in such a situation: won convincingly.
Now sitting at 6-1, they have a tough task ahead of them as the Bills will face the Minnesota Vikings on the road in Week 9. That Monday Night Football showdown will tell us a lot about this team, but for now, we can look at several power rankings from multiple outlets and see that Buffalo is entering Week 9 as kings of the NFL.
Connor Orr was mostly blown away by the fact that Josh Allen nearly had his head ripped off near the goal line in this one. Somehow, the refs missed it and that non-call hasn't gotten the attention it deserves.
”I was honestly pretty surprised at the muted response to Josh Allen getting his neck twisted almost 200 degrees on Sunday by Roquan Smith which, purposeful or not, deserved a stronger pushback from almost everyone involved. Allen remaining healthy is our best chance at getting one of a few select dream Super Bowl matchup.” Orr wrote.
ESPN had the Bills at No. 2 last week and with the Minnesota Vikings losing, they claim the top spot. That will make this coming game even more intriguing as we have two of the best teams this season meeting up.
Josh Kendall and Chad Graff combined on The Athletic's rankings once again and still have the Bills at No. 1. That said, they're not sure they learned anything since the Bills didn't get to showcase their defense against Jackson.
“Sunday didn’t teach us anything because Baltimore’s top two quarterbacks left the game with injury. Even with the Ravens and their UDFA emergency quarterback averaging 2.9 yards per play, the Bills are 29th in defensive EPA this season (minus-41.92). Luckily, they still have Josh Allen, who had three touchdowns and completed passes to eight receivers.”
Like others, Nick Shook isn't sure if the defense is truly better. He did say they played well after the bye week, but that was against Fagnano. Perhaps this can be a momentum builder for Jim Leonhard's unit.
“With Minnesota's loss at Detroit, there isn’t a blemish-free NFL team. Even the best rosters have holes. Buffalo’s offense remains explosive and was able to overcome its own early challenges to cruise to a win over Baltimore, but the big question mark lies with its defense. Sunday represented a massive improvement for the unit, which held the Ravens to 144 total yards, but it did so against an offense that was forced to rely on a third-string, undrafted-rookie quarterback,” Shook wrote.
Gary Davenport isn't sold on the defense either, but as he points out, there are some winnable games coming up following the Vikings showdown. This could prove to be a solid stretch for the Buffalo defense.
“That defense remains cause for concern, but Buffalo's schedule is manageable over the next few weeks—meetings with the Jets and Dolphins follow next week's trip to Minnesota,” Davenport wrote.
Stop me if you've heard this before, Pete Prisco is worried about the defense.
”They lead the league in scoring, which they might need to, in order to win it all with their defense. That offense faces a tough challenge this week against the Vikings,” Prisco wrote.
This week, as Prisco points out, the Bills will be taking on an elite defense in Minnesota. How they handle the pressure from Brian Flores will go a long way toward deciding if they remain the kings of the NFL after Week 9.

title: Bills' WR Corps Awaits Mid-Season Addition as NFL Trade Deadline Approaches
full_text:
It's seemingly unlikely that Josh Downs or Brian Thomas Jr. land in Orchard Park this November, but the Buffalo Bills ' receiving corps is nonetheless in line for an addition as the NFL trade deadline approaches .
The Bills, however, need not sacrifice any trade capital when pulling the trigger on this particular transaction.
Working his way back from the ACL tear he suffered last January , wide receiver Tyrell Shavers made his return to the practice field as the Bills resumed activities following their Week 7 bye.
After the Bills opened his 21-day activation window, Shavers, who has been on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list since the start of training camp, practiced in a limited capacity all week leading up to the November 1 win over the Baltimore Ravens.
"I think I'm right on time," said Shavers following the October 28 practice . "I got cleared by the doctor like three, four weeks ago, but I mean, it's just a matter of time whenever they open my window, so I'm ready to rock."
Bills' head coach Joe Brady has yet to reveal when the team plans to activate Shavers, but that time may come sooner than initially expected in response to the hamstring injury suffered by Josh Palmer late in the first quarter against the Ravens.
Buffalo is currently carrying six wide receivers on its 53-man roster, including Palmer and return specialist Greg Dortch.
After two seasons on the Bills' practice squad, Shavers made the 53-man roster out of training camp and proceeded to play in all 17 regular season games on the 2025 schedule.
The 6-foot-4 pass-catcher made nine starts, partly due to Keon Coleman falling out of favor with the prior coaching staff. Playing 39 percent of offensive snaps, he developed into an effective run blocker while catching 15 of 23 targets for 245 yards and one touchdown through the air.
Shavers also showed special teams value, playing 56 percent of possible snaps on the Bills' return and coverage units.
"We talk about ethos of special teams, a guy like Tyrell Shavers is what you want to build your team around, like the personality, the mindsets," said Brady.
The 27-year-old's size and physicality adds a different dimension to the offense as opposed to the smaller Dortch and fourth-round rookie Skyler Bell.
Brady, who remains in awe of the fact that Shavers somewhat miraculously soldiered through a torn ACL during the entire second half of the January 11 wild-card win over the Jacksonville Jaguars, openly appreciates the mentality that the undrafted wide receiver has shown.
"He obviously makes our football team better, just him being in the building," said Brady. "He's a guy that doesn't give a damn about if he has a catch, doesn't care about anything besides us, doing whatever he can do to help us win."
Quarterback Josh Allen, a five-time NFL MVP finalist, voiced tremendous respect for Shavers.
"He's got one of the best stories out there. Just how he bounced around in college, coming here, being a P-squad guy, not really getting opportunities. Finally getting his opportunities, making the most of them, getting injured, fighting back, and now he's back out here practicing," said Allen recalling what's been an eventful few years for the underdog.
Allen, who has spoken highly of Shavers in the past , explained more of what makes him valuable to the Bills.
"He's one of the best teammates I've ever had. He consistently just does what he's told to do. He finds himself in the right spot because he understands where he's supposed to be, at what time," said Allen.

title: Monroe Freeling Looks Like a Misfire, So What Should Panthers Have Done?
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers spent the 19th pick on Monroe Freeling, a move that came as a surprise to some but was praised by many. It hasn't panned out so far. Freeling has looked lost often.
From a depth perspective, tackle was unfortunately the only move they could've made . They couldn't foresee losing Taylor Moton and then losing him again seven quarters after he returned, but picking a backup for him proved to be prescient.
And in terms of immediate contributors in the rest of the first round, there aren't many. Dillon Thieneman might be the only better option, but the Panthers are probably thrilled with Zakee Wheatley instead.
So, if the Panthers did get a do-over, would they take Freeling? They would not, according to Bleacher Report's Brent Sobleski, but they would still pick a tackle.
In Brent Sobleski's re-draft, the Panthers don't select Monroe Freeling, and it's not because he outplayed his draft slot (like Tetairoa McMillan in some 2025 re-drafts). It's because he hasn't remotely been worth it.
Freeling was always seen as a raw, developmental pick, and injuries have forced him into the lineup. Still, he honestly looks a good ways away from being an NFL player. The only reason he doesn't look worse is because his tackle teammate, Rasheed Walker, is among the worst linemen in the NFL.
Freeling didn't even get picked in the first round in Sobleski's do-over, which isn't surprising. So, who do the Panthers go with? According to the insider, they pick Max Iheanachor, who originally went a couple of picks later to the Pittsburgh Steelers.
"Carolina did sink this pick into an offensive tackle, Monroe Freeling, but Max Iheanachor was the better bet among the developmental options," Sobleski said.
He pointed out how Freeling was thrown into the lineup and has, at times, looked out of his depth. Meanwhile, Iheanachor did not make the starting lineup initially, but he has worked his way onto the field and become a starter.
"Iheanachor's presence has made a difference. The Steelers are now more athletic and nasty at the point of attack, which gives him the edge [here]," he concluded.
The Panthers obviously needed a tackle, but Freeling wasn't ready to play. Maybe one day he'll be the right pick, but for now, Carolina is suffering and might wish they could do it over.

title: 9 Players the Panthers Have to Call About Before Trade Deadline
full_text:
As the NFL trade deadline grows closer, we took a stab at some players the Carolina Panthers have to look into. They won't deal for most, if any, of these players, but they should at least get on the phone and find out what it would cost.
We covered earlier how Josh Downs is actually a good idea even if he's not a cornerback or an offensive lineman, and with his desire to be traded, the Panthers have leverage. They can't just ignore the option, especially with a firesale going on in Indianapolis.
The Panthers have suffered without Nic Scourton because he rushes the passer and sets the edge on the run. Josh Sweat can do that, too. He has a 64.7 run defense grade as an edge rusher. He'll be in high demand, but the Panthers have to at least check in.
The Panthers need bodies up front on defense. They have to be able to stop the run, and adding an interior defender like Grover Stewart makes a ton of sense. Have we mentioned that there's a firesale going on in Indianapolis?
Would the New Orleans Saints sell to the Panthers with a small gap between them in the standings? Probably not, but the Panthers badly need help on the offensive line. Robert Hunt has been abysmal, so calling about guard Cesar Ruiz is not a bad idea.
This year, cornerback is a massive need for the Panthers, but it will remain so in the future. Mike Jackson's contract is up, and can we trust Jaycee Horn and Will Lee to stay healthy for 17 games? Now, Sauce Gardner has his own injury history, but between the three of them, we like the chances of getting two full seasons.
The Philadelphia Eagles have already traded an offensive lineman and saw another retire. Why not just take this lost season as a chance to reset and keep selling pieces? Landon Dickerson can play guard and center, two positions the Panthers could stand to upgrade.
There are connections between Eagles CB Riq Woolen and the Panthers' coaching staff, so the fit makes sense. The need is obvious, too, and while Gardner is a long-term addition, Woolen would be much cheaper and a whole lot simpler to add right now.
It's as simple as the Panthers needing a cornerback and Jackson being familiar with this staff. He worked under new CB coach DeAngelo Hall in 2023. Plus, the Los Angeles Chargers should be interested in trading whoever they can.
The run defense has been shockingly bad this year, and that's with the Panthers running out fourth and fifth-string cornerbacks. If cornerback is the top priority, defensive lineman has to be up there, too. Adding Zach Sieler from the dead-end Miami Dolphins is a nice idea.
