title: 7 Injuries to Monitor for Panthers: Good News on the Horizon?
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have arguably been the most injured team all season. They've lost four cornerbacks, their top two edge rushers, both starting tackles, a starting guard, the second running back, the third wide receiver, their prized rookie wide receiver, and more. Those players are all out right now.
At times, they've been without Devin Lloyd, Bobby Okereke, Jalen Coker, Monroe Freeling, Bobby Brown, and Pat Jones. It has been a bloodbath, and one could reasonably argue that it has played a hand in their 3-4 record.
After a "mini-bye," so to speak, the Panthers are back in action this week ahead of an important matchup with the Denver Broncos . And fortunately, there are some positive rumblings in the injury world for once.
Through seven contests, the Panthers have honestly dropped like flies. Starting in Week 3, it seems like every single game costs a player a trip to the IR or at least a couple of games on the bench, unable to suit up.
That didn't end last week, with Will Lee III going down. He may avoid the IR, but he probably won't play this week. It's just been that kind of season, which is a shame given the talent this roster actually has when it's healthy.
Regardless, though, things may be beginning to turn in Carolina's favor. There are several injuries to monitor this week, and there is plenty of good news that seems to be on the horizon.
On Tuesday, Xavier Legette and Jonathon Brooks both got some work in on the side. So did Mike Jackson. The Panthers reportedly plan to open the 21-day return window for Brooks and Legette sooner rather than later.
Xavier Legette and Jonathon Brooks getting some work in. Mike Jackson also. pic.twitter.com/4h3HYFakKU
Joe Person reported that Jaelan Phillips and Jaycee Horn were also working off to the side. Horn hasn't played since Week 3, and Phillips has been out the last couple of weeks.
Dave Canales: Opening the 21-day window for OL Brady Christensen. Has to "get some football under his belt" to see where he can help the Panthers.
The Panthers officially opened the 21-day return window for Brady Christensen. They want him to get his feet under him first, but he could potentially be in the lineup sooner rather than later.
And perhaps the best update of all: Bryce Young hasn't missed any snaps, but he has clearly been hobbled by a knee injury, sapping his mobility. Young said he's "good," although he has never said it's been a problem.
Head coach Dave Canales said after practice that QB Bryce Young is "ready to rock" moving forward. Canales said there was a lot of energy at practice.
Dave Canales said it was hampering his quarterback, and on Tuesday, the coach said Young was "ready to rock," and reports suggest that Young's mobility is much improved. That could be the most significant update of all.

title: Week 9 NFL Odds Reveal Panthers' Chances of Righting Ship vs. Broncos
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have endured back-to-back brutal losses. In both games, the offensive line collapsed to a level that made things untenable for virtually the entire offense. The defense wasn't in much better shape.
Despite getting a few extra days to prepare for Week 9, there is no reprieve . The Panthers are back home after a crushing trip to Green Bay, but the red-hot Denver Broncos are in town. They're coming off a huge win over the Kansas City Chiefs.
Unsurprisingly, the Panthers are home underdogs this week.
A win puts the Panthers at 4-4 and keeps them in first place in the NFC South. A loss drops them to 3-5 and puts them at risk of falling out of first place. This is a crucial game, and now that we're past the halfway point, all games carry a little bit of extra importance.
Unfortunately, oddsmakers don't think the Panthers are going to bounce back this week. On DraftKings , the Panthers are +120 to win on the moneyline. The Broncos are -142 to win outright.
The spread is 2.5 points, which is slightly down from where it began. The Panthers are -102 to cover, while the Broncos are -118 to cover the spread.
The over/under is set at 43.5 points. The over is -115, while the under is -105. Based on that, the final score is expected to be something along the lines of Broncos 24, Panthers 21. A close home defeat.
What does this tell us? It reveals that the Broncos are perhaps a little more vulnerable than we think. Their defense is absurdly good, and the Panthers have been crushed by good defenses two weeks in a row. But if the spread isn't that wide, then there's a path to victory.
The Broncos' offense is not absurdly good. In fact, it has been criticized plenty this season. Bo Nix is not playing good football. They have often won in spite of him. Could the Panthers' defense be motivated after Ejiro Evero's firing and take advantage of a lackluster offense?
Right now, the Panthers' defense is a movable object, and the Broncos' offense is a stoppable force. If the Carolina defense rises to the occasion, they might be able to gift the Panthers' offense a couple of possessions that could be key.

title: 5 Cornerbacks the Panthers Have Been Urged to Target at Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Panthers aren't just a little thin at cornerback anymore. They're running out of guys.
Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are already on injured reserve. Akayleb Evans joined them last week, and then Will Lee III went down against Green Bay with a hamstring injury. By the end of that game, Carolina was down to three healthy corners.
That's a tough way to make it through November.
CBS Sports recently named cornerback as the Panthers' biggest need at the trade deadlin e and came up with five players Carolina could look at: Riq Woolen, Donte Jackson, Alontae Taylor, Amik Robertson and Nahshon Wright.
Some of those names make a lot more sense to me than others.
Carolina doesn't need to make a trade just so it can say it did something. But with this many injuries at one position, Dan Morgan should at least be making calls.
So let's go through the five names CBS suggested and figure out which ones I'd actually want the Panthers to pursue.
Woolen is probably the first guy I'd call about.
I've liked his game for a while. He's 6-foot-4, has plenty of speed and has picked off 12 passes since coming into the league. Carolina could use all of that right now.
The only reason I'd hesitate is because he might not be here very long.
His contract is up after this season. Maybe the Panthers trade for him and two months later he's gone. I'm not crazy about that, but it wouldn't stop me either.
It really comes down to what Philadelphia wants.
If a fifth-round pick gets it done, I'd make the trade. If we're talking about a fourth, I'd have to think about it. Anything more than that and I'm out.
It doesn't need one badly enough to do something stupid.
Donte Jackson wouldn't need much of an introduction in Carolina.
We watched him play here for six years. There were good days and some frustrating ones, but Jackson started a lot of football games for the Panthers. If the Chargers aren't asking for much, I could see going back to someone Carolina already knows.
I'd have one question first. How healthy is he?
Jackson has only been on the field for four games this season because of a hamstring injury. Carolina already has enough injured corners. Before I'd give up anything for Jackson, I'd need to know he's ready to play.
Taylor is where I'd probably pass.
He can play outside or in the slot, and 40 pass breakups in four years with New Orleans isn't something I'd ignore. My problem isn't really with Taylor as a player.
Tennessee just signed him in March, and Carolina would be taking on $20.51 million guaranteed for next season. That's a lot different from grabbing Jackson for the rest of this year and seeing what happens.
Maybe Taylor would help. He probably would.
I just don't like the idea of solving an injury problem in November by taking on that much money for next season.
If I'm choosing between these two, give me Jackson at the cheaper price.
Amik Robertson might be the guy on this list I'm overlooking.
He's played seven games for Washington this season and already has eight passes defended. He's also been around long enough that Carolina should have a pretty good idea what it's getting. Robertson isn't the big swing Woolen would be, but maybe that's not what the Panthers need.
I'd have no problem calling Washington about him. Robertson has another year on his contract, but Carolina could get out of it after the season if things don't work.
Wright is the one I can't figure out.
Five interceptions last year. This year? Not one defensive snap for the Jets. He was hurt during training camp, lost the competition for a starting job and hasn't been able to get back into the mix. Wright has even admitted this season has been frustrating.
That makes me want to know what New York would take for him.
Carolina is desperate enough at corner to take a chance, and Wright shouldn't cost much considering he can't get on the field in New York.
Robertson would be the safer call. Wright would be the gamble.
At this point, I'd be willing to ask about both.
Woolen would be my first call.
This isn't a hard one for me. If I'm going to trade for a corner, give me the guy I think can help the most. I can worry about his contract when the season is over.
That doesn't mean Philadelphia gets whatever it asks for. There's a limit, and I'd be perfectly fine hanging up the phone if things got stupid.
Jackson would still interest me. I've seen him play enough football in a Panthers uniform to know exactly what comes with that deal.
I'm calling about Woolen first and going from there.
I'd rather take the shot on the best corner of these five and see what happens.

title: The Case For—and Against—the Panthers Trading for Jackson Powers-Johnson
full_text:
I've lost track of how many different offensive line combinations the Panthers have used this season. Injuries are part of it, but at some point you have to wonder how long Carolina can keep moving pieces around and hoping it works.
Jackson Powers-Johnson is an interesting name to consider.
Things haven't gone the way Powers-Johnson probably expected in Las Vegas. He was a second-round pick just two years ago, but he's already lost his spot in the starting lineup. If the Raiders are willing to move on this quickly, Carolina should at least find out what it would take.
I'm not looking at Powers-Johnson as some huge upgrade that suddenly fixes the offensive line. That's asking too much. What I like is that he's 23, he's played guard and center, and Carolina wouldn't be bringing in another veteran just to get through the next couple of months.
Especially after watching Bryce Young hit the ground six times against Green Bay.
There are reasons for Carolina to make the call.
There are also a few pretty good reasons to leave this one alone.
Powers-Johnson is a weird trade target. A year ago, I'm not sure the Raiders would've even listened. Now we're talking about whether a Day 3 pick could get it done.
He started 14 games as a rookie. Some came at left guard, others at center.
Losing his starting job bothers me. It should. I'd want to know why things changed so much from one season to the next before giving Las Vegas anything for him. But 14 starts as a rookie is enough for me to wonder if there's still something there.
There's no guarantee they can. That's why we're talking about a Day 3 pick instead of something much higher.
Maybe Carolina gets the rookie version of Powers-Johnson. If not, they move on and a late pick is gone. I can live with that.
I'd rather see the Panthers take that chance than keep moving the same pieces around up front.
This is where I get hung up. Trading for an offensive lineman sounds good right now. Trading for one who just lost his own starting job doesn't sound quite as good.
Powers-Johnson was playing right guard when the Raiders made a change. That's enough to make me wonder what Carolina would be getting. Maybe Las Vegas gave up on him too quickly. I'd still want an answer for why he isn't playing.
Then you have to figure out where he plays. Robert Hunt is at right guard. Powers-Johnson has experience at center, but he hasn't been playing there lately. If the Panthers trade for him, I'd want it to be because they have a spot in mind and not because they saw a former second-round pick available for cheap.
That's where I have a harder time talking myself into this one. Carolina doesn't need another offensive lineman to move around and figure out later.
They've done enough of that already.
For a Day 3 pick? Yeah, I would.
There's enough about Powers-Johnson that bothers me to understand why the Raiders might be ready to move on. I'm just not sure I'm ready to do the same with a 23-year-old offensive lineman who was starting games as a rookie.
I wouldn't get cute with the offer. If Las Vegas wants more than a late pick, they can keep him. Carolina has too many other things to fix to start throwing better picks at a player the Raiders just benched.
But a late pick is different. I'd send it and see if a new team can get something out of him.
If not, Dan Morgan moves on.
I think this one is worth finding out.

He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Carolina Panthers Linked to Playmaker Trade They Simply Have to Consider
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are opening the 21-day return window for Xavier Legette soon. He'll likely be back sooner rather than later. And with his return, hopefully, a return of the explosive offense we saw from the first few weeks of the season.
Because of that, and honestly, even without him, wide receiver is low down on the list of needs for the Panthers. Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker are both great, and John Metchie and Brycen Tremayne have stepped up pretty well.
The offensive line, particularly at left tackle, center, and right guard, could use reinforcements. The defense needs help in the trenches, off the edge, and at cornerback , the latter of which is something that transcends the word "need."
Why, then, is FOX Sports analyst Steven Ruiz saying he wants to see the Panthers trade for Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs? And why does it make so much sense for a team that doesn't exactly need playmakers?
Maybe it's because we've seen how great Bryce Young can be this season, but adding another wide receiver to this room is a scintillating proposition. The offensive line is a mess, and there are major holes on defense, but perhaps the right wide receiver can really transform this offense.
Enter Josh Downs, who has requested a trade from the Colts. FOX Sports insider Steven Ruiz wants to see him go to Carolina, just down the road from where he played college at UNC.
"The Panthers need more pass protection, but a receiver like Downs, who can get open quickly, can help a quarterback just as much. And Downs can be more than a pressure release valve for Bryce Young," Ruiz wrote.
Something alarming we saw against the Green Bay Packers was that the Panthers just didn't have answers. They knew pressure was coming no matter how many rushers came at Young, and when the Packers did blitz, Carolina had nothing.
The Packers, meanwhile, absorbed the blitzes with hot routes and quick answers. Jordan Love had more immediate answers than Young, and you see the difference in results. Giving Brad Idzik a weapon like Downs to provide a safety valve is crucial.
The book is out on Carolina. The Panthers can't block anyone, so send pressure. Adding Downs would help alleviate that, and a wide receiver like Downs is a lot easier to acquire right now than a left tackle or a right guard.
Ruiz also pointed out that Downs is excellent against man coverage, which would give the Panthers a good option there. Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker are better against zone, and Downs has the seventh-most receiving yards against man in the entire NFL.
To alleviate the pressure Young is facing and give the offense another wrinkle to attack different coverages, Downs makes way too much sense.

title: Panthers Reportedly Considering O-Line Changes. Here's Who Should Start Now
full_text:
As Mina Kimes put it on Thursday night, the Carolina Panthers' offensive line is a "real problem" right now. Bryce Young has been the most pressured quarterback in the NFL all season, and that came to a head in the last two weeks, both ugly offensive performances.
The Packers pressured Bryce Young on 47% of dropbacks tonight, per @NextGenStats . Last week vs Tampa it was 52%. Offensive line situation is a real, real problem right now.
Young is dealing with a knee injury that has sapped his mobility, which means the pressure he's facing is able to get home. Nothing has really changed with the offensive line, except that Damien Lewis has popped in and out with an injury. Taylor Moton returned for about a game and a half, so that doesn't really count.
Either way, the current situation is untenable. And according to Joe Person of The Athletic, a source close to Dave Canales expects the Panthers to consider making some changes up front. The offensive line we saw on Thursday may not be the one that trots out to start on Sunday.
And after allowing 11 sacks the past two games, Dave Canales is considering making personnel changes to the offensive line, per the same source.
If that's the case, here's how the Panthers should probably line up.
Ordinarily, we'd assume this was just talk. The Panthers' coaching staff has been hesitant to make big changes, often believing in their guys to the bitter end. But this is after Dave Canales fired two defensive coaches, including Ejiro Evero.
Maybe they really aren't messing around anymore. We certainly hope so, because as bad as the defense was, the offensive line reached "unplayable" status on Thursday. That was two straight weeks of just abysmal play.
Unfortunately, the best linemen aren't healthy. Taylor Moton and Ikem Ekwonu won't be playing. Damien Lewis might not, although he is hoping to be healthy enough for Week 9. Let's assume he does play.
He will start at left guard, and Monroe Freeling should slide over to be the left tackle beside Lewis. Freeling hasn't been good, but it's baptism by fire, and Rasheed Walker has been literally unplayable. He might be the worst left tackle in the NFL, and Freeling was meant to one day be the left tackle, so it's time to try it.
Sam Hecht should start at center. Luke Fortner is no longer the weakest link on the line, but he hasn't gotten better. He's been pretty bad all year, and Hecht deserves a shot to improve the position. He probably can't be any worse.
The $100 man, Robert Hunt, is sadly going to be benched in our projection. Will the Panthers sit one of their most expensive contracts? Dubious, to say the least. But they should. Like Walker, he's borderline unplayably bad right now, and there's no clear reason why. Brady Christensen (once he's cleared to return) should probably start instead, especially with Corey Bullock and Toricelli Simpkins banged up, too.
That leaves right tackle. Unfortunately, it's Stone Forsythe time. He was not good in limited action when Monroe Freeling got hurt, but he's the next man up. Having him on the right side mitigates the threat he poses to Bryce Young.
And if he can't cut it, try out Albert Reese. But for now, that should be the five-man unit.

title: 3 Carolina Panthers Who Could Be Traded If Freefall Continues
full_text:
It wasn't that long ago that I was looking at players the Panthers could add before the trade deadline . Things can change pretty fast in the NFL.
Now I'm starting to wonder about the other side of it. Carolina has been heading in the wrong direction, and the Nov. 10 trade deadline is getting closer. If this continues, Dan Morgan might have to start thinking about what he can get for a few players instead of what he can add.
I don't think that means the Panthers should start getting rid of everybody. There are still plenty of players on this roster who should be part of what they're building. But there are three guys who make some sense if another team calls.
Ja'Tavion Sanders is the first name that comes to mind for me. I liked what I saw from him at times during his first two seasons, but I don't really know what the Panthers are doing with him now.
He's behind Tommy Tremble, Mitchell Evans and Darren Waller, and we've already seen him end up as a healthy scratch. That's a big change for a guy who caught 62 passes over his first two years in the league.
Carolina probably isn't getting much back for him. Maybe it's a late-round pick, but I'd rather get something than continue keeping a young player around who isn't getting on the field. A team looking for some help at tight end could be willing to take that chance.
I still don't know what to make of Xavier Legette . There are weeks when I think the Panthers just need to be patient with him, and then there are games where I barely notice he's out there. That's tough when you're talking about a former first-round pick.
That's what makes Legette an interesting name before the deadline. I'm sure there are teams that remember the size and speed he showed at South Carolina, and it only takes one of them to make a call. I wouldn't be shocked if somebody thought they could get more out of him.
I wouldn't take just anything for him. Carolina has already put too much into Legette to turn around and dump him for a late-round pick. Unless somebody offers more than I'm expecting, I'd leave this one alone.
Bobby Brown III is different from the first two because I'd have no problem keeping him. I actually went back and forth on putting him here at all. Brown isn't somebody I've watched this season and thought the Panthers need to get rid of.
Defensive linemen are always useful this time of year, especially for a team getting ready to make a playoff run. That's why I'd at least see what teams are willing to offer. You never know when a team thinks it's one player away and is willing to give up a little more than you'd expect.
If the call never comes, that's fine too. Brown can stay in Carolina and keep doing what he's been doing. This is more about seeing what's out there than trying to find a way to move him.
The next week should tell us a lot about where the Panthers think this season is going. Keep losing and the conversation around the deadline changes pretty quickly.
Carolina doesn't have to make any of these moves. But if things continue going the way they have, Morgan should at least be willing to listen.

title: Dolphins Standout Could Be Answer to Carolina Panthers' Prayers
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have seemingly hit rock bottom on one side of the ball . For two straight weeks, Carolina has underperformed defensively, and while injuries play a major role, the production is still alarmingly bad.
The Panthers' secondary is decimated ; Carolina currently has four corners injured, leaving third-stringers on the field. That area of struggle is understandable; what's egregious is Carolina's inability to stop the run.
Through seven games, the Panthers rank among the bottom three rushing defenses in the NFL, surrendering just over 140 rushing yards per game. Even more alarming, the Panthers allow 198.3 rushing yards at home, second-to-last in the NFL behind the Dallas Cowboys.
It's safe to assume the lack of run defense was a contributing factor in defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero getting fired. Carolina has two home games in which it allowed over 258 yards on the ground.
The NFL trade deadline is in 6 days, taking place on November 10th at 4 PM ET. With that said, Carolina can add some help to a struggling run defense.
Bleacher Report's Kristopher Knox dropped his trade candidate big board entering Week 8 . On that list, shocking the potential fit, Carolina was mentioned, but it didn't have to do with the secondary.
While the secondary is injured, the defensive line has been relatively healthy throughout the season, and it's still been abysmal at stopping the run. Sieler is an established veteran in the NFL, and earned a three-year extension, worth up to $67 million.
The Miami Dolphins are a prime seller candidate for the trade deadline. The playoffs aren't a realistic goal, so trading an instant contributor like Sieler to a playoff hopeful makes sense. Knox also noted that Sieler could be a potential cap casualty.
Releasing or getting Sieler off the roster would save the Dolphins roughly $13.8 million for next year, Even more reason to ship him to a contender now.
The best part: Sieler won't command too much  as far as what the Panthers would have to return. Knox slotted Sieler's trade value as a conditional fifth-round pick.
Right now, Carolina doesn't own any fifth-rounders, but the Panthers do own two fourth-rounders, so they could give the Dolphins either one of those picks, whether it's the Vikings' fourth-rounder or Carolina's own, that's more than a fair price for a team that is 1-7 on the season and needs to load up on draft picks.
The deal seems like a no-brainer. Sieler has 2 sacks so far. Against the run, Sieler is very good, with excellent technique and great hand placement once a play has started. Carolina has to figure this out at some point, because they've already taken the most extreme measure, and another offensive coordinator won't be fired again.

title: Chicago Bears Left Tackle Braxton Jones Set to Miss Rest of Season
full_text:
The Chicago Bears will not be getting left tackle Braxton Jones back this season.
According to The Chicago Tribune's Brad Biggs , Jones, who is on injured reserve due to a knee injury , suffered a partially torn patellar tendon that required season-ending surgery.
The initial plan was for Jones to rehabilitate the injury and make his way back, but that apparently did not work out.
"Chicago Bears left tackle Braxton Jones underwent surgery on his right knee Tuesday and won’t be an option to return from injured reserve this season," Biggs wrote.
"Jones suffered a partially torn patellar tendon, and the plan was for him to rehabilitate the injury before determining if it was feasible for him to return this season and delay surgery," he added. "After a little more than a month, it was decided to have the injury repaired, an NFL source said Wednesday."
This is the second significant injury Jones has suffered in the last three years. He saw his 2024 campaign cut short due to a broken left ankle, and he just didn't look like himself in his first season back in 2025, which led to him getting benched.
But Jones had rebounded in 2026 and was playing good football while serving as the replacement for Ozzy Trapilo, who was working his way back from his own torn patellar.
Unfortunately for the Bears, Jones' injury might not be the only one at the left tackle position.
According to Bears beat writer Nicholas Moreano of Bears Roundtable , it appears Theo Benedet might have suffered a shoulder injury in the Week 8 victory over the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night.
"One observation from the Bears' locker room. I saw Theo Benedet leave with a Bears staff member before the media was allowed into the locker room," Moreano said. "When he came back, he sat at his locker, looking disappointed. As I was getting ready to record an interview, I heard him say separated shoulder."
If Benedet is indeed dealing with a separated shoulder, he could miss significant time, in which case the Bears' depth at tackle is now in a very precarious spot.
Benedet had been playing the majority of the snaps at the position since Jones went down, with Ozzy Trapilo mixing in.
It goes without saying that now the Bears will have to rely on their second-round pick for more.
Chicago has been slowly ramping Trapilo up since he returned from his injury, but he has yet to take on a full workload in any game. He played 17 snaps in Week 6, 19 in Week 7, but then Trapilo didn't play any in Week 8.
If Benedet is indeed injured, the Bears are going to have to add another player at tackle, even if Trapilo is ready to be a full go.

title: 2024 Re-Draft Has the Bears Passing on Rome Odunze After Luther Burden III Overtook Him
full_text:
When an NFL team selects a player with a Top 10 pick in the draft, they expect to get an immediate game-changer. Someone who can dominate at their position for the next decade or more. That's what the Chicago Bears hoped they were getting when they selected wide receiver Rome Odunze with the No. 9 pick in the 2024 NFL draft, but through two and a half seasons, he's fallen well short of the mark.
It can hardly surprise Bears fans when, in a redo of the 2024 NFL first-round draft , Gilberto Manzano of Sports Illustrated has the Bears passing on Odunze. "Top-10 picks should be for future No. 1 wideouts," Manzano writes. "At the moment, it doesn’t seem as if Odunze will become that for the Bears after being leapfrogged on the pecking order by second-year wideout Luther Burden III."
This is a fair assessment of Odunze's standing with the team, and it echoes what I said in the offseason when I predicted that Burden, not Odunze, would be the Bears' WR1 in 2026 . Where Manzano and I differ, however, is the proposed solution in a re-draft. Manzano has the Bears selecting cornerback Quinyon Mitchell, who originally went to the Philadelphia Eagles with the No. 22 pick.
Justifying this new pick, Manzano writes, "Top-10 picks are also meant for weekly shutdown perimeter corners. Mitchell has been just that for the Eagles." I don't disagree with that. Mitchell has been very good for the Eagles, and so far through 2026 he's earned a solid 83.9 impact grade from Pro Football Network .
However, Mitchell has benefitted tremendously from playing on a dominant defense led by one of the greatest defensive minds in recent NFL history, Vic Fangio. His defensive line is a juggernaut, and he plays alongside other solid defensive backs like Cooper DeJean and Riq Woolen. Until the Bears' blockbuster trade for Jeffery Simmons , their defense was several tiers below Philly's, and I think it's fair to wonder whether Mitchell would have been as successful in Chicago.
As disappointing as Odunze has been as a Top 10 pick, one must consider the opportunity cost of passing on him in a 2024 re-draft. If the Bears didn't have Odunze, they almost certainly would not have traded DJ Moore to the Buffalo Bills this year. And had they kept Moore, they would not have had sufficient cap space to trade for Simmons.
What this team would look like at this point in the season with Moore instead of Odunze and no Simmons on the defensive line is up to your imagination, but I don't think it looks nearly as good as it did on Monday night. Super Bowl contention would probably still be considered a bridge too far, yet some analysts consider the Bears to be Super Bowl favorites after their statement primetime victory over the Seattle Seahawks .
And, in fairness to Odunze, he's showed up in a big way for the Bears in each of their last two games. Minus a brutal drop in the endzone in Week 7, one that would have been negated by his offensive pass interference penalty anyway, he's made some mind-blowing catches and critical third-down receptions to keep drives alive.
An argument could be made that Odunze was the right pick for the Bears, even with the benefit of hindsight. If I were forced to select another player who was still available on draft night, it would be tight end Brock Bowers, but Bowers went sixth-overall in Manzano's re-draft and was arguably the last slam-dunk prospect available.
Looking at who was still on the board for the Bears in Manzano's re-draft, I would probably go with outside linebacker Dallas Turner or defensive end Jared Verse. Turner is in the midst of a breakout season and is currently the No. 5 EDGE rusher in Pro Football Network's impact rankings , while Verse's career was off to a great start before he was traded to Cleveland.
I would also consider left tackle Tyler Guyton, who went to Dallas with the No. 29 pick and has been a solid member of their offensive line, or even cornerback Kamari Lassiter. He's been up and down in Houston's secondary, but he at least has seven interceptions to his name; Mitchell has just one.

title: Sneaky Chicago Bears Need Could Lead to Trade With Eagles, Cowboys or Colts
full_text:
All of the attention surrounding the Chicago Bears ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline is on the defensive side of the ball, but could the Bears make a trade to address their offense?
On the surface, that seems preposterous. After all, the Bears have one of the best units in the NFL and there really aren't many weakness on that side of the ball.
However, that doesn't mean there aren't any weaknesses. One of them is tight end, where the Bears have a clear concern behind Colston Loveland.
After losing Cole Kmet to a season-ending knee injury, the Bears are now relying on a significant contribution from rookie Sam Roush, who has seen no shortage of struggles this season.
If Roush continues to struggle, the only other available tight ends in Chicago to step up are Stephen Carlson and Qadir Ismail, neither of whom inspire much confidence.
As a result of that and the Bears running 12- and 13-personnel at some of the highest rates in the NFL, it's not crazy to think that general manager Ryan Poles could look to make a trade for another tight end.
Three players the Bears could take a look at for tight end trades are Indianapolis Colts tight end Mo Alie-Cox, Dallas Cowboys tight end Luke Schoonmaker and Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert.
All three were mentioned as potential trade candidates by ESPN's Dan Graziano and Jeremy Fowler on Wednesday.
"Taylor isn't the Colts' only offensive player garnering interest," Fowler said on Wednesday. "Wide receiver Josh Downs and tight end Mo Alie-Cox are also on that list."
"If the Eagles trade players, I'd be looking at guys like Woolen, WR Hollywood Brown and maybe, maybe tight end Dallas Goedert for the right offer," Fowler said.
"Schoonmaker is the No. 3 tight end in the pecking order, and teams are looking for blocking tight ends," Fowler said .
They all certainly make sense as trade candidates, with the three tight ends slated to be free agents in 2027, and they are currently on teams going nowhere this season.
Any of the three would be a welcomed addition in Chicago with the team's need for another veteran.
There is no question that Goedert would be the preferred option here, and for a few reasons. He's not only a good blocker, but the Eagles tight end is also one of the better pass-catchers at his position in the NFL.
Over his first eight years in the league, the 31-year-old has six seasons with 500 yards or more, including two campaigns with north of 700 yards. He also posted 11 touchdowns in 2025, showing he can be an elite scoring threat.
Alie-Cox is a serviceable pass-catcher with a pair of 300-yard seasons under his belt, but he doesn't bring the kind of threat to the passing game that Goedert does.
However, Alie-Cox is still good in the red zone and he brings high-level inline blocking with him, which is where a lot of his value comes from.
Schoonmaker is the worst blocker and pass-catcher of the three, but he's still serviceable in both of those areas.
None them will be expensive. Alie-Cox and Schoonmaker probably garner a late Day 3 pick, while Goedert shouldn't cost more than a fourth and the Eagles might have to swap picks to get that.
Alie-Cox and Schoonmaker are the more realistic options for the Bears because of the cost, as Chicago will likely be looking to limit how much more it cuts into its draft stockpile after unloading so much of it in the Jeffery Simmons trade.
And, the Bears might not be done yet because of their needs at cornerback and edge rusher, where Chicago is reportedly focusing its efforts currently .
That said, it's not like the Bears will have to break the bank for Goedert, so we don't see a trade for him as impossible at all.

title: Bears Were NFC Championship Material Before Jeffery Simmons Trade, Coach Told Adam Schefter
full_text:
A few developments over the last few weeks have put the Chicago Bears in the conversation as one of the NFL's true Super Bowl contenders in 2026.
First, the Bears defeated the reigning AFC champions , the New England Patriots, in Week 7, 30-24.
Then, not only did Chicago acquire Jeffery Simmons in a trade with the Tennessee Titans, they also soundly defeated the defending Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks.
Making that win even better was the fact that Simmons wasted no time making an impact with six tackles, two tackles for loss, one sack and one pass defensed.
The Bears' peers already had a high opinion of them before the Simmons trade.
According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, an unnamed coach told the NFL insider that he viewed the Bears as an NFC Championship-level team prior to the blockbuster deal.
“There was a conversation I had recently with a coach who had been watching the Bears and had said to me, ‘The Chicago Bears are going to be in the NFC Championship Game. They are one of the best teams in football.’ And he said this to me before the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons," Schefter said on his podcast .
Schefter then went on to add that the team he watched dismantle the Seahawks on Monday night looked like a Super Bowl contender.
“When I watched that defense last night on Monday night with Jeffery Simmons, it looked even better," he said. "That team looked ferocious. That team looked like what that coach told me. That team looked like it’s good enough to win the Super Bowl. It looked like it’s good enough to be in the NFC Championship Game. It looked like it’s good enough to have one of those great magical seasons in Chicago, which doesn’t mean it will happen.
"There are some really good teams in the NFC, but I am more convinced than ever that the Chicago Bears are going to make a run. They’re going to have a chance, and they’re going to be there in the end, and we’ll see how that works out. But they are, Ty. They’re really good. They’re really good.”
There were definitely reasons to be high on the Bears before the Simmons trade.
For starters, the Bears have a great offense led by Caleb Williams, who is clearly ascending to an elite level in his third season. We need not look for more confirmation of that than how well he performed against Seattle's elite defense.
Chicago's defense was also playing better than expected before the Simmons trade, and now they have a true game-wrecker in the middle of that unit in the four-time Pro Bowler, who showed exactly how big of an impact he can make in his first game with the Bears.
And, lest we forget, the Bears weren't even at full strength versus the Seahawks, with the team missing its best cornerback in Malik Muhammad and one of its best pass-rushers in Dayo Odeyingbo, both of whom are injured.
After seeing how well the Bears played over the first seven weeks, it was not hard to understand why general manager Ryan Poles made the decision to go all-in with the trade for Simmons.
And the Bears might not even be done yet on defense.
Trade rumors suggest that the Bears are looking for more help on that side of the ball, including at edge rusher and cornerback, two areas that could use more help, with cornerback being more dire thanks to the struggles of Jaylon Johnson.
With a ton of talent (and possibly more coming) on both sides of the ball and elite coaching, the Bears have a real shot to make serious noise in 2026.

title: Bears Trade Rumor Confirms Edge Rusher Isn't Chicago's Only Deadline Focus
full_text:
After the Chicago Bears pulled off the trade for Jeffery Simmons , the belief has been that general manager Ryan Poles will turn his attention to edge rusher.
However, it appears that isn't the only position the Bears are looking to add to ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
According to ESPN's Dan Graziano and Jeremy Fowler , the Bears are also looking to add at cornerback.
"The Bears made their big move for Simmons, but they're still poking around on potentially available cornerbacks, as are the Lions," Graziano wrote.
"The Bears have been linked to edge rushers such as Khalil Mack, but a few league evaluators told me what you heard -- that cornerback is becoming more of a need," Fowler added.
While Malik Muhammad and Kyler Gordon have been sensational this season, the same cannot be said about Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson, both of whom have struggled.
Thankfully for the Bears, they were able to replace Stevenson with the rookie, but there is no such solution for Johnson, who has been a shell of the elite cornerback he used to be.
Chicago could certainly use someone else to challenge Johnson for his starting role.
Fowler floated two potential options for the Bears: Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen and Washington Commanders cornerback Mike Sainristil.
Fowler did note that the Commanders may not be keen on trading Sainristil but adds that Woolen may be available for a Day 3 pick.
"Washington's Mike Sainristil is a name that has circulated this week, though I don't get the sense the Commanders plan to trade him. An available corner such as the Eagles' Riq Woolen for a Day 3 pick could make sense," Fowler said.
Both players are logical trade candidates given the fact that they are both on bad teams, but only Woolen is on the final year of his contract, which makes him more likely to be dealt.
Woolen is easily the better option between the two. Not only is he having a better season, but Woolen thrives in man coverage and only one team in the NFL plays more man than Chicago .
In 2026, the veteran corner has given up a completion rate of 60% and a passer rating of 111.4. Not great, but those numbers are still better than Johnson's, and Woolen is playing in an Eagles defense that doesn't play much man (17.4%).
Woolen also brings playoff and Super Bowl experience with him, which is particularly attractive to a true contender like the Bears .
Given how bad things are with Johnson, acquiring Woolen for a Day 3 pick is a no-brainer move for Chicago.

title: Tampa Bay a Problem for Bears and Jeffery Simmons Even Without Completions
full_text:
For all of his strategic brilliance, Bears coach Ben Johnson is still a football coach at the heart of it.
Football coaches never let their team get ahead of themselves.
At least the ones with an ounce of value never do. Johnson wasn't letting his team do it even after Monday's 34-17 win over the defending Super Bowl champions in what may have been their biggest regular-season victory under their coach.
"There's a lot of places that we can get better at as well which we'll do, we'll look at in depth over the bye week but we're just solely focused every week," Johnson said. "I tried to explain this last week. We're just focused on how do we get 1-0 for the next week? Once we get into December and January, we'll start worrying about big-picture stuff, but we got to continue to improve and we got a short week coming up with a good opponent that's kind of hot right now.
"They're playing good football. So we got to keep it going. Prime time or not, we got to keep finding a way to go 1-0 each week."
The media could be forgiven if they had muffled their laughter about "playing good football." Tampa Bay just did something no NFL team would want to attempt and that's win without completing a single pass and by throwing only three against Atlanta. Even John Fox wouldn't do something like that, although it seemed he attempted it once as Bears coach.
In this case Johnson has every reason to warn the Beas against ignoring the 24-hour rule because Tampa Bay doesn't need "no steenking passes" to give the Bears a tough game Sunday night at Soldier Field. They've got the makeup already to be a Bears problem, perhaps even moreso than Seattle did based on the matchup.
Building something special pic.twitter.com/TrvCBNakX1
The only consistent offensive weapon Tampa Bay has is its running attack. This isn't to say Baker Mayfield is terrible. The Bears saw how good he was back when Matt Eberflus was coach, but he has been injured and Tampa Bay's receiver corps isn't what it was. What they do have is Bucky Irving and 728 rushing yards, Kenneth Gainwell as a second option and a good run-blocking offensive line. The Buccaneers had 324 rushing yards in the rain against the Falcons when they didn't complete a pass. Even the Bears' running game doesn't do that. They had 258 the week before that, and two weeks earlier 241. They have pulled ahead of the Bears in rushing as the No. 1 team in the league.
After the Bucs’ uneven offensive start, HC Todd Bowles and OC Zac Robinson huddled up to plot a new course. The result: A run-first blitz over the last two weeks. pic.twitter.com/TtWxRGoWRW
One defensive weakness the Bears haven't shown they've successfully covered up is their in ability to stop the run. They didn't really do it in Monday night's game, although they appeared better it with Jeffery Simmons in the lineup. They still allowed 81 yards on 19 rushes at 4.3 a carry. They have improved fourth in the NFL against the run but they're still lagging behind at 22nd in yards allowed per rush. Teams can gain on them, they just don't run it enough against the Bears. They give up on the run because they fall behind against the Bears offense. This could change once Simmons is in and settled at tackle, but he isn't in that situation yet and the Seahawks popped a couple of plus-10 runs in the game.
Tampa Bay’s running game could NOT be stopped today pic.twitter.com/aZUaXpLKQW
Tampa Bay is third in the NFL in time of possession, indicating they aren't exactly likely to abandon the run. If they didn't complete a single pass, they can't be expected to abandon the run. The most lopsided Bears loss came against Green Bay when the Packers played ball control initially but not with their ground game. They were incapable of this. Instead, they did it with a short passing game and then went to the deep ball and burned the Bears. Using ball control and the running attack could benefit the Buccaneers.
First play of the game for the Bucs. Graham Barton, Cody Mauch and Luke Goedeke go to work, and Bucky Irving shows off some really impressive contact balance pic.twitter.com/wTLCY6QruB
The second-worst game the Bears played on offense came against Minnesota's complicated blitzes. In facing Tampa Bay, they'll see a defense fifth in the league in blitz percentage at 33.6% Coach Todd Bowles has been known for his blitz packages back to his time as Jets coach. He's likely to give them the closest thing there is to seeing Brian Flores' complicated Minnesota blitz packages.
Something to watch for this morning is a few bears injuries… Kentavius Street - knee Grady Jarrett - groin Theo Benedet - unofficial, but @NicholasMoreano said he heard Theo say “separated shoulder” in locker room. Good reporting. Bears play the Bucs on Sunday night before…
The groin injury to Grady Jarrett and knee injury to Kentavius Street  suffered against Seattle deprive the Bears of two key defensive stoppers at tackle. The Bears never intended to use Jeffery Simmons 87% of the plays on Monday night but they did so with Street and Jarrett getting hurt. It's going to mean more playing time for Jayden Loving and Jordan van den Berg going forward but those are largely untested rookies. The opportunity for Tampa Bay to run and control the ball exists because of possible absences or at least with players who aren't entirely healthy forced to play. The injuries go behind those two. With Kyle Monangai still out due to toe and finger injuries, the ability of the Bears to move the chains with the running game is limited. They're averaging 105 yards rushing in four games without Monangai after averaging 196.2 in four games with him. This is a huge discrepancy.
The Bears defense by DVOA is 31st on first downs, 20th on second downs, and 2nd on third downs. Normally, this kind of thing is not sustainable. Is there something special about the Bears? Last year, their defense was also better on third down (26th, 24th, and 10th).
Johnson loves getting a lead and dictating the way the game will be played. Yet, Tampa Bay has the means for preventing this to a greater extent that other teams — even the two Super Bowl teams the Bears just beat. It could be a case where the Bears are going to need to lean heavily on Caleb Williams' passing and their offensive approach to keep from falling victims to an upset a week before their bye.
“If this is a sample of things to come for this Chicago Bears defense, then whoa.” Simmons made his presence felt. Caleb shined. Chicago has @RSherman_25 rethinking his power rankings. 👀 Seattle needs cleaner football from Darnold and more from its run game. Full reaction on… pic.twitter.com/5BcBurgazu

title: Caleb Williams Explains Reason Behind Cleats Change for Bears-Seahawks Week 8 Game
full_text:
Caleb Williams might have the most controversial cleats in NFL history.
The Chicago Bears quarterback has been wearing Caddix cleats this season because "my joints, ankles and my knees and my feet haven't bothered me as much (compared to) the other cleats that I've worn," Williams told ESPN's Josh Weinfuss .
The problem was that Caddix's logo was displayed on the cleats, which isn't allowed by the NFL. All Williams had to do was cover up the logo and he wouldn't have had any issues. Instead, he refused and was hit with multiple fines as a result.
However, Williams has now given in to the league's demands and his Caddix cleats no longer sported the logo during the Week 8 contest against the Seattle Seahawks.
When asked about the change after the game, Williams said it was all about avoiding any further distraction.
"Just to calm things down, man," Williams said of his decision to get rid of the logo. "This was a big week, and I'm not here to create any BS towards the team. I want to keep that to a minimum from my side. I'm just trying to minimize that as much as possible."
Prior to blacking out the logo on the cleats, Williams had been hit with fines two weeks in a row that totaled nearly $36,000.
Caleb Williams has removed the Caddix logo from his cleats for his game against the Seahawks. The NFL had fined Williams a total of $36,000 for displaying an unauthorized logo in his previous two games. pic.twitter.com/DOuTrCUBfJ
There was even a belief that the NFL may take the drastic measure of not allowing Williams to play if he continued to thumb his nose at the league, although that hasn't been confirmed.
"He's all about the team, and I know he's not going to hurt the team," head coach Ben Johnson said last week.
The reason behind Williams' defiance, according to ESPN's Ian Rapoport, was "a matter of principle" and because Williams wanted to "spread the word" about the cleats.
Williams, who is not an investor in the company, had offers from Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Flacco, who is an investor, and Caddix itself to pay the fines, but it isn't clear if that ever happened.
"His QB trainer called us last year and said Caleb was interested in trying them," Caddix CEO Jack Rasmussen said. "We talked for months about the cleats and trying different models, so I flew down to Jacksonville, met Caleb, made him show me what he wanted in a cleat and figured out what he needed."
The cleats, according to Caddix, feature SmartStuds that "deform slightly during pivoting and cutting, allowing for quicker stud release from the playing surface."
"This reduces rotational torque on the knees and ankles without sacrificing the traction athletes need for acceleration and cutting," Caddix explains. "By targeting safe rotational stiffness ranges identified in biomechanical research, Caddix cleats strike the balance between performance and protection."
Caddix cleats passed NFL testing back in 2025 and were approved for players to wear earlier this year.
Williams' battle with the NFL, which now appears to be over, was the best possible form of advertisement for the company.

title: Jeffery Simmons DPOY Odds Skyrocket After Bears Week 8 Victory
full_text:
The Chicago Bears put the NFL on notice in their 34-17 win over the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night. They made the defending Super Bowl champions look like a bottom-feeder organization ( which they most certainly are not ) on their own home field.
If there's one thing that's clear from the contest, it's that the Titans should've asked for more in return for Jeffery Simmons. The newest addition to Chicago's defensive line, whom they gave up two first-round selections and a fourth-round pick to acquire last week, completely reinvigorated their entire defense.
While his numbers (6 tackles, 1 sack, 2 TFLs, 1 pass deflection) are nothing to scoff at, his impact was felt well beyond the stat sheets . He drew 13 double teams over his 48 snaps, and Seattle only averaged 3 yards per play when he was on the field, as opposed to 13.3 yards when on the sidelines.
The sportsbooks clearly took notice of the performance. According to DraftKings Sportsbook , he went from being tied for the eighth-best odds (+2500) to win the Defensive Player of the Year Award to the fourth-best odds (+1000).
As it stands right now, he's behind only Will Anderson Jr. (+230), T.J. Watt (+700), and Fred Warner (+700). He might not be behind them for much longer, though...
Many casual fans probably hadn't heard of Simmons before the Bears traded for him. He played for the Titans, who only won seven games since 2023 and have gone a lowly 19-49 since 2021.
Defensive linemen thrive when they can pin their ears back and attack opposing QBs in passing situations. Despite rarely playing with a lead in Tennessee, Simmons still established himself as one of the league's premier interior disruptors.
He earned three All-Pro nods and made four Pro Bowl appearances in Tennessee. Simmons is also coming off a career-high 11-sack campaign despite playing for a 3-14 team. With five sacks over the first 8 games, he's on pace for the same mark this year.
Now that he's in Chicago, with an offense that knows how to get out to a hot start , he'll be playing with a lead much more often. That's a dangerous proposition for opposing offenses that already need to account for Austin Booker and Montez Sweat on the edges.
Simmons might've introduced himself to a wider audience on Monday night, but he's been firmly established as one of the league's premier game-wreckers.
If he can build on his dominant debut, he'll stand a good chance to add another notch to his already impressive belt. He has his sights set on far more than the Defensive Player of the Year Award , though.

title: Bears Injuries at DT Opens Door For Unheralded Rookies to Play Bigger Roles
full_text:
The Chicago Bears enjoyed a statement 34-17 victory in their Monday night clash against the Seattle Seahawks. Nobody goes into Lumen Field and beats the defending Super Bowl champions like that.
Jeffery Simmons, whom the Bears traded two first-round picks and a fourth-round selection for on Thursday, completely altered Chicago's defense . The Seahawks averaged only 3 yards per play when he was on the field, compared with 13.3 yards per play when he was on the sideline.
While the game was overwhelmingly positive for Chicago, they did lose two key players to injury on the defensive interior. Both Grady Jarrett and Kentavius Street went down in the fourth quarter, with the former suffering a groin injury and the latter being sidelined with a knee injury.
#Bears DL Kentavius Street (Knee) is ruled OUT and DL Grady Jarrett (Groin) is DOUBTFUL to return. pic.twitter.com/iwASkRGFNs
Jarrett might've avoided a long-term injury, as he was listed as doubtful to return. However, Street's injury looked bad. He immediately grabbed his knee and had to be carted off to the locker room.
If Street is out of action for an extended period, that would have a wide-ranging impact on the rest of the unit. His 173 snaps rank third among all defensive tackles.
That would create a situation where two forgotten rookies have a chance to carve out a role in the rotation.
Jordan van den Berg, whom the team selected in the sixth round of the 2026 NFL Draft , has effectively been phased out of the defense after playing a key role in the rotation (32% of the defensive snaps) in the season opener. His playing time has steadily decreased since that point, and he and undrafted rookie Jayden Loving were both healthy scratches on Monday night.
Meanwhile, Loving is still waiting to see his first defensive snaps of the season. However, the Bears notably cut Jamree Kromah , whom the Dolphins promptly scooped up off waivers, because they didn't want to lose Loving. They clearly like him.
Both players had strong preseason performances , but they're still extremely raw. That's been evident on tape with Jordan van den Berg. While he's flashed some athleticism, he's spent many of his 72 snaps getting pushed around.
Jordan van den Berg only had 8 snaps yesterday (under 70 for the year) but still is underperforming. Hes a rookie so needs some time but is 24 years old. He’s struggling to hold the point or get any pressure. Tough to play him meaningful reps right now. #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/I0FmdY7Ajj
The best thing for both players will be the weight room in the offseason. However, in the short term, playing time is the best way for them to improve, even amid the growing pains. Ideally, they'd be redshirted the rest of the way, but the NFL is a next-man-up league, and they're awfully close to being that for Chicago.
More playing time should allow them to get more comfortable. We've quietly (because he's never going to be heavily involved in the passing game) seen that on offense in the case of tight end Sam Roush. He previously only stood out for the wrong reasons, but he's shown strong blocking chops over the past three weeks.
If they can flash with whatever opportunities they receive, that'll be their fast lane to more playing time. We've seen that play out with James Lynch over the first eight games, as he's carved out a key role on the interior after not initially surviving roster cut-down day in August.
Lynch has played the second-most snaps among Chicago's defensive interior (195), and that's for good reason. He's been disruptive. He'd also see a substantial uptick in playing time if Street and/or Jarrett are out of action.
Neville Gallimore and Shemar Turner would also see more action. The former, specifically, has played at least 11 snaps in every game this season. Dayo Odeyingbo will also play a key role on passing downs once he returns from Injured Reserve (hopefully) later this month.
It'll be all hands on deck if Street or Jarrett are out of commission for an extended period. They've deployed a rotation throughout the season, and it would get injected with some youth if the vets miss time.
Whoever lines up on the interior will majorly benefit from playing alongside the Bears' newest game-wrecker. As long as Simmons is out there, something tells us they'll be alright .

title: Bears NFL Power Rankings for Week 9: Chicago Moves Closer to No. 1 After Statement Win
full_text:
The Chicago Bears secured a massive victory over the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night and experts across the board are putting Chicago inside the top five of their NFL power rankings.
The Bears' win over Seattle was the very definition of a statement win. Not only did Chicago knock off the defending Super Bowl champions on their home turf, the Bears did so in convincing fashion, and in primetime.
In the eyes of many across the NFL world, the Bears are now legit Super Bowl contenders .
In our NFL power rankings round-up below, every expert has the Bears inside their top five, and two of them have Chicago as high as No. 2. Let's check it out.
Orr isn't thrilled with the performance of the refs on Monday night, but that didn't stop him from putting the Bears on the doorstep of the No. 1 spot.
"When the referees managed to step out of the way in this one, what we predicted would be a beastly defensive line lived up to expectations," Orr said. "As Chicago finds more of a balance between its explosive offense and a more complementary defense, the Bears are rounding into legitimate Super Bowl favorites."
Refs aside, the fact remains that the Bears soundly outplayed the Super Bowl champions throughout the night.
Talk about a statement win for Chicago.
The Bears were one step away from the top spot in Davis' power rankings last week, but they were unable to leapfrog the San Francisco 49ers, who were on a bye, this week.
"QB Caleb Williams and newly acquired DT Jeffery Simmons certainly sowed fresh hope in front of a national audience on Monday night that Chicago might get its first NFL title in four decades after Da new-look Bears knocked off the reigning Super Bowl champion Seahawks," Davis said. "In Seattle. In prime time. Quite a statement win."
It usually takes a player a game or two to start making an impact for his new teams, but Simmons was a menace immediately for the Bears with six tackles, including two for loss, a sack and several pressures.
What a great first impression!
ESPN's Courtney Cronin was asked who the Bears' best in-season trade acquisition is in franchise history and she named Montez Sweat.
Three seasons before the Bears sent three draft picks, including two first-rounders, to Tennessee to acquire All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, GM Ryan Poles got aggressive in 2023 to land Sweat. Chicago sent a 2024 second-rounder to Washington in exchange for Sweat, who led both the Commanders (6.5) and Bears (6.0) in sacks in 2023, making him the first player in NFL history to lead two different teams in sacks in the same season. Sweat recorded his first double-digit-sack season and reached similar production in 2025, when he led Chicago with 10 sacks. Coach Ben Johnson called that season the best of Sweat's career," Cronin wrote.
While Sweat might be the choice for Cronin now, Simmons could very well take that mantle after this season.
No movement for the Bears in Prisco's rankings despite their incredibly impressive win on Monday night.
"They went into Seattle and beat up the Seahawks. The Jeffrey Simmons trade paid off right away with a dominant first game," Prisco said.
Simmons has been buried on a small market on a team that has been terrible for years now, so it was nice to see him remind everyone just how good he is on Monday night.
And it's even better that he did it as a member of the Bears.

title: Tee Higgins Picks Up First Career NFL Award Following Huge Outing Against Titans
full_text:
Tee Higgins' fantastic 2026 season continued with his first AFC Offensive Player of the Week award. The Bengals star had never won the honor until posting 10 catches for 155 yards and two touchdowns this past weekend in a 43-36 win over Tennessee.
He's been one of the most efficient receivers in the NFL this season, ranking third among all qualified receivers in yards per route run behind Jaxson Smith-Njigba and Zay Flowers.
Higgins ranks second in the league with 726 receiving yards and 13th in touchdowns (four).
It marks the fourth Bengals player this season to earn a weekly recognition, following Evan McPherson (Special Teams, Week 1), Joe Burrow (Offensive, Week 7), a nd Ryan Rehkow (Special Teams, Week 7).
"Yeah, don't overthink it. Just keep throwing the ball and let those guys get some chunk plays," Zac Taylor said about feeding Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase in the Titans shootout. "There were a lot of chunk plays, and you can feel a little bit when you have someone on your heels. We were starting to get a lot of momentum in the passing game. A lot of them were short throws, and those guys turned them into bigger plays."
Higgins was hyped about the performance in the Bengals' locker room.
"That just shows you what we've been preaching all season, all (training) camp. Never quit, always fight to the end, no matter what the outcome may be. Let's make sure we always fight to the end," Higgins said about the showing. "Big time players make big time plays in big time moments, and we were able to do that today. I say that about the three of us — big time players make those big time plays in big time moments. We were able to do that today."
The 27-year-old star has lived up to his contract extension and then some for the Bengals over the past year, and now he finally gets some hardware to show for it.
"Great team win. Most importantly, that was a great team win. Obviously, it didn't go how we wanted, but at the end of the day, we didn't have any quit in us and fought to the end and won," Higgins declared.
Cincinnati is hoping to get another (or multiple again) Player of the Week performance(s) from its roster on Sunday morning in the Spain battle against Atlanta.

title: Bengals Injury Report: DJ Turner's Opening Projected Practice Status Revealed in Madrid
full_text:
The Bengals' opening injury report during Madrid week dropped today, and all eyes are on DJ Turner (heel). Cincinnati did not practice today, this is all just a projection of who would've practiced.
Turner projected as a DNP in the opening session of the week, a murky sign for his availability on Sunday. Other than that, Cedric Johnson (ankle) didn't project to practice and neither did Kyle Dugger (quad).
Zac Taylor's team is in Spain, ready to take on the Atlanta Falcons as slight betting favorites.
Cincinnati left earlier in the week to get the players' bodies acclimated and firing on all cylinders with the six-hour time change.
"So your week does shape up a little different," Taylor said about the new schedule. "It just speeds up. All I'm saying is, it speeds things up a little bit, so being here in our office preparing is a little easier than being on the road. Doesn't mean we're not going to prepare on the road, but as much as you can get done here before you get on the plane, you prefer to do that and clean things up as you go.
"And so you just treat it a little bit like a six-day week for us. That's it. You'd like to sleep on the plane. Obviously, we work good hours; it's all good. But you'd also like to be able to deal with the time change when you get there, not feel sluggish. And so, we'll do our best to get our sleep."
Cincinnati won't have Cashius Howell for at least a month after he went to injured reserve following swift surgery on his injured wrist a few days ago.
"Yes, I can't get into all the medical reasons why that would have to happen, but again, it's his wrist, and we'll just gather more information as the year goes on," Taylor said about the defensive end getting the procedure done so quickly.

title: Bengals' Trade Deadline Targets Could Include Veteran RB, Talented LB
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals need to make some upgrades to their roster if they want to emerge as one of the best teams in the league. They need to add to a few spots on defense, but on offense, adding another running back would be a big move. They could target a huge player like Jonathan Taylor, but that seems more like a dream than reality.
Daniel Popper of The Athletic recently listed the Bengals as one of the best fits in a deal for Tampa Bay Buccaneers veteran running back Kenneth Gainwell.
"Gainwell left the Steelers in free agency to sign a two-year, $14 million deal with the Bucs. He has $3 million in guaranteed salary in 2027, so an acquiring team would be committing some money next season," Popper wrote. "They could, in theory, cut Gainwell and just wear that as dead money. The Bucs would not take on any dead money in 2027 if they traded Gainwell, who is a very effective receiver and potential third-down back in a rotation."
Gainwell was tremendous for the Pittsburgh Steelers last season, but he hasn't been given the same opportunities in Tampa Bay. He would be a huge addition to a Bengals running back room that features Chase Brown without a clear No. 2 running back.
But they need to add talent to other places on their roster, including on the defensive side of the football. Popper also listed the Bengals as one of the best fits for outside linebacker K'Lavon Chaisson.
"Chaisson signed a one-year, $11 million deal with the Commanders in free agency. Through six weeks, he was tied for the team lead with 17 pressures," Popper wrote. "Chaisson is a capable pass rusher. He set a career high with 74 pressures last season for the Patriots. He is always going to be somewhat of a liability against the run. He is an option for a team looking for situational pass-rush juice."
This could help the Bengals quite a bit because Chaisson is a good option, but it's not the biggest need in the world. The Bengals have seen quite a bit of production from edge rushers like Cashius Howell and Boye Mafe, among others. Given the fact that Shemar Stewart was recently a healthy scratch, the Bengals could be looking to add a different edge rusher to their roster.
Chaisson has 2.5 sacks in six games this year. He had 7.5 sacks last season as a member of the New England Patriots defense.

title: Joe Burrow Rocks Fun Outfit As Bengals Arrive in Spain For International Battle Against Atlanta
full_text:
The Bengals flew to Madrid, Spain, on Wednesday as the team landed in town for their Sunday morning 9:30 a.m. EST game against the Atlanta Falcons.
Joe Burrow rocked a Pokémon Pikachu outfit onto the plane, and the travel seemingly went smoothly as the team hits the town for some fun today before normal practice schedules on Thursday and Friday.
"It speeds up the earlier part of your week, so that we can travel on Tuesday night. It changes your days a little bit," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said about the changes this week. "For the players, it doesn't make it more taxing. It's a little more taxing on the coaches. But it's like playing on a Monday night and having to turn around on a short week. Nothing we haven't had to do before — nothing to complain about. It just changes the structure of how you'll meet."
Cincinnati has already gone through the work it normally does on Wednesdays this week and now just needs to get adjusted to the new timings.
They are going through morning practice schedules on Cincinnati time, happening in the afternoon across the pond.
"Tomorrow we'll get a day ahead here," Taylor said on Monday. "So instead of doing a Wednesday practice, we'll do Tuesday afternoon practice. We're gonna be there Wednesday when we get there. It's just about acclimation for our players, and then Thursday and Friday will be normal, so we'll be practicing as normal. We'll follow a normal Thursday and Friday routine. Obviously, bus travel and stuff like that to the practice field changes a little bit of our timeline, but that's no big deal.
"And then Saturday we'll do a walk through the stadium. And walk-throughs at international stadiums, you're not usually allowed to be in the endzone with the logo paint, so it's a little bit of a half-speed walk-through. But Atlanta, they're the home team, so they get to go first."

title: Bengals Called Best Fit in Trade for Jets Disgruntled Pro Bowl CB
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals need to make one or two more additions to their defense if they want to emerge as one of the Super Bowl favorites this season. They have quite a bit of talent on that side of the ball, but they could still use some upgrades.
The Bengals need to add help at linebacker and at cornerback, though adding a cornerback might be the easier route, considering how many of them are expected to be available at the trade deadline.
Daniel Popper of The Athletic recently listed the Bengals as one of the best fits in a potential trade for New York Jets cornerback Nahshon Wright. Wright hasn't played for the Jets' defense this year after being named a Pro Bowler last season.
"The Jets signed Wright to a one-year deal in free agency, and he has yet to play a defensive snap this season for coach Aaron Glenn. Wright should be a trade candidate even if the Jets win games over the next three weeks," Popper wrote. "He had five picks playing for the Chicago Bears in 2025. Wright lacks some burst and change-of-direction ability. But his ball production last season was very impressive. At 6-foot-4, he has receiver-like skills in 50-50 situations."
Wright was a Pro Bowl cornerback with five interceptions a year ago. Now, he's not playing for the Jets. During this offseason, this seemed like a huge signing for New York, but it hasn't proven to be that way. Now it seems like Wright is disgruntled and wants out of New York.
This would be a risky deal for the Bengals, as there's likely a good reason or two that he isn't making an impact in New York. But it would likely only cost a Day 3 pick swap in the NFL Draft to bring him to Cincinnati. Could the Bengals afford to swap a sixth-round pick for a seventh-round pick and a cornerback like Wright? The answer to that question should be yes.
Still, if there are big concerns following Wright that the national media isn't aware of, the Bengals will likely stay away from him. Either way, he's a name to watch ahead of the trade deadline.
