title: Bengals' Trade Deadline Targets: Who They Should Pursue and What They Need Most
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are sitting at 5-2 on the season after a hard fought win against the Tennessee Titans. This puts them right in the mix for the division and potentially more if they continue playing at this level. This also means that they may want to buy at the deadline to push them from good to great.
Here are the players the Bengals should target ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline:
This group of players are most likely unavailable but worth at least making a call and seeing what it would take.
This division is so tight that everyone would likely rather buy than sell. It's still worth calling about some top names like Jessie Bates III and Antoine Winfield Jr.
The Colts are selling, but Tyler Warren was a first round pick from a couple years ago and he’s playing well. He’s probably being kept as a building block for the next era of Colts football.
The Colts paid quite a bit to bring Gardner in so it’s pretty unlikely that they would ship him off for a fraction of the cost that it took to bring him in.
Baun was a first team All-Pro two years ago and a pro bowler last season. He won a Super Bowl two years ago as well. He’s an extremely intelligent player who is one of the best coverage linebackers in the league. He started as a defensive end in New Orleans and has since transitioned to mostly playing off the ball in Philadelphia. Baun can improve the Bengals second level by being a highly cerebral and talented player to lead the two younger linebackers. He can also take over as the green dot and be the main hub of communication being that he has done that for the Eagles. Baun is also a team captain for the Eagles.
Brooks was a first team All-Pro last season. He was insanely productive in that season leading the league in tackles. Brooks processes his keys very well, provides high end athleticism, and is a physical force against the run. Brooks is also a team captain but unlike Baun he has not been the green dot for the Dolphins the past two seasons. He may not take over as the green dot linebacker, but he would add a phenomenal all-pro level player to the second level of the Bengals defense. He can be tasked with the most difficult assignments allowing the younger linebackers to take on a lighter load.
Henley is a young linebacker in the final year of his rookie contract. Henley has been a full time starter for the Chargers the last three seasons. He’s a bit undersized but an asset in coverage with his athleticism and processing ability. Henley is also the cheapest and youngest of the linebacker options listed. Henley has been a captain the last two seasons and the green dot for the Chargers defense. He can lessen the responsibilities of the Bengals current linebacker room while providing valuable experience.
Baker is an 8-time pro bowler and 2-time first-team All-Pro safety. Baker is a captain for the Cardinals and has already racked up a career high in sacks this season with 3.5. Baker has lost a little bit of a step in coverage from his prime but still can play a variety of roles in both coverage and as a blitzer. He could step in at one of the safety spots and possibly create a big nickel package for a three safety set as well. He would provide the Bengals with a unique skill set at safety where he could also be used as a slot defender or in the box.
Hooker is a solid safety for the Titans. Hooker is a captain and plays a variety of roles for the Titans defense. He’s often used in the slot, man to man against tight ends, in underneath zone coverage, mugged up on the line of scrimmage, playing dime linebacker and as a deep safety. He’s a bit of a gambler when it comes to playing his zone coverage which has led to him intercepting five passes already this season (three against Burrow). Similar to Baker, he would add versatility to the defense and allow them to get to more unique defensive packages.
Cam Bynum is a captain on the Colts and would provide the team with another safety that can do a lot of different things on the back end. Bynum is a bit similar to Hooker in that he’s often used in various alignments from deep safety, the slot, the box, and as a dime linebacker. He will gamble when he’s playing zone coverage at times which is how he has caught multiple interceptions every year he’s been a full time starter. Hooker is a little better in coverage while Bynum is a more sure tackler and run defender. Bynum would also bring some of the league’s best celebrations with him.
Riq Woolen is a long, strong, and athletic cornerback. Woolen just won a Super Bowl with the Seattle Seahawks as a starting outside corner for that impressive defense as well. Woolen is an outside only corner who could provide the Bengals with a different style of player at the position increasing the depth and variability of the corner room. Woolen is even the Eagles tight end matchup guy at times.
Taylor is a fantastic running back for the Colts. He’s a very strong runner who does an excellent job of continuing to run his feet and work downfield. Taylor is a captain for the Colts, former first-team All-Pro, 3-time Pro Bowler and the current active leader in rushing yards per game for his career. Taylor could provide the Bengals with a force at running back with the ability to punish two-high shells from the gun. It’s not likely that Taylor could fix the Bengals under center offense by himself, but he would give them a spark. Taylor would certainly provide an upgrade to the Bengals rushing attack but the fit is a little less than ideal in the passing game.
Barkley is a former Offensive Player of the Year, Rookie of the Year, 3-time Pro Bowler and Super Bowl Champion. He’s also a captain for the Eagles. Two years ago, Barkley ran for over 2,000 yards in the regular season and another 499 in the playoffs. However, Barkley was a bit less efficient in 2025, managing just 1,140 yards on 4.1 yards per carry. This year, he’s been extremely efficient (5.7 yards per carry) but he also has been plagued by injuries. He’s currently dealing with both back and hamstring injuries. Similar to Taylor, Barkley would certainly provide an upgrade to the rushing attack but it’s likely that he could not fix the under center offense by himself. Barkley is a little bit better than Taylor in the passing game, but also has a longer injury history.
Overall, I think the team would be best suited to find someone in their back seven. The possible addition at running back or even slot receiver makes sense on paper, but this is a top 5 offense with a middle of the road defense. Teams that are built with a great offense and okay defense do not typically win the Super Bowl. The only teams in the last 10 years to win the super bowl and have a defense outside of the top 10 in points per game are the 2021 Rams (got a heck of a lot better on defense at the trade deadline!) and the 2022 Chiefs (one of the greatest defensive play callers in the modern era). If the goal is to win a championship, then I would put my resources into taking this defense from average to quality rather than putting more into an already excellent offense.
Mike Santagata is an offensive line and film expert. He's written and analyzed Bengals film for the past four years. He also hosts the Always Gameday in Cincinnati podcast and is a regular guest on the Locked On Bengals podcast.

title: Cincinnati Bengals Hoping Uniform Combo's Bad Juju Doesn't Carry Overseas
full_text:
The pants the Cincinnati Bengals will wear in Sunday’s game against the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid is a combination of the colors in the Spanish flag, red and yellow.
And that’s bad news based on history.
In addition to going back to their new orange pants with black stripes, the Bengals will wear white jerseys and white socks.
They are 1-4 in this uniform combo and 2-8 in all combos that include orange pants.
The last time the Bengals wore white-orange-black-white combo, they not only lost, but they also failed to score. That was the 24-0 loss to the Baltimore Ravens at Paycor Stadium last year in Week 15.
In the five games in the white-orange-black-white combo, the Bengals have been outscored 137-61.
The Bengals were schedule to depart for Spain on Tuesday evening. They will arrive in Madrid on Wednesday morning and treat that as an off day before practicing Thursday and Friday.
Cincinnati head coach Zac Taylor said he won’t rely much on his notes from the 2019 London game because the travel schedule is much different.
In 2019, the Bengals flew to London after practicing Thursday afternoon. They landed Friday morning and went straight to practice.
Cincinnati lost that game 24-10 to fall to 0-8 in Taylor’s first season as head coach.
“It’s different,” Taylor said of this year’s trip during his Monday news conference. “Then, we went on Thursday. This time it’s Tuesday. The week shapes up different. It speeds up the coaches a bit so that the comfort of being here in our office is different than on the road.  It doesn’t mean we’re not going to prepare on the road.
“As much as you can get done here before you get on the plane, you’d prefer to do that, clean things up as you go,” he continued. “You treat it like a six-day week. You’d like to sleep on the plane. We work good hours. You’d also like to be able to deal with the time change when you get there and not feel sluggish. We’ll get our sleep when we can get it on the plane.”
Here is a look at the five previous games the Bengals played in the white-orange-black-white uniform combo.
Week 15, 2025: Ravens 24, Bengals 0
Week 11, 2025: Steelers 34, Bengals 12
Week 4, 2025: Broncos 28, Bengals 3
Week 18, 2024: Bengals 19, Steelers 17
Week 11, 2024: Chargers 34, Bengals 27

title: Bengals Trade For Jonathan Taylor Would Cost Cincinnati A Lot
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are reportedly interested in swinging a blockbuster trade for Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. Taylor is one of the best running backs in the league, and the Bengals could desperately use another talented option in their backfield.
"As the Colts continue to field trade offers for star RB Jonathan Taylor, sources say the Vikings, Giants, Broncos, Bengals and Packers are among the teams that have checked in," Schultz wrote in a post to X on Sunday. "The asking price is believed to be too high right now, but sources do believe a trade is leaning to be more likely than not at this point."
A trade for Taylor would be the best move that the Bengals could make, but it would also be quite an expensive move. What would it cost for the Bengals to make a move like this?
There's a lot of speculation going around that the Colts will demand a first-round pick in return for their generational running back, but it's hard to imagine any team giving up that kind of value in a draft pick for Taylor.
Now, it could be different with the Bengals, as they could finish near the top of the league, which would put their first-round selection around the 30th pick.
The other comparison for the Colts is the Christian McCaffrey trade that sent the star running back from the Carolina Panthers to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a second, third, fourth, and fifth-round pick.
If that's the ask, the Bengals might need to be out of the running.
This kind of trade would mortgage their future in an attempt to win right now. They already opted for a win-now move by trading their first round pick last offseason in exchange for Dexter Lawrence. This deal has worked out well for the Bengals, but could they find sustained success if they move a haul of draft picks in exchange for Taylor?
This entire idea comes down to how long the Bengals feel they'd be able to keep Taylor and their willingness to commit to winning right now. The 49ers laid out the blueprint for how this kind of deal can work to the buyer's benefit. Will the Bengals follow suit?

title: Bengals Make Roster Move Surrounding Cashius Howell's Wrist Injury
full_text:
The Bengals placed rookie defensive end Cashius Howell on injured reserve, prompting a likely call-up for practice squad defensive end Isaiah Foskey at some point this week.
Cincinnati is traveling to Madrid, Spain today and may not have a ton of time to try and get another defensive end signed ahead of the game. That position can clearly be boosted by a trade at some point over the next week.
Shemar Stewart is the only healthy backup defensive end on Cincinnati's 53-man roster as of this writing. Howell had wrist surgery already this week and Cedric Johnson is also hurt.
"The Bengals today placed DE Cashius Howell on the Reserve/Injured list with a wrist injury," The team posted on its website with no corresponding move to complete the roster. "Howell, a rookie out of Texas A&M University, has played in all seven games this season and totaled three tackles with two TFLs and one sack."
Cincinnati is going to be watching the status of DJ Turner and Cedric Johnson this week. Turner is day-to-day with a heel injury as one of Cincinnati's three best defenders this season.
"Thought all those guys had significant plays that helped us," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said about his edge rushing group on Monday. "We're fortunate that we have a lot of depth in the D-Line room. So, again, to offset the loss of Cashius, we're well built in that room, so it's going to provide more opportunity. Guys like Shemar, we knew a day like this would come. It's always unfortunate when a guy gets hurt, but that's why we got the depth. And Shemar's (Stewart) just been doing everything he can to control his spot, and we trust him to make some plays for us."
Cincinnati is traveling to Madrid today and picking practices back up on Thursday.
"Like to be able to deal with the time change when you get there, not feel sluggish," Taylor said about the travel plans. "And so, we'll do our best to get our sleep. We were pretty immediate that we wanted to do this and get over there and get our players acclimated as quickly as possible and be fresh on Sunday."
They play Atlanta at 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday.

title: A Bengals Trade for Jonathan Taylor is More Necessary Now Than Ever
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are interested in a trade for Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, according to a report from NFL insider Jordan Schultz. Taylor's name has been mixed up in trade rumors for a few weeks, and a deal could come to fruition before the trade deadline.
"As the Colts continue to field trade offers for star RB Jonathan Taylor, sources say the Vikings, Giants, Broncos, Bengals and Packers are among the teams that have checked in," Schultz wrote in a post to X on Sunday . "The asking price is believed to be too high right now, but sources do believe a trade is leaning to be more likely than not at this point."
The Bengals have a lot of talent on offense, but they need to add a running back to help them establish a respectable running game before it's too late. Taylor would be the perfect solution to this massive problem on offense.
The Bengals are fifth in the league in passing yards per game, but they're third worst in the league in rushing yards per game.
The Green Bay Packers and Las Vegas Raiders are the only teams that average fewer rushing yards per game than Cincinnati. The Bengals are also bottom five in football in rushing yards per attempt and rushing touchdowns.
Chase Brown is the lead back, and he hasn't done anything noteworthy. He averages 3.5 yards per carry on 82 attempts through six games. Samaje Perine has been an issue as the backup running back, too.
Adding Taylor would be very expensive, but it's a move the Bengals need to make if they're going to go all in this season.
They have already shown their willingness to make big moves in an effort to win now. Adding Dexter Lawrence was a huge trade that showcased their desire to win right now. Trading for Taylor would double down on this and put Joe Burrow in the best spot to win that he's been in over the course of his career.

title: Browns’ Latest Injury News Opens Door for Shedeur Sanders
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns dropped a bombshell on social media Wednesday morning. Starting quarterback Deshaun Watson is in concussion protocol after a hit sustained during the first quarter of the Browns-Steelers game on Sunday:
Brisker flagged for hit on Watson #Steelers #NFL pic.twitter.com/FCOv8QtjJA
Watson began experiencing concussion symptoms Monday night and reported them to the medical staff Tuesday morning, when he was placed in concussion protocol . An unaffiliated neurotrauma consultant cleared Watson to return during Sunday’s game. He also passed evaluations after the game and on Monday morning.
Watson has helped the Browns reach 5-3, engineering a game-winning drive in each of their five victories. He has 1,806 passing yards, seven touchdowns, and three interceptions this season. This start, while unexpected, had many believing that Watson would remain the starter for the season, barring injury.
Unfortunately for Watson, that injury came.
Watson’s injury could open the door for backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders to show his capabilities once again. Sanders made seven starts as a rookie in 2025, throwing for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions.
some of Shedeur Sanders best throws vs. the Titans from the All-22 tape. #Browns The first ball to Fannin with a DE barreling down in his face is just silly... pic.twitter.com/zsZSNHxgbT
While it wasn’t all pretty, Sanders did show flashes of potential, specifically in the Browns’ matchup against the Titans in 2025. In that game, Sanders threw for 364 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception while adding a rushing touchdown. Many assumed the Browns would continue to start Sanders into the 2026 season, but ultimately that was not the case.
The Browns held a highly publicized quarterback competition between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders during training camp for the 2026 season. Sanders ultimately lost the battle to the veteran Watson, but a comment Browns head coach Todd Monken made during OTAs on June 3 still stands out today:
#Browns HC Todd Monken said he has not yet decided who will start at quarterback between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders, nor has he finalized the offensive line heading into training camp. "I think both quarterbacks have played well enough. We really haven't been in pads,… pic.twitter.com/LFLUlv99mL
Todd Monken said, “But I’m fired up by the quarterbacks. I'll tell you, we got two starting-level quarterbacks. We really do.” Now, Sanders has the opportunity to prove his head coach right.
Sanders has not been confirmed as the starter against the Saints, as Watson could still clear concussion protocol before Sunday. Sanders will take the first-team practice reps Wednesday as Cleveland prepares for the possibility of playing without Watson.
The question now, if Sanders gets the start, is whether he can seize his opportunity. If Sanders performs better than Watson has to start the season, it may be difficult for the Browns to turn back to the veteran. However, Sanders must avoid holding the ball too long. That issue surfaced against Pittsburgh, contributing to two penalties for ineligible players downfield on screen passes.
If those struggles resurface, the Browns could quickly return to Watson, who has led five game-winning drives this season.

title: A Blockbuster Trade the Browns Could Make to Completely Change the Franchise
full_text:
Rumors have begun to run wild around the NFL about the Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert.
After an unprecedented 0-7 start to the season, the Chargers may be enticed by the right offer to blow up the entire operation and go into rebuild mode.
With these rumors going around, some people, including ESPN Cleveland, have called for the Cleveland Browns to reach out and potentially make an offer for the former Oregon Duck.
Here are some of the pros and cons to a potential Justin Herbert trade.
. @BenjaminSolak lists the 3 teams that should try and trade for Justin Herbert: - Vikings - Jets - The Cleveland Browns 👀👀👀 Should the Browns explore a Herbert trade? pic.twitter.com/zpMT9W4yx9
In 2022, the Browns gave up pretty much their entire future to go out and trade for Deshaun Watson. We all know how that went before 2026 began.
Now, Watson is 31 years old and in the final year of his contract. If the Browns want to move on from Watson and go after Herbert, it would take another gigantic package.
While Herbert doesn't have legal issues off the field, his play on the field is still questionable. While some argue it's the poor system he's playing in, or the tough teams he's facing, Herbert still leads the NFL with 10 interceptions.
All in all, the move seems to be too risky for the Browns to make, especially with a potentially loaded 2027 rookie quarterback class.
While we are still looking back to the Deshaun Watson trade, let's not forget the slim amount of hope Cleveland fans had right when the trade went down.
If the Browns got Herbert, they would most likely have their best quarterback since Baker Mayfield. At times, it is easy to say Herbert is far better than Mayfield as well.
With the second-youngest team in the NFL, along with the back-to-back incredible draft classes, Herbert would come in surrounded by an incredibly talented team.
Before 2026, many argued that the Browns were a quarterback away from being a serious contender. Maybe Cleveland looks at Herbert as their "missing piece"?
While it is very unrealistic that the Browns will go make a move for Madison Beer's fiancé, there is another world of possibilities people are overlooking if the quarterback gets moved to another team.
Like I said, Moving Justin Herbert is the initial indicator that the Chargers are going into rebuild mode.
With that being said, the Browns' biggest need by far at the moment is help on that offensive line. Of course, it would be pricey, but if the Chargers are willing to move their quarterback, who's to say they wouldn't trade away guys like Joe Alt or Rashawn Slater?
If anything, the Browns should be hoping the Chargers are willing to trade Justin Herbert. Maybe then they could take a swing at a big trade, yet not for the guy you would have first thought of.

title: Browns' Loss to Steelers Confirms One Undeniable Truth About Deshaun Watson
full_text:
As the Cleveland Browns came crashing back to Earth, courtesy of a 27-6 spanking by the Pittsburgh Steelers at Accrisure Stadium on Sunday, a few things became crystal clear regarding the club and its now 5-3 record start to the regular season.
The reasons for the team’s second loss in four weeks can be traced to many things. Among them, a multitude of flags iuncluding two taunting penalties while trailing by 21 points, a mesmerizing incapability to establish the run game, and a general lack of pressure on Pittsburgh's offense .
However, one thing really stood out above all else as the Browns now attempt to gather themselves for a third road trip in as many weeks: Deshaun Watson cannot be the team’s quarterback in 2027 and beyond.
Listen, everyone can reasonably accept that Cleveland’s latest rebuild endeavour might take more than one year after the club replaced head coach Kevin Stefanski with Todd Monken, even if the Browns have hit multiple home runs on two straight draft classes.
But one thing has become evident after Week 8’s disappointing outing , one that included eight sacks on Watson: the Browns will need another quarterback to complete this comeback.
Now, the offensive line was going to be a work in progress throughout the year. Watson wasn’t. At least that’s what the team has been telling us repeatedly since he was inserted into a two-way competition for the starting job, and then again when he was designated winner of said competition over Shedeur Sanders.
Watson’s experience would help mitigate some of the issues that naturally arise on a budding young team. And an offensive line with five new starters, including two rookies playing out of their most recent college spots was going to need all the help it could get.
It’s getting zilch out of Watson.
Because Watson plays the position in a similar way as he does his pressers, he lacks general awareness of what’s going on around him. That commonly leads to dropbacks out of the shotgun where Watson ends up with 11 to 13 yards of depth, which in turn leads to the tackles getting beat constantly.
Watch Tytus Howard throw up his arms several times out of frustration. Watson takes a 7-step drop out of the shotgun. At the top of his drop he is 13 yards from the line of scrimmage. It's impossible to block the edges when a QB does this. pic.twitter.com/uyZaBuMwL5
Out of Watson’s eight sacks on Sunday , at least five of them came on plays where Watson’s deep dropback contributed to the outcome. On at least three of those sacks, he had more than 2.5 seconds to get rid of the ball, and he didn’t.
Another consequence of Watson’s deep dropbacks is that tackles are then forced to hold defenders in order to avoid a hit on the passer. That happened at least a couple of times against Pittsburgh on Sunday.
And to make things worse, Watson’s tendency to drop back so deep is so easily detectable, that you could see the Steelers’ edge rushers pinning their ears back and targeting that range around 10 yards behind the line of scrimmage because they knew that’s where they would find the quarterback.
Watson didn’t actually trim his dropback and speed up his delivery until about six minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. Even so, he was still sacked a couple more times, with Watson feeling outside pressure and then stepping into the sack on the inside.
But Watson’s issues go further than just making life miserable for his tackles. He also had two grossly overthrown passes, two one-hoppers, and two passes batted down at the line of scrimmage as part of a performance that did, however, manage to cover up some of the blunders with plenty of garbage-time yards.
As much as Browns fans might want to see the team make a splash before the trade deadline, options aren’t really that great out there . Having said that, there are several names that could be had that are currently playing better than Watson, with Kirk Cousins at the top of that list.
Nonetheless, that’s not a long-term solution either, so there’s a good chance the Browns will ride 2026 out with Watson and his plethora of sacks, and then look to the draft to pick out a passer from a once very promising class that’s now shrinking on a weekly basis.
Cleveland wanted an experienced passer capable of bringing along all the young offensive talent on the roster slowly. Instead, Watson turned into a sack magnet. Now, the Browns should take a different approach, one where a young and talented quarterback gets to grow alongside the rest of the offensive pieces already in place.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Browns Could Be Forced to Abandon Their Trade Deadline Plans After Steelers Loss
full_text:
Heading into their week eight matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers , the Cleveland Browns had in mind an idea for the upcoming trade deadline.
After finally having a winning season, Cleveland can finally be buyers at this stage of the season. Despite the loss, this status of "buyers" remains the same. However, the players they need to go after have dramatically changed.
Before facing their rivals, many rumors were swirling about the Browns going after another pass rusher to bolster the defensive line.
Guys like Khalil Mack and YaYa Diaby were being thrown around as potential targets.
Especially with the horrible start to Jared Verse's Browns career statistically, Cleveland really could still use a guy to help take some of that pressure off the 2024 Defensive Rookie of the Year.
However, there is another stat that stands out far more than all the rest, and it shows why another position desperately needs more attention.
Quite literally doing a 180 to the other side of the ball, the Browns' offensive line has completely failed so far this season.
Even after going out and getting five new starters, finding potential great future options in the draft with Spencer Fano and Austin Barber, trading for Tytus Howard, and spending big bucks on Zion Johnson and Elgton Jenkins, the unit still needs a load of work.
The reason? Deshaun Watson has been sacked 33 times this season in eight games.
Last game alone, Pittsburgh was able to ruin the Browns' offense after dropping Watson eight times.
Not only does that 33 sacks allowed lead the entire NFL, but the Carolina Panthers, who rank 31st, have allowed 10 fewer sacks.
Clearly, Cleveland needs to spend some money to improve the guys up front. Who knows, maybe it wouldn't take too much to go after a guy like Landon Dickerson from Philadelphia.
Other wide receiver names continue to come up in connection to the trade deadline: Jacksonville’s Brian Thomas Jr., Indianapolis’ Josh Downs, Minnesota’s Jauan Jennings, Cleveland’s Jerry Jeudy, Tennessee’s Calvin Ridley. But the Jets won’t trade Wilson by next Tuesday. https://t.co/F2ONImsqPX
So the issue has been addressed, and we know what Cleveland needs to do. But how will they do it?
The Browns have 11 total picks in the 2027 NFL Draft. This includes multiple late-round picks, but also two that come in the first round.
Who is to say Cleveland doesn't go after a top lineman who is still in the early stages of his career? That way, if they do use a first-round pick, they can almost "draft early" with a guy who can help out this season and for years to come.
Now let's say Andrew Berry does not want to use a first-round pick to trade for a lineman. What else do the Browns have to offer?
If there's been a player whose name has been tossed around in trade talks since training camp, its been Jerry Jeudy.
Some teams that come to mind that are trying to potentially get wide receiver help for their quarterback are the Kansas City Chiefs, Los Angeles Rams, and Washington Commanders.
Going forward, a change simply has to be made. Unfortunately for the Browns, it also doesn't look like that change will be able to be made internally.
If Cleveland seriously wants a chance to push for their first-ever AFC North title and first playoff appearance since 2023, they will need to make a move for at least one offensive lineman in the coming weeks.

title: Browns' Playoff Hopes Took a Major Hit, but Their Next Move Could Change Everything
full_text:
After the loss in Pittsburgh, the Cleveland Browns dropped to third in the AFC North and out of the playoff picture altogether in the conference. They sit at eighth in the AFC and have to get back on the winning track in order to keep pace. The Browns only play three games against teams over .500 the rest of the season.
The offense has been a black hole for the team in the first three quarters. Their ineffectiveness is driven by their i nability to run the ball and protect the quarterback . Watson leads the entire NFL in getting sacked and Quinshon Judkins is on pace for fewer yards than in his injury-shortened season last year.  Trading for help on the offense may be able to save their season.
The offensive line has struggled to both run and pass block . Harold Fannin Jr. has had to play closer to the line of scrimmage to help with blocking, which has resulted in fewer touches for him. In Pittsburgh, he had his best receiving game of the season and looked unstoppable as a pass catcher, but it came with a cost as Watson got sacked eight times and the running game was non-existent.
The Browns can save their offense by trading for a tight end that can block. Fannin Jr. can then be utilized to the best of his skill set, and the new tight end can play closer to the line of scrimmage to help the anemic line. There is a great fit at the position that could be on the trade block.
The 6’5, 260-pound tight end could be available, as the Colts have already traded away two major pieces and got throttled last week in Jacksonville. He is the Colts’ best blocking tight end and is on the last year of his contract. Trading for him would not cost any meaningful assets for the Browns and the transition should be smooth as his primary objective would be to block.
He was drafted in the sixth round out of Youngstown State. Ogletree only has three catches this season and 25 in his career. He has been the blocking tight end for star running back Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones has been sacked 11 fewer times than Watson.
On obvious passing downs, Fannin can line up on the outside and become a pure pass catcher. Ogletree can be used as a true blocking tight end. When Fannin has played downfield, the Browns have used running backs to try and provide extra protection. That strategy has not worked, and they need a bigger body to handle that duty.
Fannin is a key factor in the offense , as he can turn a short gain into a large one with his ability to break tackles. He is too fast and elusive to be covered by linebackers and too strong to be covered by a slot corner. Any other player trying to cover Fannin would benefit KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston.
Ogletree can also be used to slip out of the backfield on obvious passing downs. The Browns ran a play with Blake Whiteheart on their game-winning drive against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, where the defense ignored him, thinking that he was only going to be used as a blocker, and he slipped out for an uncontested touchdown.
Although the Browns got defeated handedly in Pittsburgh, the offense is not too far off. The last half of the schedule lends them to be able to stack wins and save their playoff hopes. A non-consequential trade for Ogletree can help them fix their biggest problems down the stretch.

title: This Switch Up Front Could be the Key for Cleveland Moving Forward
full_text:
Week 9 was not kind to Browns fans, as they saw Cleveland get trounced in Pittsburgh, as they usually do, 27-6. The Steelers were able to run the ball very effectively, gaining 200 yards on the ground from their tandem of Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle.
The Steelers were also able to protect Aaron Rodgers well, as he was only sacked once on the day; the same could not be said for the Browns. Deshaun Watson was sacked eight times for a total of 41 yards lost; Cleveland also could not run the ball whatsoever, totaling just 34 yards on 15 carries.
There have to be some changes made on the offensive line, and it needs to happen soon. Tytus Howard has mostly struggled this season on the right side , as he is graded 44th out of the 69 qualified tackles in the league per PFF. He supposedly had his best game on Sunday, grading out the highest of any Browns o-lineman, but by watching the game, you might have some different opinions.
TJ Watt ended the game with multiple sacks where Howard was matched up against him; on the first sack, there was pressure up the middle from Keanu Benton, but also on the outside from Watt, where he beat Howard and got home.
On the second sack, Watson takes a deep drop on 3rd & 18 to try to maximize his time to throw, but Watt can get around Howard again, and as Watson steps up, he sacks him from behind. To Howard’s credit, it looked like he was expecting a chip from Jaleel McLaughlin that he did not get, but it is not a good look as your quarterback is getting thrown down to be throwing your arms up at the 5’7”, 186 lb running back.
Howard has been the most penalized tackles in the NFL also, as he has 7 penalties this year, which ranks 62nd of 69 tackles. His false starts seem to be him overcompensating for faster rushers (like Watt), which can also be said for his holds.
The Browns traded for Howard in the offseason for a fifth-round pick , then immediately gave him a three-year, $63 million extension, a risk that doesn’t look like it’s paying off. What Cleveland was also banking on was the fact that Howard can play more than just the tackle spot, as he also had significant snaps at left and right guard in 2025.
The time for him to move inside might be soon, and with right guard Austin Barber having lots of experience playing tackle, it could be a hot change. Howard getting benched is unlikely, but if he continues to not provide much in the run game and not be consistent in the pass game; it may be sooner rather than later.
Hi, I’m Paul, I’m from Northeast Ohio, and a recent graduate of Kent State University. As an Ohio native, I’m a huge fan of the Browns, Guardians, and Cavaliers. Just don’t ask me about my favorite college team, though.

title: Todd Monken Sends Blunt Message to Browns During Monday Press Conference
full_text:
The Browns entered the AFC North showdown with an opportunity to improve to 6-2 and remain unbeaten in division play. Instead, Cleveland struggled offensively , surrendered eight sacks and committed several costly penalties in a game that quickly got away.
While Monken addressed many of those shortcomings immediately after the loss, his comments Monday provided a more detailed assessment of what went wrong and how they need to show more discipline against New Orleans.
“ We weren’t very poised and we didn’t keep our composure ,” Monken said when asked about three unnecessary penalties. “And you are how you play, not how you talk.”
Monken made it clear that his message to the team wasn’t limited to one disappointing performance.
The Browns also struggled to protect quarterback Deshaun Watson, allowing eight sacks against Pittsburgh’s aggressive defensive front. Rather than placing the blame on one player or position group, Monken emphasized that the responsibility belongs to everyone.
“Ultimately eight sacks is below the line,” Monken said. “When you get anywhere near that number, we all got to take a big bite of it and say it’s not good enough.”
He pointed to several contributing factors, including protection breakdowns, play calling and Watson’s ability to get rid of the football.
“It’s not one individual person. It’s a collective thing that we’ve got to continue to fight to get better at.”
“We got behind. We didn’t really get into a rhythm and we didn’t get any auxiliary yards,” Monken said.
He also acknowledged that the coaching staff must improve its approach.
“Certainly got to scheme it better and got to coach it better and execute better...We weren’t at our best the last couple weeks in stopping the run. All right. Now what? What are we going to do to stop the run?”
Despite those concerns, Monken isn’t ready to let one disappointing afternoon define Cleveland’s season.
The Browns are 5-3 through eight games, and their head coach believes they have considerable room for improvement.
“We haven’t really even scratched the surface yet of where we can be,” the head coach said proudly.
He believes the disappointment following Pittsburgh reflects how much the Browns expect of themselves.
“This is a good spot to be in, right? To be disappointed that you’re not 6-2 and that you didn’t find a way to win the game on the road and be 3-0 in the division.”
Monken stressed that the Browns have earned their five victories, just as they must accept responsibility for Sunday’s performance.
“We also earned the way we played yesterday and we weren’t poised and we weren’t composed and we earned that.”
Now the challenge is turning those words into a better performance.
“We’re going to circle the wagons. We’re going to figure out what we can fix. Get after it on Wednesday. Flush it today. Get after it Wednesday and take another step forward.”

title: Eight Sacks, One Major Concern: Browns Must To Make This Change Before It's Too Late
full_text:
Some things can be ignored, others can't.
The Cleveland Browns' offensive line struggles fall into the latter.
On Sunday, Nov. 1, the Browns lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers, 27-6, with the offense failing to score a touchdown. Across the first three drives, Cleveland managed to fumble twice and punt once, with quarterback Deshaun Watson being pressured over and over again.
While the early blunders set the team up for failure, the surplus of bodies in the backfield all day long did as well.
Watson ended up being sacked eight times and was pressured on a whopping 65% of his dropbacks in the first half alone. He did complete 27 passes for 324 yards, averaging 8.3 yards per attempt, but he wasn't able to get the offense moving until the final few drives, when the game was too far gone.
Watson took the blame postgame, but it was obvious that he wasn't given enough time to make anything happen.
“I’m always going to put the sacks on me. … I’m always going to take responsibility for those," he said.
But it is hard to keep putting the blame on him, as sacks have been a recurring issue all season long. He has taken 33 total sacks , 16 of which have come from the Steelers game and the loss to the New York Jets a few weeks back.
While the issue can't fall solely on one player, but right tackle Tytus Howard has been having a tough time this season.
He is routinely called for penalties up front and has allowed too much pressure in the backfield for Watson and the running back room. In run blocking, he ranks 51st out of 69 individuals with a mark of 56.9, while his passing grade helps him out a bit at 75.2. That is good enough to rank him 21st out of 69 individuals.
However, when combined, he is graded as the 45th-ranked offensive tackle out of 69, placing him towards the bottom of the list.
And honestly, such a ranking makes sense. He just hasn't played well. In total, he has allowed 17 pressures, two sacks and five quarterback hits, all while being flagged seven times.
He doesn't just have to clean up multiple areas of his game, but pretty much everything.
If the Browns want to continue elevating the play up front around rookies Austin Barber and Spencer Fano, they may need to make a move as the NFL Trade Deadline approaches. Whether it is signing a player from free agency or even just making a subtle trade that might not break headlines, Cleveland needs to round out the offensive line.
And that might mean cutting ties with the 30-year-old Howard if things don't start getting better.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Browns' Embarrassing Loss to Steelers Exposes a Major Problem Todd Monken Can No Longer Ignore
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns talked the talk last week , but tripped over their own feet when it came to walking the walk against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Nothing went the Browns’ way in Sunday’s matchup and they fell out of first place in the AFC North. From the defense’s inability to stop the run to the offensive line’s inability to provide any breathing room, there was plenty of blame to go around for the loss in Pittsburgh.
Todd Monken’s offense has not been able to run the ball, and Deshaun Watson was sacked eight times in a game for the second time this season. The offense turned the ball over on the first two drives, and the Browns fell behind early in the game.
In all five of their wins, the Browns have relied on game-winning drives and fourth-quarter magic. They consistently get behind in games, and the offense struggles to score in the first half. Their opponents have used big runs to get into scoring position in the first quarter.
Monken can no longer ignore the slow starts as the schedule flips to November and each game matters more and more.
The Browns were down 20-6 heading into halftime. They came back from a 14-point deficit in the prior game, but that was against a lowly Tennessee Titans team. Coming back in a game for the division lead, in a stadium where they have not won a regular-season game since 2003, was too much to ask from an inexperienced team.
The offense had two first-half drives that started promising, but ultimately led to field goals. The Steelers got the ball with under a minute left and drove down the length of the field with little resistance for a touchdown right before halftime. Monken has to find a way to win games starting in the first half.
There is a lot to fix all the way around and they have to play like a more complete team to get out to early leads. The offense has looked lost to start games, which should be the opposite, as the first 15 or so plays are scripted. The offensive line has given Watson no time to throw, and when he does get time, he holds on to the ball too long and ends up bailing out of the pocket.
The first series or two should have an emphasis on getting the ball out on time to the correct read. The lack of a running game has also hurt the line’s ability to protect Watson. There were few running lanes for Quinshon Judkins and when he did have room to run, he was leg-tackled by a single defender. The running game has to be established early to make life easier for Watson and the passing game.
The defense has started games slow and their tackling has been suspect. Jaylen Warren had over 100 rushing yards in the first half alone. Aaron Rodgers was hitting wide open receivers in the middle of the field against zone coverage and they did not put the offense in the best position to succeed.
They are dealing with injuries on the defensive front, but the guys who are playing need to step up to get the offense the ball with a tie or a lead. Too often, the Browns have been down before fans even get settled into their seats.
The trend of starting the game slowly was one that was in the back of the mind as the Browns were winning. The team is young, and Monken is still trying to install his offense with all the new players. However, halfway through the season, the problem is becoming too big to ignore, and Monken has to address their first-half performances.
The Browns sit at 5-3 with a light schedule in the back half of the season. If they want to make the playoffs, Monken can no longer rely on game-winning drives.

title: Jared Verse’s Struggles Raise a Costly Question for the Browns
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are facing a decision that looked like a foregone conclusion just months ago. Does it make sense to exercise Jared Verse’s fifth-year option, or should the Browns reconsider a major commitment to a centerpiece of the Myles Garrett trade?
On Monday, June 1, the Cleveland Browns traded franchise cornerstone Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in exchange for a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick, a 2029 third-round pick, and 25-year-old edge rusher Jared Verse.
Verse came to Cleveland with high expectations; Browns GM Andrew Berry went as far as to say, “He’s a perfect DNA match for our attacking front.”
Browns GM Andrew Berry on the trade of Myles Garrett: “It wasn’t something that we anticipated certainly coming into this year or coming into the spring or quite honestly coming out of the draft.” pic.twitter.com/3ITBfea5kn
The praise Verse received was well deserved, as he had already won the AP NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year award in 2024 and recorded 12 sacks across his first two seasons. Before the 2026 season, Verse seemed to be an ascending star in the league.
Verse came to Cleveland with energy, expressing confidence in the team’s work ethic and winning potential during his introductory press conference:
#Browns edge Jared Verse says “that’s not a losing team out there” pic.twitter.com/rnw3JYF7Uu
Despite the optimism surrounding his arrival , Verse has struggled to deliver the expected pass-rush production. Verse has yet to record a sack during the 2026 season and only has 13 total pressures on the season, according to PFF , putting him well behind the pace of his 80-pressure season in 2025.
That decline raises an important question: should the Browns pick up Verse’s fifth-year option on his rookie deal?
A fifth-year option allows a team to extend a first-round draft pick’s four-year rookie contract by one season at a salary determined by league rules that account for position, playing time, and Pro Bowl selections. Teams make that decision after the player’s third season, and the option salary becomes fully guaranteed once exercised.
In Verse’s case, his fifth-year option is projected at approximately $28 million for the 2028 season, according to Over the Cap , because of his two original-ballot Pro Bowl selections.
Cleveland must decide in spring 2027 whether his production justifies that commitment. Declining the option would still leave Verse under contract for the 2027 season. A strong finish would give the Browns more reason to make that substantial financial commitment.
The Browns felt comfortable moving on from Myles Garrett due to the timeline fit Verse provided, as his age is in line with the team's many young stars. Verse still has nine regular-season games to show that he belongs in Cleveland’s long-term plans. His past success earned him the opportunity, but his remaining performances must justify the price.

title: ESPN NFL Insider Pinpoints Cowboys Trade Candidate Not Named George Pickens
full_text:
There has been a lot of trade chatter surrounding George Pickens lately because of how down in the dumps the Dallas Cowboys are.
But all signs continue to point to the Cowboys not trading him , even though that might be the best course of action right now.
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler was tasked with picking a Cowboys trade candidate and he named tight end Luke Schoonmaker.
"There are a lot of directions Dallas could go here," Fowler said. "But the struggling defense can't afford to move players on that side of the ball. Schoonmaker is the No. 3 tight end in the pecking order, and teams are looking for blocking tight ends. I just don't see Dallas moving key players at this point."
Schoonmaker had served as the Cowboys' No. 2 tight end in the past after being a second-round pick in 2023.
But Schoonmaker has not met expectations and he began losing his grip on the TE2 job last season, when Brevyn-Spann Ford began ascending.
And Spann-Ford's ascension was enough for the Cowboys to give him an extension, which was the first sign of trouble for Schoonmaker.
Eight weeks into the season and not only has Spann-Ford totally passed Schoonmaker on the depth chart, but the latter has also been completely irrelevant in the offense.
Schoonmaker has appeared for just 16% of the snaps and has three catches for 30 yards and no touchdowns on three targets. That continues his production decline after he went from 27/241 in 2024 to 14/132 in 2025.
Aside from his clear decline in the offense, Schoonmaker is also a free agent after this season and he has no future in Dallas. If there is a taker for his services, the Cowboys shouldn't hesitate to unload Schoonmaker before he leaves for nothing in 2027.
If that happens, the Cowboys could deploy practice squad tight end James Mitchell as their TE3, or they could even give rookie Michael Trigg a look.
There doesn't seem to be a lot of chatter about teams in the tight end market right now, but one team that makes sense for a trade for Schoonmaker is the Chicago Bears.
Chicago runs a lot of two- and three-tight end sets and recently lost its TE2, Cole Kmet, to a season-ending injury , which leaves the Bears depending on rookie Sam Roush, who has struggled, and a one-dimensional veteran in Stephen Carlson.
Schoonmaker is a serviceable blocker and pass-catcher and is probably a better option than Carlson, and he offers the experience the struggling Roush doesn't have.
If the Bears are willing to offer a seventh-round pick, the Cowboys should jump at the opportunity.

title: Stephen Jones Reveals Conditions for Cowboys to Make In-Season Coaching Change
full_text:
Brian Schottenheimer has a record of 10-14-1 as he enters Week 9 of his second season as the head coach of the Dallas Cowboys. His latest loss was a complete meltdown as Dallas surrendered a 14-point fourth quarter lead against the Arizona Cardinals.
Schottenheimer’s seat was already heating up before that game, but now it’s turned into a complete inferno . The calls for his job are coming from every corner and now Jerry and Stephen Jones find themselves fielding questions about making a coaching change in-season .
The Cowboys aren’t known for making such a drastic call, doing so just once since Jerry Jones bought the team. That happened in 2010 when Wade Phillips was fired following a 1-7 start. He was replaced by offensive coordinator Jason Garrett, who kept the job through the 2019 season. As of now, both Jerry and Stephen are backing Schottenheimer, although Stephen Jones recently revealed what would allow him to feel comfortable making a move during the season.
Jones didn't dive into what type of failure on the field would warrant a change, but instead focused on who they would have in line. While speaking on KRLD-FM on Monday, Jones said the Cowboys wouldn't hesitate to make a necessary change if they " had a succession plan in place .” Jones did reiterate, however, that they are still behind Schottenheimer.
Fans hoping that will change shouldn't hold their breath. According to Mac Engel of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram, the Cowboys “ will not fire Schottenheimer during this season , but after it feels plausible.” Engel adds that Jerry Jones hates the idea of paying a coach who is not actively coaching the team.
That sentiment lines up with recent statements made by Jones, who delusionally said paying top dollar for coaches doesn't equate to success. That claim has no basis to it whatsoever, and just feels like Jones trying to gaslight a fan base that is tired of him being cheap when it comes to coaches.
That said, it gives us all the proof we need to know that Jones is not going to fire a coach in the middle of the season out of pure stubbornness. Sure, he did fire Phillips in 2010, but at that time he was looking for an excuse to promote Garrett. With no one on the staff being groomed to replace Schottenheimer, Jones will just play out the season before making any decisions, which means we are all in for quite a ride during the second half of the year.

title: Cowboys Linked to Underrated Steelers EDGE Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
Jerry Jones continues to say the Dallas Cowboys will explore every opportunity to improve their roster ahead of the November 10 NFL trade deadline .
While Jones will be open to making moves, the Cowboys are limited in draft capital in 2027 , which could hurt their chances of pulling off a big move. That doesn’t mean they can’t still find someone who can help them this year, and beyond. John Owning recently revealed an intriguing option while appearing on 105.3 The Fan.
Owning said he doesn’t think the Cowboys will be “big buyers” at the deadline, but believes there’s one target worth keeping an eye on, saying Alex Highsmith of the Pittsburgh Steelers makes a lot of sense.
”Everyone talks about Maxx Crosby as kind of the golden goose that everyone wants to get. And I think obviously bringing him in would be a huge impact. He'd be a very valuable defender. But I just don't think that's very feasible given the draft picks that the Cowboys have, but I do think someone like I've talked to (Bryan) Broaddus about this a few times is Alex Highsmith from the Pittsburgh Steelers,” Owning said.
“I think he's someone who is young enough, he's impactful enough, and if you brought him in, he's someone who, even if this year is not your year, he can be impactful year two, year three, year four for you. So it's still, it legitimizes trading for him. So I think he's someone who can make an impact, not only in the pass rush department, but also defending the run on the edge. He would immediately walk into the team and be the number one edge defender.”
Should the Cowboys be buyers or sellers at the trade deadline? John Owning says they may not make a big splash, but that Alex Highsmith might be the "big move." pic.twitter.com/qgX0Z5uBXp
Highsmith has 18 tackles and 3.5 sacks this season, working in a rotation that includes T.J. Watt and Nick Herbig. Highsmith signed a four-year extension worth $68 million in 2023, keeping him under contract through the 2027 season .
This offseason, the Steelers signed Herbig to an extension as well, which led to us at Cowboys On SI asking if Highsmith could be a potential trade target for Dallas.
Seeing Dallas and Pittsburgh make a trade wouldn’t be surprising at all given their recent relationship.
The Cowboys have added George Pickens, Broderick Jones, and Joey Porter Jr. in trades with the Steelers over the past two seasons. So far, they’ve been satisfied with the results of those trades and it’s hard to see them regretting a move for someone as talented as Highsmith.

title: 3 Dallas Cowboys With Most to Prove Entering Week 9 vs. Colts
full_text:
Fresh off their latest worst loss of the season , the Dallas Cowboys will be on the road in Week 9 to face the Indianapolis Colts.
Indianapolis is entering the week with a record of 2-6 and they’ve been sellers as the NFL trade deadline approaches. They’ve traded away guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner as they have their sights set on the 2027 season. That doesn’t mean the players on the field aren’t going out there trying to win.
That’s why the Cowboys, who are just 3-5 and boast one of the worst defenses in the league, can’t treat this game like an easy win. They need to understand the urgency they’re facing and no one knows that more than the following three Cowboys who are under the most pressure.
During the Week 7 win over the Philadelphia Eagles , Javonte Williams looked like the player we saw in 2025. He ran for a career-high 155 yards while averaging 6.2 yards per attempt. In Week 8 against the Cardinals, it was a completely different story.
Williams had just 56 yards on 24 attempts, which is an average of 2.3 yards per rush. That was a major reason the Cowboys couldn’t close the game out and Williams will be feeling the pressure to turn things around this week against an Indianapolis defense that’s ranked 27th against the run .
The entire Dallas defense has been awful this season, but Caleb Downs has to be feeling more pressure than most players on that side of the ball. The 11th overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft has struggled in coverage and is coming off a rough outing against the Cardinals. He was targeted three times and surrendered a catch each time. In all, he gave up 49 yards and a touchdown.
On the year, he’s now surrendered 20 receptions on 22 targets for 211 yards and three touchdowns. Opposing quarterbacks have a rating of 146.2, which is concerning. It’s tough on any defensive back when the front seven struggles to generate pressure consistently, but Downs knows he has to be better going forward for this team to turn things around.
No one in Big D has a bigger bullseye on their back right now than Brian Schottenheimer. The second-year head coach has a roster loaded with talent but is just 10-14-1 overall. What’s worse is that the team seems to regress each week and they continue to play to the level of their opponent.
Dallas has no real identity on offense and their defense is arguably the worst in franchise history. The calls for his job continue to grow loud and if he’s unable to deliver a win against the Colts, there could be a riot from the fan base.

title: Cowboys Trade Rumors Offer Updates on Chances of Josh Sweat, George Pickens Deals
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have been viewed as likely buyers ahead of the trade deadline for months now, but things have at least shifted a little bit now that Dallas is sitting with a 3-5 record and looks to be going nowhere in 2026.
In fact, they have shifted enough to the point where teams around the NFL are wondering if George Pickens might be available , which is logical to wonder because he's not under contract beyond this year and clearly he isn't helping the Cowboys much.
Well, don't expect the Cowboys to trade Pickens, with ESPN's Dan Graziano reporting that he doesn't expect the veteran wideout to be moved before the deadline, although he does see the logic in making such a move.
"Staying in the NFC East, teams are wondering if the Cowboys would consider trading WR George Pickens if they suffer another loss this week and fall to 3-6. I do not get the sense that Dallas would consider such a move, but if it isn't planning to sign Pickens to an extension next offseason, it would make sense to at least take the call," Graziano wrote.
Adding to Graziano's report, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport is hearing that the Cowboys "aren't trading Pickens."
"As of right now there's nothing there," Rapoport said on The Pat McAfee Show on Tuesday.
When it comes to the Cowboys' making any addition at the trade deadline, Graziano thinks it's possible Dallas stands pat.
That's because of the dwindling draft capital the Cowboys have , with Dallas sporting just 10 picks the next two years, including four in 2027.
"As for potentially adding players, it's always possible," he said. "But with just four picks in next year's draft and having already made a jump-the-market move to get CB Joey Porter Jr. earlier this season, the Cowboys might not have another big deadline deal to make."
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler adds the Cowboys might be in the market for an edge rusher and Dallas has been linked to Arizona Cardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat.
"Cardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat has been linked to Dallas, which could be in the pass rush market but hasn't made any moves there yet.
Fowler also notes that a potential hurdle for a Sweat trade comes from his contract situation. The belief is Sweat either wants a new deal or will want a "sweetener," like a raise, for example.
"The sense I get from teams in the edge rusher market is that Sweat would prefer a new deal as part of a trade -- or at least a sweetener, such as a raise on his $18.1 million salary this year or next. He's in the second year of a four-year, $76 million contract, so wanting it reworked so early in the deal could be a hurdle to a trade," Fowler wrote.
So, not only would the Cowboys have to give up draft capital for Sweat, they may also have to shell out more money to keep him happy.
All of this points to a tall task for the Cowboys to bring Sweat in. Bear in mind, Dallas will have plenty of competition for Sweat, so they might have to overpay in draft capital just to get him and it's possible that will further deter Jerry Jones.
Another thing that could make Jones hesitant to make a trade is if he sees the writing on the wall that his team is cooked and a trade isn't going to save the sinking ship.
Jones is likely more optimistic about the Cowboys than we are, but he must seriously consider if it's worth it to further kneecap his draft stockpile to try and save a team that almost certainly can't be saved.

title: Colin Cowherd Destroys Cowboys as 'Worst Coached Team' in NFL
full_text:
Colin Cowherd has never been afraid to speak his mind and has been doing so ever since Brian Schottenheimer was named the head coach of the Dallas Cowboys.
Some of Cowherd's takes have been a little over the top, like when he lost his mind over Schottenheimer wearing a backward visor . Many of his other criticisms have been warranted, however, including his take following their Week 8 disaster.
Cowherd unloaded on the Cowboys after surrendering a 14-point lead in the fourth quarter to Gardner Minshew and the Arizona Cardinals. He said Dallas is "the worst coached team in the NFL," and expressed surprise by the fact that they actually had not bottomed out before this meltdown.
"I thought the Cowboys had bottomed out, but they grabbed a shovel and they continue to dig, which is great when you're searching for oil, Jerry, but not for football teams. I think this was like a five-year low. At home, 24-10 lead in the fourth, a backup quarterback, Gardner Minshew, bottom three roster, comes back and beats you. You can't stop them, and they stop you. I mean, I had no idea Tyler Allgeier was like the second greatest running back in the history of the sport," Cowherd said.
"Like, what is happening here? I mean, Gardner Minshew became the only quarterback in the NFL this year to throw for three touchdowns in the fourth quarter. And I'm not nitpicking. I can do that with Kansas City's field goal decision. I mean, Dallas has played the fourth easiest schedule. They're 3-5. The Giants are on a third quarterback. They lead the division. This isn't nitpicking. This is like way out in front of you.
"The Cowboys have become those two robbers in Home Alone. They're falling down the stairs, tripping over paint cans, stepping on toys... This is the worst coached team in the NFL." @colincowherd on the Cowboys' collapse against the Cardinals pic.twitter.com/mn7aEEDPb8
What really bothered Cowherd is the fact that this isn't new. Instead, he's saying the Cowboys continued to find ways to lose, and compared them to the robbers in Home Alone.
"And most alarming, they lose different ways. The Cowboys have become those two robbers in Home Alone. They're falling down the stairs. They're tripping over paint cans. They're stepping on toys. It's a different way to be ridiculous throughout."
It's hard to argue against Cowherd on this one. The Cowboys were bullied in Week 1 by the New York Giants, which was frustrating, but could be overlooked.
As for their other losses, they gave up a field goal with seven seconds remaining to lose to the Baltimore Ravens in Rio, lost to an undrafted rookie quarterback in Jalon Daniels (who was leading a winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers squad at the time), and never stood a chance against the Green Bay Packers as their highly-paid offense failed to show up.
What makes it worse is Schottenheimer's continued confidence . Despite the blunders, he's recently claimed to be an elite play-caller and following the loss to the Cardinals, he said he was a " problem-solver ."
Despite what Schottenheimer thinks, the fact remains that he's a coach with a record of 10-14-1 and is sitting on an incredibly hot seat. If he really is anything like the robbers from Home Alone, that seat is going to burn him for a while before he moves.

title: Dallas Cowboys Trade Rumor Pinpoints Deadline Focus, 3 Potential Targets
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is rapidly approaching and the Dallas Cowboys are running out of time to improve their defense.
Owner Jerry Jones has remained steadfast in his desire to add to the defense, which continues to play at a historically putrid level.
On Tuesday, Jones said the Cowboys don't have anything cooking right now, but things should heat up the closer we get to Nov. 10, which is the last day Dallas can make a trade.
Also on Tuesday, NFL insider Jason La Canfora reported that the Cowboys' deadline focus is adding an edge rusher, which is not surprising given the current state of the position group.
La Canfora named the Las Vegas Raiders' Maxx Crosby, the Arizona Cardinals' Josh Sweat and the Los Angeles Chargers' Khalil Mack as possible trade targets for Dallas, and he thinks Dallas will ultimately come away with one of them.
"Adding an edge rusher remains Jones’ top priority, as we hear it, with Maxx Crosby, Khalil Mack, and Josh Sweat all potential targets," La Canfora wrote.
"We expect him to land one of the three. Jones has committed too heavily to improving this roster to come back without someone now," La Canfora added.
Just because the Cowboys are targeting players doesn't mean they will actually land them. We're highly skeptical Dallas will be able to come away with Crosby or Mack.
According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Raiders have no plans to trade Crosby and he doesn't want to be traded, either.
The Cowboys were one of the teams in hot pursuit of Crosby back in March before they were outbid by the Baltimore Ravens, who ultimately decided to cancel the deal.
Since then, Crosby re-committed to the Raiders and Las Vegas has shown improvement this season, so that will only make him more inclined to stay.
As for Mack, the Chargers have continued to state publicly they don't want to trade him despite their 0-7 start, and reports are suggesting the team isn't willing to sell off pieces.
“I want Khalil Mack here. Khalil Mack wants to be here. He’s one of the pillars of our team," head coach Jim Harbaugh said on Monday.
Of course, that could change, but even if it does, there has been a lot of buzz about Mack going to the Chicago Bears, and it's logical to assume that he would want to go there given his affinity for his former team and its status as a true Super Bowl contender, something the Cowboys are not.
If that's the case, the Chargers will almost certainly oblige given the immense amount of respect the franchise has for the future Hall of Famer. They certainly won't banish him to Dallas, where Mack would have zero shot to contend for anything big.
According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, Sweat is open to being traded out of Arizona, although it remains unclear just how open Arizona is to trading him .
Another problem, Schultz adds, is that Arizona's asking price is high and the Cowboys aren't in a good enough position from a draft pick standpoint to unload significant draft capital.
"The belief around the NFL is that Cardinals DE Josh Sweat would be open to a trade, as he has been dating back to the offseason, and it’s up to Arizona whether it ultimately decides to deal him," Schultz wrote.
"Multiple teams would have interest in Sweat, but the asking price is believed to be high. Arizona has given the impression they’re fine keeping him," Schultz added.
We believe the Cardinals will end up trading Sweat because it just makes sense to do so given the rebuilding situation Arizona is currently navigating and the boost that rebuild will get from sending Sweat packing.
But there are going to be other suitors and Dallas might have a tough time competing against other teams because, again, the Cowboys don't have a great draft pick situation.

title: Dallas Cowboys Get Mixed Signals From Latest Josh Sweat Trade Rumor
full_text:
One of the players the Dallas Cowboys have been linked to ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline is Arizona Cardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat.
Granted, there haven't been any rumors directly tying Dallas to interest in the former Pro Bowler, but multiple NFL insiders have suggested the Cowboys as a potential landing spot given their need at edge rusher.
On Tuesday, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that Sweat is open to being traded out of Arizona, but the impression is that Arizona is open to keeping him.
"The belief around the NFL is that Cardinals DE Josh Sweat would be open to a trade, as he has been dating back to the offseason, and it’s up to Arizona whether it ultimately decides to deal him," Schultz wrote.
"Multiple teams would have interest in Sweat, but the asking price is believed to be high. Arizona has given the impression they’re fine keeping him," Schultz added.
Talk about mixed signals there. It's all well and good that Sweat is open to a trade, but it doesn't appear he's demanding one, and Arizona has to actually want to trade him for Dallas to have an opportunity to land him.
As if all that wasn't enough, a high asking price will make it less likely Sweat gets moved and the Cowboys aren't in a position to overpay given their lack of draft capital .
It makes all the sense in the world for the Cardinals to move the former Super Bowl champion.
You wouldn't have known it from watching the Cowboys' Week 8 loss to Arizona , but the Cardinals are in the very early stages of rebuilding and it doesn't make much sense to hold on to Sweat, who will turn 30 next year.
The Cardinals would be better served unloading him now and picking up more draft capital to accelerate their rebuild.
Given his history of production that includes two double-digit sack seasons, with the last one coming in 2025, we suspect Arizona could fetch a third-round pick for Sweat.
Despite heavy investments into the edge rusher position, with the Cowboys trading for Rashan Gary, signing Von Miller and drafting Malachi Lawrence, those three players have combined for just three sacks this season.
Cowboys edge rushers have 6.5 sacks combined, with Donovan Ezeiruaku (2.5) and James Houston (one) accouting for the other three. Safe to say, that is not what the Cowboys expected to get from their investments.
Sweat, who notched his third sack of the season against Dallas in Week 8, could theoretically provide a boost, but we're not sure he can make enough of a dent to fix the sunken ship that is the Cowboys' defense.

title: Jerry Jones Give Updates on Cowboys' Prospects of Buying or Selling at Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have long been viewed as potential buyers ahead of the NFL trade deadline next month.
However, with the team flailing at 3-5 after another brutal loss at the hands of the Arizona Cardinals in Week 8, many are now wondering if the Cowboys might sell, and more specifically, George Pickens' name has come up .
Cowboys owner Jerry Jones did his normal spot on 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday and made it quite clear the team has no interest in selling at this time.
"Cowboys owner Jerry Jones on (105.3 Tha Fan) further confirms that the team is not looking to sell at the trade deadline," The Fort Worth Star-Telegram's Nick Harris relayed .
Ever since the offseason and through the trade for Joey Porter Jr. , Jones has remained steadfast in his desire to make another move to try and improve the defense.
While he remains open to doing that on Tuesday, Jones said that there is currently nothing cooking for the Cowboys.
“At this particular time, I don’t see anything," Jones said, per Jon Machota of The Athletic .
That's not at all surprising. With a week still to go before the trade deadline, teams are going to stick to unreasonably high asking prices in the hopes that a team bites.
But as we approach the deadline, teams will begin to lower those asking prices, which will help spur on trades.
The overwhelming expectation from NFL insiders is that this could be a wild trade deadline, with several deals going through. We've already seen plenty of fireworks recently, with guys like Jeffery Simmons, DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson all getting traded.
But, as we're well aware of, it takes two to tango and just because Jerry wants to make a deal doesn't mean he'll actually be able to. The price has got to be right, and so does the fit with the player. Adding to that, the Cowboys also have to be certain that the player they are acquiring can actually help them.
We're extremely skeptical anyone short of a truly elite player, like Maxx Crosby, for example, can help the Cowboys dig out of the massive hole they are in defensively.
In fact, we're not even sure a player of that caliber can help a team like the Cowboys that has systemic issues, from the coaching staff on down to the players themselves.
The harsh reality is that the Cowboys are probably better off just doing nothing and saving what's left of their draft capital instead of making another trade that isn't likely to help change their fortunes.
