title: 3 Things Still on My Mind After Broncos' Huge Win Over Chiefs
full_text:
The Denver Broncos beat the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, avenging their season-opening loss at Arrowhead Stadium, and taking a half-game lead in the AFC West.
The Broncos are now the betting favorites to win the division , and all of their goals are still in front of them. At 6-2, the Broncos are poised to extend their four-game winning streak, while the Chiefs have yet to face the toughest stretch of their schedule.
But I'm still sifting through the aftermath of Broncos-Chiefs. Coming off Denver’s sixth win of the season, here are three things on my mind.
Nix’s ankle may have healed and felt good enough to begin the season as the starter, but psychologically, he wasn’t at that same level of recovery. It was clear he didn’t trust his eyes or his weapons to make plays around him.
And yet, the Broncos kept winning, thanks, in part, to Nix stepping up in some critical moments in Week 2 and Week 3. After an ugly showing against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 6 (Denver won that game, by the way), the Nix pile-on reached epic proportions around the league, as fans finally rushed to social media to voice their fears that something was indeed wrong with the Broncos’ quarterback.
However, Nix kept plugging away, and in Week 7, we finally saw him take some chances downfield and utilize his legs as the weapon they can be against the Arizona Cardinals. His 62-yard rushing touchdown seemed to snap him out of his funk, as his confidence came flooding back.
Nix had four explosive passing plays against the Cardinals, and he followed that up with four more against the Chiefs. He finished with 200-plus passing yards in both games, passing for three touchdowns with zero interceptions over that span.
Some say we should pump the brakes. That it’s too early to say that Nix has fully returned to his pre-injury form, but he’s clearly taken some big leaps in that direction over the past two weeks. He’s trusting his eyes again, and he’s unafraid to use his legs to help move the chains.
Nix wants to be peaking as the Broncos hit their stretch run, and the signs are pointing in that direction. I’ll say it, Broncos Country, even if some pundits won’t:
I don’t know if, like Nix, Dobbins is struggling with the mental aspects of bouncing back from the Lisfranc injury that ended his 2025 season in Week 10, or if it’s the cumulative effect of having dealt with three major injuries as a pro, but he’s not the same guy we saw last year.
The Broncos re-signed Dobbins in the spring, giving him a 4x raise , and they’ve tried to extract some blood from that turnip, but nothing has worked. He’s having a career-low season as a rusher, and he’s purportedly healthy.
But something isn’t right with Dobbins. Meanwhile, rookie Jonah Coleman has sparked the Broncos’ offense, and his efficiency and productivity have rendered Dobbins a spectator.
Against the Chiefs, Coleman had 41 snaps to Dobbins’s 13. Payton doesn’t typically take the bell-cow approach with running backs, but that’s the way this thing is trending with Coleman.
Dobbins has proven that he can’t be trusted to move the chains. And until he does something to show that he can be a net-positive for this offense, Payton would be foolish to take any snaps away from the ascending Coleman.
I’m not sure if we’re getting the full story with Dobbins. When healthy, he’s always been one of the NFL’s most productive backs, so he’s either nursing a top-secret ailment (unlikely), or Father Time has combined with his injury history to force a rapid decline.
It’s a shame. But the Broncos can’t overthink it. Until and unless they orchestrate a trade ahead of the November 10 deadline, it’s the Jonah Coleman show moving forward.
But it's worth remembering the Broncos are the betting favorites to land Jonathan Taylor.
With Talanoa Hufanga still out of commission (maybe he’ll return to practice this week), and Brandon Jones now nursing a hamstring injury, the Broncos have relied on Taylor Rapp and Devon Key as the backup safeties, though they left much to be desired against the Chiefs.
However, Week 8 proved that Skinner is deserving of a bigger seat at the table. He’s not the greatest in coverage — okay, fine — but he could be used to devastating effect as a dime-backer and big nickel.
Skinner took on Kenneth Walker III on the goal line, in a situation where the game was on the line, and he single-handedly stopped one of the NFL’s toughest running backs to tackle from scoring. It was impressive, and it showed how big Skinner’s heart is.
JL Skinner is like, "Not today, Kenneth!" pic.twitter.com/v8pcr1BYk6
Skinner is big, he’s physical, and he’s in a contract year. He might not be the best coverage safety, but he’s probably better than linebacker Justin Strnad in coverage.
The Broncos would be wise to reward Skinner with a slightly expanded role, using him as a dime-backer on first and second down when the opponent is in multiple tight-end sets.
I’d trust Skinner to run with a tight end more than I would Strnad, and if the opponent calls a run, he’s more than equipped to sift through the muss and make the tackle, as we saw on the goal line against the Chiefs.
Skinner is in a contract year, and he’s screaming for an opportunity to prove he offers more than mere third-phase value. It’s time the Broncos start giving him a few more snaps each week, even if Hufanga returns this week for the Carolina Panthers game.

title: Broncos Dethrone Chiefs as AFC West Betting Favorites—What Lies Ahead
full_text:
Sean Payton stopped short of calling the Denver Broncos' rematch with the Kansas City Chiefs a "must-win" game, but the stakes were about as high as they could get at the mid-season point.
The Broncos came out on top 28-24 on Sunday , overcoming an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit to beat the Chiefs and overtake them as the AFC West leaders. At 6-2, the Broncos are winners of four in a row and are in the driver's seat in the division.
Even the oddsmakers see the Broncos as the new favorites to win the AFC West. DraftKings Sportsbook has Denver as -130 favorites, with the Chiefs at +115, the Las Vegas Raiders at +2500, and the Los Angeles Chargers at +1500.
As the defending AFC West champions, the Broncos were always going to draw a first-place schedule in 2026. Add to that the rotation of the AFC West drawing the NFC West and AFC East on the schedule this season, and the Broncos' road to repeating as division champs got a little tougher.
Then the NFL front-loaded the Broncos' schedule with most of their toughest opponents coming through the first eight weeks. The NFC West and AFC East produced five playoff teams last season. The Broncos played all four NFC West opponents within the first seven weeks, going 3-1 against them, losing only to the San Francisco 49ers.
The Chiefs in Week 8 were the last big test to end the Broncos' brutal first-half-of-the-season gauntlet, and they passed with flying colors. Now, the Broncos' schedule opens up dramatically.
The Broncos will go on the road this week to face the 3-4 Carolina Panthers, followed by their Week 10 bye. From there, it's home against the 4-4 Raiders in Week 11, then back on the road to play the 6-2 Pittsburgh Steelers on Black Friday.
The Steelers have out-kicked their coverage thus far, so that game could end up being tougher than it appeared to be at first glance. The Broncos then come back home to host the 1-6 Miami Dolphins in Week 12, followed by a two-game road trip to play the 2-6 New York Jets and the Raiders.
That's when the schedule begins to stiffen again. The Broncos come home for a Week 16 game on Christmas Day against the 6-1 Buffalo Bills, followed by a road trip to face the 5-3 New England Patriots, and a home stand against the winless Chargers in the season finale.
The Steelers, Bills, and Patriots could be tough, but if the Broncos take care of business, and beat the teams they're supposed to, they could hit Week 16 at 12-2 or 11-3 at worst. The Chiefs, though, have a much more treacherous road ahead.
The next three weeks aren't too bad for the Chiefs, with a home game against the Jets, a road trip to face the 3-5 Atlanta Falcons, and then back home to play the 3-5 Arizona Cardinals. But it gets gnarly from there.
From Week 12 on, the Chiefs will play the Bills, Patriots, 49ers (6-1), and Raiders at home, and the Los Angeles Rams (4-4), Cincinnati Bengals (5-2), and Chargers on the road. It's about as a brutal a closing stretch as the Broncos' initial schedule was.
The difference is that, in theory, by the time a team hits its stretch run, it's had the chance to build up a callus to begin peaking at the right time before the playoffs. The Broncos went from summer football straight into a playoff guantlet, which forced them to quickly build a callus against such fierce resistance training.
As I wrote when the NFL first dropped the schedule last spring, the Broncos' initial slate of games could be a blessing in disguise — so long as they emerge from Week 8 no worse than 4-4. The Broncos did even better than that, and that's why they're in firm control of the division from here on out.
As the Broncos emerge from the first half of the season, Bo Nix has regained his confidence after suffering a fractured ankle in the playoffs. Rookie running back Jonah Coleman has emerged as a bona fide RB1, and the Broncos have much bigger plans for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle.
Vance Joseph's defense is getting healthier, and has done an amazing job of keeping the who's-who list of elite NFL quarterbacks at bay long enough for Nix and the offense to get their fourth-quarter licks in and win games.
Nobody will want to face the Broncos down the stretch.

title: Broncos Sign RB Amid Trade Rumors
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have added a running back — just not the running back everyone's hoping for .
Denver announced Tuesday that it has signed former Chargers RB Jarett Patterson to the practice squad, along with defensive lineman Jordan Miller and defensive back Ugo Amadi.
In corresponding moves, the club released wide receivers Eli Pancol and Cameron Ross from the practice squad.
Undrafted in 2021, Patterson (5-8, 195) has six years of NFL service and 27 games of experience, split between time with the Washington Commanders (then the Football Team) and the Los Angeles Chargers. He's handled 126 career carries for 503 yards and three rushing touchdowns.
Patterson, who turns 28 in December, is now the senior-most RB on Denver's practice squad. The other back, third-year man Cody Schrader, was promoted to the 53-man active roster prior to Week 8 and figures to again earn an elevation with the Broncos relatively thin at the position.
This will be Miller's second stint in the Mile High City after spending the majority of 2024 and 2025 on Denver's taxi squad. He was signed to — and eventually released from — the Miami Dolphins' practice team in September.
Amadi initially joined the Broncos' practice squad last month but was cut loose ahead of Week 8 with the club's secondary nearing full strength.
The defensive additions come only one day after head coach Sean Payton rued the fact that Denver currently leads the NFL in snaps taken on that side of the ball.
“There’s a lot that goes into that. That’s a stat I don’t like," Payton told reporters via conference call on Monday. "It’s a stat that on offense, we have to do a good job of possessing the ball. So that’s something that we pay attention to.”
Many among Broncos Country have already taken to social media following Patterson's addition, vexed over the possibility that his signing rules Denver out of contention for Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, who's been consistently linked in trade rumors.
The reality is, the Broncos have one more game (at Carolina) until the Week 10 bye, and two of their running backs (RJ Harvey, Tyler Badie) remain on short-term injured reserve. With rookie Jonah Coleman and aging vet J.K. Dobbins left primarily in the backfield, this is as much about temporary insurance as anything else.
If you're one of the many who want Denver to land Taylor, fret not. "Jaret Patterson" would not prevent them from making that move ... if they want to make the move in the first place.
"(General manager) George (Paton) and I will spend time looking at the team and anywhere we can improve it, but I’m not going to answer questions about internet gossip,” Payton said Monday.

title: Broncos Suddenly Become Favorites to Land Jonathan Taylor—Here's Why
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are 6-2 and in sole possession of first place in the AFC West after defeating the Kansas City Chiefs at Mile High on Sunday.
Broncos rookie running back Jonah Coleman turned in his most dynamic performance of the season , finishing with 100-plus total yards and scoring the go-ahead touchdown. Like two ships in the night, as Coleman rises, J.K. Dobbins falls, as illustrated by the rookie's 41 snaps and the veteran's 13 in Week 8.
However, Coleman's emergence hasn't dampened the trade speculation connecting the Broncos to Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor . In fact, coming out of Week 8, the Broncos have the highest odds of being Taylor's team after the November 10 deadline, according to Hard Rock Bet .
Going into Week 8, the Seahawks were the most favored in the Taylor sweepstakes, but the Broncos have edged in front of them at +200. The Seahawks and the Vikings are the Broncos' biggest competitors for Taylor's services, and the law of supply and demand could see the Colts' asking price climb.
There have been reports of the Colts receiving at least one second-round pick offer for Taylor, so that's the likely starting point if the Broncos want to land the three-time Pro Bowler. The Broncos have a full complement of draft picks next year, so they have the ammunition to acquire Taylor.
Taylor could be a game-changer for the Broncos' offense. He's a back who can create on his own as a playmaker. Among the Broncos' running backs, we've only seen that from Coleman this season, so pairing him with Taylor could form a formidable one-two punch.
However, Taylor is the same age as Dobbins (turning 28 soon), and he's nearing the dreaded 2,000-carry milestone (1,699). That's when backs often began to decline, some faster than others.
Taylor would be relatively affordable salary-wise, with salaries of $15 million and $9.65 million in 2027 and 2028, respectively. That's not the obstacle; it's the draft capital the Colts will demand to part with their only star player on offense.
The San Francisco 49ers gave up a second-, third-, fourth-, and fifth-round draft pick to acquire Christian McCaffrey from the Carolina Panthers in 2022. Taylor is roughly two years older than McCaffrey was when he was traded, so that has to be factored into the calculus.
That's the precedent , though. So, the question is whether the Broncos believe that Taylor would be worth a similar haul. Maybe it wouldn't take quite so much; say, a second-rounder, a third, and a 2028 fourth-rounder.
I'm just spitballing here. But if the Broncos were to countenance such an expenditure, they'd have to really believe that Taylor would be the missing piece to help get them over the Super Bowl hump.
Week 8 didn't change anything . Despite Coleman's emergence, the Broncos are still the favorites to land Taylor — for a reason. With RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie on injured reserve, the Broncos not only need reinforcements, but they need another difference-maker back there.
Whatever is going on with Dobbins's regression, there's no end in sight. We're eight games into the season, and while it's possible he could finally snap out of it, the Broncos can't count on it.
Last year, the Broncos were forced to rely on a rookie as their lead back down the stretch, and while they managed to win the division and the No. 1 playoff seed, their inability to run the ball consistently was a major Achilles heel. GM George Paton and head coach Sean Payton — having weathered the storm of the Broncos' brutal first-half schedule — may be willing to pay top dollar, so to speak, to hedge against a history repeating in 2026.
Coleman is much better equipped to carry the RB1 duties as a rookie than Harvey was, but do the Broncos really want to chance that? We'll find out soon, as the NFL trade deadline is only a week away.

title: Broncos' Week 8 Snap Counts Send Telling Message About J.K. Dobbins
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are still riding high after erasing an 11-point fourth-quarter lead to defeat the Kansas City Chiefs 28-24 .
Comeback wins are nothing new for the Broncos, but the stakes in this game made the victory all the sweeter. Not only were the Broncos looking to balance the scales and avenge their season-opening loss to the Chiefs, but first place in the AFC West was on the line.
The Broncos wouldn't be denied, although it was a wild and zaney finish , they out-executed the Chiefs when the chips were down to take a half-game lead in the AFC West. Now, the Broncos are poised to continue their four-game winning streak, and really go on a run, with the worst of their schedule behind them.
Week 8's win over the Chiefs gave us some insight into specific player roles and playing time. Whose role is expanding and whose is eroding? The snap counts tell the tale.
Bo Nix and the Broncos' starting five offensive line played 100% of the snaps, with 62. Offensive tackle Alex Palczewski received five snaps when the Broncos deployed their heavy package.
With that said, let's examine the rest of the snap counts and break down the gleanings.
Once again, Coleman outearned all backs, including Dobbins, in snaps and touches. The rookie finished with 11 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown, with four catches on five targets for 63 yards.
This was the second straight week that Coleman has been the lead back. Dobbins was given his chances, but managed just 13 yards on seven carries.
When the fullback in a Sean Payton offense is matching you in snap share, it's an alarming reflection of just how far you've fallen. Dobbins simply hasn't been able to produce at an acceptable level, let alone at a starter level.
With RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie on injured reserve, Schrader was elevated from the practice squad. He only saw two snaps, though, and didn't touch the ball.
Coleman is the Broncos' new RB1 and I don't expect that to change anytime soon, given how productive and explosive he's been for the offense.
Sutton saw the most action once again, catching all four of his targets for 53 yards. This was the first game this season where Sutton looked like himself, making some tough contested catches and playing the most of his targets.
Franklin played a selfless game in this one, blocking his rear end off . He only had one catch on three targets for three yards, but he contributed a lot to the Broncos' ground attack and made one heck of a block on Coleman's 51-yard catch-and-run.
With Waddle nursing a chest injury, Franklin saw more snaps. But Waddle still led the team in targets, with six, catching three for 39 yards and a touchdown. He also caught a two-point conversion.
Mims contributed with two catches on three targets for 10 yards and carried the ball twice for 19 yards, but on the plays where the ball was designed to go to him, his effort was lacking. That's been a theme of his this season, which is troubling, given that he's playing on an expiring contract.
Humphrey caught his one-and-only target, picking up 10 yards. Nix is clearly looking for Waddle and Sutton first, but it would be nice to see Franklin and Mims begin to win more in their routes to earn more targets.
Trautman again led in snap share, but this time, he also led the tight ends in receiving, catching two passes for 30 yards. Adkins had two catches for four yards, but one of them was a crucial touchdown on a 4th-&-Goal.
Alas, Engram was on the field for half the game, and he was targeted three times, but he and Nix were unable to connect. Engram's role continues to shrink as the season marches on, and really, since Payton took back the play-calling.
Despite nursing a hamstring injury, Allen led the room in snap share. He totaled three pressures, all of which were hits on Patrick Mahomes. Allen didn't get a sack, but he impacted the game as he always does.
Roach was again fantastic. With the second-most snaps up front, he notched a clutch-time sack on Mahomes to end the game, and finished with four tackles. Roach also had two pressures.
D.J. Jones didn't create pressure on the passer, but he had two tackles. Uwazurike helped stop the run and notched two pressures on Mahomes.
Sai'vion Jones continues to rise up the ranks. He had a hit on Mahomes, showing the Broncos that he can create interior pressure on the quarterback when he's on the field.
Cooper led the way in snap share and in pressures, finishing with a team-high five pressures on Mahomes. He didn't get a sack, but he was a constant force as a pass rusher, and finished with three tackles in the Broncos' effort to neutralize Kenneth Walker III.
Bonitto had one of his more forgettable games of the season, with zero tackles and two pressures, though he was able to get one hit on Mahomes. Kansas City's undrafted rookie left tackle, Khalil Benson, had Bonitto's number in both head-to-head matchups this season.
Robinson is a whirling dervish. He's a future starter, and he showcased his impact play once again. He totaled three pressures and one hit on Mahomes, and contributed as an edge-setter against the run.
Tillman is a workhorse. It's not always flashy, but he gets the job done. Sunday was much the same, though you'd like to see him get at least one pressure.
Singleton played 100% of the defensive snaps, and turned in another starring performance. He had a team-high 14 tackles, and a sack. He's on pace to earn a Pro Bowl nod.
Strnad had one of his worst games of the season. Missed tackles. Out of position in coverage. He only had two tackles, despite playing 72% of the snaps.
Like Singleton, Surtain and Moss played 100% of the snaps, and both were excellent. It was Surtain's first game back since Week 4, and he made his presence felt, finishing with a whopping eight tackles — though he missed two — and he only gave up one catch in coverage.
Surtain also had a big pass break-up in the end zone to save a touchdown. He was a big reason the Broncos were able to limit Walker on the ground, and he keep the Chiefs out of the end zone at the end of the game.
Chiefs passing game was heavy underneath, quick game, screen etc. Not a major coverage day for Pat Surtain II in his return from 3-game absence. But one of the best tackling outings I can recall for the All-Pro. 8 tackles (T-2 for his career), including two on Kenneth Walker in… pic.twitter.com/RQKTcZ3XpB
Moss was targeted four times, allowing just two catches. He had one excellent pass breakup that was almost an interception, and he contributed four tackles on the perimeter.
McMillian remains this team's nickel, but this was a tougher game for him. On one hand, he allowed all five of his targets to be caught in coverage, but it was for just 26 total yards. In other words, with a long of seven yards, McMillian was able to keep everything in front of him, and limit completions in their tracks.
Barron was relegated to a supporting role, with Surtain back in the lineup. This is how it'll be when the Broncos have their top three corners healthy.
Jones suffered a hamstring injury, which put pressure on Rapp and Key with Talanoa Hufanga missing this game. Rapp had his worst game as a Bronco thus far, but led the safeties in snap share, showing how much the coaches trust him.
Rapp had four tackles, but took a bad angle on Emmett Johnson's 73-yard touchdown reception, getting comically turned around near the goal line. Rapp was targeted twice in coveage, allowing just one completion of four yards.
Key was a major contributor, notching eight tackles. He gave up two completions for 32 yards on three targets, but one of them was an unfortunate case of slipping on the wet turf due to the rainfall.
Let's hear it for Skinner, though. He played a season-high nine snaps, and his contributions on the goal line to end the game helped preserve the win. He took Walker on one-on-one in the hole, and stopped him, forcing the Chiefs to burn their final timeout with four seconds remaining.
Still thinking about this tackle…

title: How Broncos' Huge Win Over Chiefs Changed Their NFL Trade Deadline Outlook
full_text:
Jonah Coleman has been a revelation over the past two weeks.
But in the face of J.K. Dobbins's continued regression, has Coleman's emergence been enough to move the Denver Broncos away from trading for a running back ahead of the November 10 deadline?
That's the question. The Broncos are riding high after stunning the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday , erasing an 11-point fourth-quarter lead to win 28-24 at Mile High.
Coleman was a big part of that fourth-quarter resurgence , with some explosive running, a massive 51-yard catch-and-run, and the go-ahead touchdown. Dobbins was again relegated to the bench in the second half on the heels of his impotent 13 yards rushing on seven carries.
Obviously, the Broncos didn't expect Dobbins to be this slow in getting up to speed after recovering from the Lisfranc foot injury that ended his 2025 campaign in Week 10, or else they wouldn't have given him the two-year, $16 million deal he signed in March. If Denver had a crystal ball, it would have let him depart to Jacksonville and let his recovering be the Jaguars' problem.
Alas, nobody can see the future, but the past can often serve as a reliable predictor. After Dobbins was lost for the season, the Broncos' ground game was reduced to a rookie RJ Harvey late last year, complemented occasionally by a Jaleel McLaughlin or Tyler Badie carry.
Harvey was nowhere near up to the task of carrying a playoff team's run game, though he did have a few shining moments. Sitting at 6-2 now, with a half-game lead over the Chiefs in the AFC West, the Broncos have to decide whether they're willing to roll the dice on the possibility of Coleman being the only reliable playmaker in the backfield behind Bo Nix.
It doesn't appear that Dobbins is going to suddenly turn the ship around, despite his recent comments , and Harvey is on injured reserve for at least three more games, after suffering a knee injury during practice last week. Meanwhile, the trade deadline is a week away, and the Broncos have a full complement of 2027 draft picks.
Jonathan Taylor sure looks attractive , although the Indianapolis Colts have already received an offer of a second-round pick for the talented back. Taylor is the same age as Dobbins (almost 28), but he's rapidly approaching the 2,000-carry milestone, which is often when a running back will begin to decline, sometimes precipitously.
Taylor has 1,699 NFL carries, plus 208 receptions since entering the league in 2020. That's a lot of wear and tear on his tires. Unlike Dobbins, Taylor has managed to avoid major injury as a pro, but because of that, there's a lot of mileage on his odometer.
Taylor is also averaging a career-low 4.1 yards per carry and his explosive play rate has declined this season. Whether that's due to the Colts' offensive line or the vagaries of Father Time is anyone's guess, but those are the facts.
The good news is that, about the time Taylor hits the 2,000-carry milestone, his contract will be much closer to expiring, so that could offer the Broncos a bit more peace of mind. He's under contract for $15 million in 2027 and $9.6 million in 2028, so he's not overly expensive — it's more about the draft capital the Colts will want in exchange for him.
There are other backs the Broncos could consider, like Tennessee's Tony Pollard, who has just 15 fewer rush yards than Taylor's 610 yards this season, and would come at a fraction of the cost. Another option would be Breece Hall, whom the New York Jets are obviously protecting ahead of the deadline, holding him out of Sunday's game.
Hall is having a terrible season, having appeared in only three games, with 163 rushing yards and a touchdown on 51 carries (3.2 avg.). Perhaps a change of scenery could do him wonders, but he has an injury history and ball security issues, at times.
The Broncos have been linked to Hall in the recent past , so it's possible they could reach out to the Jets and talk to GM Darren Mougey, who served as GM George Paton's top lieutenant for years. Who knows? Perhaps Mougey would cut Paton a deal for Hall.
I held out hope that Dobbins would eventually snap out of his funk, and turn things around. I attributed his struggles to the brutality of Denver's inital schedule, but he's just not improving.
And when Coleman hits the field, and finds plenty of yards and plays to be had behind the same Broncos offensive line that was getting pilloried for not opening things up for Dobbins, it's much harder to give the veteran the benefit of the doubt. Perhaps the third major injury of Dobbins's NFL career was the straw that broke the camel's back and he may never return to form.
The Broncos are paying him moderately well to perform, though. And Sean Payton has nine more games to prepare for, and if the Broncos achieve their goal of winning the division, a playoff run to anticipate.
Denver will need a reliable ground attack to go the distance. Coleman has been an exciting revelation, but as a rookie, I'm not sure the Broncos would be wise to rely on him to carry the load when things get tough in late December and January.
Despite Coleman's huge day against the Chiefs, because Dobbins was so terrible yet again, the Broncos have to stay in the trade conversations taking place across the league. Pollard or Hall could be an asset to the Broncos' ground attack, but Taylor would be an immediate difference-maker capable of elevating the offense to another level, especially with Coleman as part of a one-two punch.
Harvey will eventually return from IR, but he's more of a 'joker' receiving option than a ball carrier the Broncos could lean on. This team has Nix on a rookie contract for only two more seasons, so if there's a big move to be made to get the Broncos over the hump, now's the time to swing.

title: Broncos Grades After 28-24 Win Over Chiefs: Bo Nix Returning to Pre-Injury Form
full_text:
The Denver Broncos now sit atop the AFC West with a 64% chance of winning the division after yet another fourth-quarter comeback victory, this time against the Kansas City Chiefs .
Had the Broncos lost this one, their chances of winning the division would have dropped to 30%, so this game was a must-win, even if Sean Payton stopped short of calling it that last week. His boldness and aggression against the Chiefs reflected the importance of the game, as the Broncos came out on top 28-24 and Payton earned the 200th victory of his career, reaching that impressive milestone the sixth-fastest in NFL history.
While the Broncos' defense allowed some explosive plays, the unit actually played well overall, and so did the offense, except in the third quarter. There were a lot of high grades this week, though a few players still ended up below the starting grade of 50.
With that said, let's dive into Week 8's player grades.
Bolles played a great game and didn't allow a single pressure. That makes three games this year where he hasn't given up any pressure, and makes him the only left tackle to have achieved that so far this year.
Bolles continues to play at an All-Pro level and was a key part of the Broncos' offensive line producing its best game by far, with the lowest-graded blocker being right guard Quinn Meinerz (64.4).
Surtain was back after missing a few weeks and was only targeted twice, allowing one catch for eight yards. He was a shutdown corner in the truest form.
Surtain also played a great game against the run and helped shut down a few attempts for minimal gains.
This was a solid game from Nix , though there were a lot of yards left on the field due to some serious ball placement issues. However, he wasn't afraid to push the ball, was quick and decisive with his throws, and didn't bail on a clean pocket.
Nix looks like he is getting back to his late-season form before his injury, which could push Denver back into the Super Bowl conversation.
Waddle didn't have a huge game with three catches for 39 yards, but his 35-yard reception was a big play for the offense. He also showed how much of a difference he makes even when he isn't being targeted, based on how the Chiefs were covering him.
There's a reason why Payton has plans for Waddle's role to continue growing as the season marches ahead.
Robinson has been excellent for Denver and picked up three pressures while doing great against the run. There is a good chance he becomes a quality starter in the future due to his explosive athleticism.
Teams try to pick on Moss, but the Chiefs mostly avoided him with four targets his way. He only allowed two catches for 10 yards, and he broke on one ball, forcing the receiver to break it up to avoid an interception. His tackling and run defense were sound as well.
Jones has continued to show his value as an interior pass rusher, but his run defense has been a question. He not only did well against the run this week, but his high grade was because of his run defense rather than his play as a pass rusher.
This was the first time Jones looked like he could be a starter or the fourth player on the unit, instead of the fifth or sixth.
Not only did Powers do well in the run game — he was great — and he held up well in pass protection. Powers didn't allow a single pressure against the Chiefs and put together one of the best games of his Broncos career, by far.
Whenever Adkins has been on the field, he's been consistent and reliable, both as a receiver and as a blocker. He's not a tell when he's on the field, thanks to his versatility, which the Broncos have exploited well this season.
The only question is why Adkins isn't seeing the field more, as he has been far and away the Broncos' best tight end.
With Talanoa Hufanga out again, the Broncos signed Rapp to the 53-man roster ahead of this game, using him and Devon Key to replace Hufanga. Alas, Rapp really struggled against the Chiefs and was at fault for more than one explosive play.
Strnad has been playing at a high level for most of the season, but the Chiefs had his number on a couple of big plays. On one such play, he got stiff-armed into the turf, while on another explosive run, he struggled to wrap up with good technique.
Bonitto struggled against the run and failed to generate much pressure (only two). He also got caught in a broken-coverage situation that resulted in a 73-yard touchdown by Emmett Johnson. It was a rough game all around for the pass rusher.
With two targets and zero catches, Engram had another quiet day. He has not lived up to expectations as the ‘joker’ tight end for Payton, and his blocking remains a liability. It's time to limit his snaps even more.
Mims's effort was once again questionable whenever the play wasn't designed to get him the ball, especially as a route-runner. Sure, he can generate explosives for the offense, as evidenced by his 14-yard run, but he needs to show consistent effort to get more utilization.
If Mims doesn't run every route with 100% effort, it eliminates a potential target from the passing equation, making it harder on Nix to move the chains.
Trautman's blocking wasn't all bad, but he only had two good blocks on 14 run-block snaps. Adkins only had 13 run-block snaps, but nine of his blocks were positively graded.
What saves Trautman’s grade was his one long catch, though it wasn't really a great play by him. Again, it's time to give Adkins an increased role, and it should be at Trautman's expense.

title: Film Room: How Broncos Erased 11-Point Deficit to Stun Chiefs
full_text:
Here we go again with the “Heart-Attack Horsies."
It’s inexplicable how the Denver Broncos win close games nearly every week, yet here we are. This team, led by quarterback Bo Nix , somehow pulls a rabbit out of its hat when the chips are down.
Once again, the Broncos erased an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit in miraculous fashion, beating the Kansas City Chiefs 28-24 . It took a pair of touchdown drives and a last-second sack to pull it off, but the Broncos are officially in first place in the division, once again.
Everyone says this isn’t a sustainable way to win football games, but the Broncos have won 15 consecutive one-score games. Eventually, it has to become the expectation that they’re going to pull it off.
This week was crazy, though. Let’s break down the fourth quarter by the offense in this week’s film room.
Jonah Coleman's vision is awesome on this play. Franklin is doing such a great job as a blocker, too. pic.twitter.com/kA3Wvx0J9N
The Broncos hadn't gotten the ground game rolling for most of the game. J.K. Dobbins was a non-factor in the second half , and the Broncos leaned into the explosiveness of Jonah Coleman when the game was on the line.
To open the Broncos' first scoring possession of the fourth quarter, Coleman showed off his vision on an inside zone run for 10 yards. Watch wide receiver Troy Franklin and tight end Adam Trautman at the point of attack.
Franklin has developed his blocking incredibly well over the course of the season. Denver slices him across the formation as a kick-out blocker on the cornerback, and he does a good job up front. Trautman, who actually gets run into by Coleman, digs out the linebacker at the second level and helps pave the way.
This is a great run by Coleman. There really isn’t a lot there to begin with because center Luke Wattenburg gets beaten at the line of scrimmage, forcing the rookie to cut it back to the outside. Once he hits Trautman in the back, he bounces it outside and buries his head to finish the run with good power.
Wattenburg gets dumped in Bo's lap, but he escapes and hits Sutton camped out in the zone on a stop route. pic.twitter.com/cyQZ7HoOqa
I wanted to highlight this play because it shows how much differently Nix is playing while throwing on the run.
Wattenburg loses immediately to the bull rush and gets dumped directly into Nix’s lap, making the quarterback roll to his right. The Chiefs are in zone coverage, and wide receiver Courtland Sutton sits down in the soft spot to pick up eight yards and keep the drive rolling.
This isn’t a spectacular play, but we haven’t seen this very much over the course of the season. Nix would escape pressure and roll to his right, but he wouldn’t keep his eyes downfield and would usually throw the ball away. Keeping the offense on track is critical when you’re down 11 points in the fourth quarter.
This is a ridiculous catch by Trautman. Watch Bo pull it back when he sees Dobbins is covered underneath. Bolton actually fell down, which allowed Trautman to make this catch. Tack on 15 for roughness at the end. pic.twitter.com/sfLT86S1tg
This play was absolutely insane for a handful of reasons. It was raining at this point in the game, further accentuating how insane this play is.
The Broncos are trying to take a shot on first down near midfield, but nothing is there. Nix gets antsy in the pocket and goes into creation mode.
Watch as Nix looks to Dobbins underneath on the checkdown. He has to eat the football because Dobbins has a defender draped all over him. Nix resets his feet and fires a dart to Trautman, who makes a ridiculous catch in front of Chiefs linebacker Nick Bolton — who slipped on the wet field — and scampers upfield for an explosive gain.
The fact that Nix held onto a wet football on the pump fake is nothing short of incredible. That easily could have been a fumble, but he kept the play alive and took a chance to hit Trautman in a tight window. Bolton could have broken that pass up if he didn’t fall.
The Broncos also got 15 yards added to the result of the play thanks to an unnecessary roughness penalty by Chiefs safety Alohi Gilman, setting the offense up in the red zone.
This is really cool. Denver scored 2 times in the flat. Watch Tranquill closely on the 2 point conversion. He crashes to the flat to cover Engram and leaves a massive window for Waddle on the crossing route. That was schemed up to perfection. pic.twitter.com/W7gi4BA2vF
A few plays later, on 4th-and-Goal, Nix hit tight end Nate Adkins for his second touchdown pass of the game, which was followed by a great play design for a two-point conversion to cut the deficit to three points.
I’m splicing the first touchdown of the game into this to show how they schemed the two-point conversion open, and how great a play call it was.
On the first touchdown, the Broncos run Franklin across the formation into a bunch formation. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle runs a quick out route to the flat, with Franklin and Sutton muddying up the defense at the release. We’ve seen this look before when Peyton Manning was in Denver, and it’s a great design to get an easy throw for points.
On the second touchdown, Adkins runs an arrow route to the flat from an attached wing alignment, and Sutton draws a pair of defenders upfield to open the flat.
Watch Chiefs linebacker Drue Tranquill closely on this play. He gets his eyes inside and bites on the play-action fake while Adkins sprints to the flat. Tranquill isn’t responsible for the flat on this play, but keep this in mind.
On the two-point conversion, Denver runs a 'sail' concept right in front of Tranquill, who dashes to the flat to cover tight end Evan Engram’s out route. That opened up a massive throwing window to Waddle, who finishes in the end zone for the second time.
Nix takes his time letting Waddle clear Bolton, and puts a good ball into his target's chest plate. This was a great way to take advantage of Tranquill’s aggressiveness in coverage.
Perfect play call against an overload blitz. Bolton gets caught inside and lets Coleman get a free release to the flat. Franklin doing yeoman's work as a blocker down field once again. pic.twitter.com/LvvuunTASh
After Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal, the Broncos are set up with great field position, plenty of time, and a pair of timeouts.
Sean Payton dials up a halfback “dash” play, running Coleman across the formation and into the opposite flat. Denver catches the Chiefs in an overload blitz to the left side, and Coleman gets a free release through the line of scrimmage, running wide open.
Bolton gets caught inside and doesn’t touch Coleman in the hole, then rushes upfield to try to pressure Nix. That simple mistake was all it took to break this play open.
Watch Franklin as a blocker downfield. He draws his defender across the field, then blasts Gilman into the boundary, opening a cutback lane for Coleman to gain more yards.
You don’t get explosive plays without receivers doing their jobs downfield, and this is the second week in a row where Franklin has done a fantastic job as a blocker on an explosive play.
Coleman's 2nd career TD. His vision is so freaking good. pic.twitter.com/wEcUD9TPcK
On the next play, the Broncos run wide zone inside the 5-yard line. Coleman’s vision on this play is incredible.
Left guard Ben Powers gets blown into the backfield at the point of attack, forcing Coleman to cut it back. Coleman puts his foot in the ground and gets north in a hurry, squeezing behind wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr., who does a good job at the second level to seal the lane to the end zone and help the Broncos take the lead.
You can watch these plays a hundred times, and it still won’t explain how the Broncos managed to turn it on so intensely when the game is on the line. They got some luck, some help from key penalties, great schemes and play designs, and cleaned up some execution errors.
But it doesn’t explain why . There’s something about this team that is supernatural. It’s Mile…

title: Why Sean Payton Expects Broncos WR Jaylen Waddle's Role to Expand
full_text:
Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle delivered his first official "Penguin" celebration during Sunday's comeback victory over the Kansas City Chiefs.
And there might be more where that came from.
Speaking Monday, Broncos head coach Sean Payton said he expects Waddle's role—and therefore his production—to continue to expand as the division-leading club enters the stretch run toward the postseason.
“Absolutely, let’s keep going," Payton said via conference call with reporters. "It’s something that’s going to be important for us. He’s dynamic, he’s quick. Each week as we gameplan, it was a little bit more challenging last week because Wednesday he didn’t go and there’s that uncertainty. We’re going to need his plays down the stretch.”
Indeed, Waddle entered the Week 8 contest as questionable with a chest injury he re-aggravated the game prior. The Broncos' top receiver looked no worse for wear, catching three of his team-high six targets for 39 yards and a touchdown, after which he hit the aforementioned move.
HE HIT THE PENGUIN DANCE pic.twitter.com/3mJ0u48DVl
Perhaps most notably, Waddle was featured prominently over the middle of the field, highlighted by a 35-yard snag on a rope from quarterback Bo Nix, who went 20-of-32 for 222 yards, two scores, and zero interceptions amid the 28-24 conquest — his NFL-leading 15th game-winning drive since 2024.
“It means a lot," Nix said in his postgame press conference. "That’s a big divisional win for us, obviously—one of our toughest opponents in the division, one of our rivals. They played us really well again, and we just responded this time. That’s just a good football team, and they’re going to give us their best every time, and so we just have to respond well.”
Sunday's game marked the seventh time this season that Waddle recorded at least five targets in a game. However, it was also the seventh time that he failed to eclipse 50 receiving yards; that lone occasion came in Week 2, when he hung 138 yards across 10 catches on the Jacksonville Jaguars.
For the Broncos' passing offense to take the next step — especially important in January and beyond — they must continue finding ways to get the ball in the hands of the threat for whom they surrendered a first-round pick to acquire.
Denver has one last matchup prior to its Week 10 bye, facing a hapless Carolina Panthers defense that just fired their defensive coordinator. If there's ever going to be a week for Waddle to replicate the success he had against Jacksonville, and for Payton to make good on his intentions, this is it.

title: Sean Payton Reveals Broncos Loved Two Other RBs in Draft Besides Jonah Coleman
full_text:
Jonah Coleman has arrived.
The Denver Broncos' rookie running back has only been active for four games this season. He's actually touched the ball in three of those contests and in each one, he's been a difference-maker.
In his second game since returning from injured reserve, Coleman posted a season-high 104 yards from scrimmage and scored the Broncos' go-ahead touchdown to vanquish the Kansas City Chiefs 28-24. Once again, the rookie out-earned J.K. Dobbins in snap share and touches.
Coleman has momentum, and the spark he has provided the Broncos' offense has been palpable. One play before his touchdown, late in the fourth quarter, the rookie caught a Bo Nix pass and rumbled 51 yards downfield to set the Broncos up on the 5-yard line.
JONAH COLEMAN DOWN TO THE 4 KCvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/nRd1e0xIhC
It was a huge, explosive play that electrified the Mile High faithful at Empower Field. Suffice it to say, Broncos Country loves its rookie running back.
On the other side of the field, Kansas City's rookie running back also had himself a day, totaling north of 100 scrimmage yards, almost all of which came as a receiver. Johnson scored a 73-yard touchdown on a play where Patrick Mahomes beat the Broncos' blitz, lofting the ball over everyone's heads and into the rookie's hands, who then turned on the jets and rumbled to the house.
With a running back like Kenneth Walker III at the top of the depth chart, Johnson doesn't get many carries, but the Chiefs find creative ways to utilize him. The Broncos met with Johnson as a prospect, but ultimately chose to draft Coleman about a round-and-a-half before Kansas City selected the former Nebraska star.
The Broncos' interest in Johnson during draft season was public, but Payton confirmed it after Sunday's game, complimenting the running back class in the 2026 draft.
“Yes, that’s right... Emmett was one [of the running backs Denver liked]," Payton said post-game. "We just didn’t like two [running backs], but we loved Emmett."
Payton said the Broncos also liked Indiana's Kaelon Black, whom the San Francisco 49ers drafted late in the third round.
"The 49ers drafted one (Black) that we really liked," Payton said. "We felt this was a good running back draft, and I’m not even talking about those guys that went early. The kid from Indiana (Black), the player that Kansas City took, all of those guys have good tape and [are] different type runners, right? Exciting backs that are going to play a long time in this league.”
For what it's worth, Coleman has rushed for 134 yards and two touchdowns in the four games he's been active, with nine receptions for 97 yards. Black has touched the ball in all seven of San Francisco's games, and with the 49ers on bye, he's sitting with 233 rushing yards and one touchdown, with three receptions for four yards.
Johnson has touched the ball in all seven of Kansas City's games, totaling 77 rushing yards, with 14 receptions for 237 yards and one touchdown. Coleman is on pace to obliterate the numbers of Black and Johnson, but both of those rookies are playing behind two of the best running backs in the NFL.
What's so exciting about what the future of Coleman's rookie campaign could hold is that he's become the de facto No. 1 running back in Denver. There's always the chance that Dobbins could wrest back the RB1 duties because Payton likes to ride the hot hand, but the arrow is pointing straight up for Coleman.
Coleman's football IQ and make-up are very unique for a rookie. Crediting his offensive line and teammates for helping to spur his big day and secure a tough win over the Chiefs is only the latest example of the intangible traits that drew the Broncos to him.
Coleman has already caught the clutch-time bug. He's been part of two big fourth-quarter comebacks and without his contributions in those games, including Sunday vs. the Chiefs, the Broncos don't come back to win.
From the locker room after the final gun, Coleman showed his appreciation to Broncos Country and talked about the team's mindset that head coach Sean Payton helped cultivate this past week.
“Coach [Payton] said it was going to be a fourth-quarter game and it’s hard to play at [Empower Field at] Mile High when they got the crowd rocking like how they [were]," Coleman said. "Broncos Country showed up today. It helped us get that win."
Of course, without the Broncos' defense stopping Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs from racing down the field and scoring a touchdown in the closing 1:48 of the game, this one would have shaken out differently. It was another complementary win for the now 6-2 Broncos, and Coleman was thrilled to contribute to it in such a big way .
"It was good to just go out there and punch in the game winner and rely on the defense and allow them to dominate like they’ve been doing all year," Coleman said.
The rookie garnered rave reviews from his head coach and veteran teammates, including Nix. Like Payton, Nix complimented Coleman's explosiveness, burst, and ability to create big plays for a Broncos offense that's — let's face it — still finding its way.
“Jonah played great, ran the ball really tough. He’s explosive when he gets the football," Nix said. "He runs hard, hard to tackle, very quick to the hole and through it. I thought he did a really good job of... He just made the plays that were there. He didn’t let the moment get too big."
The rookie was even doing his part to motivate his veteran teammates and keep their eye on the prize as the fourth quarter approached.
"I just got to give a shoutout to my O-line and my teammates for keeping the confidence up the whole game," Coleman said. "The game didn’t go our way the whole entire game until the fourth quarter. I went up to all the O-linemen and the receivers and the defense [saying],  ‘It’s going to be a four-quarter game,’ like Coach [Payton] said, just to remind them it’s not over. So when the fourth quarter hit, that’s when the spark just lit up in the whole team.”
With how well this kid is playing, it makes you wonder how serious the latest rumors are of Denver's interest in the running back market ahead of the NFL trade deadline, especially Jonathan Taylor in Indy. If the Broncos traded for a player like Taylor, Coleman would take a back seat, and it might affect his development.
For this reason and many others, when it comes to the rumors of Denver's interest in Taylor and other backs on the trade block, I'll believe a move when I see it. The NFL trade deadline is November 10, and the Broncos have one more game until then — a road trip next week to face the Carolina Panthers.

title: Jack Campbell Statement: Has Lower Body Movement, Issues With Upper Body
full_text:
The Detroit Lions and Jack Campbell have released another update regarding his current health status.
Campbell was hospitalized Sunday after a collision in the fourth quarter of the Lions' 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings. After the hit, he remained on the turf while being tended to by the team's medical staff before being carted to the ambulance and taken to the hospital.
Head coach Dan Campbell has spoken multiple times since the injury, noting the duality between the concern he and the team faces regarding Campbell's situation while also taking into account the necessary preparation required for their upcoming game against the Miami Dolphins.
Teammates and fans alike have shown an outpouring of support for their injured teammate, with several players speaking at length about the impact Jack Campbell has both in the locker room as a leader as well as on the field as a player.
The Lions will have to brace for the reality of being without their middle linebacker and defensive on-field play-caller. Campbell, an All-Pro in 2025, handled a hefty responsibility that will not be easily replaceable for coordinator Kelvin Sheppard.
Detroit's linebacker room currently is headlined by a trio of veterans in Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez and Trevor Nowaske. Amen Ogbongbemiga is also a journeyman in his first year with the Lions, while they added KJ Britt off of the New England Patriots' practice squad.
It is shaping up to be a challenging week for Detroit, who also has multiple other key contributors dealing with ailments. Defensive end DJ Wonnum and safety Brian Branch are both in concussion protocol, while D.J. Reed is dealing with a hip injury.
On offense, the Lions could be without center Cade Mays, who suffered an ankle injury in the first half of the Vikings game, as well as running back/kick returner Jacob Saylors (neck).
Detroit is currently 5-2, with back-to-back wins over NFC North opponents heading into Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins. It begins a challenging stretch, as this upcoming game will be followed by a trip to Germany, a home game against the Buccaneers and then a Thanksgiving showdown with the Chicago Bears.
Here is the Campbell statement in full, released by the team on Wednesday afternoon.
"My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we’ve received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express. I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better. My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we’ll get through this. I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. I also can’t say enough about the incredible care I’ve received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They’ve been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I’m truly grateful for everything they’ve done. To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I’m proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn’t ask to be surrounded by a better group of people. One thing I’ve learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That’s exactly how I’m going to approach this challenge. Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can’t thank everyone enough. God is good. My faith is strong."
For more comprehensive Detroit Lions coverage and NFL insider analysis, follow us on X, @detroitpodcast , head on over to our Facebook page and give it a like, follow us on TikTok , subscribe to the Detroit Lions On SI Lone Wolves YouTube Channel for daily videos, news, member-exclusive content.
Sports journalist who has covered the Detroit Lions the past three NFL seasons. Christian brings expert analysis, insights and an ability to fairly assess how the team is performing in a tough NFC North division.

title: Goff, St. Brown, Hutchinson React to Serious Jack Campbell Injury
full_text:
Several key members of the Detroit Lions roster have shared their support, prayers and reaction to linebacker Jack Campbell suffering a serious injury and being carted off the field against the Minnesota Vikings.
Both quarterback Jared Goff and defensive end Aidan Hutchinson have weekly scheduled interviews on 97.1 The Ticket, the Lions flagship station.
"We're doing all right," said Goff on Tuesday, the players day off this week. "There were a lot of injuries that affected a lot of guys' seasons, but certainly the one that's scariest is Jack (Campbell's). The positive updates are great and we know that things are heading in the right direction right now and hoping for the best for him."
Hutchinson indicated the game left him feeling drained, due to all the events surrounding Campbell and other key defenders leaving the game injured.
"After that game, it was just the weirdest feeling, just with Jack and everything. You know, even D.J. (Wonnum) leaving the game on a cart, if I remember correctly. And then with B.B. (Brian Branch). So many things happened, and it was just a lot on my mind after the game," said Hutchinson. "So much stuff happened on defense where it was just a lot to process. A lot of stuff is still up in the air right now. Once we get into tomorrow, into our first- and second-down game plan for Miami, we can kind of really put our focus on that. Definitely, still processing, for sure."
Wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown shared his thoughts on the latest episode of the St. Brown Bros. podcast.
"I don't know any more than anybody else does," said St. Brown. "Obviously, the Lions posted. I just want to say, all you guys that are watching is to keep him in your thoughts and your prayers. You hate to see anyone go down in this game, whether it is someone on our team, someone on their team. Any team in this league. I think injuries is something that makes this game so tough, so real at the same time. I remember being out there on the field watching. Seeing him on the ground from a distance. All I could think about was his wife and his newborn baby that he just had a few months ago. I just want him to be okay to go play with his kid, honestly. And to be normal.
"When things like that happen throughout the game or throughout the season, it does make it hard for us to go back and play. Its like, 'Damn.' We took care of him, put him on a stretcher and sent him out back to the hospital and now we have to play again," St. Brown added. "That kind of sucks. It is what I signed up for. What we signed up for. We get paid a lot of money to play this sport that we love. We have got to finish the game. Injuries like that, it makes you put things in perspective . He has done that for a lot of us on that team. I'm think about Jack. We are all thinking about Jack. I hope he continues to get better and all we can do is pray for him."

title: Pros and Cons of Detroit Lions Trading For Mike Sainristil
full_text:
The Detroit Lions find themselves in dire need of cornerback help at the present moment.
Since day one of the 2026 season, the Lions have needed to strengthen the position. And now with D.J. Reed, Detroit's No. 1 cornerback , going down with a hip injury this past Sunday against Minnesota, the void has only increased.
To add insult to injury, Reed was just hitting his stride. The ninth-year defensive back had morphed into a shutdown corner over the last three games, earning no less than a 78.9 coverage grade from Pro Football Focus for his efforts in each contest.
And he was especially stout in coverage in the Lions’ Week 8 victory over the Vikings, recording an interception and allowing just one completion on five passes thrown his way by QB Kyler Murray. It was an elite-level performance from Reed, and as a result, he earned his best coverage mark (91.3) and overall grade (88.2) from PFF for the season.
Consequently, if the 29-year-old has to miss an extended period of time, it will be a significant blow to Detroit's secondary.
It furthers the reason why Lions general manager Brad Holmes needs to make a concerted effort to land a cornerback prior to the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
With that said, one of the corners he could target is Washington Commanders defensive back Mike Sainristil. He was named by Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer, in his most recent video mailbag, as a defensive back Detroit could pursue.
Sainristil has had a brutal start to the season, highlighted by his league-worst PFF coverage grade (28.5) and overall mark (29.4). Furthermore, he failed to log a single defensive snap for the first time in his career on Sunday against the Eagles.
As a result, he could be had on the cheap right now by Holmes & Co., likely only costing a late-round pick. And fans and pundits alike both know that the sixth-year Lions front-office executive is a big proponent of bargain shopping, and trading for Sainristil would be the definition of that, considering his myriad of struggles so far in 2026.
Plus, he could have some good football still ahead of him and could benefit from a change of scenery, since he's only 26 years old. Additionally, if he could re-find his rookie form (two interceptions, nine passes defensed and a 64.1 PFF coverage grade), it'd make giving up a late-round draft choice for him well worth it.
Still, adding Sainristil, who's in the midst of the worst season of his three-year NFL career, would do little to move the needle for Detroit's defensive backs group. He'd be more of a depth piece than anything for the team's depleted cornerbacks room at this juncture.
Subsequently, even if Holmes were to pull the trigger on a deal involving Sainristil, he'd still definitely need to make another move for a higher-impact corner.

title: Report: Lions Will Ink Former Cardinals, Titans LB To Practice Squad
full_text:
After visiting the Detroit Lions Allen Park Performance Center, a decision was made on former Arizona Cardinals, Tennessee Titans linebacker Owen Pappoe.
According to multiple reports, the 26-year-old will ink a deal to join Detroit's practice squad.
Detroit's linebackers unit was in need of added depth this week after two players went down against the Minnesota Vikings with significant injuries.
Rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder was lost for the remainder of the 2026 season due to a hamstring injury. Captain Jack Campbell is still hospitalized after a frightening neck injury suffered in the second half of a 19-15 Week 8 victory against a division rival.
According to an Athletic scouting report , "The Tigers’ two-year captain ran the fastest combine 40 (4.39) among the linebackers. The 6-foot, 225-pounder isn’t particularly big, but was an effective leader/communicator in the middle of the Auburn defense who should benefit as a run-and-chase, weakside linebacker at the next level. Pappoe had a pair of 90-tackle seasons at Auburn."
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: Grading Week 8 Victory Against Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field
Head coach Dan Campbell was asked earlier this week how the coaching staff plans to prepare, if Campbell is out for the foreseeable future.
“Well, luckily we have some depth in there with (Malcolm Rodriguez) Rodrigo and (Trevor) Nowaske and (Derrick) Barnes. Those three guys and (Lions LB) Amen (Ogbongbemiga)’s been up for us, which is good," said the sixth-year NFL head man. "And then we have got (Joe) Bachie ready to roll.
"So, we may need a little bit of help. We're looking at everything. We'll adjust as we go. (Lions Executive Vice President and General Manager) Brad (Holmes) and I will get together here this afternoon, tomorrow and figure some of this out.”
The roster has been regularly updated regarding Campbell's current health status.
“Well, I think we acknowledge it, right? I mean, it's not going away," said Campbell. "That is what it is and it's important. And he's important to us and that he's okay is important. And so we acknowledge that, we talk about it and at the same time we get ready for this next opponent. So, I think you kind of do a little bit of both, honestly.”

title: Lions Week 8 Snap Counts Reveal Secret to Countering Vikings Defense
full_text:
Injuries forced the Detroit Lions to adjust with regards to their snap count distribution Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings.
Several players suffered injuries that forced them to exit the game, including Cade Mays, Jack Campbell, D.J. Reed, D.J. Wonnum and Brian Branch. As a result, the Lions could rely on their depth to get through what could wind up being some lengthy absences.
Campbell had a positive update from head coach Dan Campbell on Monday, while Rolder is expected to miss the rest of the season with a hamstring injury.
Notably, the Lions' cornerback rotation essentially excluded Ennis Rakestraw, who played one defensive snap after playing 21 last week, and Trevor Nowaske stepped up in place of Campbell after he exited.
Additionally, the Lions found creative ways to counter the Vikings' blitz-heavy defense. They used several personnel packages featuring two or three tight ends, as backups Brock Wright and Tyler Conklin both played season-highs in snaps.
Conklin  had played just 30 offensive snaps all season prior to Sunday, and he nearly had that many in Sunday's game with 22. Wright also had a significant increase, as he played 55 snaps which cleared his previous season-high of 44.
By adding this muscle to their offense, Detroit was able to counteract the blitzes with extra blockers. Additionally, they used these tight ends as extra assets in the run game , which allowed the Lions to run for 230 yards in Sunday's game.
Here's a look at the Lions' snap counts from their Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings.

title: Lions Create Two Roster Spots After Cutting DB, Placing LB on IR
full_text:

The former fourth-round pick suffered a hamstring injury in the second half against the Minnesota Vikings, ending his rookie season.
Detroit could look to Malcolm Rodriguez, Trevor Nowaske, Derrick Barnes and Amen Ogbongbemiga to steady the ship, given the absence of Rolder and Jack Campbell.
Bishop Fitzgerald was not able to find a path to see the field, given the return of Brian Branch and the likely return of Thomas Harper soon.
Rookie Keith Abney and vetran safeties Chuck Clark have been able to manage the back end, with Branch having departed the Vikings game with a head injury.
Kerby Joseph is practicing, but his return is not imminent, as head coach Dan Campbell expressed during his weekly radio interview he would not be suiting up against the Dolphins on the road.

One of the remaining roster spots is set to be filled by K.J. Britt, who is set to sign with the NFC North squad, after a stint on the practice squad of the New England Patroits.

title: Lions Give Further Jack Campbell Update, Avoid What We Want to Hear
full_text:
Another update regarding the status of Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell has been revealed.
Lions coach Dan Campbell, appearing on 97.1 The Ticket, discussed the former first-round draft pick, who was carted off the field in the second half against the Minnesota Vikings.
He noted that he has tried to keep the team focused on their upcoming game against the Dolphins while updating them on Campbell's status as opportunities to do so arise. His concern is that the team will need to be focused on the opponent to play at their best.
"It's not easy because he's always going to be on our minds over here. The good news is he is improving, but we also, we've got a job to do, and this is what we're tasked with and there's a reason why we go through all this stuff," Campbell told 97.1 The Ticket Tuesday. "It's to get to where we wanna go collectively as a team, and adversity comes in all shapes and sizes and we've got to overcome everything that comes our way."
Campbell suffered the injury Sunday in the team's 19-15 win attempting to make a tackle in the fourth quarter. There was a collision, and Campbell remained motionless on the turf for several minutes before being strapped to a backboard and carted off the field.
The linebacker was taken to a local hospital, where he has remained while undergoing evaluation from medical professionals.
A first-round pick of the Lions in 2023, Campbell has become a centerpiece of the team's defense. After showing growth as a rookie, Campbell has been a starter in every game since his second season in the league.
The head coach knows his teammates will be worried about Campbell's status, and while he is willing to provide updates, he knows that he also must prepare them for their game against the Dolphins.
"I think that helps everybody just get a better handle on all this and once you know that, then you've got to move on for yourself, too, in that moment," Dan Campbell said. "If you let things wonder and you drift and you worry a little, then you're trying to play or prepare, that's when bad things can happen to you because you're not all in on what you need to be doing. That's why it's important that you get back to your own business. All we can do at this point is just continue to pray for Jack, put our thoughts on him when we have a minute and his family, and it's working, like I said, because he is improving."
His growth hit a big jump in his third campaign, last year, as he earned All-Pro honors after setting a career-high in numerous categories including tackles, sacks and tackles for loss. Ahead of the start of the 2026 season, he inked a four-year, $81 million contract extension that is set to go into effect next season.
In his fourth season, Campbell has yet to miss a game for Detroit. He made 12 starts in 17 appearances as a rookie, and has started every game since. As a result, Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins will be the first game he's missed in his entire career.
Campbell has logged 459 combined tackles in his career, with 20 tackles for loss, 8.5 sacks, four forced fumbles and three fumble recoveries.
The Lions have further injury issues to navigate ahead of their Week 9 game with Miami. Fellow linebacker Jimmy Rolder is expected to be done for the season, while safety Brian Branch and defensive end DJ Wonnum are both in concussion protocol.
Detroit has already taken measures to address their depleted linebacker room, signing veteran K.J. Britt off of the New England Patriots' practice squad on Monday. Interestingly, the Lions will take on the Patriots on Nov. 15 in Munich, Germany.
General manager Brad Holmes could also look to seek depth for the linebacker position before the NFL trade deadline, which is slated for 6 p.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 10.

title: Lions Can Be Serious Contenders If They Make Key Defensive Additions
full_text:
The Detroit Lions notched arguably their biggest win of the season on Sunday, defeating the previously unbeaten Minnesota Vikings.
And for a second straight week, they proved they don't have to be perfect on either offense or defense in order to emerge victorious.
Quite notably, offensive coordinator Drew Petzing's unit was not clicking on all cylinders in the NFC North divisional tilt. The offensive line struggled mightily in the first half to protect Jared Goff, surrendering four sacks to Brian Flores’ blitz-happy defense. Goff proceeded to throw his first interception of the season, and threw for a season-low 176 yards.
Plain and simple, Detroit was stymied by Minnesota's No. 1-ranked defense in the opening half, and entered halftime with just six points.
Petzing & Co. learned the hard way that they weren't going to beat the Vikings through the air. Subsequently, they adjusted in the second half and got back to being physical, placing a heavy emphasis on the ground and pound.
And the Lions’ run game answered the bell. Spearheaded by do-it-all back Jahmyr Gibbs, the team's backfield produced a sensational performance in the final half of play.
Gibbs put Dan Campbell's squad on his back, compiling big run after big run en route to amassing 116 yards, including a 30-yard TD run, in the final two quarters.
Additionally, in a positive development, the superstar runner's production was supplemented by that of third-year back Sione Vaki.
Vaki, a fourth-round pick of the Lions in 2024, had a career-best day, rushing for 65 yards on 11 carries. He also recorded runs of 12 yards and 10 yards on back-to-back rushing attempts in the fourth quarter, fighting for extra yards on both carries. In doing so, he, along with Gibbs, helped put the Lions in position for their game-winning score: a 7-yard TD pass from Goff to Jameson Williams.
Vaki spelled Gibbs in a big way Sunday, providing Detroit with a much-needed change-of-pace back. And if he's able to sustain that level of production in future weeks, he most certainly will continue to have a significant role in the Lions’ backfield.
“Vaki was one of the guys we challenged this week going into this game," Campbell told reporters after the game. "We were going to need him. He needed to show up. He was going to need to get some carries for us, some significant carries.
"They needed to be real yards, and he was going to need to be able to pass protect for us. And I thought he took a big step today. That's a huge step. He gained a lot of trust today, a ton.”
Altogether, it was a gritty performance by Vaki & Co. in the Week 8 contest. And with the win, Detroit proved that it belongs on the same field as yet another NFC North contender .
Unfortunately, the victory did come at a major cost for the Lions on the injury front, though. Detroit lost five total defensive players – along with center Cade Mays and running back/kick returner Jacob Saylors – in the divisional matchup.
Among the defensive injuries, the Lions lost rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder, EDGE rusher DJ Wonnum, two core members of their secondary – safety Brian Branch and cornerback D.J. Reed – and linebacker Jack Campbell.
Campbell, the team's defensive captain, suffered a gruesome injury on the opening play of the fourth quarter. He fell straight to the Ford Field turf on a tackle attempt of Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson, and laid motionless on the field for several minutes following the injury. He then needed the assistance of multiple medical staff personnel prior to being placed on a stretcher and carted off the field.
Per the Lions, the fourth-year linebacker was eventually transported to a local hospital, where he remained overnight for continued evaluation for a neck injury.
There is no timetable for the return of any of the aforementioned players, especially Campbell. And it furthers the reason why Detroit GM Brad Holmes needs to strike a deal – or two now – to upgrade the team's defense leading into the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
Particularly, he needs to make a concerted effort to grab a corner who can complement the production of Reed, who has played much better in recent weeks. Along with that, it wouldn't hurt for Holmes to add a safety, considering the unknown future health of Branch and uncertain capability of Kerby Joseph upon his return.
Plus, Holmes & Co. now have a sizable void to fill at linebacker with Campbell likely out for the foreseeable future.
Just take a look at the Chicago Bears. The addition of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons has paid immediate dividends, as Ben Johnson's squad are among the top seeds in the NFC and Super Bowl contenders.
The situation has become dire for the Lions’ defense, and Holmes cannot afford to wait until the deadline to pull the trigger. If a trade presents itself in the next day or two for Budda Baker or Riq Woolen or an impact linebacker, Holmes needs to act immediately.
The longer he waits, the greater the likelihood he misses out on landing a difference-making talent who can take Kelvin Sheppard's defense to the next level.
Simply, Holmes cannot allow that to happen. And if he does, you can almost certainly kiss goodbye Detroit's Super Bowl hopes for 2026.
