title: Three Linebackers Lions Could Trade For After Recent Injuries
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will have to navigate some injuries at the linebacker position.
Both Jack Campbell and Jimmy Rolder suffered significant injuries , which saps the team of its depth at the position. Rolder will miss the rest of the season, while Campbell's injury has had fewer updates as fans outpour their support after the scary moment that led to his exit from Sunday's game.
With the stretch run approaching and the NFL trade deadline one week from Tuesday, general manager Brad Holmes and company could see fit to add talent through a trade to the linebacker room.
Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez and Trevor Nowaske all have starting experience and will be looked at to contribute, but Amen Ogbongbemiga is the only other healthy option currently on the active roster. It should be noted that Detroit could also elevate veteran Joe Bachie to the active roster, as Bachie began the year on the active roster before being released and re-signed on the practice squad.
Here are three possible trade targets the Lions could look to add at the linebacker position.
Henley was an intriguing player coming out of the draft in 2023, and is now entering the final year of his rookie deal. A rangy athlete, Henley is a weakside linebacker who could help some of the Lions' issues in coverage.
He has three career interceptions, and has also flashed some pass-rush potential with five career sacks. With the Chargers now sitting at 0-7, Henley could be expendable as the team evaluates whether or not to extend him.
For Detroit , Henley fits an ideal mold and would give them another athletic option within their linebacking corps.
Gay is a veteran option who is in his second year with the Miami Dolphins. He has traditionally played at the Will linebacker spot. He has been a reliable tackler up to this point, with a miniscule 8.7 missed tackle rate through his first six games.
The Lions could get an up-close look at the linebacker this week, as the Lions are set to travel to Miami to take on the Dolphins on Sunday. Miami is currently 1-6 under first-year coach Jeff Hafley, and Gay could be a player who nets them some valuable draft capital.
Like the previous two names, Barton is currently a leader on a struggling AFC team. The veteran is on his fourth NFL team in eight seasons, and has had at least 80 combined tackles in each of the last four campaigns.
Barton is another middle linebacker option, and has had a missed tackle rate under 10 percent in each of his NFL seasons. This year, the number is currently a touch higher at 10.8 percent through eight games, but solid performances would likely get that number back below double digits.
The Lions could use another veteran option amidst their linebacking corps after the injuries, and Barton fits that mold. He's another affordable option, and still has one year of control beyond this year.

title: With Micah Parsons Returning to Practice, Today Could Change Everything for Packers
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers didn’t exactly thrive without Micah Parsons but they certainly survived with their 5-3 record.
Parsons is expected to practice for the first time on Wednesday following last year’s torn ACL. He won’t play on Sunday against the Patriots and probably won’t play the following week against the Vikings, but he’ll be available for the stretch run.
Acknowledging that “everything around here (is) pretty fluid,” coach Matt LaFleur said: “If I had a bet on it, it’s going to be more towards the longer end than the shorter end.”
Only time will tell if Parsons will be Peak Parsons upon his return, but he will provide a jolt to a defense that defied expectations during the first half of the season.
Defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said he thinks “every day” about how he will incorporate Parsons.
His unit has been surprisingly good without him. The Packers emerged from Week 8 ranked 10th with 20.5 points allowed per game, a number skewed by the Week 1 avalanche at Minnesota stemming from the offense’s late-game implosion, and the one bad game at Atlanta in Week 3.
They are 10th in total defense (314.9 yards allowed per game), 13th in yards allowed per rushing play (3.89) and third in yards allowed per passing play (5.75). They are second with 15 takeaways – they had 14 all of last season – and 12th in sack percentage.
The sack production – and the impact it’s had on the pass defense in general – is the shocker. They are tied for sixth with 22 sacks even without a single player in the top 15 in sacks and only one (Lukas Van Ness) in the top 44.
For the Packers, it’s been a strength-in-numbers approach. With Gannon deploying his rushers from here, there and everywhere, they have an NFL-high 11 players with at least one full sack.
“Wins and losses are the only stat I’m worried about,” Gannon said, “but, yeah, I think our guys have done a good job of taking the coaching and affecting the game in a positive way, executing the game plan as much as we can and we got some guys winning at a pretty good rate of one-on-ones right now. It’s about the players.”
That’s good deflection from Gannon. Statistically, his defense has been slightly better without Parsons than it was with Parsons under Jeff Hafley. Last year, the Packers finished 11th in points allowed (21.2) and 12th in total defense (311.8 yards per game). Even with Parsons having an All-Pro season, they wound up 22nd in sack percentage and tied for 26th in takeaways.
After Thursday’s victory over Carolina, Packers coach Matt LaFleur called Gannon a “savant.”
“I wouldn’t use that word because I’m not,” Gannon said on Tuesday.
But the proof is in the pudding. Without Parsons, who is his best player, and linebacker Edgerrin Cooper, who is his second-best player, the Packers are on a five-game streak of not allowing more than 20 points.
The defense is in the top 10 in numerous categories. One of them is “havoc plays,” a TruMedia stat that combines sacks, tackles or losses, forced fumbles, interception and pass breakups. Green Bay is second with 107. It’s ninth in explosive plays allowed (12-yard runs and 16-yard passes), first in stuffs (a running play that gains 0 yards or less) and fourth in opponent passer rating.
“When we went through Phase 1, Phase 2, then we went from OTAs and then we took the summer off, kind of adapted,” Gannon said. “‘Here’s some things we want to add.’ Then we went through training camp and added a few things, took out a few things that I always thought, ‘Oh this is going to be good,’ and our guys, for whatever reason, it wasn’t really good for us. (So), take it out.
“Then I think week to week, they’ve done a good job of executing staples that we have and then taking a couple different things, the different wrinkles – the wrinkles are only in because of the opponent you’re going against or who you have available – they’ve done a good job of taking the wrinkles, curveballs so to speak, and executing on that. And they understand the why behind why we’re doing it and those typically change week-to-week.”
To one of the NFL’s surprisingly strong defenses, the Packers will be adding one of its most dominating defenders. He is the only player in NFL history to start his career with five consecutive seasons of 12-plus sacks. That streak presumably will end this year. If he returns for Thanksgiving Eve against the Rams, he’d have seven games.
Still, while offensive coordinators and quarterbacks are losing sleep over who Gannon is blitzing from where, they probably aren’t especially fearful of Lukas Van Ness, who leads the team with 4.5 sacks. The entire edge group has 9.5 sacks; Parsons had 10.5 sacks in a seven-game span last year.
There’s also a bit of an elephant in the room. Of the top-10 teams in scoring, the Packers have played four. The Lions, who are third in the NFL in scoring, scored only 20 points, though they had more than 400 yards and two freakish turnovers. The Bears are eighth in scoring but played a backup quarterback. The Panthers are ninth in scoring but played without three-fifths of their starting line.
The one game in which there’s no asterisk was against Dallas. The Cowboys are seventh in scoring but managed only 13 points.
More challenges are coming. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye almost won NFL MVP last year. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford did win MVP last year. Bills quarterback Josh Allen is the MVP front-runner this year. There are rematches looming against the Bears and Lions.
The Packers have survived without Parsons. Now, they’ve got a chance to thrive with a difference-making player who has the potential of making a greater impact than any player available at the trade deadline.
The Packers were 9-3-1 last season headed into the Denver game during which he was injured. Without him for the stretch run, the Packers crumbled.
This year, Parsons will be on the field for the stretch run with the goal of making opponents pay for his pain.
“I think when you come out of these situations, you’re either going to be better or you’re worse,” Parsons said during training camp. “And for me, I’ve done everything I possibly can to be better. So, I think people are worried about if I come back. You know, I just feel like people should just be worried about how I’m going to be when I come back. You know? That’s kind of like my mentality – how I feel, and how I’m going to approach when I’m back.
“Like, people are worried about the knee. They should be worried about how I’m going to play when I get back. The anger, the frustration, the things that I’m going to have to let out because of how long it’s been since I played. So, I think that’s what people should really worry about. Like, how great is Micah going to be when he gets back? Not about when I get back, because that’s the short term. It’s about how great I’m going to be, how I can help my teammates, and how far we’re going to go into a playoff run.”

title: New Packers Safety John Saunders Jr., Who Has NFL Cousin, Had to Learn How to Practice
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Among a wave of moves on the practice squad, the Green Bay Packers signed promising safety John Saunders Jr.
Saunders is the cousin of Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker – more on that later. He played three seasons at Miami (Ohio) before closing his college career at Ole Miss in 2023 and 2024. He had three interceptions in both seasons, giving him 11 for his college career, and led the SEC with four forced fumbles in 2024.
“He’s amazing. He knows all 11 positions on defense,” Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said . “He could coach me and a second later he is coaching a defensive tackle. He is so versatile and knows where everyone is supposed to be. He coaches my technique a lot and pushes me to become a better player every day.”
Despite a strong combination of size (6-foot-2 3/8) and athleticism (4.57 in the 40), Saunders went undrafted in 2025. He signed with the Dolphins, failed to make their roster during training camp and spent the first two months of the season on their practice squad before being poached by the Patriots. In three games on their roster, he did not play in a game. He was released and spent the rest of last season on their practice squad.
This year, he competed with the Patriots during training camp but didn’t earn a roster spot despite a big-time preseason of 13 tackles, one interception, one forced fumble and two passes defensed.
Saunders also led the team in interceptions on the practice field.
“He’s been balling out of control. He’s a ballhawk,” safety Kevin Byard said at the time.
After his release from the Patriots, he served practice-squad stints with the Jets and Browns, meaning the Packers will be his fourth team this year.
When Saunders joined the Patriots’ practice squad last season, he wasn’t practicing to coach Mike Vrable’s standard.
“John showed up, and we just asked him to practice a little better and use practice," Vrabel said during training camp . “We talked about those days where we're letting the show team go and letting them try to really improve throughout the season. When John was back, we just said, ‘Hey, you have to practice better. You have to have better practice habits. That's the only place you're going to get your reps.’
“And it got to the point where we had to dial him back where he was blitzing or tackling, and I was like, ‘This is great.’ And I think he used those examples in practice to improve, and mentally he's kept working, and it's been great to see him show up and get into that competition.”
So, Saunders started practicing harder. Too hard, as it turns out, so he had to dial it back.
“In practice, it’s about taking care of the team. So that’s something I really had to learn, like practicing like a pro,” he said.
To create a spot on the practice squad, the Packers released safety Kahlef Hailassie.
Saunders was among three additions to the practice squad who will be on the field on Wednesday.
With quarterback Kedon Slovis signing to the Ravens’ 53-man roster, the Packers signed Cam Miller , who was drafted by the Raiders in 2025 and got this incredible endorsement from possibly the greatest quarterback of all-time.
The Packers also signed D.J. Johnson , third-round pick by Carolina in 2023. While he played on both sides of the ball at Oregon, he will work on the edge for Green Bay.
Saunders can turn to a veteran NFL starter for advice. Jaquan Brisker spent his first four seasons with the Bears before signing with the Steelers in free agency. He’s started all eight games this season.
“It’s been amazing, honestly. Growing up, he was from the east side of Pittsburgh and I moved to North Carolina, so we didn’t really talk that much,” Saunders told On3’s Andy Staples in 2023. “But then once we got back in contact, it’s just been amazing man. Like, I just talked to him yesterday. He’s just telling me to just make sure to stay focused.
“When I first got to college, one of the things he told me was to listen to the coaches. And most players in college think they know it all. But I’ve been making sure that everywhere I go — because the coaches are extremely knowledgeable. They know their stuff. That was one of the main things he told me and that just stuck with me ever since. It sounds so simple to just listen to your coaches, but when you actually do it and apply what your coaches are telling you — it’s been great. I’m really appreciative of him, too.”
Saunders was impressed by the Patriots’ Super Bowl pedigree. So, this quote probably holds up now that he’s joined by the Packers.
“The main thing I remember is when you walk in the player entrance, you’ve got all the Super Bowls right there,” Saunders said. “Then, outside the doors, all the Super Bowl titles. This is football tradition. Serious, rich tradition. Winners. This is the winningest team since I’ve been born. Being a part of this is a blessing. Just excited to help continue this legacy.”

title: Packers Add Former Third-Round Pick Who Played Both Sides of Ball to Edge Room
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers signed D.J. Johnson, a third-round pick by the Panthers in 2023, to their practice squad, a source told Packers On SI.
Johnson was among five players who worked out for the team; the Packers opted to sign the former top-100 draft pick with some starting experience.
Johnson had six sacks and 8.5 tackles for losses as a sixth-year senior at Oregon. He had a huge Scouting Combine, where he measured 6-foot-4 and 260 pounds and ran his 40 in 4.49 seconds.
DJ Johnson is a LB prospect in the 2023 draft class. He scored a 8.32 RAS out of a possible 10.00. This ranked 414 out of 2465 LB from 1987 to 2023. https://t.co/QDFPqcGcCh #RAS pic.twitter.com/WFxDEOPN78
“Power merchant with jarring initial hand strikes that can create early advantages,” was the start of Lance Zeirlein’s scouting report at NFL.com . “Johnson is big, explosive and rugged but lacking the experience and technique to consistently capitalize on his physicality.
“He has broad, tight hips that make it challenging to keep the pad level where it needs to be as a rusher, tackler and while taking on run blocks. He has very few moves or counters, but his bull rush can put opponents on skates. There is significant technique work that needs to take place, but his NFL Scouting Combine testing should only help his draft stock.”
Johnson even played a little tight end at Oregon. He switched sides of the ball for the 2020 season and finished with 10 catches for 113 yards and three touchdowns. At the time, linebacker Troy Dye called Johnson a “freak of nature” because of his size and athleticism.
After not playing a single snap on defense that season, he played on both sides of the ball in 2021 and then focused on defense in 2022 and finished with an excellent final season.
He will play on the edge for the Packers.
“It was definitely a nice thing to play in that position,” Johnson said after being drafted. “Allowed me to gain experience in doing stuff like that, where previously I might not have been able to do that primarily just playing defense. Being able to have experience on offense and defense, both physically and mentally. Being able to take the offensive and defensive play book at the same time definitely has prepared me for where I'm at now.”
For the Panthers, Johnson played in 13 games with three starts as a rookie and 14 games with two starts in 2024, when he had the only sack production (one-half sack) of his career but recorded 44 tackles. He was released after four games in 2025 and hasn’t played in a game since.
“I definitely feel like my best football is ahead of me,” he said after the Panthers traded up to draft him. “I have always taken a lot of steps from the end of the season to now to prepare and get better. I have been watching a lot of film from last year. Fixing little technique things, bad eye things. Then working on things like polishing your pass rush of your striking in the get-off.”
This year, he spent training camp with the Commanders but failed to make their 53-man roster. He spent the first two weeks of the season on their practice squad.
Johnson is from the same draft class from which the Packers drafted Lukas Van Ness in the first round. He was selected at No. 80 overall, two picks after Green Bay landed Tucker Kraft.
“There was a run of pass rushers that went,” then-Panthers GM Scott Fitterer said at the time. “We were aggressive. You never want to force need, but this is a 6-4 260-pound guy that ran 4.4. He's got rare traits. And with our staff and the conviction that EJ [Eviro Evero] and Dom [Capers], and our coaching staff had with him, the way our scouts felt about him, there's a ton of development with him.
“His upside is huge. Once he settles in and gets the coaching, this guy can be a force off the edge. I think his best ball is in front of him.”
At Oregon, a teammate called Johnson the player he’d least like to fight.
“I think it's a mutual respect thing,” he said at the Scouting Combine. “It's also a testament to my work. They see how much work I put in, the numbers I put up lifting and running. To see someone my size that athletic, that fast, that strong, you maybe want to stay clear of him.”
He said Khalil Mack and Myles Garrett were his favorite players to watch.
“I love the way they attack guys in one-on-one situations,” he said. “I've seen Khalil Mack beat three guys and still get the sack. When you watch guys like that giving that much effort, you have to unload. You have no other option.”
Johnson’s brother, P.J., a nose tackle, was drafted by the Lions in 2019.
“He’s a quiet and reserved person,” P.J. told The Athletic . “He’s a hard worker, but if you ask him about himself, he’ll tell you that he’s the best. Even when stuff isn’t going his way, he thinks he’s the best because he works for it. He knows he’s going to outwork everybody.”

title: Packers-Patriots Matchups: One ‘Knockout’ Advantage for New England
full_text:
The Green Bay Packers are heading on the road after a mini-bye following their 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers. On Sunday, they’ll be taking on the New England Patriots, last year’s representative in the Super Bowl for the AFC. The Patriots are banged up but coming off a win over Jeff Hafley’s Miami Dolphins.
Both teams need a win to keep pace in a division that is either incredibly competitive in Green Bay’s case or the home of one of the dominant teams in the conference in New England’s case.
Who has the advantage? Let’s dive in.
The Patriots’ pass catching corps was a pressure point for them coming out of last season, so they addressed it in the offseason.
The problem? Their two biggest acquisitions have been out of the lineup. A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs have battled injuries this season. Doubs is on injured reserve and will miss Sunday’s game. Brown has been working through lower-body injuries all season and missed Sunday’s game against Miami with a knee issue. An elite player when healthy and dialed in, he has nine catches in three games.
Moreover, tight end Hunter Henry, who leads the team with 29 catches, was knocked out of the game with a foot injury.
What’s holding them all together is the play of quarterback Drake Maye. He’s been asked to make chicken salad over the last few weeks, and the numbers reflect it. He’s thrown 15 touchdowns to eight interceptions and has been sacked 16 times. He’s third in the league in yards per attempt, sixth in yards and fifth in touchdowns but has thrown the fourth-most interceptions.
“We got to do a good job of trying to contain him the best you can, because a lot of their explosive plays are when he gets loose in the pocket and can get out,” Packers coach Matt LaFleur said. “And he’s got a big-time arm. He’s really athletic. He’s a really good young quarterback in this league.”
Conversely, the Packers are coming off a good performance against Carolina in which they had six sacks from six different players. Their pass rush looked as good as it has all season and may see an opportunity to tee off on Maye if the Patriots are missing their top pass catchers.
With the way Green Bay’s defense is playing, the Patriots could find it difficult to gain much going through the air.
The Patriots’ ground game has been up-and-down through the first eight games. They have three players with more than 200 rushing yards, including quarterback Drake Maye.
Their leading rusher is Rhamondre Stevenson, who has a punishing running style. He’s only averaging 45.9 yards per game, which is the highest on the team, though he had a season-high 82 yards against the Dolphins even with a long run of just 9 yards.
Nobody has really gained much traction as the Patriots’ lead runner. While last year’s second-round pick, Treyveon Henderson, has only 203 rushing yards in six games, the committee approach has worked, as the Patriots are still a top-12 rushing team. Some of that is pumped up by Maye’s ability to move around, but it all has to be accounted for by Jonathan Gannon and Co.
Green Bay’s defense is ranked 15th in the NFL, allowing 110.9 rushing yards per game. Realistically, they’ve only had one bad game against an opposing run game, when Atlanta’s Bijan Robinson ran wild against them in Week 3.
This matchup is close. It could change based on who is available in the passing game for the Patriots. If Brown and Henry are sidelined, the Packers can realistically commit more resources to stopping the run, which would make things more difficult for the Patriots.
The Packers have certainly obliged. Through eight weeks, he leads the league in pass attempts and passing yards. (He’s third in passing yards per game.) Of course, some of that is a byproduct of the team having a putrid run game, so everything has fallen on Love’s shoulders.
Christian Watson is coming off a dynamic performance straight out of a WWE script by leaving the game in an ambulance before returning to action after being medically cleared. Matthew Golden scored another touchdown but also added two more drops to his league-leading total . Combined, they have six 100-yard games and 10 touchdowns and are on pace for 2,819 receiving yards.
Tucker Kraft started to look more like himself the further removed he is from the knee injury that knocked him out for the rest of the 2025 season. Those three men are being asked to carry Green Bay’s passing game, which could get interesting on Sunday.
New England boasts one of the premier cornerbacks in football with Christian Gonzalez. For all the hoopla about the Packers passing on Jaxon Smith-Njigba with the pick they used to take Lukas Van Ness, Gonzalez was also available and has grown into a premier player. Gonzalez struggled earlier in the year with a shoulder injury, but is back in the lineup and should see plenty of both Watson and Golden.
He has not allowed a touchdown catch since 2024, according to PFF.
Up front, the Patriots have a group of talented players. Elijah Ponder is their team leader in sacks with six. He also has eight TFLs, one forced fumble and two fumble recoveries. Gabe Jacas has been a find for the Patriots on the edge as a second-round pick, as he already has three sacks and six TFLs. On the interior, Christian Barmore and Milton Williams are disruptive forces that should give the Packers’ interior plenty to work around.
If the Packers have time for Love to throw, there should be some open areas to work with. This will be a good test for them, however, as the Patriots rank 13th in passing yards allowed per game and fifth in sack percentage.
Defensively, the Patriots are sixth in rushing yards allowed per game and 10th in yards allowed per carry. Offensively, the Packers might as well be ranked 33rd in a 32-team league.
The run game has not gotten any better for Green Bay with the return of Josh Jacobs. He scored a rushing touchdown on Thursday that he probably is the only one on the roster capable of doing, but overall the results have been poor.
The Packers have faced two of the worst run defenses in the NFL and yet incredibly have the worst rushing attack in NFL history. Here's a closer look ... if you dare. ⬇️ https://t.co/IaIJH9Yxrt
Can the Packers continue to survive this way by being one-dimensional as soon as the game starts? That feels like it would be unsustainable, to say the very least.
“Frustrated, yes, but not discouraged,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said on Tuesday.
The second half is where the lack of a ground game can start to rear its ugly head. The Packers led 27-10 against the Panthers, but ultimately had to outlast them 27-19. Love cooled off after starting the game 17-of-20 passing, and the Packers could not rely on anything other than his right arm to gain yards.
That’s a long-winded way to say this matchup belongs to the Patriots by total knockout.
The Packers have a problem at kicker. Trey Smack leads the league with eight missed kicks after adding another to his total with a missed extra point after Green Bay’s first touchdown of the game.
The Packers are coming off one of their worst special teams games in terms of catastrophic mistakes. Smack missed a PAT, and Coleman Owen, who is filling in for the injured Skyy Moore, fumbled the opening kickoff to give away Green Bay’s first possession of the game. They were able to weather the storm of those two mistakes, but the Patriots are a much better team than the Panthers.
The Patriots have some issues in the kicking game, as well.
Andy Borregailes has missed three field goals and one extra point. He’s only made one kick from beyond 50 yards this year, which could affect how the coaches play the game strategically. In coverage, the Patriots are a well-coached group all around, with Mike Vrabel leading the charge as the head coach.

title: Week 9 Consensus NFL Power Rankings: Packers Have ‘Chance to Soar’
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers beat the Carolina Panthers on Thursday night but didn’t soar in our Week 9 Consensus NFL Power Rankings.
The Packers did move up from 15th to 13th in this week’s Consensus Power Rankings, which take eight of the best national power rankings and turn them into one better-than-the-best power ranking. Being the No. 1 team gets one point, the No. 2 team gets two points and so on.
With Micah Parsons set to return to practice this week, the Packers could be soaring soon. More on that as we dive into each of the individual rankings below.
The Packers moved up two spots in the rankings from Conor Orr, who offered a note on Green Bay , Josh Jacobs and NFL teams “backsliding on morality.”
The Packers moved up one place in Pete Prisco’s rankings, one spot behind this week’s opponent, the Patriots.
“With Jordan Love and a much-improved defense, they have a chance to really soar when Micah Parsons gets back. He's practicing this week. Do they make a deal for a back?”
The Packers climbed two spots in Nick Shook’s rankings, with Jonathan Gannon’s defense “becoming a monster” after handling the potent Panthers on Thursday.
“Matthew Golden is quickly becoming a legitimate difference-making receiver for an offense that still can’t run the ball consistently,” he wrote, “fortunately, the latter detail hasn’t prevented the Packers from stacking wins. They feel like they’re a level or two from becoming their best version, but Micah Parsons’ anticipated return might help in that department.”
The Packers are up two spots in the rankings selected by Josh Kendall and Chad Graff. This week’s theme is reality check, and they honed in on the simple one.
“Jordan Love and the defense have been great, but Josh Jacobs’ return has not fixed the run game, and it’s going to be a problem moving forward. Jacobs averaged 1.9 yards per carry on 21 carries against Carolina, and Green Bay is 31st in the league in rushing success rate (31.5 percent).”
The Packers inched up one spot in the rankings selected by the team beat writers. This week’s theme, with the trade deadline approaching, is the best trade acquisition of all-time. Rob Demovsky picked the trade that sent cornerback Mike McKenzie to the Saints for a second-round pick used on Nick Collins.
Demovsky also provided a history lesson: “When it comes to in-season trades, the Packers might be known for one of the worst ones of all time: giving up two first-round picks, two second-round picks and a third-rounder to get quarterback John Hadl from the Rams in 1974.”
The Packers are up one spot in Frank Schwab’s rankings. With the trade deadline approaching, he said running back is the biggest need.
“The Packers are one of a few teams in need of a running back and it's a different situation than the rest. If Josh Jacobs was a sure thing the rest of the season, the Packers might concentrate on more offensive line help or simply hold tight, knowing Micah Parsons is on the way soon.”
The Packers held steady in Mike Florio’s rankings. The running game “remains a liability,” he said.
The Packers remained at No. 15 in Ralph Vacchiano’s rankings. They’d be in a much better spot in the NFC North if they could run the ball “even a little,” he said.
“The Packers really can’t run the ball, and that’s going to be a problem for them, unless they ditch RB Josh Jacobs (as they should) and trade for Jonathan Taylor. But they showed in their Week 8 win over the Panthers that all the other elements are in place. QB Jordan Love is playing at an elite level. He has strong receivers. The defense is playing well, and they’re about to get pass-rusher Micah Parsons back. And Matt LaFleur is a pretty good coach.”
The New England Patriots will host the Packers on Sunday afternoon. The Patriots are 11th in the Consensus, with their individual rankings ranging from 10th to 14th.
The Patriots are No. 10 at Fox, with Vacchiano noting the Patriots got off to an “ugly start” before beating the Dolphins. Their injury report this week will be critical.
“They were playing without their top two receivers and one of their two best running backs, so it probably was never going to be easy,” he wrote. “With the Packers and the Lions coming up before the bye week, they better get healthy soon. It would really help if they could get No. 1 WR A.J. Brown back since they’ll need a lot more out of Drake Maye and the passing game to beat either of their next two opponents.”
Sportsbook odds aren’t used in our rankings, but they do provide an additional perspective on the state of the league. In Packers-related odds at FanDuel Sportsbook :
The Packers, who were +2000 to win the Super Bowl before Week 1, plunged to as low as +6000 following their slow start to the season. They rebounded to +3000 during their winning streak, fell to +3500 after losing to Detroit but are back to +2700 after beating Carolina. That is 13th on the board.
Among NFC North teams, the Bears made a big move from +1400 to +800. The Lions are +1600 and the Vikings are just ahead of the Packers at +2500 after their first loss.
Green Bay opened the season ranked seventh in the NFC playoff odds at -112 but fell to as low as 12th at +250 after the win at Tampa Bay. Now, they’re back to -110. That’s seventh in the NFC though still last in the division. It was a big shakeup this week, with the Bears at -800, the Lions at -350 and the Vikings at -310. Last week, Minnesota was -520, Detroit was -270, Chicago was -255 and Green Bay was +126.
Quarterback Jordan Love’s rapid rise in the MVP race hit a snag. Love, who opened at +2200 but crashed at +10000, rebounded to +2500 following a winning streak and a narrow loss to Detroit. Now, he’s +4000. Buffalo’s Josh Allen is the favorite at +160, followed by Brock Purdy at +430 and Joe Burrow and Caleb Williams at +600.
The Packers are last in the NFC North standings and remain well off the pace in the division odds at DraftKings. Minnesota is +164, followed by Chicago at +184 and Detroit at +280. After that tightly grouped pack, the Packers are +920. That’s an improvement over +1125 last week.

title: Bears Beat Seahawks, And That’s Good News for Packers in Big Playoff Shakeup
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Chicago Bears beat the Seattle Seahawks 34-17 on Monday night. At one point, a “Green Bay Sucks” chant briefly broke out at Lumen Field.
Really, the Bears did the Green Bay Packers a favor on Monday night.
Here’s a look at the NFC playoff standings entering Week 9.
The Packers remain the No. 7 seed in the NFC playoffs. However, there were two key developments following Week 8. First, it’s the playoff opponent. Second, it’s getting some critical breathing room. More on those things in a moment.
1. San Francisco 49ers, 6-1
The NFC North is CLOSE 🍿 Who will take the division? pic.twitter.com/aJuZJsof3q
10. Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 3-5
NFC North teams are 17-3 in non-division games this season
12. Arizona Cardinals, 3-5
14. Washington Commanders, 2-4-1
15. New Orleans Saints, 2-5
16. Philadelphia Eagles, 2-6
If the season were to end today, the Packers would be playing at the Vikings in the wild-card round rather than playing at the 49ers.
With Minnesota losing on Sunday at Detroit while San Francisco was on its bye, the 49ers and Vikings flip-flopped spots in the race for homefield advantage in the NFC. While it’s obviously too early to be projecting playoff matchups, the Packers might prefer Round 3 against a division opponent rather than going on the road and facing a longtime playoff nemesis.
Then again, it wouldn’t really matter. As the standings look now, the Packers would have to beat the Vikings to face the 49ers or the 49ers to face the Vikings.
Here’s the big development from Week 8: The Packers went from seventh place in the NFC because of a flimsy tiebreaker to seventh place in the NFC outright.
The Packers are 5-3 after beating the Panthers on Sunday. The Seahawks fell to 4-4 with their loss to Chicago, so did the Bears did the Packers a favor by giving them a one-game lead over their nearest challenger in the playoff race.
The Rams, who beat the winless Chargers on Sunday, also are 4-4 but in ninth in the NFC. Everyone else is at least two games behind the Packers, including the Falcons, who beat the Packers at Lambeau in Week 3 so would have the critical tiebreaker.
“I feel like that, for sure, that there’s so much more out there for us as an offense,” quarterback Jordan Love said after the Carolina game. “I’ve talked about that time after time. It just comes down to us executing and making plays out there.
“I think that’s the cool part is we know there’s more out there, we know we can be a lot better, we know we can put up more points, but we’ve got to find ways to do it. That’s the challenge for everybody is how do we get there? How do we keep that mindset? Keep improving, keep stacking, improving on the little things. But there’s definitely a lot out there for us, so I think that’s the nice part, the cool part.”
From Tankathon , here are the remaining strength of schedules for the teams that matter to the Packers in the playoff race:
Chicago has the toughest remaining schedule in the league at .585, with Minnesota next at .580. So, the NFC North race is far from decided.
In the race for the final wild-card spots, the Packers are sixth at .561, the Lions are ninth at .526, the Rams are 14th at .514 and the Seahawks are 21st at .486.
For Green Bay, its final nine games include five against teams with winning records – led by the Patriots on Sunday – and a sixth game against the Rams. The Texans, Saints and Dolphins are the three teams with losing records.
What Do Playoff Simulators Have to Say?
Even with their one-game lead in the playoff race, the Packers have only a 50 percent chance of qualifying for the postseason, according to The Athletic . That includes an 8 percent chance of winning the loaded NFC North.
The game at New England will be big. With a win, the Packers would move to a 63 percent probability of reaching the playoffs. With a loss, it would fall to 42 percent.
At NFL.com , the Packers have a 48 percent probability. The Seahawks trail in the standings but are at 50 percent.
At ESPN.com , the Packers have a 49 percent probability, which ranks seventh in the NFC – behind both Seattle and Tampa Bay, with the Bucs being in the thick of the “race” to win the NFC South. The Packers have an 8 percent chance of winning the division.
At Stick to the Model , the Packers have a 47 percent chance of reaching the playoffs and a 6 percent chance of winning the division. What’s a stake against the Patriots? Their chances would rise to 59 percent with a win and fall to 38 percent with a loss.
No simulator likes Green Bay’s chances as much as Playoff Status , where the Packers have a 56 percent chance of qualifying, though only 7 percent as the division winner. By beating the Patriots, that would improve to 65 percent.
Just like the Bears earned a big litmus-test win against Seattle, the defending Super Bowl champions, the Packers will face a measuring-stick game against New England, the defending AFC champion. The Patriots have won four of their last five games and are 3-0 at home.
They are coached by Mike Vrabel, who was Tennessee’s coach in 2018 when LaFleur was offensive coordinator. LaFleur categorized their relationship as “fine” on Monday.
“I learned a lot from Mike,” LaFleur said. “I got a lot of respect for how he goes about his business and holding people to a high standard. Especially, he was always toughest on the best players, and so I learned a lot from my time with him.”

title: Packers WR Matthew Golden’s NFL-Leading Totals Are Great, Horrible
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers receiver Matthew Golden giveth and he taketh away.
First the negative. Including two against Carolina, Golden leads the NFL with nine drops, according to Pro Football Focus. The Steelers’ D.K. Metcalf is next with six, the Saints’ Chris Olave is third with five and former Packers receiver Romeo Doubs of the Patriots is among a group of players with four.
It’s not just a matter of volume. Of the 70 receivers who have been targeted at least 24 times, Golden is first with a drop rate of 17.3 percent.
Golden is the odd player who has shown great hands but has shown great problems catching the ball when it matters.
“I talk to our guys about it every single week, and it’s just a process of continuing to get better and better and better,” passing-game coordinator Jason Vrable said on Monday. “Every single game he’s made an incredible catch – like, even the one last week that was thrown a little bit behind him on the in-breaker. He’s made some incredible catches.”
Using PFF’s data, Golden has at least one drop in seven games. That includes two against Carolina and three against Dallas. According to Stathead, Golden has eight drops – three more than a group of players with five that includes Tucker Kraft.
“It’s just about consistency,” Vrable said. “That’s what we always evaluate our players on is being consistent and getting better every day. I know you guys have asked him about it a lot and talked with him about his approach. I think he’s been working his butt off, and it’s just in the heat of the moment, you’ve just got to be able to make those plays.
“So, I feel like the second half of the season here, just got to grow, just got to continue to get better. And when you get your opps, it’s our job to make those plays.”
Golden’s got to make them because he’s going to keep getting opportunities. Golden ranks fourth in the league with 80 targets. He has had at least 12 targets in three consecutive games.
Receivers coach Noah Pauley noted that trust from quarterback Jordan Love. That, of course, was evident when Golden dropped a 24-yard touchdown pass against Carolina, only to catch a 24-yard touchdown pass on the next play.
It’s also evident in really being the go-to player at crunch time.
Players with 200+ scrimmage yards in the 4th quarter this season: 1. Jaxon Smith-Njigba – 296 2. James Cook – 273 3. Jaylen Warren – 243 4. Chris Olave – 242 5. Matthew Golden – 239 6. CeeDee Lamb – 223 7. Kyren Williams – 221 8. Drake London – 218 9. Tee Higgins - 216
“It’s just something of his focus in the moment of truth when that ball’s ahead of him. That’s part of just continuing to grow and hammer on the details,” Pauley said.
Hammer the details, yes. Hammer Golden over the head for the drops, no.
“It is a lot of just the focus,” Pauley said. “When it comes down to it, that ball’s in the air, that last 2, 3 yards, ‘My focus has got to heighten up and I’ve got to make a big play,’ and I think that’s just the details of it when it comes down to catching the football.”
In eight games, Golden has caught 43 passes for 619 yards. He enters Monday night ranked in the top 10 in both categories and just outside the top 10 with four touchdown catches. He has three 100-yard games this season and four consecutive games of at least six catches. His 17-game pace is 91 receptions, 1,315 yards and 8.5 touchdowns.
The numbers would be better without the drops. They’d also be better with the interference penalties he’s drawn.
According to Sumer Sports, Golden and Arizona’s Michael Wilson have drawn a league-high six interference penalties. Those penalties have resulted in 115 penalty yards – 19 more than Houston’s Nico Collins.
Is there an art to drawing interference penalties, or is it simply a matter of Golden is so fast and so technically sound in his route-running that defenders have to resort to grabbing?
“He has the speed to get by a defender, right? So, oftentimes, let’s say they’re bringing pressure and they’re telling their defensive backs to kind of squat near the sticks,” Vrable said. “That happened in the Jets game.”
In that game, he drew two interference penalties for 61 yards. He also drew one against Carolina on third-and-11.
“Some teams teach their DBs to be slow in the back pedal because we’re pressuring to force the ball out,” Vrable said of third down. “And he’s ran through the contact and, obviously, he has the ability to get behind. When you get behind a defender, what do they do? They panic, right?”
Yes, that’s a trait that scouts call “DB panic mode.” Rather than trusting their technique and skill, they grab. Given Golden’s elite speed, they are more apt to grab, figuring a 30-yard penalty for interference beats the alternative.
“They don’t want to give up the big play,” Vrable continued. “You’re on national television, so then what do they do? They try to make up for it with effort. Well, then the ball might be up there, and he’s done a really good job.”
The interference penalties are great. The next step is to make the catch.
“Our motto is always like, yeah, it’s great to draw the pass interference or the holding,” Vrable said. “That’s great, but let’s do both. Let’s draw that and make the play. You know, I think that’s got to be the standard, kind of the Packer way. Playing like a ‘G’ is just getting both and coming down with the ball still. And there’s no excuses. They call pass interference, you still make the play, right? That’s got to be the standard.”

title: Packers Needed New Practice Squad QB; He Got Big Endorsement From GOAT
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers made a change to the practice squad on Monday by signing quarterback Cam Miller. The move was necessitated by the Baltimore Ravens responding to injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley by signing Kedon Slovis off the practice squad.
Miller was a sixth-round pick by the Raiders last year after completing 69.3 percent of his passes with 81 touchdown passes and 19 interceptions at North Dakota State, which he led to two FCS national championships.
Before the 2025 draft, Miller got a Hall of Fame endorsement.
Tom Brady “liked the way he threw it, his technique, throwing from the ground up and his motion," Raiders GM John Spytek told The Athletic after the draft. “And he thought he had the potential to improve.”
That Miller was a winner mattered in the scouting process.
“I haven't had any interaction with Tom,” Miller said after being drafted , “but from every conversation that I've had with the GM [John Spytek], he has talked to me about how they want to bring in people that are winners, and who have been accustomed and used to winning games. And I think that that was really the x-factor in their choice to take me in the draft.”
He spent his rookie season on the Raiders’ practice squad without playing in a game; the Dolphins signed him to their 53-man roster late in the season.
“Probably his intellect and his accuracy will help him push it down the road,” then-Raiders offensive coordinator Greg Olson said at the time . "He's been a good player and has played in big games. The game's not too big for him, so I think his internal makeup is a real positive for him.”
With the Dolphins this preseason, he completed 42.1 percent of his passes for 170 yards with zero touchdowns and two interceptions and failed to make the roster or earn a spot on the practice squad.
“I think just my knowledge of the game” is what grew the most, he said late in training camp. “I think [offensive coordinator] Bobby Slowik has done such a great job of teaching the quarterbacks defense and running his system.
“I've been such a huge fan of him and the way that he's helped develop quarterbacks in the past, and it's been so great to just learn the game of football from him. I think that's been some of the most improvement, just seeing the field a lot better than I did in the past.”
Miller, a native of Solon, Iowa, was a first-team All-American as a senior in 2024, when he finished second in voting for the Walter Payton Award, which is the FCS equivalent of the Heisman Trophy.
Miller set school records for total yards (11,998), completion percentage (69.4) and passing yards (9.721). He tied Easton Stick’s school record with 129 total touchdowns.
While he played lower-tier competition, he was well-schooled in the factors necessary to be an NFL quarterback.
“I just think coming from a pro-style offense at North Dakota State, I’m accustomed to playing under center, playing in the gun, playing a pro-style offense,” he said after being drafted. “I think NDSU prepared me well, just with the system, doing under center play action, everything that we did in the gun I think is going to translate to the next level. I’m excited to dive into the playbook and start to understand it a little bit more.”
Before the 2025 draft, The Athletic’s Dane Brugler called Miller “an intelligent game manager” who lacked a “power arm” but delivered with anticipation and accuracy.
“The son of a football coach, his mental approach and on-field production showed improvements each season, although he will continue to have his doubters because of the level of competition he faced,” Brugler wrote.
“Overall, Miller won’t wow you right away because the physical traits are average. The more you watch, though, the more you come to appreciate his decision-making and feel for the position. He can be an asset in an NFL quarterback room as a reserve.”
The Packers’ practice squad quarterback had been Kedon Slovis, who might wind up playing sooner than later in Baltimore. Slovis competed for a roster spot with the Cardinals during training camp and spent the last two months on Green Bay’s practice squad.
“Just to develop and I think get to the point where coaches trust you to be a guy where they can, whether it’s a backup role or feel like they can bring you in and play in some games,” he told Packers On SI after being signed .
“Obviously, the goal is to be a guy that they want to play but, obviously, there’s some steps to go before that. So, I think that’s the next part is just develop as much as I can and kind of let the chips fall with me.”

title: Packers Sticking With Josh Jacobs; Here Are Jonathan Taylor Next-Team Odds
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers are standing by running back Josh Jacobs.
“Obviously, we’re aware of the prior allegations on Josh,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Monday, a few days after more allegations threw his future with the team in doubt . “We’re going to allow the NFL to do its process, but I would anticipate him being a member of us moving forward. That’s really all I have to speak on.”
With the uncertainty over Jacobs swirling and the NFL trade deadline looming, the Packers are considered one of top contenders to acquire superstar running back Jonathan Taylor.
The Packers are the sixth-most likely team to have Taylor suit up for them after the trade deadline at Hard Rock Bet . Their +1200 odds mean an implied probability of 7.7 percent, which isn’t great but they’re still perceived to be among the front-runners.
Here are the odds from Hard Rock ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. The Seahawks, who won last year’s Super Bowl, and the Broncos, who reached last year’s AFC Championship Game, are the betting favorites.
New England Patriots: +2000
Green Bay has the sixth-shortest odds; staying in Indianapolis is fifth.
“You know that day always comes,” Taylor told reporters in Indianapolis last week. “For many players, whether you like it or not, the day may come. You may get lucky enough to stay somewhere forever, but you understand the business side of it.”
He added “I'm always proud to wear the horseshoe, proud to be here.”
The Packers are near the top of the board for the odds. However, after the Colts sent All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the 49ers, three NFC teams have shorter odds than Green Bay.
Seattle, which failed to replace Kenneth Walker, are the betting favorites. The Giants, looking for a stud runner to help offset the loss of Jaxson Dart, and the Vikings, who are looking for a premier playmaker to help their defense, all have considerably shorter odds.
The Colts are looking for more than a second-round pick for Taylor. They are under no obligation to trade him and are looking for an offer too good to refuse. The frame of reference is the 49ers giving up picks in the second through fifth rounds in the 2022 trade for running back Christian McCaffrey.
The Packers don’t have a first-round pick following last year’s trade of Micah Parsons. They do have a second-round pick, and they could end up with bonus third- and fourth-round picks after losing Malik Willis and Romeo Doubs in free agency last year.
“You think we’re rebuilding?” Taylor responded to a reporter on Thursday.
“I would say, we’re going out there trying to win. So, for me, being a competitor, and not only for myself but everyone in the locker room, no one goes out there to wave the white flag and surrender. We’re going out there to compete. We’re going out there to get a win. Every time you go on the field, you want to dominate and show that you’re the best.”
The NFL allowed Jacobs to rejoin the Packers a couple weeks ago, and he started in games against the Lions and Panthers.
However, the NFL said it would look into allegations from three women stemming from Jacobs’ time with the Raiders.
Coach Matt LaFleur has had Jacobs’ back ever since he was arrested following a Memorial Day Weekend incident. Has anything changed?
“Like I said, I’m not going to get into that up here right now. We’ll just let the process play out,” LaFleur said.
Jacobs scored three touchdowns in his two games back in the lineup. While it hasn’t been reflected in team rushing success , he is by far the team’s best running back. The former team captain has had the support of the locker room throughout and was welcomed back to the lineup with open arms.
“Yeah, I would anticipate as we go through everything, him being a part of it,” LaFleur said.
Jacobs, who missed the first six games of the season, carried the ball 21 times for just 39 yards in the victory over Carolina.
“I'm sure that's definitely a process for him from that standpoint,” running backs coach Ben Sirmans said on Monday. “We did a lot of work when he wasn't with the team just making sure he was still doing the right type of drills to try to keep him in tune to what he's going to face on a Sunday, like a lot of run simulation drills.
“But I do think he's still getting his footing, especially when it comes to contact and all that.”

title: Winning Isn’t Everything, Truth Is Only Thing for Packers And Josh Jacobs
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – After spending the first six games of the NFL season on the exempt list following an altercation with a female for which he pleaded no contest, the spotlight is back on Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs for all the wrong reasons.
After starting and scoring two touchdowns against Carolina on Thursday, WGBA-TV Channel 26 in Green Bay received records from the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department on Friday following an open-records request. The records show that three additional women contacted the department to allege similar altercations with Jacobs from his time with the Raiders.
Jacobs’ legal team offered a strong rebuttal on Sunday.
From Jacobs’ legal team. pic.twitter.com/ASGAmTLIMX
It concluded with this final statement:
“The three accounts are old, are hearsay, and easily disproven, yet released to the media by police without any investigation to determine whether they were accurate or contradicted by evidence. Josh is answering them in detail because of the character assassination that is occurring, unfairly threatening his career.”
There’s no reason to jump to conclusions and believe the women on face value about the alleged incidents from four or five years ago. That doesn’t mean they are lying – let’s make that abundantly clear – it’s just that in today’s world, really, nobody deserves the benefit of the doubt. Nobody – and that absolutely includes the player, the lawyer, the team and the league.
There’s no reason to believe Jacobs when he (through his lawyers) said that these old allegations are “hearsay” and he’s done nothing wrong.
There’s no reason to believe coach Matt LaFleur when he said, “I know the guy and I know the character of the guy. I’ve said that many times. And, unfortunately, situations occur in life and it’s just an unfortunate situation.”
There’s no reason to believe the team and the league hadn’t stumbled upon this information while doing their own investigations into the May incident. No reason to believe everyone isn’t just kicking the can down the road.
At the same time, contrary to what my colleague, Conor Orr, wrote for SI.com, this should not be about the Packers being “the adult in the room” and releasing Jacobs because the rest of the teams are “sacrificing (their) morals.”
The NFL is a bottom-line business. “Winning isn’t everything, it’s the only thing” is a saying that isn’t too far from reality. Jacobs gives the Packers their best chance of winning games, which is why they stood by him throughout the ordeal. They chose to believe the Memorial Day Weekend incident is a one-off, one horrendous moment for the former team captain.
“I think a lot of times you get in a situation where you might not make the right decision,” LaFleur said when Jacobs returned a couple weeks ago. “I think people learn from their mistakes, and I think he’s extremely remorseful and I do believe that he’s a good person. I’ve been around him quite a bit and I believe in second chances.”
If you’re looking for a hot take on the worthiness of that second chance, I’m sorry. Not today, because none of us know the facts.
We don’t know what happened in May, the incident for which Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and damage to a property. There is a video, which both the Jacobs and victim have asked to be sealed for understandable reasons.
Speaking of the video, the NFL removed Jacobs from the exempt list after six games because, without getting to view it, its investigation was at a standstill. It couldn’t keep Jacobs sidelined forever, so it allowed Jacobs to play while saying the investigation was ongoing.
Remember, on the battery charge, the Brown County District Attorney’s Office – which has seen the video – handed down a $1,000 fine. That’s not even a slap on the wrist. That’s like putting your arm around your kid and telling him in a soothing voice, “Don’t do that again.”
Was the penalty so minor because what happened that night was so minor – relatively speaking, obviously – or did Jacobs and the victim agree to a payoff so Jacobs could avoid much harsher discipline legally and from the league?
We all have thoughts and opinions, along with stances on winning games vs. having the moral high ground, but we don’t know the facts behind any of the allegations made by this year’s victim or the other women. There are snippets from those incidents on the police reports and there are rebuttals by his lawyers but, ultimately, the only people who know are the women and Jacobs.
The NFL didn’t suspend Jacobs, so the Packers’ hands are tied a bit in terms of his contract, the collective bargaining agreement and the salary cap.
If the Packers trade for Jonathan Taylor, it means they are moving on from Josh Jacobs. Here's the complexity: Josh Jacobs was never suspended. As such he currently qualifies for 100% termination pay - Meaning if released and he doesn't sign with another team the Packers will…
At the end of the day, Jacobs pleaded no contest to a misdemeanor and not a felony. The old allegations that were made public last week could lead to a suspension, which would open the door for the Packers to release him due to conduct detrimental to the team, but, again, what is the truth? And is there any appetite for actually finding the truth?
Maybe, if the team deems Jacobs misled them about the May incident, but, again, that’s nothing more than speculation based on limited knowledge of what happened.
LaFleur will talk to reporters on Monday afternoon. He will be asked to answer questions that he shouldn’t have to answer. Jacobs’ place on the roster presumably was made by the organization – general manager Brian Gutekunst and team President and CEO Ed Policy. That they aren’t taking the lead on this is absurd. The team hasn’t even offered a wishy-washy statement in the wake of Friday’s news.
What we do know is Jacobs remains on the roster. That’s all we know. Everything else is opinion. It’s up to the NFL and the Packers to sort out the details honestly and to the best of their ability and do what’s right for the organization and the league. Winning isn’t everything. The truth is the only thing.
Whatever the decision, everyone better be damned sure it’s the right one.

title: What We're Hearing About the Texans Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Houston Texans are now less than a week away from the NFL trade deadline .
And compared to the rest of the league and their potential activity around this time of year, the Texans aren't being viewed as the most active on the trade market. They already made one big mid-season move earlier this year by trading for Marvin Harrison Jr., and are still looking to see how that investment pays off.
However, that doesn't mean the Texans shouldn't be expected to make a move or two in the coming days.
There are a select few situations for players either in Houston or around the league that make sense to consider a potential trade on, and if the right deal comes across the table of Nick Caserio, perhaps we could see this front office pull the trigger.
With that in mind, let's sort through a bit about what we're hearing around the Texans and their trade deadline plans, along with who around the roster could be viewed as a potential mover in the near future:
Now, it might not come as a major surprise to hear that there haven't been any rumblings around a major move being in store for the Texans . But Houston's current situation doesn't exactly put them in a bucket of being a true buyer or a seller.
The Texans are three games under .500 heading into Week 9 without a second, fifth, or sixth-round pick in this year's draft. Trading away another one of those picks for this offseason could be seen as a little too short-sighted, or even reckless to a degree.
But a selling move doesn't make a whole lot of sense either. The Texans entered this year with expectations of being one of the top teams in the AFC, and while their record might not show that right now, Houston has proven to be more than capable of a late-season turnaround, as recently as 2025.
So while the Texans could still be prone to one or two moves around the edges of the roster, a big-time swing doesn't seem to be in the cards.
A name from the Texans who did pop up in some lingering trade rumors this past weekend was one of their more recent signings heading into the season: veteran edge rusher Jadeveon Clowney, who reportedly had interest building around the league from those looking to acquire help on their defensive line.
And perhaps if the Texans get an intriguing enough offer on Clowney and his expiring contract, maybe that's a move to keep in consideration. But it seems as if Clowney's entry into trade rumors is stemming more from external interest in his services rather than Houston's own desire to pivot off of him.
Clowney still fills a key role on the Texans' defensive line as a rotational edge rusher behind Danielle Hunter and Will Anderson, and the defense doesn't have any direct replacements to turn to in the event that Clowney is shipped out.
So at the very least, keep this trade idea on the radar. But don't get your hopes up that anything will come of it.
This is more of a speculative gauge on the Texans' current roster. Not much buzz has come out around the front office's intentions over the next few days, and who around this current group could potentially be on the move.
But one area of the Texans' roster to keep watch for a potential surprise shakeup is the offensive line . It's a group that has improved a bit this season from their turbulent state of the past few years, but the position group has a couple of bigger-name veterans not getting the playing time you would've expected coming into the year.
Former Pro Bowler Wyatt Teller has been stuck as a reserve on the interior for all but two games this season, and veteran Braden Smith has also been stuck on the bench after starting the new season off on injured reserve.
Both names were viewed as plug-and-play starters for the Texans heading into the season, but now have seen their stock take a turn for the worst as Keylan Rutledge and Trent Brown have been the ones winning the starting gig in their respective positions.
Maybe, if the Texans are able to find another offensive-line-needy team over the coming days, they could strike on some minimal draft value to send off both Teller and Smith. Doing so could replenish Houston's lack of capital in 2027, while also giving both veterans a chance to compete for a starting spot elsewhere.

title: Texans Cost Themselves Millions by Delaying C.J. Stroud Extension
full_text:
Throughout the most recent NFL offseason, the Houston Texans had been stuck in contract negotiations with their quarterback, C.J. Stroud for several months.
After an up-and-down first three years, Stroud was eligible for a new deal after the 2025 season to make him the Texans' starting signal-caller for the foreseeable future. He had been fresh off a third-straight playoff appearance and Wild Card win for the franchise, but also paired that with a four-interception performance in Houston's divisional loss vs. the New England Patriots.
Houston's lead decision-makers had publicly backed Stroud over the course of the offseason, but finding terms to that extension proved to be a task much easier said than done. Both sides had different visions for what Stroud's value should be worth.
Eventually, Week 1 arrived, and the decision was made that Stroud would not sign a new deal with the Texans and enter the 2026 season with just two years remaining on his current rookie contract.
It was effectively a decision that sent a message from both sides. Stroud was essentially betting on himself and his chances at netting a better contract offer after the 2026 season was over. The Texans felt as if they could hold off on that deal and be well off.
However, now eight weeks into the 2026 season, and it seems like there's a clear winner within this ongoing saga. And that's especially so based on some new intel stemming from ESPN 's D.J Bien-Aime and Jeremy Fowler .
According to ESPN , the Texans had made an initial offer for Stroud to be paid "well within the $50 million-per-year club," which was an effort that was then matched with a counteroffer from Stroud's representation.
The Texans felt as if that counteroffer wasn't worthy enough to be accepted. And as a result, Stroud and his camp were ready and willing to hold off on the extension until next offseason, and bet on himself in hopes that his value can jump in the meantime.
"Before camp, Houston made an initial offer to Stroud that reached what sources called a 'respectable' range -- not at the top of the quarterback market but well within the $50 million-per-year club that 13 quarterbacks now occupy," Bien-Aime and Fowler wrote.
"Stroud and his agent, David Mulugheta, made a counteroffer... But despite the back-and-forth, a deal was not imminent. Meanwhile, Stroud had made clear he was comfortable playing without a new deal, per sources. 'Unless there's a better offer, we're good,' is how one source recalled the messaging from Stroud."
In hindsight, that decision from the Texans to hold off on paying Stroud a new deal might now be costing them in the form of millions of dollars––which becomes even more costly knowing how much money Houston paid out to the defensive side of the ball earlier this offseason.
Houston's gone from offering Stroud a deal "well into the $50 million range," declining a counter that was presumably a slightly higher offer, and are now forced into paying an even higher offer than that first counter come next offseason when negotiations are back at the table.
Executives around the league are well aware of Stroud's jump in value, with one in the AFC outlining a scenario where the Texans might be due to make their quarterback the highest-paid in the NFL.
"He's making himself a lot of money,' an AFC executive said, via ESPN . 'New tax bracket. If he keeps playing like this and they somehow get in the playoffs and make a run, there's no reason why he can't be somewhere close to the highest paid."
Now, if Stroud were to help command a turnaround in the AFC, get the Texans into the playoffs for the fourth straight season, and help lead a deep run into the postseason, that's all a positive for Houston. After all, putting together a team that can make those victories deep in the postseason possible is the end goal for any front office.
But there's no question that if Stroud is able to continue on the strong run he's put together so far this season, the Texans' decision to hold off on an extension for their starting quarterback will be an extremely expensive one.
And if the Texans do wind up being forced to pay Stroud as one of the highest-paid quarterbacks in the NFL, they'll be due to pay for it in the form of making some big sacrifices around a talented roster.

title: What the Texans Can Realistically Afford at NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Houston Texans are just a week away from the NFL trade deadline.
And for a team that sits with a record of 2-5 , it's pretty noteworthy knowing that there's a world where the Texans could approach this deadline with the mindset of being buyers on the market.
While the first half of the season hasn't gone the way anyone in Houston would've anticipated, this roster still has a ton of talent to bank on for their second half stretch. And if the Texans are able to pull out a win in Week 9 to sit just two games back from .500, there's a case to be made for this team to take a swing on the trade market, if the right opportunity presents itself.
But what might the Texans have the ability to spend on if they wanted to go and make a trade at the deadline? Houston only has a finite number of resources in terms of draft picks and cap space for a potential deal, and thus holds back just how aggressive they'll be able to be.
However, knowing that, let's break down just what those limitations look like for the Texans, and how it might affect any trade deadline plans they may have over the coming days:
1st (own) 3rd (own) 4th (own) 3 7ths (ARI, PHI, SF)
When it comes to draft capital, the Texans do have a good bit of flexibility to work with beyond the 2027 draft. Through both 2028 and 2029, Houston will be without only one of their own draft picks, that being their 2028 sixth-round pick.
But Houston will be without a decent amount of wiggle room for how many picks they can pivot off of in this year's draft. Houston has only three of their own selections between the first, third, and fourth round, then has three sevenths from others around the league.
Perhaps the Texans will make a minor "selling" move on their roster to replenish some of that day three capital that's been lost from previous trades. But if not, it's hard to imagine Houston gutting their share of picks in this year's draft any further than its current setup.
The Texans don't have a ton of flexibility in terms of cap space, as they have just under $10 million in free money to spend on other acquisitions.
However, that number does put them right in the middle of the league in terms of available cap space. Houston is ranked 15th in the NFL when it comes to cap space, and might be able to provide some room to bring in a short-term, smaller contract rather than a big splash from a high-cost veteran.
Another factor to keep an eye on as it relates to the Texans' future cost of the roster is that they are ranked with the second-lowest available cap space for 2027 with -$41.5 million on the books. That's even further reason for Houston not to go out and be crazy spenders at the deadline.
So when taking a step back to look at the Texans' situation and the amount of assets they have on hand, it's pretty clear to recognize that a big splash deadline move probably isn't in the cards for this team.
Unless the Texans found a player on an affordable contract that they'd be willing to move off of multiple first-round picks for––which is a task much easier said than done––Houston simply doesn't have the chips or financial flexibility to make such a move go down.
Now, that doesn't mean that the Texans can't at least involve themselves in some form of deadline activity to bring in new talent. If Houston is able to get back on track with a win in Week 9 against the LA Chargers, it's certainly possible that this front office wants to build up this roster even further.
But if that were to happen, expect the Texans to make a minor addition on the edges of this roster to help propel their current core forward, rather than making a big-time star investment like the Chicago Bears just did for Jeffery Simmons.

title: Texans Week 9 Consensus Power Rankings: Where Houston Sits After the Bye
full_text:
The Houston Texans got some much-needed time off during their Week 8 bye week that can only hope to recharge this group and help rally back from the 2-5 deficit they're currently stuck in .
But as the Texans were taking their time off in Week 8, teams around the league continued to fight on. The action that unfolded tended to shift the stock of several teams around Houston –– for better or for worse–– and has since led to a few changes across multiple power rankings because of it.
With that in mind, let's sort through a new batch of consensus power rankings to see just where the Texans stack up around the league as they head into their Week 9 game against the LA Chargers :
Sports Illustrated's Conor Orr was one of the highest pundits on this list when it came to the Texans earlier this season. But now, he's dropped them to just barely inside the top 25 teams in the NFL. A disappointing falloff.
"The Texans will face the Chargers this weekend in a battle of the two most confoundingly disappointing teams I can ever remember. This is the kind of hype that forces me to never trust again."
NFL.com 's Nick Shook does see reason for optimism surrounding the Texans moving forward, simply because of their upcoming schedule facing a batch of beatable opponents. But that still didn't stop him from dropping Houston one spot in his rankings.
"While we can officially agree Houston’s defense isn’t the unit we’ve known it to be in recent years, the Texans have a favorable road out of the bye. Dates with the Chargers and Colts sandwich a meeting with the Browns, so while 2-5 is a tough place to be after eight weeks, there’s still a path back to relevance. Keep an eye on Marvin Harrison Jr.’s role in the offense, too."
ESPN 's writers also dropped the Texans by one spot in their rankings and continue to keep them outside of the top 20. D.J. Bien-Aime was tasked with finding Houston's best in-season trade acquisition within franchise history, landing on wide receiver Demariyus Thomas in 2018.
"Historically, the Texans haven't made many in-season trades. Zero have resulted in Houston receiving a game-changing player. The hope is Marvin Harrison Jr., who was acquired from the Cardinals in early October, could become exactly that. Thomas was at least the most effective player out of all the choices. In 2018, Houston started 0-3 and reeled off nine consecutive wins to finish 11-5. Houston acquired Thomas after five wins in a row, and in his first game, he had 61 receiving yards against his former team, the Broncos. He finished the season with 275 receiving yards for Houston with two touchdowns."
The Athletic 's Josh Kendall and Chad Graff aren't ready to count the Texans out of playoff contention just yet. However, that isn't to say that they still aren't disappointed with the results of Houston's latest loss to the New York Giants.
"It’s frustrating, honestly. Houston started 0-4, showed a spark of life, but then disappointed in a 27-21 loss to the Giants in Week 7.The Athletic’s most recent playoff projections have the Texans with just a 19 percent chance to make the playoffs. But here’s the problem: Houston has the second-easiest remaining schedule, according to Tankathon."
CBS Sports ' Pete Prisco highlights the defensive woes Houston has faced as his biggest cause for concern on the Texans now and moving forward.
"It's hard for many to see how this team is down this low in the rankings. Here's why: the defense has been a mess. They can't afford another loss or they might be done."
FOX Sports ' Ralph Vacchiano tends to have a bit more to like about the Texans compared to the consensus. Not only does he have them within the top 20 teams of his current rankings, but he's the only pundit who ranked Houston higher than their previous spot heading into Week 8––which becomes especially surprising knowing that this team didn't play a snap this weekend.
"Here’s the good news for the Texans coming out of their bye: They’re in second place in the AFC South despite a 2-5 record. They’re 2.5 games out of a wild-card spot, but the point is that their division is pretty awful and they still have to play the two worst teams — the Titans and Colts — one more time each. They also get the Chargers, Ravens, Commanders and Eagles, so there are a lot of soft spots in the second half of their schedule. If they can get over their pre-bye loss to the Giants, they still have an outside chance to be OK."
