title: 5 Best 2027 Draft Prospects Jets Need on Their Radar as Colts Sink Further Into Basement
full_text:
At 2-6, it's clear the Jets aren't going to be booking their tickets to the postseason for a 16th straight season. The good news is that they are well within striking distance of collecting two of the top five overall selections in the 2027 NFL Draft.
They have the Colts to thank for that. By trading Sauce Gardner to Indy for two first-round picks, and with the Colts at an abysmal 2-6 mark, the Jets could very well come away with two top picks to rebuild the roster.
Projected team as of Week 9
Should that happen as expected, there are several players the team should be focused on.
With that said, let's look at the five prospects that make the most sense for the Jets to start thinking about now that April is only five months away.
What a ride for Mestemaker. The Oklahoma State quarterback didn't start a game at quarterback in varsity during high school. He's grown to be the top quarterback of the 2027 class, with a lightning-quick release and the arm strength to win downfield.
He's not the perfect prospect. Mestemaker is still raw in his footwork, but this is the kind of athlete and player that teams will line up for, giving him the chance to grow into a franchise quarterback.
Going into the 2027 offseason, New York's chief focus should be the quarterback position and along its defensive line. While Geno Smith has played well this season, he is not the long-term answer at the position for the franchise.
If the Jets bring in Mestemaker, they will have him sit behind a veteran to start his career. The benefit is that they can get the top quarterback of the class, and one with the skill set to be an excellent starter in the NFL.
Mestemaker is going to be the top quarterback taken in the 2027 draft. That seems to be a foregone conclusion. But people shouldn't be overlooking what Carr has done over his college career at Notre Dame.
This season, Carr has thrown for 1,849 yards, 18 touchdowns and one interception through eight games. He has an NFL-ready release, is very good from the pocket, and can make all throws. His issue comes in the differences between modern NFL quarterbacks.
Unlike players like Josh Allen or other quarterbacks who can make things happen when the offensive line breaks down, Carr isn't quite known for that. He isn't the greatest athlete in the world. In the Fighting Irish's loss to BYU this season, he did manage to escape many sacks, but things will be different in the NFL.
I expect him to be the second quarterback taken off the board, and someone the Jets seem very comfortable with, having visited Notre Dame games four times this season.
Is it a bad look that the Jets had Quinnen Williams on the roster and they traded him... only to pick his replacement in the hopes that he becomes Williams? Maybe.
But the Jets' defensive line was poor with Williams on the field to start the year. They need to refocus their efforts on bringing in players who can rush the passer along the interior line. Enter Echoles. The defensive tackle from Ole Miss has been excellent throughout his career. Echoles is known as one of the better run defenders in the country but also adds an excellent array of pass-rushing moves.
He appears to be a perferct fit for what the Jets need along their line.
David Bailey is not enough to fix the Jets' pass-rushing woes. They need more help, and from players who can both play the run and get after the quarterback. There will be people debating who the better edge rusher is between Stewart and Colin Simmons.
At this moment, attitude aside, I think Stewart is the player who offers the most upside moving forward. He can play the run better than Bailey and has the explosiveness needed for an edge rusher in the NFL.
Dylan Stewart is too ELITE to not go top 5 Athletic traits like his are exceedingly rare https://t.co/EcmZUyR5hM pic.twitter.com/TSeMmz6IZ1
There will be health and character questions that follow him, but the Jets need ballplayers right now. Not nice guys. Stewart would fundamentally shift what the defense can look like in 2027.
I see Simmons in a similar way to Bailey for the Jets.
The Texas product has a long history of getting to the passer and has caused plenty of turnovers on his own. But he does have an injury history and can be overwhelmed by bigger tackles. He's still a great enough prospect to be a lock for the top five, but I think the Jets should focus on Stewart's upside over Simmons at this point.
Either pick would be celebrated, though.

title: Breaking Down Jets' Injury Report Heading Into Week 9 (Who's Hurt & Who Could Return vs. Chiefs)
full_text:
Despite leading by double digits multiple times and doing more than enough offensively to get back in the win column, a second-half collapse doomed the Jets in a 38-33 loss to the Raiders on Sunday and dropped them to a 2-6 record.
While there was a lot to dissect from the loss , including special teams struggles, poor defensive play, and a lack of adjustments from the coaching staff, injuries continue to be a recurring theme for the Jets and are worth monitoring going into a huge road test at Arrowhead Stadium.
With various injuries impacting the team, here's who should be fine and who could miss some time for Gang Green.
Hall has been out of action for the last five weeks after injuring his right quad in the Week 3 loss to the Lions, but he is expected to return this week. That said, he is not going to have the same role he previously had as RB1 after three consecutive 100-yard rushing games from Braelon Allen, who also punched in this 21-yard TD (h/t NFL) in the loss to the Raiders.
Braelon Allen scores and now has 142 rushing yards on the day! LVvsNYJ on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/aGaC9Th33s
Hall is in a much different position than he was before the injury, but it would behoove the Jets to completely ignore him and not employ a workload split between the two. Allen briefly left the Week 8 game with an ankle injury before returning, but he should remain a key factor in the run game as Hall likely makes his long-awaited return.
The second overall pick missed the first game of his NFL career with a groin injury, but it is not out of the question that he returns on Sunday. Although he is currently listed as questionable as of Tuesday, Bailey's return cannot be ruled out, especially given his impact on the defense this season, with team highs in sacks (5.5) and forced fumbles (three).
The schedule will only get tougher, and the season will continue to get away from the Jets in a hurry at this point. But a strong week of practice and some encouraging signs could be enough to limit Bailey's absence and at least give the Jets some help up front that was lacking against the Raiders.
Although he has not made any starts, Mitchell appeared in the first six games of the season before missing the last two contests after suffering a concussion in practice. As a result, Mitchell must clear the NFL's five-stage concussion protocol to get back on the field, which is part of the reason he is still listed as questionable.
Additionally, logging practice reps will be crucial as well if Mitchell wants to show he is ready to return to live-game action.
The offensive line was instrumental in establishing lanes for Allen to take advantage of and giving quarterback Geno Smith plenty of time to throw against Las Vegas. It got healthier with the return of starting left guard Dylan Parham, but it remains to be seen whether the same applies to Mitchell for a unit that is showing a lot of potential.
Ossai has missed the last three games after suffering an ankle injury against the Browns in Week 5 and was held out of practice and ruled inactive for the Week 8 matchup with the Raiders . Still listed as questionable going into the Week 9 contest against the Chiefs, Ossai's return will depend on how much practice time he receives and what he can do with that opportunity as he looks to get back to full strength.
To make matters worse, Ossai was one of four defensive linemen who did not play this past week as injuries continue to take a toll and test New York's depth at this point in the season. He may not have to clear the concussion protocol like Mitchell will need to, but Ossai's return is still up in the air until he can log consistent reps in practice.
While players like T'Vondre Sweat (knee), David Onyemata (groin), Kiko Mauigoa (quad), Marcelino McCrary-Ball (ankle), Kingsley Jonathan (thigh), and Tyler Baron (knee) are on injured reserve and still have a chance of returning at some point, the same cannot be said for Braiden McGregor (torn pectoral) and Arian Smith (torn ACL).
Additionally, Tre Brown (undisclosed) and Chip Trayanum (neck) were lost before the season even began. Meanwhile, rookies VJ Payne (bone bruise) and Anez Cooper (shoulder) remain eligible to return even though they have yet to play a snap this season.

title: Getting Nahshon Wright Into Week 9 Lineup Is a No-Brainer Move Jets Can't Ignore
full_text:
From T'Vondre Sweat to David Bailey to Omar Cooper Jr., the Jets have seen plenty of their offseason additions make an early impact —even if a 2-6 record as of Week 9 is less than ideal. That said, one new face in Gotham that hasn't made much noise is veteran cornerback Nahshon Wright, who joined the Jets on a one-year contract after notching a career-high five interceptions and his first-ever Pro Bowl nod last season.
It's fair to say that Wright's presence in Gotham has been nearly invisible. The 28-year-old defender has been a healthy scratch for more games (four) than he's played (three), and he hasn't seen a single defensive snap—all 22 of his opportunities have come on special teams.
No matter how you dress it up, Wright has clearly fallen out of favor with head coach Aaron Glenn's staff. That said, Gang Green has two legitimate reasons to consider getting the former 2021 third-rounder on the field this weekend, especially with the trade deadline almost here.
One of the reasons why the Jets signed Wright was his defensive playmaking ability. Not only did he have five INTs with the Bears last season, but he also recovered three fumbles, showcasing the game-changing potential New York needed on defense.
While the Jets' defense has improved, their takeaway ability hasn't improved by much. Minkah Fitzpatrick's 27-yard interception against the Bears in Week 4 is still the only pick the Jets have recorded in their last 25 games. Sure, a few more were negated due to penalties this season, but that doesn't change the fact that winning will always be tougher if New York can't take the ball away.
Minkah Fitzpatrick gives the Jets their first INT in 636 pass attempts NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CQUCl4JVnt
His coverage skills occasionally left something to be desired in the Windy City, but Wright's knack for intercepting the ball could be what the Jets need right now.
Brandon Stephens is back in penalty trouble and struggling to defend consistently, so it might be worth seeing what Wright can do with a few snaps. Jarvis Brownlee Jr. has slowly become a concern in the slot , while rookie D'Angelo Ponds still needs more seasoning before New York trusts him in a full-time role. He's mostly played on the outside throughout his NFL career; however, Wright played a career-high 36 slot snaps with Chicago last season,  according to Pro Football Focus .
Patrick Mahomes's 1.7% INT rate is the lowest it's been in the last six seasons, but that doesn't mean he can't make mistakes. He's thrown four interceptions in the Chiefs' first seven games, including two in the last three. He also threw two INTs when he last faced the Jets in Week 4 of the 2023 campaign, giving Glenn more reason to dress Wright and see if lightning can strike twice.
Having Wright in the Week 9 lineup wouldn't just be about bolstering Gang Green's INT numbers; it'd be about potentially shoring up his trade value.
After all, this year's deadline is coming up on Nov. 10, and all signs point to general manager Darren Mougey putting on his seller hat for the next week. The Jets have too many issues to overcome for the playoffs to be a realistic goal, meaning it's in their best interest to move any veterans they have no intention of keeping long-term.
Since he's on a one-year contract with an affordable cap hit, Wright could be a rental target for contenders. Furthermore, an interested party would only need $833,333 in cap space to make a deal work, according to Spotrac , which is a lot easier to swallow than other potentially available names. A solid effort against Kansas City would add to that value, potentially leading to New York getting a better late-round pick in return.
Sunday's clash with the Chiefs is the last game before the trade deadline, meaning the Jets won't have another chance to maximize Wright's worth. They clearly don't plan to consistently use him, so they may as well cut their losses and get something back rather than nothing in March.

title: An Old Brandon Stephens Concern Has Quietly Reemerged for Jets
full_text:
Despite posting season-highs in points and rushing yards, the Jets fell to the Raiders Sunday, losing 38-33 at MetLife Stadium. The defense has experienced a sharp decline recently and has played a significant role in the team’s three-game losing streak.
After giving up just 95 total points over the first five games, New York has allowed 92 points over the past three. During this stretch, the secondary has been picked apart by opposing quarterbacks, allowing 227.3 passing yards per game, a 64.5% completion rate, eight touchdowns and zero interceptions.
Cornerback Brandon Stephens, who started the season strong, has fallen back into some of his bad habits.
After being penalized just three times last season, the six-year veteran has hurt the defense with costly mistakes, committing five penalties this year, four of which came over the past five games.
Against Las Vegas, Stephens was called for a blatant defensive pass interference on third-and-goal while trying to cover tight end Brock Bowers. This gave the Raiders a new set of downs, and they scored three plays later.
#Jets defense gets a stop on third and goal BUT get called for holding. Brandon Stephens. Why is Brandon Stephens on Brock Bowers? Not sure. But it's a fresh set of downs for the Raiders out of the half.
With the Jets dropping to 2-6 and their playoff hopes virtually out of reach, the team could be tempted to explore a trade for Stephens if his penalty problems continue.
Gang Green knew what they were getting themselves into when they signed Stephens to a three-year, $36 million contract in the 2025 offseason. The Texas native had a track record of drawing penalties with the Ravens, committing 19 over his four-year tenure, seven of which came in his final season.
Brandon Stephens's penalties
New York was hoping that, with D.J. Reed, who also had penalty issues, leaving for Detroit, Stephens’s physicality and strong play against the run would work well alongside CB1 Sauce Gardner. However, Gardner was traded ahead of the 2025 deadline , and Stephens was tasked with taking his role.
Although he committed just three penalties, Stephens struggled mightily in coverage, allowing 47 receptions (70 targets) for 509 yards and eight touchdowns, tied for the second-most among qualifying corners, per Pro Football Focus.
While Stephens's coverage grade slightly improved from 63 to 65.2 this season, per PFF , allowing just one touchdown across 289 coverage snaps, his run defense has declined from 75.7 to 64, the lowest mark of his career.
Additionally, Stephens's inability to create turnovers has held the secondary back. He’s produced just two interceptions, both coming during the 2023 season, and one forced fumble in his career.
Although Stephens was never known for his ball-hawking ability, he often fails to turn his head to locate the football and rarely attacks it when it's in the air. With New York having just one interception and 12 turnovers over the last 25 games, Stephens must do a better job of creating takeaways if he wants to remain in the team's long-term plans .
With the Jets likely to extend their playoff drought to 16 years, it would be wise to move on from Stephens and try to get some value in return. However, I don’t believe they should depart from him just yet.
If Gang Green can somehow pull an upset against the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium, what’s there to lose by trying to keep the current core together and trying to build on that momentum? Given that they have both the Colts and Cowboys first-round selections, they don’t have a strong reason to tank like other teams.
And given Stephens's recent struggles, the best the Jets could get for him is a fifth-round, or potentially a fourth-round selection, depending on how desperate a team is for cornerback help.
If New York keeps him but isn’t impressed with his performance, they can release him before the 2027 season with a $6 million dead cap hit , per Spotrac .

title: 5 Jets Are Officially Lost Causes Heading Into Week 9 vs. Chiefs
full_text:
"You are what your record says you are."
That line from Bill Parcells is a good indication of where the Jets are right now . There is a lot to feel good about when it comes to the future of the organization, but there are also major issues across the roster and coaching staff that remain problems.
Because of this, it's time to look at five people (or groups) who should be considered "lost causes" both in the present and beyond the 2026 NFL season. That list includes Jets players, positional units and coaches.
So let's get to it now as Gang Green prepares to visit the Chiefs in Week 9.
From a game management perspective, Aaron Glenn is making the same mistakes he made back in his first season . He's kicking field goals when the team needs to go for touchdowns, utilizing timeouts either too early or too late, and directly impacting games with his calls, whether he believes in them or not.
But these in-game adjustments could be forgiven, as they were with former head coach Robert Saleh at the beginning, if the team's defense played at an elite level.
So how has that gone? Well, Glenn's "superpower" as a play-caller resulted in the team giving up 38 points on Sunday to a mediocre Raiders offense , and 24 second-half points. He cannot simulate enough pressure; the team has issues in coverage, and the leader that Glenn hitched his wagon to is among the league leaders in missed tackles.
In short, there is nothing really positive that Glenn is bringing to the table that is actually helping the Jets win football games. And it's clear that he won't be back next season .
To say the last few weeks have been a disaster for Jarvis Brownlee Jr. would be an understatement. Last week, he was a healthy scratch for being late to several meetings. After seeing the field again on Sunday, Brownlee was repeatedly picked on in coverage.
Las Vegas targeted Brownlee four times, completed three passes and scored a touchdown. He was also targeted for two penalties (not including a third that was overturned on the field) and gave up a passer rating of 155.3. A perfect passer rating is 158.3, so the Raiders were nearly perfect when going after Brownlee .
From being late to meetings to putting up poor performances, it's time for the Jets to cut their losses with Brownlee, and see what second-round rookie D'Angelo Ponds can do going forward.
This one was the hardest to put up. A player as talented as Breece Hall should not be tossed aside, especially after earning a lucrative extension in the offseason.
But the reality is that the Jets are not going to have a choice.
It's not just that Braelon Allen is playing well , or that the Jets' rushing offense has taken a step in the right direction. It's the fact that Allen has been historically great for the team over the last five starts since Hall went down with his injury.
Allen is the first Jets' running back since Curtis Martin in 2004 to run for 100 yards in three straight games. He has recorded 419 yards on the ground in his last four games. Hall has never touched that total over his career.
To further emphasize how terrific Allen has been, if his production since becoming a starter were to be extended to a full 17-game season, then he would have over 1,800 yards and nine touchdowns. Those numbers would be the most in a single season in Jets history.
Hall is still a very good player, and one the Jets will covet as a complement to Allen, but his time as the feature back is over.
Darren Mougey has done a solid job as general manager so far in his year and a half with the team. That said, one spot has been an unequivocal disaster: the defensive line. Outside of 2026 draft picks David Bailey and Darrell Jackson Jr., there may be a total overhaul of this group next offseason.
Harrison Phillips and David Onyemata are on expiring deals, T'Vondre Sweat may not be a scheme fit, and the collection of pass rushers—including Joseph Ossai, Kingsley Enagbare, and Will McDonald IV— has not done enough either .
New York needs to start over across their front four. Bailey and Jackson are important pieces, but more needs to be done. The rest of the group may be out the door.
We're at the point now in the season where it's not just Glenn holding the team back. By January 2027, the entire coaching staff will most likely be overhauled . That includes offensive coordinator Frank Reich, special teams coordinator Chris Banjo, and prominent defensive positional coaches like Karl Dunbar.
There is a reason for this, of course. New York's players have not risen to the occasion when they have needed it most. If players wanted their positional coaches to remain, they needed to do a better job on the field than they have.
As of now, it's clear it's not just Glenn who will be gone; it's the rest of his staff. They haven't been remotely good enough in their own right.

title: Jets Rookie & Sophomore Power Rankings: Who's Rising (and Falling) Ahead of Week 9
full_text:
The Jets dropped another winnable game, losing to the Raiders 38-33 at MetLife Stadium. While questionable coaching decisions persist, such as calling a Hail Mary with 14 seconds left, Sunday’s loss was largely a result of the players’ failure to execute.
From a costly special teams touchdown to the defense surrendering 24 points in the second half, nothing went right for Gang Green.
With another humiliating loss in the books, New York drops to 2-6, and head coach Aaron Glenn’s hot seat is sizzling . Despite the defeat, there were some positives, including the offense’s red-hot performance and promising contributions from the young players.
With that said, let’s take a look at where the rookies and sophomores rank heading into the team’s Week 9 meeting with the Chiefs.
Note: Anez Cooper and VJ Payne are currently excluded from the list. Both Cooper and Payne are on injured reserve but are eligible to return after missing the first four games of the season.
With how things are unfolding this season, several players on this list likely won’t be on the team next year. One of them is Arian Smith.
The former Georgia Bulldog hasn’t proven that he can contribute beyond special teams or show any significant progression as a receiver. One thing New York will be looking for this offseason is to strengthen its depth at receiver.
Given Smith’s lack of production, it's safe to assume we’ve seen the last of him in green and white.
While the stats won’t tell the whole story, Geno Smith had one of his best seasons against Las Vegas. Playing against his former team, Smith completed 62.5% of his passes for 290 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception.
He was comfortable in the pocket, took shots downfield, and put the offense in scoring position more often than not. Smith did everything he could to help the team win, leading the offense to a season-high 33 points. The defense just didn’t hold up its end of the bargain.
Even though the loss isn’t on Smith, New York could turn to Cade Klubnik if the team can’t get into the win column over the coming weeks. With head coach Aaron Glenn on the hot seat and the Jets sitting at 2-6, upper management could want to see what they have with Klubnik once they are eliminated from playoff contention.
Once again, Kiko Mauigoa was inactive for Sunday’s matchup against the Raiders, as a lingering quadriceps injury has kept him out of five of the past six games.
Even though Mauigoa wouldn’t have changed the outcome, New York could have given him some reps, given how poorly Demario Davis has been this season .
Outside of his leadership and locker room presence, Davis just hasn’t cut it for the Jets. He’s regressed immensely in coverage and as a run defender, already recording 11 missed tackles so far.
While Mauigoa wasn’t significantly better in his rookie season, the Jets must consider giving him an opportunity if they continue to drop games.
If you told Jets fans a few months back that Malachi Moore played just nine defensive snaps across eight games, they would be surprised.
The former safety from Alabama has seen his starting role reduced to a depth role with the additions of Dane Belton and Minkah Fitzpatrick. Despite this, he’s made the most of his opportunity on special teams.
Although the unit allowed the first kickoff-return touchdown of the season, Moore has been New York’s most productive special teamer, recording eight tackles.
If his production continues and the Jets' losing streak extends, we should expect to see Moore earn reps on defense.
With Jarvis Brownlee Jr. listed as a healthy scratch last week and D’Angelo Ponds playing well in his absence, it felt like the Jets would lean more on their 50th overall selection at nickelback.
That wasn’t the case against the Raiders, however, as Ponds played just one defensive snap. Meanwhile, Brownlee played in 27 snaps and delivered another underwhelming showing, giving up a touchdown and committing two defensive pass-interference penalties (one accepted).
Additionally, his 27.8 coverage grade was the lowest among all Jets defenders , per Pro Football Focus.
With Brownlee underperforming and New York four games under .500, it’s time for Glenn to make a change and give Ponds the starting nickelback job. The team used a second-round pick on him, yet he’s played just 65 defensive snaps over six games.
We already know that, at best, Brownlee is a serviceable contributor. With Ponds, however, we have no clue what he can bring to the table. Now’s the time to start increasing his reps.
Another week, another quiet game for Kenyon Sadiq.
While the former Oregon Duck made a great 22-yard grab that set up Braleon Allen’s touchdown on the next play, Sadiq just hasn’t been involved or utilized since Week 3.
Offensive coordinator Frank Reich designed plays for him in the first four weeks: from jet sweeps to screen passes. Now, we don’t even see the Jets try to use his athleticism.
However, Reich isn’t entirely at fault. Sadiq hasn’t consistently created separation downfield, while Mason Taylor continues to outshine him as a pass catcher and blocker. While Sadiq has improved as a blocker over the last few weeks, it’s evident the team prefers Jeremy Ruckert and Jelani Woods on running downs.
At some point, Reich has to find a way to get him involved, much like the team tried to get Garrett Wilson going against Las Vegas.
Taylor wasn’t nearly as dominant as he was last week versus the Dolphins, but he still managed to haul in three catches for 19 yards on five targets.
It hasn’t been a pretty season for Taylor, but he continues to see an increased role in the offense since returning from a thumb injury, posting 15 receptions (20 targets) for 138 yards and two touchdowns across four games.
The former LSU Tiger has also stood out as a run blocker, earning a 67.5 run-blocking grade , per PFF . With his solid play as a receiver and blocker, Taylor remains the Jets’ TE1.
Omar Cooper Jr. has balled out since his return from the injured reserve. In the past two games, the former Indiana Hoosier has posted two consecutive 100-yard performances, showcasing his speed and playmaking ability.
Heading into Week 8’s matchup against the Raiders, it felt like Cooper would have another terrific game in store, considering how bad their secondary has been. However, Cooper was a complete non-factor, as he didn’t even receive a single target.
Yet, this isn’t a total surprise. With Wilson visibly frustrated by his lack of targets over the past few weeks, Reich and Co. needed to get him involved in every way possible. Additionally, with Mitchell back, he’s taken some of Cooper’s downfield opportunities.
Hopefully, Cooper can bounce back against Kansas City.
If you look solely at the stat sheet, you’d think Darrell Jackson Jr. had a quiet game. That couldn’t be any further from the truth, as the fourth-round selection was one of the few impactful defenders in the loss.
Playing a career-high 42 defensive snaps, he helped New York hold the Raiders to 95 rushing yards and 2.9 yards per carry. With his presence upfront, Jackson did an excellent job clogging running lanes and shutting down the Raiders in short-yardage situations.
His best play came late in the second quarter, when he and Harrison Phillips stopped the Raiders on a sneak attempt to force a turnover on downs. Although he didn’t generate pressure, Jackson continues to showcase that he can be a reliable contributor in the defensive line rotation.
With T’Vondre Sweat sidelined for the foreseeable future, the Jets will need to rely on the former Florida State Seminole.
Azareye’h Thomas started the season strong, emerging as one of the Jets’ breakout players in coverage. Over the past few weeks, however, Thomas’ play has steadily declined.
Against Las Vegas, Thomas allowed five catches (six targets) for 50 yards and a touchdown, earning a 50.4 coverage grade , per PFF . This marks the third straight game Thomas has finished with a coverage grade below 55.

title: Biggest Decision Aaron Glenn Got Wrong vs. Raiders Show What Needs to Change in Week 9
full_text:
Despite getting off to a much quicker start and leading by double digits in the second half, the Jets still found a way to suffer an excruciating 38-33 loss to the Raiders on Sunday at MetLife Stadium.
Even with a 100-yard receiver (Adonai Mitchell), a 100-yard rusher (Braelon Allen), more first downs (26-22) and the advantage in total yards (439-333), red-zone struggles, special teams issues and a poor defensive game plan came back to bite Gang Green in a game they will certainly want back.
Granted, rookie edge rusher David Bailey missed his first game with a groin injury , and the defense was without four of its starters overall on the D-line, but that is still no excuse for New York to drop its third straight game, all of which have been by single digits.
The Jets did feast on a Raiders rushing attack that averages the second-fewest yards per game (77.3 ypg), giving up just 95 total yards in the game. While that may have been the case, head coach Aaron Glenn did a poor job making defensive adjustments coming out of the break to ensure his team protected its lead and remained in control of the game.
From consistently leaving smaller corners on Raiders tight end Brock Bowers and allowing him to shred the middle of the field to costly third-down penalties and allowing three consecutive touchdowns out of the locker room, it was a second-half collapse for Glenn behind some more questionable coaching decisions.
With points on each of their first-half drives, everything appeared to be lining up well for the Jets to have a shot on Sunday. They even answered the Raiders' TD drive to begin the second half with one of their own to stretch the lead back to nine in the third quarter, but that is when the momentum started to shift in favor of Las Vegas.
The Raiders marched down the field on another 10-play, 65-yard drive to get within two and followed up a three-and-out from the Jets offense with a nine-play, 84-yard drive to take the lead early in the fourth quarter. Back-to-back three-and-outs ensued from both sides before the two teams traded field goals on their next two drives and set the stage for one last Jets drive trailing 38-33.
Despite advancing all the way down to the Raiders' 35-yard-line, offensive coordinator Frank Reich made the bizarre decision to go for a Hail Mary with 14 seconds on the clock instead of getting a little closer to the end zone with time to work with. That is when quarterback Geno Smith accounted for the game's only turnover as Jeremy Chinn came down with the toe-tapping interception (h/t The Goal Line Grind ) to end the game.
Jeremy Chinn seals the victory for the Raiders and shows off some toe drag swag for the INT off Geno Smith. pic.twitter.com/Eqd8TQpAH4
Glenn has made it clear that play-calling is his "superpower ," but it was anything but that in this game and has been for most of the season. The blown lead in the second half was one thing, as was the offense's inability to convert in the red zone (2-of-6) and on third down (4-of-11), but the decision to isolate New York's smaller corners on Bowers proved detrimental.
Between Bowers (seven catches, 92 yards, two TDs) and Michael Mayer (five catches, 53 yards), Glenn failed to find an answer for either of them or make the appropriate adjustments to account for the success they were having. That, in turn, allowed QB Kirk Cousins to establish a rhythm and the Raiders offense to stay on the field, even without a go-to wide receiver on the field.
There is no denying that the 95-yard kickoff return from Dylan Laube was the difference in the game for the Raiders in a five-point outcome, but the Jets still did more than enough offensively to come away with the win. The defense, however, could not put a full game together and could not get the timely stops that were needed to secure the victory.
The Jets hit the road again to take on the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, and if they want to avoid another frustrating outcome and pull off the upset, Glenn needs to simplify his defensive approach and be willing to adapt to what is happening on the field.
His superpowers failed against the Raiders and it is important that he can get his unit to eliminate the back-breaking penalties and make it tougher on opposing QBs to establish any rhythm. After all, Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes always keeps opposing defenses guessing with his versatility and ability to evade pressure in the pocket. Running back Kenneth Walker III, meanwhile, has the third-most rush yards in the league (770) and has been an absolute force in his first season with the franchise.
After giving up a combined 92 points over the last three games, when you include the kickoff return from Sunday's game, Glenn needs to become more flexible with his schemes and disguise some of his coverage, especially if the Jets want to create more red-zone stops after allowing the Raiders to convert all four of their attempts.
There were a lot of positives to take from the Week 8 loss, but if Glenn is going to have his bunch ready to face the challenge the Chiefs will present on Sunday, he has to be willing to make defensive adjustments throughout the game.
If he fails to do that and keeps making questionable decisions with his schemes, it could get ugly this week and moving forward as his time in Gotham continues to run out.

title: Jonathan Greenard's Early Eagles Woes Force Vic Fangio to Defend Disappointing Start
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — It’s been a frustrating season not only for Jonathan Greenard but for those who thought he’d be the key ingredient to the Eagles' pass rush this season. It's at the point where he's being talked about as a Bryce Huff 2.0 in some circles.
No need to rehash just how bad Huff was . Greenard is not Huff.
Vic Fangio gave his thoughts on the team’s big offseason acquisition who is still looking for his first sack with the Eagles.
“What I see is a guy who has had very, very little practice,” the Eagles’ defensive coordinator said. “I mean, when I say very little, minuscule. Okay?”
Greenard missed all of training camp with a pec strain. He didn’t play until Week 3, and then it wasn’t long after his return that he injured his ankle. He played 19 snaps the following week, but the ankle wasn’t quite ready to let him play in Week 5, so he missed that game as well.
“(Jonathan) missed the first two weeks of the season; no practice,” Fangio said. “Started practicing, was on a pitch count, played 19 plays. Was gonna increase the next week, got hurt early in that game. Didn't finish that game, didn't play the next game, and he's been limited in practice. You know, contrary to some people's popular belief, practice is important.”
“Practice is important for everybody,” Fangio said. “He's just not into a groove, you know? He's not totally comfortable in our system and what we want him to do. It's not because he doesn't know or doesn't want to. It's just that he hasn't executed it. Walkthroughs are an assignment check. It's not an execution. I don't know if I've had a guy that's had so little practice."
Surely Fangio has had a player who practiced as little or less than Greenard in his 40 years in the business, but you get the idea.
There is another factor in play here; his contract.
The Eagles signed Greenard to a $98 million extension , and the weight of it could be forcing Greenard to press when he’s in to prove he was worth the investment. It could also explain why he could be playing even though he perhaps shouldn’t be.
The Week 10 bye could help Greenard keep getting healthier, and maybe he can show Eagles fans what he is capable of delivering. Right now, though, it hasn’t been much, with just two tackles and one quarterback hit in 118 snaps (33%).

title: 3 Potential Eagles Trade Chips That No One Is Talking About to Begin Week 9
full_text:
To say the Eagles' season has not gone to plan would be putting it lightly.
As of Week 9, the Eagles sit at 2-6 after dropping six straight games for the first time since 2012. It's a streak that likely puts general manager Howie Roseman in the business of selling ahead of the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10.
There are a number of obvious trade chips at his disposal. Cornerback Tariq Woolen could bring championship experience to a secondary and is playing on a one-year deal. Tight end Dallas Goedert could add a new element to a contending offense and will be a free agent at the end of the campaign.
Roseman has never been someone to take the obvious route, though. He will drop the hammer on a blockbuster deal or snag players flying under the radar if it improves his roster. The possibilities are endless.
Here's a look at the three Eagles trade chips that no one is talking about.
Nolan Smith should be one of the most popular names at the trade deadline, yet his name has only just started floating around. The Georgia product has posted 15 tackles and four sacks across seven games in 2026. He recorded 10.5 sacks and two forced fumbles during his first three NFL seasons.
Philadelphia committed over $100 million to defensive end Jonathan Greenard, so he isn't going anywhere anytime soon. Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia has also reported that the Eagles "still really like Jalyx Hunt."
Hunt could prove to be more affordable in extension talks than Smith.
That leaves Smith expendable, especially considering his value. Philly picked up his fifth-year option. That means any team that acquires Smith would have him under contract for 2027 as well, with a projected affordable cap hit of $2.8 million , per Spotrac . A high-motor pro who can win with speed on the edge and squeeze running lanes should entice contenders.
That extra year gives Roseman a chance to be aggressive, so expect an asking price of a Day 2 pick.
Offensive lineman Fred Johnson was an underrated part of Philly's Super Bowl run in 2024, starting six games when Jordan Mailata and Lane Johnson battled injuries. He returned to the Eagles via trade to start eight more games in 2025 before being re-signed to a one-year deal in March of 2026.
Lane Johnson's abrupt retirement ahead of Week 5 opened a spot in the offensive line, but the Eagles opted to give rookie Markel Bell the nod. Philly has to see if he has the skills to stick around. As a result, Fred Johnson has only been on the field for 16 offensive snaps and 20 special teams snaps.
Johnson has proven he can step in at a moment's notice and will likely only require a seventh-round pick to acquire him. Roseman would be smart to get whatever he can for someone buried on the depth chart. That late-round pick could end up being what he needs to trade up in April.
Byron Young is likely better known for sharing a name with a prominent Rams pass rusher than for his contributions in Philly. The former Alabama star is a rotational piece at defensive tackle, playing 27% of the defensive snaps in 2026. He was on the field for 30% of defensive snaps in 2025.
Young has totaled 56 tackles and 2.5 sacks in 31 career games. He uses his large frame (6'3", 292 lbs) to be an anchor in run defense and drive linemen back in pass defense. It's worth noting he still has room for development at 25 years old, too.
Young will be a free agent next offseason.
Defensive tackle is becoming an incredibly important position in the NFL, and an injury can hinder a contender at any moment. Cheap players like Young should be getting more attention. Roseman could net another late-round pick, while opening up playing time for second-year pro Ty Robinson.

title: Kracz: Nick Sirianni's Approach to Eagles' Losing Streak Feels Completely Wrong
full_text:
The Eagles have suffered back-to-back beatdowns in primetime . National TV audiences saw them get torched by the Cowboys on Monday night, then laid to waste by the Commanders six days later on Sunday night.
It’s the first real low point the Eagles have had in 14 years. That was 2012, when Andy Reid's team lost eight in a row, and then he lost his job.
Sirianni was a 31-year-old offensive quality control coach at the time with Reid’s next team, the Chiefs. Now, Sirianni is in the eye of the storm .
Reid fired offensive coordinator Juan Castillo in 2012, but the Eagles were still just 3-3 when Reid pulled the plug on the miscast Castillo. When a season is swirling down the drain, most people want major changes, either to personnel, coaches or approach.
Sirianni isn’t like most people.
That’s not to say he isn’t averse to making an in-season change. Sirianni did it when he demoted Sean Desai in the 2023 season, only to fire him weeks later. That was totally different than now. The Eagles were 10-3.
Now, they are 2-6. Not doing something drastic in this situation feels like the wrong move, but then again, I don’t have 61 regular-season wins, one Super Bowl title and two Super Bowl trips on my resume.
Still, doesn’t at least one head have to roll here just to appease a fan base that, based on a much smaller crowd of fans that made the relatively short drive to Northwest Stadium in Landover, MD, is losing interest?
Sean Mannion is staying put as the offensive coordinator.
“We understand, Sean [and] myself, that when it's not going the way we want it to go, the blame will fall on us,” Sirianni said on Monday. “That is our job. We truly do feel that way as far as coaches. Whether it is an execution thing, whether it is a scheme thing, whether it is a fundamental thing, whatever it is, it's our job as coaches to be problem solvers.
“This is never just on one person. So, I'm not making any changes there. It is on all of us to figure out how to get things going in the right direction.”
Chris Kuper will remain the offensive line coach.
“Chris is coaching his [butt] off,” Sirianni said. “He's fighting his [butt] off; he's coaching his [butt] off on a daily basis. You guys don't get to see that. I get it on a daily basis. You get to see that for three hours on Sunday, but he's coaching his [butt] off, and he's fighting his [butt] off, and I know he's giving the players good tools to use fundamentally and helping them be the best players that they possibly can be. But we all have to be better, and we know that.”
Tanner McKee will make his fourth straight start after going 0-3 in his first three, so b ackup and newcomer Joe Milton won’t be taking over this week when the Eagles host the Giants in Week 9.
“Tanner's our guy,” Sirianni said. “We're not making any changes there.”
Sirianni has said repeatedly that everything is on the table. Except it really isn’t. He said there have been some behind-the-scenes changes, but nobody is privy to them.
“I won’t get into any of that,” he said. “I don't know if that benefits us, but we'll continue to do the things that we need to put it on the right track. That's our job. How are we going to be problem solvers as coaches? That's what we're working on doing.”
It doesn’t feel like enough.

title: Eagles Week 8 Report Card: Grading Every Position After Sunday's Loss vs. Commanders
full_text:
The Eagles' nightmare season continued with a 27-10 loss to the Commanders in Week 8. They have now lost six straight games for the first time since 2012. This also marks the first time the team has started 2-6 since 1999, which was Andy Reid's first year as head coach.
The struggles that have plagued the Eagles for over a month returned on Sunday Night Football. Philly jumped out to a 10-0 lead before stalled offensive possessions and shaky defense allowed Washington to take over. The Eagles were outgained 339-268 and shut out in the second half.
Before looking ahead to a Week 9 clash against the Giants, let's hand out some grades for each unit following another demoralizing defeat.
Quarterback Tanner McKee's outing on Sunday was simply not good enough. The fourth-year pro's third-quarter fumble erased Philly's momentum, and his fourth-quarter interception all but ended the game. He failed to throw a touchdown pass for the first time in his five career starts.
McKee has been heralded as an accurate pocket passer, yet 10 of his 23 completions came behind the line of scrimmage in Week 8. Whether or not play calls are holding him back, he is hesitating to throw into tight windows. Jeff Kerr emphasized just how poorly the offense has performed with McKee.
The #Eagles offense -- in 3 games Tanner McKee has started PPG -- 15.0 (29th in #NFL ) Yards Per Play -- 4.2 (32nd) Passer Rating -- 76.6 (26th) Yards Per Attempt -- 5.6 (31st) Yards Per Game -- 270.3 (30th) Pass % -- 64.9% (2nd) Points Per Possession - 1.4 (28th) 3-and-out % --…
Eagles running backs logged 64 rushing yards on 24 carries on Sunday night. The duo of Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell averaged a lackluster 2.7 yards per carry and did not have a single rush for more than nine yards. Philly is averaging the sixth-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL (88.1).
Now, it's worth pointing out that Barkley is not fully healthy and Mitchell is Philly's RB6. Asking either one to carry an offense missing its stars would be foolish. Barkley isn't helping this squad by playing 32% of the offensive snaps, though. Sitting out in Week 9 would give him nearly three weeks to rest.
DeVonta Smith's hamstring injury and Dontayvion Wicks's ankle injury hindered the Eagles in Week 8. Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, and Hollywood Brown played the majority of the wide receiver snaps with those two sidelined. Cooper and Brown barely made a ripple, totaling 36 yards on four catches.
Lemon flashed his upside for the second straight week, recording 57 yards on six catches (nine targets). The rookie is using crisp routes to get open on passing plays and draw defenders away on running plays. Lemon's increased impact should be a top storyline in the second half of the season.
Philadelphia tight ends put in a solid effort in Week 8. Dallas Goedert finished with 30 yards on four receptions. He has been on the field for at least 69% of the snaps and posted a catch of 15 yards or more in five of his six games played. Those stats should maintain his value in the trade market .
Rookie TE Eli Stowers impressed during his 13 snaps, hauling in three passes for 53 yards. The second-round pick was explosive after the catch and should see more action as the season progresses. This grade is brought down a bit by more blocking struggles from Johnny Mundt and Grant Calcaterra.
Jordan Mailata praising "Jeff Stoutland University" in his Sunday Night Football intro made fans reminisce about what used to be Philly's biggest strength. The offensive line has become the team's biggest weakness in 2026. Running lanes are not opening up, and McKee is not being protected.
Washington generated pressure on 46.5% of dropbacks versus Philly and posted 10 pressures on 12 blitzes (h/t NFL+). It resulted in a whopping five sacks for the Commanders. Free rushers got in McKee's face within seconds as Landon Dickerson and Markel Bell whiffed on crucial blocks.
Washington mixed up looks all night long but what in the world has happened to this Eagles front five. This is unacceptable at the highest level of the sport. pic.twitter.com/RWza2lCVix
There were a few highlight plays from the defensive line on Sunday, with two sacks and four tackles for loss. However, the Eagles gave up 135 rushing yards on 26 carries. They have surrendered over 100 rushing yards in each of their first eight games. That hasn't happened in Philadelphia since 1968.
A failure to stop the run not only tires out Philly's defense, but it also puts pressure on the secondary to be perfect. Every mistake becomes costly. Committing more than $300 million to Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, and Jonathan Greenard has hurt the team more than it has helped so far this season.
Jeremiah Trotter Jr. stepped up in place of the injured Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) on Sunday, leading the Eagles with 10 tackles. It'll be interesting to see if Trotter takes over the ILB2 role moving forward. The former Clemson standout has shown glimpses of improved instincts and technique.
Meanwhile, veteran Zack Baun stayed consistent with seven tackles and a fumble recovery. It's important to hold Baun and Trotter. accountable in run defense. The easiest way to combat open running lanes is by making tackles at the second level. That isn't happening as often as it needs to.
If there's any room to move away from defensive doom and gloom, it's in Philly's secondary. Safety Andrew Makuba forced a first-quarter fumble deep in Washington territory that spurred the Eagles' only touchdown drive of the contest. The Texas product finished with nine tackles and a pass breakup.
FLIPPING THE FIELD pic.twitter.com/hfqKnSxz0C
The Eagles held quarterback Jayden Daniels to a 55.2% completion rate by jumping passing lanes and forcing low throws. Depth issues came into question, though, as cornerback Kenny Moore II was picked on for an eight-yard touchdown pass, a 30-yard completion, and a 20-yard completion.
Braden Mann is the only reason this grade is not an F. The veteran punter landed three of his five punts inside the 20-yard line. Otherwise, the special teams unit was a disaster. Kicker Jake Elliott missed a 41-yard field goal that would've turned a six-point deficit into three during the third quarter.
It has to be mentioned that Philly's kick/punt coverage continues to put the defense in tough spots, too. Washington's Luke McCaffrey's sole kickoff return of the night went to the 50-yard line, and his sole punt return went to the 50-yard line as well.
The Eagles lost the field position battle yet again.

title: 3 Eagles Who Won't Survive the Trade Deadline After Losing Streak Reaches 6 Games
full_text:
Changes are coming for the Eagles after they dropped their sixth consecutive game to the hapless Commanders on Sunday Night Football. With the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline right around the corner, some of those changes will be imminent.
Here's a look at three Eagles players who will likely be continuing their careers elsewhere outside of Philadelphia after the deadline.
It almost feels like the writing is on the wall when it comes to Landon Dickerson's future in Philadelphia. The Eagles are in the midst of a complete overhaul of the offensive line following the retirement of Lane Johnson and the trade of Cam Jurgens, and Dickerson could be the next player on the line to be traded .
Dickerson has spent the bulk of the current campaign on the sideline due to injury, and when he has played, he hasn't been great. He did decently against Dallas in Week 7, but he played poorly against the Commanders in Week 8. He hasn't played enough snaps to qualify for a Pro Football Focus ranking, but his grades at his position are all well below league average.
For the Eagles, it feels like the right time to just pull the bandage off, move on from Dickerson and spend the rest of the season evaluating young players along the offensive line to see if any have a future with the franchise as a potential building block.
During an appearance on 97.5 The Fanatic following Philadelphia's Week 8 loss to Washington, Ryan Fowler of NBC Sports Philadelphia named Dickerson as a player to keep an eye on leading up to the deadline.
"Keep an eye on Landon Dickerson," Fowler said. ". . . I don't think he's healthy still. I think he's a guy who's battling, similar to what Saquon Barkley is doing. He's trying, but at the end of the day you're not going to make excuses for anybody. It's just not good enough right now, and I think Landon Dickerson, along with those guys you just mentioned, is a name to know as we approach the deadline."
At this point, it feels like it would be a surprise if Dickerson were still on Philadelphia's roster after the deadline.
This is almost painful to write, given how integral Dallas Goedert has been to Philadelphia's offensive attack for the past decade, basically.
But it certainly feels like his time with the Eagles could be coming to an end in the near future, and that's not an indictment of Goedert. He'sstill a productive player at his position, and that could make him intriguing for contending teams in a potential trade. He's currently playing on a one-year deal, so it might make sense for the Eagles to try to get something in return for him, as opposed to potentially losing him for nothing in free agency.
Tanner McKee connects with Dallas Goedert for the first down! PHIvsWAS on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/dpHuatfr1Z
Rookie tight end Eli Stowers is finally healthy, and he had his most productive and promising performance of the season against the Commanders in Week 8, as he caught three passes for 53 yards and also showed promise as a blocker. This could provide the Eagles with additional reason to move on from Goedert. In a lost season, it would be beneficial for Stowers to get increased on-field opportunity so that the team can see exactly what they have in him.
There's really no reason for the Eagles to hang on to Riq Woolen at this point.
They're not legitimate contenders in the NFC, so it doesn't really matter who they trot out at cornerback opposite Quinyon Mitchell. And it's not like Woolen has been great anyway. He's been average in coverage , according to PFF, and he leads the team in penalties this season with five. He's been called for a holding penalty in each of Philadelphia's last two losses.
Woolen, who is playing on a one-year contract, doesn't appear to have a real future in Philly, so it would make sense for the Birds to flip him for some draft capital before the deadline.

title: McMullen: Eagles Might Have a Nick Sirianni Problem After Loss to Commanders
full_text:
LANDOVER, M.D. — With his team in freefall, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni has spent the past several weeks stressing the idea of attention to detail.
The message landed with team leaders like Saquon Barkley and Jordan Mailata, and the trains have run on time from Monday through Saturday if you believe the self-scouting, only to derail on game days.
On Sunday night at Northwest Stadium, the Eagles opened an early 10-0 lead, while trying to halt the only five-game losing streak in the Sirianni era, only to watch the limited Commanders lap Philadelphia with 27 unanswered points the rest of the night, sending Sirianni into “uncharted territory.”
A frustrated Sirianni played what's becoming an all-too-familiar hit, holding himself accountable while shielding his assistant coaches and players.
“Until we coach better, until we have better detail as coaches, until our players play with better detail, then we’re gonna see the same results,” he said. “And that falls on me."
“I feel like with all the detail that’s not happening right now, I got to try a different approach. And so that’s 100% on me. With how many of those issues are happening right now, I’ll do everything I can to try different things to make sure that we’re getting that point across.”
Detail is literally part of Sirianni's coaching mantra of “tough, detailed, together.” The coach is obsessed with “mastering the things that require no talent,” yet in the biggest moment of the game, the Eagles draped themselves in unforced errors.
Trailing 16-10, Philadelphia was moving the football and preparing to go for a fourth-and-four conversion at the Washington 13-yard line with 9:04 left in the game.
The Eagles were late on the play clock as Tanner McKee began imploring for the snap. Feeling the urgency, rookie right tackle Markel Bell moved early, forcing the Eagles into a 36-yard field goal attempt that Jake Elliott drilled.
That successful kick would have made it a 16-13 game with plenty of time to keep pressing, but the attempt was wiped out because Jordan Mailata was not on the line of scrimmage. The illegal formation penalty backed the kick up five yards, and Elliott banged it off the left upright.
DOINK 🚨 PHIvsWAS on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qtlhWoqpGe
The Eagles got nothing out of the drive.
Subsequently, the Commanders responded with an eight-play, 45-yard march, ending with a 42-yard Drew Stevens field goal—his fourth of the night—making it a two-possession game, 19-10 with only 3:43 remaining.
A six-game skid for the Eagles was assured, not to mention being outclassed by two division foes with a combined record of 5-9-1 on national television in less than a week.
Straining for answers, Sirianni mused about messaging.
Mailata was angered by his own miscue, throwing a tablet to the ground after rewatching his mistake on the sideline.
"It sucked the wind out of our momentum," Mailata admitted.
You can blame Bell, McKee, Mailata, Elliott, or all of the above, and that's kind of the point. In the ultimate team game, too many are contributing to the Eagles' poor results.
Sirianni, though, wears the product on his sleeve.
“Every product on that field—Offense, defense, special teams, fundamentals, situational football, player making a mistake, coach making a mistake—that’s my freaking job,” Sirianni said. “And so I’m pissed at myself, and I know I’ll fight like hell to do everything I can to get it fixed.”
When discussing a conservative offensive approach at the end of the first half instead of a bolder approach, Sirianni sounded defeated.
“That’s just kind of a product of what we have been," he admitted.
And that product has now bled over to the other phases.
"I feel like we’re doing a great job in practice and throughout the week,” Barkley said. “And for some reason, it’s not transferring over to the football field when it matters most.”
The Eagles are 2-6 because those details have gone missing when the bright lights are on. Whether that will be corrected or just another routine postmortem against the Giants in Week 9 will be decided on the field, not in lip service.

title: 5 Losers & 2 Winners From Eagles' Loss to Commanders in Week 8
full_text:
Changes are coming to the Eagles. How can they not be after not showing any signs of turning things around in their sixth straight loss —a 27-10 defeat by the Commanders in a game that saw the home team score 27 unanswered points after Philly took an early 10-0 lead?
Those changes could come as soon as their bye week, which kicks in after they host the NFC East-leading Giants in Week 9
Until then, here are some winners and losers. Mostly losers:
Nick Sirianni, HC: The head coach’s seat is very hot, to say the least . If his team loses out, which is a distinct possibility, Sirianni is probably gone. He can still save his job by turning things around, but this team certainly doesn’t give any confidence that a win is anywhere in the near future.
Sean Mannion, OC: The offensive coordinator could only find a way to score 10 points against a team that was giving up 28 per game. Sirianni was asked afterward if he was thinking of making a change with the OC.
“I'm not thinking about any of that stuff right now,” he said. “I got a bunch of guys in that locker room that are hurting—every player, every coach. Right now, I'm getting through this moment with those guys. I'm not thinking about any of that stuff right now. … I got a lot of faith in everybody in that locker room.”
The Eagles’ had just two plays that gained more than 20 yards and the longest one – a 34-yard pass to rookie Eli Stowers came with just two seconds left and the Commanders’ defense not pressing.
Michael Clay, STC: The special teams coordinator has had his hands full filling his units with healthy bodies, but he won’t use that as an excuse, nor should he. The kickoff team gave up a 47-yard return to start the game that would have led to a quick 3-0 lead, except rookie Drew Stevens missed a 55-yard field goal. That wasn’t the case at the end of the first half when a 27-yard punt return put Washington at midfield with 50 seconds to play. That led to a 39-yard field goal with 23 seconds to go, and a 13-10 Commanders lead at halftime.
Riq Woolen, CB: The cornerback keeps giving up too many completions and too many yards. And he had his second straight game with a holding penalty. It might not be
Markel Bell, OT: It was bound to happen sooner or later that the rookie third-round pick would melt in the spotlight. He’s done well for the most part since stepping in at right tackle after the abrupt retirement of Lane Johnson. Sunday night was his worst game yet.
Bell surrendered two sacks and was called for a costly motion penalty to turn fourth-and -three at Washington’s 14 midway through the fourth quarter into fourth-and-eight. The Eagles had been lined up to go for it on fourth down, but the penalty changed Sirianni’s mind, and he opted to send out the field goal team.
Jake Elliott made the 36-yard kick, but Jordan Mailata was called for an illegal formation penalty. The re-kick, from 41 yards, hit the upright.
Saquon Barkley, RB: What a leader he is . Despite battling hamstring and back injuries, Barkley played 22 snaps, got 13 carries and posted 30 yards. He scored the Eagles’ only touchdown and a direct snap, three-yard run in the first quarter. It was his second straight game with a rushing TD. He also made a nifty 24-yard catch off a wheel route to the 2-yard line that set up his TD.
Barkley never sat down the entire game, trying to keep his back from tightening up.
Jeremiah Trotter Jr., LB: Did the Eagles miss injured Jihaad Campbell, who didn’t play? It didn’t look like it. Trotter led the team with 10 tackles while playing 54 snaps (90%).

title: 9 Eagles Observations After Commanders Hand Philly a 6th Straight Loss in Week 8 SNF
full_text:
Move over Andy Reid’s 2012 team. You have company. The Eagles lost their sixth straight game on Sunday night , and that is the first time the organization has lost this many in a row since Reid’s last year, when the losing streak reached eight.
The Eagles went 4-12 and Reid was fired after that dismal season.
The Eagles are now 2-6 after Sunday night’s 27-10 loss to the host Commanders. They went winless in October and started November with another loss. They haven’t tasted victory since Sept. 20, when Jalen Hurts drove the offense for a game-winning touchdown against the Titans in Nashville.
It’s fair to wonder if head coach Nick Sirianni will suffer the same fate as Reid did in 2012. Yes, the Eagles are banged up, but nothing seems to be getting better. Maybe in small snippets they do, but not enough to find a way to win a game.
There are too many mistakes, such as left tackle Jordan Mailata not lining up on the line of scrimmage on a 36-yard field goal made by Jake Elliott. Pushed back five yards, Elliott hit the top of the left upright with about nine minutes to play, keeping the score at 16-10.
The effort seemed better, but again, that didn’t help win a game. The run defense was still not nearly good enough, allowing the Commanders to run for 135 yards, and the offense still cannot find a consistent rhythm.
The Eagles jumped to a 10-0 lead, doing all their scoring in the first quarter, but they couldn’t score a single point over the final three quarters. The Commanders methodically scored 27 unanswered points, getting four field goals from rookie kicker Drew Stevens.
Making his third start, quarterback Tanner McKee was again too inconsistent. He had a costly fumble late in the third quarter just as the Eagles had pulled into a long-range field-goal attempt at minimum. Rookie Markel Bell allowed the strip-sack. McKee, who also threw an interception, was sacked five times.
The Commanders cashed the turnover into a field goal and a 16-10 lead with 1:33 to go in the third quarter.
1. Three-and-outs: The Eagles had fewer of them. After going three-and-out on their first possession, the offense had just one more.
2. Points: The Eagles doubled their first-quarter point output for the season, putting up 10 points. They had been outscored 40-10 coming in and now it’s 43-20 after taking a 10-3 lead into the second quarter.
3. Fumble recovery: The Eagles finally got one. It happened in the first quarter when Drew Mukuba belted tight end Chig Okonkwo after catching the ball. Zack Baun fell on it to set up the offense at the 26, and they turned it into a 3-yard touchdown run by Saquon Barkley.
FUMBLE 🗣️ Zack Baun recovers for the Eagles! PHIvsWAS on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CbAEhq9j0k
The Eagles were the only team in the NFL not to recover a fumble. That streak is over. Still, it was just the fourth turnover the defense has forced all season.
4. First road start: It was McKee's first start on the road,  and he entered the game for the first time not trailing. He led the offense to 10 points before the Commanders got off the deck and started carving up the Eagles’ defense. McKee cooled off, too, and the Eagles didn’t do anything after that.
5. Eli Stowers: Hey, the rookie tight end made his first catch, which went for seven yards on second-and-six in the third quarter. He finished with three catches for 53 yards.
6. Tyler Steen: The offensive line struggled mightily even though Washington was without the injured Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw, but Steen’s play was particularly glaring. And not in a good way.
7. Unblocked pressure: The Eagles allowed a pivotal sack in the first half when it appeared the offensive line slid right, allowing a free rusher to sack McKee. It was Landon Dickerson who stepped right, allowing the rusher to get home. That could either be a bad scheme by line coach Chris Kuper or a miscommunication about what the Commanders were showing. Maybe both.
8. Pass rush: It’s still too inconsistent, though it showed some life. Jalen Carter notched a big sack to force a punt midway through the third quarter. It was his fourth of the season to take over the team lead, one ahead of Nolan Smith.
Jalen Carter and Jonathan Greenard teaming up for the SACK! PHIvsWAS on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QB0jrdQCHq
Smith forged back into a tie with a fourth-quarter sack. The outside linebacker also clobbered Jayden Daniels at the end of the first half on a dropback. Still, the Eagles have 10 sacks this season.
Oh, there was a Jonathan Greenard sighting but only because he jumped offsides to negate an interception from Mukuba in the end zone.
9. Third downs: The worst team in the league at converting third downs at 30.9%, the Commanders converted five of 13 (38.5%).

title: Eagles-Commanders Stock Market: Collapse Continues in DC
full_text:
LANDOVER, MD - After a 2-0 start this season, the Eagles are now 2-6 after losing a sixth straight game in the shadow of the nation's capital against the Washington Commanders.
In a microcosm of the season, Philadelphia got off to a 10-0 start on Sunday night and never scored again en route to an ugly 27-10 setback.
A very limited team due to circumstance that has included everything from significant injury attrition to questionable coaching and the retirement Land Johnson, the once powerful Eagles were outgained for the eights consecutive time this season with the Commanders piling up 339 yards to 268 for Philadelphia, the latter number buoyed by the garbage time of the last drive of the night.
The Eagles are now 0-2 in a key three-game stretch against NFL East foes in what's considered a bad division, a run that will finish against the first place New York Giants (4-2-1), who will be coming off their bye week next Sunday.
With tonight's loss, the Eagles are now at the bottom of the division. Dallas (3-5) is in second despite losing to Arizona in troubling fashion Sunday, and the Commanders leapfrogged the Eagles with their second win (2-4-1).
SAQUON BARKLEY'S HEART - There wasn't much to like in this game but Barkley played despite hamstring and back injuries because he felt he could and that his team needed him. In a Super Bowl-or-bust society, the fact that Barkley didn't embrace the tanking mentality is the kind of culture setter that is meaningful in the NFL.
It wasn't great statistically -- 13 carries for 30 yards and a reception for 24 yards -- but the lone touchdown was all Barkley with the 24-yard catch on a wheel route and a three-yard scoring run after a turnover.
LONG-SUFFERING WASHINGTON FANS - For years, the Commanders fans have had to take it as their Eagles peers would invade Northwest Stadium and take over. While Washington is not exactly lighting the league on fire, its faithful enjoyed serenading the Eagles fans out of the stadium in the waning moments. It felt like a cleansing for a long-suffering fanbase although the suffering looks far from done inside the Beltway.
ATTENTION TO DETAIL - Nick Sirianni has claimed that the detail hasn't always been there during the Eagles' skid. That showed up in the fourth quarter when a promising drive that could have stolen the game was quickly derailed by a series of mistakes that "take no talent."
Trailing 16-10, Philadelphia was preparing to go for a fourth-and-four conversion at the Washington 13-yard line with 9:04 left in the game. The Eagles were late in the play clock, as Tanner McKee began imploring for the snap. Feeling the urgency rookie right tackle Markel Bell moved early, forcing the Eagles into a 36-yard field goal attempt that Jake Elliott made drilled.
That worst-case would have made it 16-13 with plenty of time to keep pressing but the kick was wiped out because Jordan Mailata was not on the line of scrimmage. The illegal formation backed the kick up five yards and Elliott banged it off the left upright.
The Eagles got nothing out of the drive. In turn, the Commanders responed with an eight play, 45-yard marching, ending with a 42-yard Drew Stevens field goal -- his fourth of the night -- that made it a two-possession game, 19-10, with only 3:43 remaining.
PLAY ACTION - Everyone should have someone who believes in them like Sean Mannion believes in play action. No matter how ugly George Halas' creation looks in Philadelphia, Mannion is going to throw out 13 personnel with poor blocking tight ends and watch his quarterbacks turn their backs to heat-seeking missiles on the blitz.
THE PASS RUSH - It’s almost amazing that the Eagles have not been able to generate any real consistent pressure with an interior that includes Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis and Moro Ojomo, and an edge group of Jonathan Greenard, Nolan Smith and Jalyx Hunt .
The front has been the key to their success for a very long time and the organization invested heaving in Carter, Davis and Greenard this offseason. The Eagles had just three pressures in the first halft and nine total with two somewhat emoty sacks. The lone bright spot was one strong rush by Smith that seemed to rattle Jayden Daniels for a stretch.
In a Vic Fangio defense, the four-man rush has to be significantly better to generate the expected success.

title: Emerging Eagles' Defensive Concern Needs an Answer to End Losing Streak in Week 8
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Head coach Nick Sirianni found nothing wrong with the Eagles' effort in Monday night’s loss to the Cowboys . Nothing. Nada. Zip.
He stated it unequivocally, too, during the week: “I did not see an effort issue on Monday night. … There were other things. But effort in no way, shape [or] form was an issue here.”
Two days later, Jordan Davis contradicted his coach.
“It was poor from everybody, and that's just simple and plain about it,” the Eagles defensive tackle said. “It was poor.”
Linebacker Zack Baun pulled no punches when asked if the effort level was up to par. “I do not, no,” he said succinctly.
Sirianni is a player's coach, so hopefully he is just saying publicly that there was no issue with effort, and behind the scenes he is harping on it. It was apparent to those who watched the Cowboys dust the Eagles by 17 points that effort was an issue.
The turnaround has to start on Sunday night when the Eagles visit the Commanders in another primetime game.
Is that even possible at this point?
While key offensive players have been injured at historic levels, the Eagles defense has remained mostly healthy—save for Jonathan Greenard, who can’t seem to shake an ankle injury that has dogged him the last few weeks.
There is talent on the defense. It simply didn’t go away overnight.
“When I first got in the league, they let me know the NFL's not easy to win in,” Jalen Carter said. “It's gonna be hard, day in and day out. And this year's proven that it's hard to win in the NFL and that we just gotta change things now, change things around.”
It should start with effort, and the way to turn that around is through leadership. Who in the Eagles’ locker room has stood up to demand that effort on defense?
There’s no issue on the offensive side, where Jordan Mailata stood in the middle of the Lincoln Financial Field locker room shortly after it opened after a loss to the Panthers, telling reporters he would take their questions right then and there. He was still dressed in full pads and was beginning to unlatch his shoulder pads as he took questions.
Saquon Barkley spoke for more than 15 minutes after the loss to Dallas. Landon Dickerson was on the verge of tears after losing to the Cowboys, saying he played horribly.
Meanwhile, the only players on defense who spoke after losing to Dallas were Cooper DeJean and Jihaad Campbell.
Davis said he thinks players aren’t having fun, that they are approaching things as a “job,” and not enjoying themselves.
“You ask anybody in this locker room, you're not having fun playing the game; it kinda seems like a... That's when it really seems like a job,” Davis said. “When you're having fun, it doesn't seem like a job. It feels like something that you get to do; you have to enjoy this game. It's gonna be wins and losses and everything, and that's in life. You have to find those little moments to enjoy, and right now we're trying to find those little moments, those little wins.”
Nakobe Dean was the player who held everyone accountable. The linebacker made sure his teammates were having fun, whether he was on the sidelines, in practice, in the locker room, or in a game.
This isn’t to relitigate the decision to let Dean walk in free agency to Las Vegas on a three-year, $36 million contract. It's simply to ask: who is the leader of the defense? That is to be determined. Maybe it will be Davis.
“We know what we're capable of,” he said. “We've reached the highest of highs. We've seen the lowest of lows now. We have to do something to fix it, and that's one of the things that we've been a part of in practice this week: fixing the effort. We have to give effort.”

title: Jack Sawyer Shares Worrying News on Steelers' Sebastian Joseph-Day
full_text:
Pittsburgh Steelers EDGE rusher Jack Sawyer offered a worrying update about Sebastian Joseph-Day, who's currently on the reserve/injured list with a triceps injury.
Sawyer told Gerry Dulac on 102.5 WDVE's "Chalk Talk" that while the Steelers are "looking forward" to Derrick Harmon's eventual return from IR, there's a chance Joseph-Day misses the rest of the season.
"Obviously, we're looking forward to getting Derrick back. It sucks we're not gonna be able to get Sebastian back for- maybe at all," Sawyer said.
Head coach Mike McCarthy stated last week that he thought, "they'll all have a chance to come back," when referencing Pittsburgh's players who are on IR.
If Sawyer's comments are any indication, however, Joseph-Day's odds of a return in 2026 are up in the air.
Joseph-Day signed a two-year, $11 million deal as a free agent with the Steelers this past offseason.
He was a little banged up during training camp and did not play throughout the preseason, though he was back on the field and ready to go by the time Week 1 rolled around.
Joseph-Day was on the field for 111 defensive snaps through Week 6, which made up 29 percent of Pittsburgh's total reps on that side of the ball (per Pro Football Reference ), and he logged 10 tackles with a fumble recovery over that span.
The 31-year-old was later placed on IR ahead of the team's Week 7 matchup with the New Orleans Saints in Paris, however.
Joseph-Day will miss four games at the absolute minimum while on IR, meaning he isn't eligible to be activated until Week 12 regardless of his status.
Given Sawyer's comments, though, Joseph-Day's timeline for a return now appears to be stretched out.
The exact nature of his injury isn't yet known, but it seems like it's rather significant if there's even a chance that he won't play again this season.
As a key rotational piece, potentially losing Joseph-Day for the remainder of the campaign would deliver a blow to a Steelers' defense that's emerged as one of the league's elite units .
Pittsburgh has an impressive amount of talent and depth along the interior of its defensive line. While it's not ideal, it could likely withstand a long-term absence of Joseph-Day.
Cameron Heyward and Keeanu Benton have both played at a high level this season. The same could be said for Harmon before he went down with a foot injury in Week 4, and the hope is that he's back sooner rather than later now that he can technically be activated from IR after missing the minimum of four games.
Yahya Black has also excelled at nose tackle, and sixth-round rookie Gabriel Rubio has stepped up in a big way, playing 70 defensive snaps over the Steelers' last four games.
Even undrafted rookie Kevin Jobity Jr. has gotten into the mix since Joseph-Day landed on IR, garnering 25 defensive snaps over the past two weeks and recording his first sack in the team's Week 8 win over the Cleveland Browns.
