title: Let's Be Real About Steelers' Trade Deadline
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers need help at the NFL trade deadline. They're 6-2, in first place in the AFC North and tied for the second-best record in the conference.
But does that mean they're going to shoot for the stars? And if they do, are they certain they'll land a deal, or is there a chance they'll fall back to Earth with nothing to show for their efforts?
Or, even worse, another veteran addition that matches the contributions of Mike Williams, Adam Thielen and others whom they tried to utilize to "fix" their wide receiver problem in recent years.
Let's be real about the Pittsburgh Steelers' trade deadline. There's plenty to dive into.
The Steelers could use help at wide receiver and cornerback . They're going to look into both positions as the deadline approaches. Wide receiver ranks first on their priority list, but they won't ignore cornerback if the right name is available.
The only problem with the cornerback position is that there aren't many big names available. This team doesn't need a starter; they need a depth addition. Someone to provide reps they hoped Sean Murphy-Bunting would when they signed him off of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers practice squad.
As for wideout, they can look a little bigger. They need immediate help while Roman Wilson (finger) and Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) are on Injured Reserve. So, whoever they do end up getting - if anyone - will come in with a shot to step into the rotation on day one and then sort of fill in as needed once players start to return from injury.
So far, we know the Steelers have shown interest in Indianapolis Colts' Josh Downs, and then there are rumors floating around that New York Jets' Garrett Wilson could be a name to watch.
Brian Thomas Jr. from the Jacksonville Jaguars is probably on their list as well.
As for cornerback, there are no known names Pittsburgh has their sights on. Nahshon Wright, Altontae Taylor and Amik Robertson are all expected to be available at the deadline. SI's Albert Breer made the connection of Washington Commanders' Mike Sainristil as an option as well.
And if they're ready to fully take advantage of the Colts' fire sale, Charvarius Ward could be a veteran name to watch.
Here's the thing, this is a new Pittsburgh Steelers team. That's exciting for fans.
Mike Tomlin isn't ready to carry this group of players through the mud and into the "dance." That's just not how this organization is going to operate anymore, and that may be a blessing. Not that what Tomlin did wasn't impressive.
This is a team that believes they are real contenders, as they should. They want to win the AFC North and move into the playoffs, but they want to WIN in the playoffs.
They want a Super Bowl, and they're watching contenders around them make Super Bowl-caliber moves.
So, what happens? Well, only time will tell. But this is a team ready to win it all. Those teams generally make "win it all" moves this time of year , and that's what you should expect from the Steelers.
Maybe it's only one trade, and maybe it's not Garrett Wilson. But don't expect the Steelers to leave next Tuesday empty-handed. And don't expect them to trade for a last-resort option to save their wide receiver room.
There are big names available. The Steelers feel ready to land one.
That's what likely happens at the trade deadline.
Noah Strackbein is a Publisher for On SI, covering the Pittsburgh Steelers since 2019. A Jessup, PA native, Noah attended Point Park University, where he fell in love with the Steel City and everything it has to offer. You can find Noah's work at Steelers On SI and weekdays as the hosts of All Steelers Talk.

title: Steelers Defense Deserves an Offensive Trade
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers' defense is incredible. Through the first eight weeks of the NFL season, this group is an undisputed top-5 defensive unit and they are just hitting their stride. After a 27-6 win over the Cleveland Browns, the Steelers improved to 6-2 and sit at the top of the AFC North and conference standings.
It's hard to dispute that this defense is Super Bowl-caliber. They have star power, the statistics to back it up, and multiple players with championship experience to draw from.
The offense, on the other hand, still needs upgrades and improvements. As the Steelers enter the bye week and rapidly approach the NFL Trade Deadline, general manager Omar Khan must add the playmaking wide receiver they need. Otherwise, they risk squandering one of the best defenses in recent franchise history.
The defense passes the eye test with flying colors, but what makes it so impressive are the numbers that back it up.
Let's start with their pass rush, the heart and soul of this group. Led by 7.5 sacks from T.J. Watt , the Steelers have posted a league-leading 26.0 team sacks through the first eight games. And they're doing it without dialing up the blitz. According to data from SumerSports, the Steelers send pressure just 36.5% of the time and blitz even less, sending the house just 26.7% of the time. Despite this, they are wreaking havoc on opposing quarterbacks.
And while they give up yards, this defense is the definition of bend-don't-break. They've allowed the seventh-most total passing yards this season, but they've allowed the fewest passing touchdowns, giving up just seven in the first eight contests.
This defense is also full of playmakers and turnover machines. According to ESPN team data, the Steelers have forced 13 takeaways this season, tying for the third-most in the NFL. The defense has seven interceptions through eight games, tied for the fifth-most.
They've also caused disruption, even when it doesn't lead to a turnover. They have the most pass breakups of any secondary this year, with 50 passes interrupted by the Steelers' secondary. SumerSports data shows they have also forced 10 fumbles despite only recovering five of them.
By nearly every metric, this defense is one of the best in the NFL. It's so good, in fact, that it could carry this team to a second consecutive division championship. But to rely so heavily on this group could backfire, and that's why this team needs to do something to bring a similar balance to the offensive side of the ball.
The Steelers thought they figured out the passing attack in the offseason, and I give them credit for the attempt. In theory, the addition of Michael Pittman Jr. and drafting Germie Bernard was the needed depth at wide receiver.
Bernard has been great, but he's still a rookie and is earning quarterback Aaron Rodgers' trust. Pittman hasn't played since Week 4, and there is no clear return date for the veteran pass-catcher.
With just days until the deadline, the Steelers have to treat this year like the all-in campaign they claim it to be. Rodgers is doing enough, Jaylen Warren is playing like the best running back in the NFL and the offensive line is firing on all cylinders.
The only other need that must be filled is wide receiver depth. DK Metcalf is not consistent enough right now to be a true top wide receiver. Combine that with the injuries, and this offense needs an outside addition.
The team has been linked to multiple players on the trade block. From Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs to bigger names like Los Angeles Chargers pass-catcher Ladd McConkey, the Steelers keep popping up in the NFL rumors and rumblings.
The team has to act before they can't. This defense is one of the best this franchise has produced in recent memory, and their Hall of Fame quarterback is in his final year in the league. If this team really wants to go for it, they have to add a playmaker. Otherwise, this year will go down as nothing but a wasted opportunity.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Linked to Commanders CB With Ties to Coaching Staff
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers have a week until the Nov. 10 trade deadline, and while offense has been the main source of discussion, the defense could always use some help.
The Steelers have put up one of the best defenses this season, but the secondary likely needs some reinforcements and one trade target could seriously help them.
Albert Breer of SI.com wrote that Washington Commanders cornerback Mike Sainristil is one player who could be available at the trade deadline.
"I don’t think the Commanders are sellers yet—they’re actually still just two games back of the Giants in the NFC East. But they’ve gotten calls about guys. And one player I’ve heard that could be available is 2024 second-round corner Mike Sainristil," Breer wrote. "After playing over 80% of the team’s defensive snaps in Washington’s first two games, he’s played less than half every week since. On Sunday against Philadelphia, he played only on special teams."
Sainristil has ties with the Steelers, as secondary coach Joe Whitt Jr. was previously the Commanders' defensive coordinator and worked with Sainristil in his first two NFL seasons.
The Steelers secondary has been a solid unit, but injuries have hurt their depth over recent weeks.
Cornerbacks Brandin Echols and Doneiko Slaughter both missed the 26-7 blowout of the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium in Week 8 with hamstring injuries.
Jalen Ramsey is the only nickelback/slot corner the Steelers have healthy at the moment, and relying on the 32-year-old to stay healthy all season is risky.
Sainristil could feature there, or even help provide help for Asante Samuel Jr. and Jamel Dean, the two starting cornerbacks.
Daylen Everette, Terell Smith and Sean Murphy-Bunting are also healthy cornerback options for the Steelers.
Sainristil played for five seasons at Michigan under Jim Harbaugh and won the National Championship for the 2023 season, earning First-Team All-American honors.
He excelled for the Wolverines during that campaign, with six interceptions, two pick-sixes, four tackles for loss, a sack and two forced fumbles.
The Commanders took Sainristil in the second round of the 2024 NFL Draft (50th overall), and he signed a four-year rookie contract.
Sainristil had a strong rookie season, starting 16 of 17 games played at cornerback, with 93 tackles (62 solo), a tackle for loss, two interceptions, 14 passes defended and one forced fumble.
He helped the Commanders make the playoffs with a 12-5 record and the NFC Championship Game, making two interceptions in the 45-31 road win over the Detroit Lions in the NFL Divisional Round.
Sainristil started 14 of 17 games for Washington in 2025, spending some time at nickelback and also going outside too, with 85 tackles (51 solo), a tackle for loss, four interceptions, 12 passes defended and a forced fumble.
He's seen less time this season, with just two starts in six games, 17 tackles (14 solo) and a tackle for loss.
Sainristil has had some coverage issues in 2026, with a 71.4% completion rate on passes thrown his way, 15-of-21 for 196 yards and six touchdowns.

He would write for Pittsburgh Sports Now after college and has years of experience covering sports across Pittsburgh.

title: Steelers Urged to Move On From DK Metcalf
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers are in a good spot at the bye week at 6-2, but there is one player who hasn't lived up to expectations.
Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf hasn't had the season he or the team hoped for, and it's drawn criticism from Colin Cowherd, who admonished the veteran on his show, " The Herd," on FOX Sports
“The DK Metcalf thing, it’s not working," Cowherd said. "Like, Aaron, I think is almost throwing to him out of a feel that he should, he’s expensive, he’s DK Metcalf, like, it’s not working and the cap hit is enormous. It triples.
"I mean, I look at that, and I’m like, I almost think it’s time to move off him now and get out of that business and let Aaron concentrate on the guys, on the younger guys."
It's been a tough year for Metcalf, who has 33 catches on 64 targets for 378 yards and one touchdown in 2026.
Metcalf had his worst game in a Steelers uniform in the 27-6 blowout win over the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium in Week 8.
He made just one catch for four yards on six targets and bobbled a ball on what should've been a 40-yard completion from Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers, and instead it ended up in the hands of Browns cornerback Denzel Ward for an interception.
Metcalf has had some good games, including five catches for 95 yards in the 27-24 loss to the Browns at Huntington Bank Field in Week 4 and a season-best 11 catches for 93 yards in the 26-19 overtime win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium in Week 6.
The issue is that outside of those two contests, he has a combined 17 catches for 170 yards across the other six games.
Rodgers has spread the passing attack out more, targeting other options to keep the ball moving and score points.
Steelers running back Jaylen Warren is second with 25 catches for 294 yards, rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard has 32 catches for 284 yards, tight end Pat Friermuth has 25 catches for 234 yards and fellow tight end Darnell Washington is breaking out with 11 catches for 254 yards.
The Steelers traded for Metcalf back on March 9, 2025, sending their 2025 second-round pick (52nd overall) to the Seattle Seahawks.
Pittsburgh then signed Metcalf to a five-year, $150 million contract extension, with the Steelers committing four years and $132 million from 2026 to 2029.
The Steelers restructured Metcalf's contract this offseason, converting his base salary ($23.6 million) into a signing bonus, but he still has a large contract remaining.
If the Steelers move on from Metcalf, they would have to incur a huge cap hit, that they are unlikely to do, unless his play continues to get worse.
Don't expect the Steelers to move on from Metcalf just yet, but they need much more from their wideout going forward.

title: Steelers Hit Home Run With Patrick Graham Hire
full_text:
Defensive coordinator Patrick Graham has come in and immediately made his mark during his first season with the Pittsburgh Steelers .
While ranking all of the best new coordinators around the NFL, CBS Sports' Garrett Podell slotted Graham in at the No. 2 spot, only behind Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator and former Arizona Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon.
“The Pittsburgh Steelers’ defense has come back to life under new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham," Podell wrote . "They’re the league’s No. 3 scoring defense (18.0 points per game allowed), No. 6 total defense (305.6 total yards per game allowed), No. 3 run defense (83.9 rushing yards per game allowed), No. 8 third down defense (34.3% third down conversion rate allowed), No. 2 red zone defense (37.5% third down conversion rate allowed) and tied for No. 3 in takeaways (13).
"Having All-Pro edge rusher T.J. Watt turning back the clock also helps. After he had just 7.0 sacks in 14 games last season, Watt has 7.5 in eight games this season, which is tied for the league lead with  Texans All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. No team has more sacks in the NFL than Graham's unit's 26, one more than the Brian Flores blitzkrieg Minnesota Vikings attack."
Though it's only about the halfway point of the season for the Steelers , who are sitting at 6-2 and have rode a four-game win streak into their Week 9 bye, the early returns on Graham's work with the defense are overwhelmingly positive.
Along with all of the metrics Podell laid out, which includes giving up the sixth-fewest total yards and third-fewest points per game, the unit is also tied for the fifth-fewest EPA per play allowed (-0.12) while being tied for the sixth-best missed tackle rate (10.4 percent), according to SumerSports .
The defense is reaching heights thus far that it hasn't in quite some time. In 2025 under head coach Mike Tomlin and defensive coordinator Teryl Austin, the group allowed the seventh-most yards per game (356.9) and ranked right in the middle of the league at No. 16 for points allowed per contest (22.8).
Pittsburgh's defense was strong during the 2024 campaign, allowing the 12th-fewest yards per game (326.7) and eighth-fewest points per game (20.4), but those totals still don't sniff what Graham and company have accomplished thus far.
You'd have to go all the way back to 2020 for comparable production of the unit, as they gave up the third-fewest yards (305.8) and points (19.5) per game that season en route to a 12-4 record that also saw them open the year 11-0.
Pittsburgh's offense has also taken a step forward this season, particularly with Jaylen Warren and  the ground game, with head coach Mike McCarthy calling the plays.
As things currently stand, though, the defense is the backbone of the team and is the unit that will propel the Steelers to the type of playoff success that's eluded the franchise over the past decade.
From the 2023 Kansas City Chiefs to the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and the 2025 Seattle Seahawks, we've now seen three elite defensive teams win the last three Super Bowls.
Though there's still plenty of season left, Pittsburgh's defense is playing at a similar level , which will give the team a chance to compete against anyone and go on a run should they make the playoffs.
Graham really has breathed new life into the unit, and it's provided the Steelers with their highest ceiling in years as a result.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Defense Reaching Super Bowl Level
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers defense is elite.
The Steelers have played just eight games during the 2026 season, jumping out to a 6-2 record. The road to that impressive start hasn't been perfect, but the defense has paved the way.
This was the case once again in Week 8 against the Cleveland Browns. The group has become a weekly symbol of an approach best summarized as opportunistic, and it's propelled this team into Super Bowl contender status midway through the regular season.
When defensive coordinator Patrick Graham joined the staff under new head coach Mike McCarthy, excitement washed over the organization and the fanbase. Sure, Graham didn't have the best years in that same role with the Las Vegas Raiders, but he showed two things that made him a perfect addition in Pittsburgh.
The first is creativity. Graham constantly changed up his disguises pre-snap, adapted his approach in-game, and found ways to move his star players around the field. So far with the Steelers, that's been the case. Graham has adjusted as a coach, going from calling plays in the booth to the sidelines after the first few games.
He's displayed a willingness to change and respond, and his defense is mirroring that on a weekly basis.
The second was an old-school, physical attitude. He set the tone at training camp, demonstrating proper form during drills and getting right up in the mix with his players. It's a small thing, but that energy and tone-setting are infectious. The entire defense would run through a wall for Graham, and opposing offenses pay the price.
The bread and butter of this defense is, of course, their pass rush. It's not just that their outside linebackers are game-wreckers. Yes, that is true, as T.J. Watt has 5.5 sacks to begin the year, Alex Highsmith has 3.5 and Nick Herbig has 3.0.
What makes this pass rush so fearsome, however, is their defensive line. They are a group of absolute monsters at the point of attack. Even as injuries have taken away two key players, they continue to create pressure and wreak havoc on opposing quarterbacks.
That's helped the Steelers produce an NFL-leading 26.0 sacks and the third-most takeaways through Week 8 of the regular season.
That's all a testament to Graham's impact on this defense. The Steelers regularly produce sacks, but this year is different. They are nasty, fearsome and momentum-generating.
Even when the offense has faltered, the defense has carried the team. It's still a bit early to make this comparison in good faith, but it's becoming harder and harder to deny the similarities between this defense and some of the best ones in the organization's history.
And that's putting the Steelers on the level of Super Bowl contenders.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Could Upgrade With Garrett Wilson's WR Teammate
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers won't play their next game until after the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline. After a drudging of the Cleveland Browns, the Steelers earned their upcoming bye week.
After the brief break, the Steelers buckle in for a difficult second half of the regular season. The next nine games feature two contests against the Baltimore Ravens, another meeting with the Cincinnati Bengals, a cross-state battle with the Philadelphia Eagles, and games against top AFC teams, the Denver Broncos and Jacksonville Jaguars.
The Steelers need to bolster the offense before this year's deadline passes. In an ideal world, they would spend the necessary capital, whether it’s draft picks or roster players, to bring in another top-tier pass-catcher for Aaron Rodgers to target. More realistically, or at least a more skeptical view of the situation, is to anticipate a Day 3 pick going to another franchise for a wide receiver three or four on the depth chart.
That’s a lot less exciting, but it doesn’t mean the Steelers won’t acquire an impactful receiver. In fact, there might be one overlooked option that could be just that.
New York Jets wide receiver Adonai Mitchell has quietly put together an impressive start to the 2026 season, and for very little cost, the Steelers could add someone who brings an explosive dynamic to their offense.
Everyone is talking about Garrett Wilson and rumors of Pittsburgh's interest, but maybe they can go with a smaller name that fits their outlook a little better.
What stands out about Mitchell’s 2026 campaign is his ability to form chemistry with a veteran quarterback. The 24-year-old Mitchell has quickly become a trusted target for Jets quarterback Geno Smith. Over the first two weeks, Smith targeted him 15 times, connecting for nine receptions and 123 yards.
A finger injury suffered in practice robbed him of playing in Weeks 3 through 6, and the passing game in New York suffered.
Despite missing time, Mitchell quickly got back to being a productive receiver. He was held off the stat sheet in Week 7, but he posted a monstrous performance in Week 8 against the Las Vegas Raiders. The Jets dropped the contest, but Mitchell produced seven receptions on nine targets for 142 yards and a touchdown.
What has made Mitchell so effective is complex, but one reason is his explosive lower body. The 6’2”, 205-pound receiver is long and agile, and he’s been beating defenses over the top repeatedly. He's averaging 16.6 yards per reception this season, highlighted by posting 20.3 yards per catch against the Raiders in Week 8. His speed created trouble all game for the Las Vegas secondary, and he was able to put up multiple big plays.
That’s exactly what the Steelers need. They haven’t had anyone who could stretch the field with consistency in 2026. At times, DK Metcalf has been that player, but inconsistencies continue to underscore his season.
Mitchell gives them that option as an outside threat. The speedy receiver has been lined up on the outside for 71% of his offensive snaps this season, according to data from SumerSports . And when he lines up out wide, he possesses a high chance of producing an explosive play. Pulling from the same data compiled from SumerSports, Mitchell has a 25% explosive play rate in 2026. In layman's terms, that means one out of four plays he's involved in goes for 20 yards or more.
What also makes Mitchell a realistic trade target for the Steelers is the cost to acquire him from the Jets. New York is once again at the bottom of the NFL standings and staring down a top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. They surely have a need for young talent moving forward, but is Mitchell an important part of their continued rebuild?
The Jets acquired Mitchell as part of the trade return for cornerback Sauce Gardner last season. The Jets are the clear-cut winners of that deal, securing two first-round picks from the Indianapolis Colts in addition to Mitchell in exchange for Gardner.
So, to be fair, the Jets clearly value Mitchell. That doesn’t mean, however, that they are unwilling to move on from him.
The Steelers have learned the price for receivers around the NFL right now, and it’s reportedly a bit steep. The Colts want a third-round pick for wide receiver Josh Downs.
But if the Steelers want to expend that draft pick, Mitchell is an overlooked, but far better fit. He gives the team a much-needed playmaker on the outside, allowing Metcalf and rookie Germie Bernard the chance to keep growing in their current roles.
I don’t think it would take a third-round pick, however. The Steelers don’t hold a 2027 fourth-round draft pick, but they do own that choice in 2028. If the Steelers don’t want to give up a Day 2 draft pick to bring in another receiver, they can still improve the offense if they target Adonai Mitchell.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: T.J. Watt Makes History in Steelers Win Over Browns
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns renewed the hatred in their AFC North rivalry during their Week 8 contest. The Steelers routed their divisional foes, winning by a final score of 27-6.
The win evened the season series between the Steelers and Browns and kept Pittsburgh atop the AFC North standings.
The game was highlighted by the defense's ability to get to the Browns' quarterback. The Steelers sacked Deshaun Watson eight times, led by superstar T.J. Watt with 2.0 sacks on the day. With that performance, Watt now has 19.5 sacks against Cleveland in his career. According to Assistant Director of Communications for the Steelers, Michael Bertsch, that is the most by any individual against the Browns.
"T.J. Watt now has 19.5 career sacks vs. Cleveland," he wrote. "Which is the most by any player against the Browns in League history. He is the ninth player in NFL history to hold sack record vs. multiple teams."
The other team that Watt holds the sacks record against is the Baltimore Ravens. Watt has produced 17.0 sacks against the Ravens in his career.
T.J. Watt now has 19.5 career sacks vs. Cleveland, which is the most by any player against the Browns in League history. He is the ninth player in NFL history to hold sack record vs. multiple teams (Cleveland, 19.5; Baltimore, 17.0). #HereWeGo #CLEvsPIT #BertschyBits
Watt adds yet another accolade to his long list of accomplishments in the NFL. Elected to eight consecutive Pro Bowls and named First-Team All-Pro four times, Watt is now officially the most productive pass rusher the Browns and Ravens have gone up against.
But more importantly for Watt and the Steelers is the fact that this team is cruising as the bye week arrives. Following their fourth consecutive victory, the Steelers are at the top of the AFC North and one of the best teams in the NFL.
With the bye week coming at the perfect time, there is a feeling in Pittsburgh that this team might be a contender.
With the latest two sacks, Watt is trying to renew his campaign for Defensive Player of the Year, a far cry from the hopes of Cleveland's head coach Todd Monken and his offense. They had to suffer through a monstrous performance by Watt, and it should put him back among the best defensive players in the league.
Through the first seven games, he has 17 total tackles, 11 of which have been recorded individually. He also has nine quarterback hits, seven tackles for loss, 5.5 sacks, a forced fumble, a fumble recovery, an interception and two pass batted down at the line of scrimmage.
It's been an All-Pro-caliber season for Watt, and his production is a key reason why the Steelers have a fearsome defense and a 6-2 record.
And the Browns keep learning firsthand just how elite Watt still is.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: 'Stay Tuned': Insider Hints at Steelers' Garrett Wilson Trade Interest
full_text:
An NFL insider seems to think that there's something potentially brewing between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the New York Jets when it comes to star wide receiver Garrett Wilson.
On X, Jason La Canfora responded with, "Stay tuned," after Dave Dameshek wrote, "Color me...INTRIGUED," after the former initially connected Wilson to the Steelers.
Stay tuned https://t.co/xX8jPjFwhB
Pittsburgh is 6-2 as it begins its Week 9 bye after blowing out the Cleveland Browns 27-6 this past weekend. The franchise has been connected to a number of different wide receivers ahead of the November 10 trade deadline, though all signs have pointed to Wilson not being available, which makes La Canfora's report eye-opening.
In an interview on November 2, La Canfora explained why Wilson could intrigue the Steelers as a possible target over the next week.
“I'd keep an eye on the Pittsburgh Steelers. I'm told they're being pretty ambitious behind the scenes and would love to add another playmaker," La Canfora said . "DK Metcalf has some limitations in terms of the route tree he runs, but if you were to add someone like Garrett Wilson to that offense, it starts to get really interesting. With the tight ends they have, a running back like Jaylen Warren who can catch a lot of passes, and Metcalf stretching the field on go routes, adding a receiver like Wilson would give them another dynamic dimension. That could be a very intriguing offense.”
ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on October 31 that a "well-placed source" stated there was "no way" Wilson was moved by New York ahead of the deadline, and he also told reporters last week "no" when asked if he will or has asked for a trade (per SNY's Connor Hughes ).
La Canfora has pushed back on that notion , though, and perhaps the door is still at least a little open for the Steelers and Jets to come together and make a mega deal.
With 527 yards and three touchdowns on 43 receptions over eight games this season, Wilson has proved himself to be a top-10, if not better, receiver in the league.
New York has struggled to the tune of a 2-6 record, but it does own three first-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft and has plenty of assets that could help it turn things around rather quickly.
Because Wilson is a building block piece who signed a four-year extension worth $130 million in July 2025, there aren't a ton of reasons for the Jets to consider moving him unless he makes it abundantly clear that he wants out, which doesn't appear likely to occur at this stage.
Wilson and Aaron Rodgers, who were teammates with New York in 2023 and 2024, don't seem to have much of a relationship either.
In fact, The Athletic's Zach Rosenblatt reported last year that the pair, "weren’t exactly the best of friends," by the time their final season together concluded, and that they, "took subtle shots at each other in press conferences."
Considering it would take at least one first-round pick and then some to acquire Wilson, the Steelers might have some real reservations about parting with a treasure trove of assets in order to bring Wilson in if he and Rodgers won't be on the same page.
For that reason, it's hard to imagine Pittsburgh being a realistic landing spot for Wilson for the time being, even if he were to ever hit the trade block before the deadline arrives.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: One Stunning Number Sums Up Seahawks’ Lopsided Loss to Bears
full_text:
A clash of reigning division champions turned one-sided on Monday night in the Pacific Northwest. The Chicago Bears marched 80 yards in 17 plays for a touchdown on the opening possession of their clash with the Seattle Seahawks. Ben Johnson’s team took a 7-0 lead that they would never relinquish on the way to a decisive 34-17 triumph over the Seattle Seahawks.
It was the worst loss by Mike Macdonald’s squad since a 30-13 home prime time setback to the Green Bay Packers i n Week 15 of 2024. And eight weeks into 2026, the defending Super Bowl champions have already dropped one more games than it did all of last season, when they concluded a 17-3 overall campaign by hosting a Lombardi Trophy.
How truly stunning was the 17-point setback? As the sideline leader of the Seahawks, Macdonald owns a 31-14 overall record, which includes the team’s three-game postseason run in 2025, and it was just the fifth time the team lost a game by double digits.
And just how odd was it that the club lost by such a margin? Go back to 2025 and the team’s only three defeats that season were to the San Francisco 49ers (17-13), Tampa Bay Buccaneers (38-35), and Los Angeles Rams (21-19). Entering last Monday night’s battle with Johnson’s team, there were losses at the hands of the Washington Commanders (33-31), the 49ers (32-29) , and a Thursday night overtime setback to the Denver Broncos (17-14) in Week 6 this season.
3 FOR D'ANDRE SWIFT 🎩 #NFL #Bears #DaBears #Seahawks #GoHawks #CHIvsSEA pic.twitter.com/OMkHpCPdfM
This is easy math. Combine the margin of defeat in those six losses and it adds up to 17 points—equaling the surprising result on Monday evening at Lumen Field. Spooky stuff, indeed, post Halloween.
Coincidence aside, it was indeed a disturbing Monday night for Macdonald and company. The visiting Bears won the total yardage battle (363-252) and owned time of possession, 35:03-24:57. Chicago totaled 35 running plays for 126 yards. D'Andre Swift ran for 69 of those yards and three touchdowns.
Sam Darnold's pass is deflected and intercepted by Chicago! That Bears front has been relentless all night. Darnold didn't even realize it was picked off and started slowly jogging off the field. pic.twitter.com/9GQP5gNVkS
And while turnovers were a big part of Seattle’s regular-season showing in 2025, quarterback Sam Darnold finds himself in unchartered personal territory. In 2026, his completion percentage is a shaky 60.2 percent. He’s thrown for 10 scores opposed to nine interceptions. Darnold has been picked off at least once in six straight games, the longest-such streak of his nine-year NFL career.
Obviously, there’s a chance to rebound on Sunday against the division-rival Cardinals, who the Seahawks have defeated 10 straight times. But Monday night’s uncharacteristic lopsided loss by the Macdonald’s team was certainly an eye-opener.

title: Seahawks' Mike Macdonald Has a Request Ahead of Cardinals Game
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are 1-3 in their last four games , but things could be looking up as they take on the last-place Arizona Cardinals in their Week 9 matchup.
The Seahawks have already beaten the Cardinals this season, and it was arguably their most dominant performance of the year to date. The Seahawks scored 31 points and held the Cardinals to just a touchdown and 151 total yards throughout the game. Head coach Mike Macdonald hopes that version of the Seahawks comes to the field against the Cardinals.
"We have to focus on recapturing us and making sure that we're us when we turn the tape on. There were too many times throughout that game where that wasn't us in terms of just our style of ball. That's where we need to get better," Macdonald said.
The mindset of the Seahawks remains the same as it was at the beginning of the season. They want to do whatever it takes to win every game and hoist the Lombardi Trophy at the end of the season. They are doing it one step at a time, but are encountering challenges they didn't face last season.
The loss against the Chicago Bears in Week 8 marked their fourth of the season. Last year, the Seahawks only lost three games throughout the entire year. Macdonald knows his team is trying, but their poor execution is why they aren't succeeding.
"They want to play that way too. It's the same thing, we come together and we go forward and we tell each other the truth on the tape and where we can improve on what's us and what's not and how we fix it, and we find those solutions and we go. That's what we do. That's part of our process here, we're always going to do it that way. But it definitely stings, for sure it stings," Macdonald said.
Simply put, there's a target on the Seahawks' back this season after winning the Super Bowl last year. Teams are preparing for them a little differently and are attacking some weaknesses that may not have been discovered over the last year. Teams are getting stronger and smarter against them, and it's leading to Seattle's struggles.
It's very hard to beat a team twice in one year, and the Cardinals are going to come up with a new game plan to try and dethrone the defending champs. It's up to the Seahawks to play their game and execute the plans that have built them up over the last year or so.

title: The Best, Worst and Likeliest Scenarios for Cardinals vs. Seahawks in Week 9
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are preparing for their Week 9 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals at Lumen Field.
While the Seahawks beat the Cardinals 31-7 in Week 2, anything can happen in a divisional game, especially when it comes to Arizona. The Cardinals stormed back from down 14 points in the fourth quarter in Week 8 to beat the Dallas Cowboys on the road. All three of Arizona's wins so far this season have come away from Glendale.
Here's a look at three possible scenarios for the game this weekend.
The Seahawks have won their last 10 meetings against the Cardinals, dating back to the rematch in the 2021 season. The Seahawks are coming off a loss, and they know they need to make a big effort to come back with vengeance.
Their spot in the playoffs is teetering, and they need to figure out how to fix their offense before the season gets away from them. A game like this against the Cardinals should be treated as a get-back game, and with the 12s in their corner, Seattle might be able to blow them out like they did in Week 2.
The Seahawks have shown a bit of a regression over the past couple of weeks, and it could bite them this week with the Cardinals coming to town. They have a lot of momentum from their offensive rejuvenation in the fourth quarter, when they replaced Jacoby Brissett with Gardner Minshew, who has been named the starter for the game against the Seahawks.
If Arizona can find that same offensive rhythm throughout the game against Seattle while Sam Darnold continues to put up subpar performances, the Cardinals might be able to walk away from this one with a win, stunning the Seahawks.
While the Cardinals were able to come back against the Cowboys, their poorest defense does not compare to what Seattle has in store. On top of that, the Seahawks are coming off one of their worst defensive performances of the season, giving up 34 points to the Chicago Bears.
The Seahawks' defense is going to play a lot more focused this week, and having them go up against a quarterback in his first start of the year is a recipe for a Seattle victory by multiple scores.

title: The One Word Mike Macdonald Used to Describe Seahawks Loss vs. Bears
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are picking up the pieces after falling to the Chicago Bears 34-17 in Week 8's edition of Monday Night Football.
The Seahawks started out 2-0, but they have lost four of their last six games, and this defeat was the worst of them all. It's the first loss the Seahawks have had by multiple scores this season, and Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald shared his thoughts on the loss.
"Frustrating's a good way to put it," Macdonald said on Seattle Sports 710AM Tuesday morning. "Like I said after the game, we lost the game, it was a three-phase Seahawk loss, and that's a tough pill to swallow. That's something where you're disappointed."
The Seahawks' loss put them on the outside looking in for the NFC playoff picture. They need to win their final two games before the bye against the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders.
They will be eager to return to practice this week to correct some of the errors that they have made over the last couple of weeks. However, Macdonald and the coaching staff aren't looking at this situation like the sky is falling.
"Let's stay the course, let's go back to work. There are things that we need to improve on and we need to get better at that are in our control, and that's all you can do. That's where our focus needs to be," Macdonald said.
With the Cardinals on deck, the Seahawks know they cannot underestimate their NFC West rival. While the Seahawks beat the Cardinals 31-7 in Week 2, the Cardinals have a flare for the dramatics.
They managed to complete a two-touchdown comeback in the fourth quarter last week against the Dallas Cowboys, with Gardner Minshew as their backup quarterback entering the game. Minshew is expected to start for the Cardinals against the Seahawks this week as a result of his success, so the Seahawks need to be ready for an Arizona team with a lot of momentum.

title: Seahawks Week 8 Snap Counts: Running Back Split Surprises
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks suffered arguably their worst loss since the 2024 season on Monday night at home against the Chicago Bears. Almost everything went wrong in all three phases , and Seattle’s place in the NFC playoff picture is growing bleak at the midseason point.
Seattle had both running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price return after extended absences, and they also had major shakeups on the offensive line with the addition of Quenton Nelson at left guard.
Here’s a look at how the Seahawks’ offensive and defensive snap counts shook out from their loss to the Bears.
* All snap count statistics are courtesy of Pro Football Reference
RG Grey Zabel (63; 100%), RT Abraham Lucas (63; 100%), LT Josh Jones (63; 100%), LG Quenton Nelson (63; 100%), QB Sam Darnold (63; 100%), C Jalen Sundell (62; 98%), WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba (61; 97%), TE AJ Barner (60; 95%), WR Cooper Kupp (5; 92%), WR Tory Horton (43; 68%), RB Jadarian Price (30; 48%), RB Zach Charbonnet (23; 37%), TE Eric Saubert (15; 24%), RB George Holani (11; 17%), FB Brady Russell (10; 16%), TE Nick Kallerup (4; 6%), C Olu Oluwatimi (1; 2%)
Unsurprisingly, Nelson played every snap in his first game with the Seahawks. Zabel also played every snap in his first NFL game at right guard. Sundell exited with an injury, but he only missed one snap, and that’s why Oluwatimi logged a play. The offensive line performance left a lot to be desired, with three players in new positions.
Smith-Njigba has averaged about 55 snaps per game, so his usage went up in this game. That was likely to make up for Rashid Shaheed’s absence, but Horton also saw a healthy dose of snaps after Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp.
Price saw more usage at running back, and that translated to the box score. Charbonnet logged nine touches for 29 yards in his first game this season, and Price totaled 12 touches for 37 yards. Neither was efficient on a bad day for the offense.
LB Ernest Jones IV (70; 100%), CB Devon Witherspoon (70; 100%), S Ty Okada (70; 100%), CB Josh Jobe (69; 99%), S Julian Love (66; 94%), LB/DB Nick Emmanwori (64; 91%), LB Drake Thomas (59; 84%), DL Byron Murphy II (54; 77%), LB Derick Hall (51; 73%), LB DeMarcus Lawrence (45; 64%), DL Leonard Williams (41; 59%), DL Jarran Reed (33; 47%), DL Mike Morris (26; 37%), DL Rylie Mills (23; 33%), CB Nehemiah Pritchett (13; 19%), LB Dante Fowler Jr. (8; 11%), S Rodney Thomas II (4; 6%), LB Connor O’Toole (4; 6%)
Williams was lower on the defensive line rotation only due to suffering a stinger in the second half. That increased snap counts for Morris and Mills, who overall filled in well. Even on a bad day for the defense, the Seahawks’ run defense held up and proved that their depth up front remains quite good.
Jones, Witherspoon, Okada, Jobe and Love are still the mainstays of the defense who rarely come off the field. Emmanwori is getting to that point, but he still plays somewhat of a specialist role. Head coach Mike Macdonald is starting to find a role for him on every play, however.
The main deficiency was at edge rusher. Without Uchenna Nwosu, the rotation remained largely reliant on Hall and Lawrence, and they didn’t get much pressure. Seattle’s defense relies on Nwosu’s presence more than many realized.

title: Seahawks' Defense Needs to 'Get Together' After Loss to Bears
full_text:
Plenty went wrong in the Seattle Seahawks’ primetime loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday night, with most of those issues unsurprisingly coming on the offensive end . But the defense isn’t free of blame in the loss.
The Seahawks’ defense, though given little rest all game, gave up 363 total yards and 34 points. Chicago turned all four of its red zone trips into touchdowns and converted 7 of 15 third-down conversions.
Numbers are one side, but the Seattle defense simply didn’t look like itself . That was partly due to the Bears’ offensive excellence, but also because the Seahawks didn’t seem to have the same fire they showed against the Kansas City Chiefs the week before.
“We go into a lot of games knowing that if we play our brand of football — clean, efficient, on the same page — then we play well,” Seahawks safety Julian Love said after the game. “Kudos to them for sure, but we’ve got to go to work, man. People need to step up, guys need to get together here, and just play better football together.”
The “Dark Side” defense has created an identity since Mike Macdonald became the Seahawks’ head coach in 2024, and it’s clear when they are playing to their standard.
Five players flock to every ball carrier; they get consistent quarterback pressure with four rushers, they never lose the line of scrimmage, and the secondary plays with a moxie and swagger no other defense in the league has. We saw none of those things against the Bears, at least not consistently.
“It’s a tip of the cap to the Bears,” Macdonald said postgame. “They won the game, they won it fair and square, they won it in all three phases. And we just got beat. No other way to sugarcoat it. I think when you look at the things it takes to win in our league, we didn’t do those things and they did.”
It’s been expected that the offense would struggle with identity this season, as the growing pains under offensive coordinator Brian Fleury have been immense. The defense having those issues, on the other hand, speaks to a larger problem with Seattle being at a midseason crossroads.
Love offered some solace, however, about the team’s mindset after losing four of their last six games. As Super Bowl champions last season, they’ve worked through adversity in the past.
“I would say a lesser team would be really frustrated, pointing fingers, turning on each other,” Love explained. “I think the guys in the room, or at least me, it’s like, ‘Man, there’s so much out there for us.’ We play a good brand of football; teams know kind of what we’re about; I think we play tough, we’re connected. But we’re still chasing efficiency.”
The Seahawks (4-4) have a short week of preparation before they host the Arizona Cardinals (3-5) at 1:25 p.m. on Sunday, Nov. 8. That will be their first non-primetime game since Week 4.

title: How the Seahawks' 2026 Season Gets Worse After Week 8 Loss
full_text:
This 2026 NFL Season has been an incredibly rough setting for the Seattle Seahawks (4-4 as they've encountered the worst-case scenario with their offense through eight weeks. The Brian Fleury hire looks like a disaster, multiple offensive players have regressed, and the Seahawks look to be wasting away their Super Bowl window.
​The Seahawks suffered a disastrous 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 8 on Monday Night Football. It was the Seahawks’ worst loss since 2024 as the team was dominated through all three phases of the game.
​There are still ways for the Seahawks to get back into the playoff race , likely as a Wild Card team. Seattle, however, has a chance to turn it around, but there are also ways for the season to get worse. The question is, can things get worse in Seattle? The short answer: of course it can.
Seattle’s offense has been its Achilles’ Heel this season. Quarterback Sam Darnold looks flustered multiple times in games. There hasn’t been a pass-catcher to step up outside of star wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The offensive line has regressed to a point that the front office traded for guard Quenton Nelson to add some stability this season , and hopefully, beyond.
​The biggest fault lies with Fleury, who has yet to get a rhythm with the offense and learn what works best for the offense. Seattle had veteran Zach Charbonnet and rookie Jadarian Price return on Monday, only for them to combine for 52 yards on 16 carries. Fleury mishandled the running game because he isn’t comfortable with the players, the tempo and the play-calling.
​Fleury will likely remain as the team’s offensive coordinator through the rest of the season. He has to admit that he has problems taking a bigger role with an offense and he isn’t capable of diagnosing and addressing the problems. If he still isn’t capable of utilizing the players as the season progresses, the Seahawks will continue to lose games.
​Seattle has two winnable games coming up with the Seahawks hosting the Arizona Cardinals (3-5) in Week 9 and then going on the road to take on the Las Vegas Raiders (4-4). Seattle could see some progress with its offense coming off those two games before having its scheduled bye week in Week 11. The Seahawks can’t afford to believe their offense could be efficient after those two games.
​Seattle could have their 10-game winning streak snapped by the Cardinals and/or lose to the Raiders, led by head coach and former Seahawks offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak. A loss to either of these teams would be absolutely embarrassing and severely hurt Seattle’s playoff odds .
​The Seahawks have three games against the NFC East and a road game against the Carolina Panthers left in their schedule. They also have one game against the San Francisco 49ers and two games versus the Los Angeles Rams, who look dysfunctional. There are several winnable games, but if the offense continues and the team’s frustrations continue to rub off on the defense, then the Seahawks could easily miss the playoffs and go under .500%.

title: Week 9 NFL Power Rankings Roundup: Seahawks Tumble Following Loss to Bears
full_text:
It was a tough loss for the Seattle Seahawks on Monday Night Football as the Chicago Bears walked out of Lumen Field with a 34-17 victory . That score makes it look far worse, but Seattle was in the fight during the fourth quarter before some untimely miscues, which included some uncharacteristic penalties.
Seattle is now just 4-4 on the season, which is a shock considering they went 14-3 a year ago and won the Super Bowl. There's no reason to panic yet, but they do need to start putting some wins together to ensure they don't miss out on the postseason .
The good news is that they still have an elite defense. The bad news is that their offense is still suspect. That's why they enter Week 9 sliding down many NFL power rankings.
Connor Orr dropped Seattle three spots, point out that Seattle had chances in this one but the pressure Sam Darnold was under proved to be too great.
"This was a game both select Bears players and striped-shirt gentlemen tried to invite Seattle back into time and time again. But Sam Darnold had defenders in his face all night. Jeffrey Simmons led the team in tackles and tackles for loss, and tied the team lead in quarterback hits," Orr wrote.
ESPN moved them back three spaces as well, with Seattle landing eighth overall in their rankings and spending Week 8 at No. 5.
Josh Kendall and Chad Graff worked together for The Athletic and says the Seahawks need to start converting in the red zone. If not, they could be in danger, especially now that they're three games behind the San Francisco 49ers.
"The Seahawks are still one of the better teams in the league, but they’re now a full three games behind the 49ers in the loss column in the NFC West, and playoff seeding is going to matter. A good place to start turning things around would be in the red zone, where Seattle is 29th in offensive touchdown percentage (46.4) and last in defensive touchdown percentage (83.3), according to TruMedia."
Nick Shook accurately points out that Jaxon Smith-Njigba is being asked to carry too much. While he's more than capable of racking up massive numbers, expecting him to be the sole source of offense for an entire season is not a winning strategy.
"Seahawks fans are likely entering Brian Fleury watch after what they saw Monday night. The oft-criticized offensive coordinator isn’t the only problem -- the three personal fouls committed by Seattle in the second half didn’t help, nor did Sam Darnold’s struggles under pressure -- but the way he approached the final seven minutes of regulation might loom large in his greater evaluation. The Seahawks’ defense is still largely a monster (save for red-zone situations), but the offense simply isn’t holding up its end of the bargain. Jaxon Smith-Njigba can’t save everyone," Shook wrote.
Ranking: 13 | Last week: 7
Now that Seattle has lost three of its last four games, Brent Sobleski is wondering if their convincing win over the Kansas City Chiefs was the anomaly.
"At 4-4, Seattle's record properly represents who the reigning Super Bowl champions have been this year. In fact, the Seahawks have lost three of their last four, so their previous domination over the Chiefs appears to be an aberration," Sobleski
Ranking: 14 | Last week: 6
Pete Prisco has Seattle on the edge of the playoffs at No. 14. He dropped them eight spots and says Darnold doesn't look right.
"They don't do enough on offense. Sam Darnold just doesn't look right. They got beat up at home by the Bears, which is not a good sign," Prisco wrote.
Darnold was beaten up all night, so perhaps the pressure was the issue. That said, Seattle must find a way to make him feel comfortable going forward. They also need to find some offense outside of JSN, although the return of Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price will help.

title: NFC Playoff Picture: Seahawks Slipping After Bears Loss
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are back in the loss column after a 34-17 loss against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field.
The loss saw the Seahawks take a tumble in the standings as they cling to one of the final wild card spots. Here's a look at the standings after eight weeks in the NFC.
1. Minnesota Vikings (6-1) 2. San Francisco 49ers (6-1) 3. New York Giants (4-2-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (3-4) 5. Chicago Bears (6-2) 6. Detroit Lions (5-2) 7. Green Bay Packers (5-3) 8. Seattle Seahawks (4-4) 9. Los Angeles Rams (4-4) 10. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-5) 11. Atlanta Falcons (3-5) 12. Arizona Cardinals (3-5) 13. Dallas Cowboys (3-5) 14. Washington Commanders (2-4-1) 15. New Orleans Saints (2-5) 16. Philadelphia Eagles (2-6)
With the loss, the Seahawks are now on the outside looking in for the playoffs. Had they beaten the Bears, they would have been on the other side of the playoff picture, while the Bears would have found themselves on the outside looking in.
The entire NFC North currently occupies four of the seven playoff spots. That isn't likely to happen by season's end, as they will face off against each other many times between now and the end of the year.
Regardless of what will happen in the second half of the season, this should serve as an alarm for the Seahawks. The team has plenty of talent, especially on the defensive side of the ball, to return to the playoffs this season. If they make it to the postseason, they might be the one team that nobody wants to face.
However, they simply aren't playing well enough to be a true contender in the NFC at this point. The offense can be credited mostly for these struggles , but there is still a lot of time to figure things out between now and the end of the season.
With just two games until their Week 11 bye, the Seahawks need to attack this stretch of games with force as they look to pull out one of those final wild card spots in the NFC.

title: Loss to Bears Underscores Season-Long Failures of Brian Fleury, Seahawks' Offense
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks’ offense has reached a crisis point at the midseason mark, as it struggled mightily to move the football once again in a 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday night.
Seattle’s defense gave up a season-high 34 points, also its most since the 2024 season , but that was more a product of offensive ineptitude that led to massively disproportionate time of possession than it was an indictment of the Seahawks’ offense.
Chicago held the ball for 35 minutes, and the Seahawks had just two double-digit-play drives. One of those was Seattle’s final possession of the game — already trailing by 17 — when they needed to be attempting to score quickly.
“If we’re not efficient on early downs, or we’re not moving the ball forward all the time, it’s tough sledding,” Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said postgame about the offense. “And when you play a team like that that is really proficient on third down, then that’s the type of stuff that happens. But the sense of urgency for us to improve right now is high.”
The blame can’t go to any one place. Offensive coordinator Brian Fleury appears out of his depth, quarterback Sam Darnold was as bad as he has been much of the season, and the offensive line looked drastically worse post-Quenton Nelson trade with Charles Cross out and Grey Zabel moving to right guard.
Seattle’s offense has faced a litany of other issues throughout the season, but this was a catastrophic collapse in primetime eight games into the season that put them 3.5 games behind the San Francisco 49ers for the NFC West lead.
Following a three-play touchdown drive that was gifted to the offense by a defensive takeaway, the Seahawks trailed by just three. Then Chicago pushed it back to 10, and Seattle had nine minutes left in the fourth quarter to make up that difference.
That’s when Fleury, if he wasn’t already, began to fail. After a free first down off a penalty, the Seahawks had 1st and 10 at their own 22-yard line with 7:13 remaining. Fleury called two straight run plays that netted three yards, and Darnold threw an interception on third down.
Four plays later, it was a 17-point game, and the Seahawks were deflated.
“We didn’t do the things on offense that we need to be able to do to play Seahawk football,” Macdonald said. “To me, it’s inputs. If we’re playing the way that we’re supposed to, and we’re running off the rock, and we’re targeted right, and we’re dialed in on what we should be doing, we’re way more efficient and then the ball is distributed more evenly. So, that’s where we need to put our focus.”
If this were a one-time thing, it might be easier to swallow. But it feeds into a broader trend of how the pacing of the offense has continued to fail to adjust to the present in-game situation through eight games, and that falls on the offensive coaches — and ultimately the coordinator at the top — not putting their unit in positions to win games.
Do Darnold and the offensive weapons need to stop turning the ball over? Absolutely. Does the offensive line need more grit in the run game? Of course. And Fleury needs to start taking what’s working (i.e., the Chiefs game) and lean into it.
“As the season goes on, there’s always room to grow and continue to learn each other,” Darnold said of Fleury after the game. “I feel like the last couple of weeks we’ve been continuing to develop that relationship, and I feel like it’s been going good. Again, for whatever reason, today, we’ve got to watch the tape, but it just wasn’t getting enough, and we’ll continue to dive deep into it and be very honest with each other really throughout the next day.”
The messaging from Macdonald, Darnold and the rest of the team is similar to what was being said after the Week 6 loss to the Broncos, a defeat that punctuated a 1-3 stretch. There was hope after a dominant win against the Chiefs, but it now feels like they're back searching for answers.
Even with many critical pieces rolling over from 2025, this Seahawks offense is failing, and the team knows it. With no bye until Week 11, they have to get better tomorrow, or it could doom their chances of a second straight Super Bowl run.

title: Only One Wide Receiver Trade Makes Sense for the 49ers
full_text:
Trading for a wide receiver has been hot topic surrounding the San Francisco 49ers .
With all the injuries at the position, it's caused a ton of knee-jerk reactions from fans advocating for the 49ers to acquire a receiver . I don't believe the receiver position is that pressing an issue .
Most of the injured receivers will be back in the next week or two. Plus, there isn't a blockbuster trade for the 49ers to make. Garrrett Wilson is the only possible one, but the New York Jets aren't budging.
Still, the 49ers would like to add a receiver. Otherwise, they wouldn't have checked in with the Minnesota Vikings for Jauan Jennings. That leaves only one wide receiver trade that makes sense for the 49ers.
Trading for Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts is the only one that makes sense. For starters, he would be a solid fit for the 49ers, providing them with the vertical threat that they're missing.
Downs can take the top off the defense and open things up for everyone else underneath. The best part is that defensive backs won't be too worried about Downs because of Mike Evans.
Are they going to let Downs run by them down the field? Or will they suffer with Evans gashing on intermediate routes? It's a pickle for defenses to deal with.
Not to mention there's George Kittle, Deebo Samuel, Christian McCaffrey, and Demarcus Robinson to worry about. The 49ers' offense will stress defenses with Downs.
He may not be a premier receiver, but he has enough skill to make an impact for the 49ers. Plus, the 49ers already made a deal with the Colts last week when they reunited with DeForest Buckner.
They have a connection with the Colts, so they can easily call them up and check on Downs. Indianapolis is having a fire sale up until the trade deadline on Nov. 10.
Along with Buckner, they traded All-Pro offensive lineman Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks. Even star running back Jonathan Taylor might be on the move.
A fifth-round pick should do the trick to pry Downs from them. It's also the highest the 49ers should go, since Downs is playing in the final year of his rookie contract.
Adding Downs hits all of the markers for the 49ers. He's a fit, plays for a team in the dumps, and his face value is very affordable.
The biggest issue with trading for Downs, any wide receiver, really, is that several teams need one. If other teams are calling the Colts for him, his cost will drive up.
If the 49ers are going to overpay, they might as well do it for an edge rusher, not a receiver. It's an overblown issue that can be masked, especially if they can add another pass rusher.

title: Brandon Aiyuk has Filed for Reinstatement and will Report to the 49ers on Friday
full_text:
Brandon Aiyuk has the most incredible timing.
We haven't heard from this guy in months. He tried so hard to force the 49ers to release him all offseason, and then he went silent. It seemed like he had given up on playing football entirely.
Now, less than a week before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, he has hired mega-agent Drew Rosenhaus, filed for reinstatement with the NFL, and intends to report to the 49ers facility this Friday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .
Suddenly, Aiyuk is moving extremely fast, and it's unclear what he ultimately wants now that Rosenhaus is representing him. Does Aiyuk want to play for the 49ers again, or does he think he can get them finally to trade him? Or cut him?
Unless the 49ers have been in contact with Aiyuk, they're probably confused as well. They have to figure out what they're going to do when he shows up.
Option 1: Call the police. Technically, there's a warrant out for Aiyuk's arrest because he filmed himself driving past Levi's Stadium while going more than 100 miles per hour. This was an error in judgment.
Pros: Aiyuk would get arrested and humiliated in front of his teammates.
Cons: He would bail out of jail in five minutes and come right back to the facility, so this would just delay the confrontation.
Option 2: Remove Aiyuk from the reserve/left squad list and try to find some team that's willing to trade a conditional seventh-round pick for him if the 49ers pay part of his salary. If no such team exists, cut him.
Pros: The 49ers never would have to deal with Aiyuk again.
Cons: A former All-Pro wide receiver who's 28 could go to a contender such as the Chiefs, the Bills, Rams, or the Seahawks. And if he plays well, the 49ers would look incompetent because they need a wide receiver like Aiyuk, and someone might get fired.
Option 3: Let Aiyuk return to the team as if nothing happened, provided he addresses his teammates and coaches and reconciles face-to-face with them.
Pros: The 49ers might get a former All-Pro wide receiver who's 28 and healthy and hungry to prove that he deserves a big contract this offseason. This version of Aiyuk could carry the 49ers to their first Super Bowl victory since 1995, assuming Mike Evans returns at some point this season and stays relatively healthy.
Cons: Aiyuk could come back for one day, pull his calf on the practice field like Nick Bosa and Dante Pettis did, sign an injury settlement and never play for the 49ers again.
I couldn't tell you what the right thing to do is. I hope the 49ers and Aiyuk reconcile. That would be a wonderful, heartwarming ending to a bizarre story.
I like a heartwarming ending.

title: 3 Trade Deadline Targets for 49ers Who Fit Raheem Morris's Scheme
full_text:
When you think of the San Francisco 49ers edge rushers, you typically think of a long-armed, strong run defender who can slide inside on pass-rushing downs. Mykel Williams and Keion White tend to fit that mold. They were additions when the team ran their old scheme, though.
With Raheem Morris, they are more multiple . They lean on speed rushers and players who can drop into coverage more. That is why they drafted Romello Height, who plays the same position as Williams, but is more than 2 inches shorter, 21 pounds lighter, and has arms that are inches shorter based on their combine measurements.
With that in mind, Daniel Popper of The Athletic listed three speed rushers as options for the 49ers at the trade deadline. While a 49ers team of the past would never add these options, the Morris version would see them as fits.
McDonald is similar in height and weight to Romello Height, but he has longer arms and more proven pass rush production in the NFL. He could be a one-year rental, so he would not stall the development of Height in the long term. Still, with 18.5 sacks in the past two years combined and three sacks already this year, he would be a great addition.
Smith is a former first-round pick in the fourth year of his rookie contract. So the acquiring team could add Smith this year and have him on the fifth-year option next year. Smith is a Super Bowl winner and starter on the Eagles' defense. His game is based on speed, but he could be a strong mentor for Height and would fit this defense more than units in the past. Smith already has four sacks this season.
Chaisson is another former first-round pick. He is a bit older than Smith and McDonald, but he is still just 27 years old. Chaisson is not much of a run defender, which is why he has bounced around the NFL. Still, he has 3.5 sacks this year and had 7.5 sacks on the Patriots last year. He also added three sacks in the Patriots' playoff run last year. He has proven playoff experience and would be a good fit for a rental.

title: These 5 49ers Could Lose Playing Time After the Bye Week
full_text:
The bye week is usually a time for players to see increases in role or more put on their plate. However, that can often mean that players see reductions in playing time on the flip side. Which players on the 49ers could end up playing less after the bye week?
The team is not going to bench Colby coming out of the bye week. However, at the same time, he is trending in the wrong direction. His first four games were okay, but the last three before the bye week raise a lot of questions.
The team already has rookie Carver Willis preparing as a potential option to step in. Willis played tackle in college, so it was always going to take him some time to adjust to the NFL. Now that he has the bye week, he might be ready for a bigger role. If Colby does not continue to play well, they are going to bench him. Do not be surprised if Colby is not the starter throughout the second half of the season.
Cowing has only been playing due to the injuries at the position. However, the team is supposed to get a little bit healthier after the bye week, with Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans returning to the lineup. Demarcus Robinson might be back soon as well. Christian Kirk is healthy too, and he might be able to take the punt return job from Cowing, so Cowing could end up being inactive.
Valdez was signed from the practice squad when the team had multiple injuries on the defensive front. However, now the 49ers have traded for DeForest Buckner, and they got UDFA James Thompson back healthy. With the bye week to get the group in line, it looks like Valdez is the fifth man in the rotation. That might mean being inactive on game days.
Brown has started every game this season, but both Malik Mustapha and Marques Sigle have been better than him. Sigle has been injured, but when he comes back, the team might elect to start him next to Mustapha and keep Brown on the bench.
Mike Williams is healthy and starting to play more. Nick Bosa is expected to come back after the bye week, and the team is starting to get more production from rookie Romello Height. None of these three will lose time for White, who will be fourth in the rotation.

title: 2 Teams That Did the 49ers a Huge Favor in Week 8
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers will return to the field on Sunday in Week 9 to take on the Las Vegas Raiders after receiving much-needed rest i n Week 8.
Before the 49ers can fully lock in against the Raiders, they must thank two teams that did them a huge favor in Week 8. Maybe even a gift is warranted.
The 49ers are sitting atop the NFC thanks to the Detroit Lions. They're the first team to hand the Minnesota Vikings their first loss of the season.
Minnesota is now tied with the 49ers at 6-1, but thanks to the strength of victory tiebreaker, the 49ers get the nod to sit atop the No. 1 seed.
The playoffs are still a long way off, and much can change. But the fact that the Lions disrupted the Vikings is huge for the 49ers.
I also think the Vikings' loss will be the beginning of a rough stretch for them. They might suffer losses in the next three games, as they take on the Buffalo Bills, Green Bay Packers, and finally the 49ers in Mexico City.
That can easily be three straight losses for the Vikings, who can't continue to hide behind their vaunted defense. The Lions may have started a snowball effect that the Vikings cannot overcome.
It's a bummer that the Los Angeles Rams won, but they're not that much of a threat to the 49ers. The Seattle Seahawks, on the other hand, are.
A win in Week 8 would've cut the 49ers' lead in the NFC West over them, but they suffered a brutal defeat at home on Monday night to the Chicago Bears.
The 49ers can thank the Bears for their service. Winning the division grows in likelihood for them with another Seattle loss. So long as the 49ers don't have an insane collapse, the NFC West will be theirs.
Similar to the Vikings, the Seahawks might face a snowball effect after losing to the Bears. Their offense can't move the ball efficiently outside of spamming targets to Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
Their defense is still elite and an issue for the 49ers, but their offense is a mess. The Bears, and even the 49ers, laid out the blueprint for disrupting the Seahawks' offense.
If they can't go on a run soon, the 49ers will run away with the division sooner than anyone anticipated. The only downside to this game is that the Bears are now fierce competition for the 49ers to clinch the No. 1 seed.

title: Why the 49ers Should Be Pushing Harder for a Trade After Week 8
full_text:
Having a Week 8 Bye was perfect timing for the San Francisco 49ers .
One overlooked benefit for it was that they could observe the lay of the NFC . The 49ers haven't been able to dig in and do that outside of their division.
Now that Week 8 has concluded, the 49ers should be more motivated and push harder for a trade. The biggest motivator should be from watching the Chicago Bears beat up the Seattle Seahawks.
No one does that to Seattle. Not even the 49ers. Yet the Bears did that on the road in primetime. That's a massively impressive win for them.
It should put the 49ers on notice that they are a significant threat, if not greater than the Seahawks, who were their greatest threat entering this season.
The Bears are clicking on offense, as well as, if not better than, the 49ers when they're healthy. But the scary part about the Bears is that their defense is actually good now.
Acquiring defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons has greatly improved them. But the one weakness they showcased was that their defensive backs can be taken advantage of.
This makes a trade for a wide receiver more of a need. Maybe the 49ers can pick up the phone and call the Indianapolis Colts again and see if they can acquire Joshua Downs.
He's a solid vertical threat that can stretch every defense. If he's not available or viewed as a good enough improvement to the 49ers' offense, then they can still look at an edge rusher.
This is where I've advocated for a trade to be made by the 49ers. Defense will always win championships. Yes, they brought in DeForest Buckner .
He will help them immensely, but why stop there? Adding an impactful edge rusher will evolve the 49ers' defense from an amazing one to an overpowered one.
That will do wonders when they have to face the Bears in the playoffs. It will also make it miserable for other electric offenses in the NFC, like the Detroit Lions.
Not to mention some of the mediocre offenses that will be in a nightmare facing the 49ers' defense, like the Minnesota Vikings or the Seahawks (again).
Whichever path the 49ers take, they should be further motivated to make a trade. They cannot stand idly by and waste a prime shot at making the Super Bowl.

title: The 49ers Most Underrated Trade Deadline Options
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are likely to be buyers at the NFL trade deadline. While there are some names that get tossed around often, who are some lesser-discussed options that are realistic fits for the 49ers?
Johnson is a former first-rounder by the New York Jets when Robert Saleh was the Jets' coach. Now that he is the Titans coach, he traded for Johnson. Still, Johnson is in the last year of his rookie deal and will be a free agent. He likes Saleh, but money will talk, and the Titans could lose him. So, a trade makes sense. Raheem Morris has changed the defense, but Johnson is still a strong fit.
Bateman is 27 years old and is signed through 2029. However, a new coaching staff and off-the-field questions have brought up some trade speculation. Adding to that, the Ravens are now 4-4, in last place in their division, and they just lost Lamar Jackson for what appears to be the rest of the season. Selling Bateman now makes sense.
His speed in the 49ers would be a bit of a missing piece right now, and he might not cost the team too much to acquire.
It appears as though the only realistic name to upgrade the 49ers' left guard situation would be Landon Dickerson. However, Suamataia is a name to watch after being benched by the Kansas City Chiefs twice this season. The former second-round pick has had a lot of ups and downs with the Chiefs but appears to be in their doghouse right now.
Suamataia is in his third NFL season and could start for the 49ers for the next two seasons. The Chiefs are in buy-mode, so the 49ers might need to add a player to get Suamataia back. However, someone like Tatum Bethune might be all that it takes.
Robertson is signed through the 2027 season, but an acquiring team could save $7M by moving on from him. So, the Commanders will likely cut him after the year. Still, the veteran has slot and outside experience. He replaced Jack Jones on the Las Vegas Raiders last year and could replace Jones again this year if the 49ers trade for him.
More than that, he gives them protection if Stout is hurt again or remains hurt. The only question is if Washington thinks they are in contention in a poor NFC East.
