title: Commanders News: Both Starting DTs Hit IR as Rams’ Matthew Stafford Deals With Arm Soreness | Burgundy Roundup
full_text:
Tuesday made three more Commanders absences official. Daron Payne, Javon Kinlaw, and Jeremy McNichols went on injured reserve . Payne is out for the season; McNichols must miss at least four games. According to a report from Adam Schefter , Kinlaw underwent season-ending surgery Tuesday on his MCL. Robert Henry Jr. is back in Washington. The Commanders claimed him off waivers after Seattle waived him Monday to activate Jadarian Price. The Seahawks had signed Henry from Washington’s practice squad on October 6. Henry has yet to play in a regular-season NFL game, so his return gives Washington another option without settling who takes McNichols’ snaps. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler are the other backs on the active roster, with Devin Neal and Craig Reynolds still on the practice squad. Terry McLaurin was watching Sunday’s win from home, but his teammates made sure he was part of it. Jayden Daniels and Mike Sainristil wore shirts bearing his picture before the game. After Stefon Diggs scored, he joined Daniels, Antonio Williams and Josh Conerly Jr. at a camera for McLaurin’s “Scary Terry” celebration. Williams said the receivers wanted McLaurin to see it. The Rams had their own roster work Tuesday. They placed Dean Connors on injured reserve after he broke his hand against the Chargers, then waived Alex Bachman, who had handled nine punt returns and 13 kickoff returns this season. Kyren Williams and Blake Corum remain in the backfield. Bachman’s departure leaves Los Angeles with a punt return job to fill before Sunday. Los Angeles also signed Cam Lampkin from its practice squad to the active roster, brought Nyzier Fourqurean back to the practice squad and released linebacker Garrett Nelson from that unit. The cornerback move comes with Jaylen Watson’s shoulder and Trent McDuffie’s back under observation . Watson aggravated his injury against the Chargers. McVay said Monday that McDuffie felt better than expected, but neither player has an official Week 9 practice designation yet. Then there’s Matthew Stafford. He left Sunday’s game with ice on his right elbow, and McVay acknowledged soreness in his throwing arm. Ian Rapoport said Tuesday he expects Stafford to be ready for Washington . The Rams’ first injury report arrives Wednesday, when Stafford is also scheduled to speak with reporters.
Payne reportedly suffered a season-ending Jones fracture during Friday's practice, while McNichols is expected to miss significant time with a midfoot injury. Tim Settle Jr. and Shy Tuttle remain available at defensive tackle, although Washington could still look for additional help . Byron Cowart was elevated from the practice squad before the Philly game; he isn't automatically part of the active roster for the Rams game. Jer'Zhan Newton is still in his 21-day practice window and must be activated before he can play.
At 2-4-1, the Commanders have reasons to examine the interior offensive line, defensive tackle, and possibly running back before the November 10 trade deadline at 4 p.m. Eastern. Daron Payne's foot injury and the availability questions around Javon Kinlaw and Jer'Zhan Newton leave the defensive front short. Jeremy McNichols' midfoot injury could create another need, pending additional scans. The three pairings below are my proposals for how Peters could improve the roster this season.
We have claimed RB Robert Henry Jr. off waivers from Seattle pic.twitter.com/KrBsy1cjmu
While the Washington Commanders have struggled to stop opponents from getting explosive plays, they haven't been very successful at getting them either. That changed Sunday night. With 2:51 left in the third quarter, Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels found receiver Treylon Burks for 53 yards, moving Washington from its own 40 to Philadelphia’s 7. It came exactly one play after Dorance Armstrong forced Tanner McKee’s fumble, which Charles Omenihu recovered, and it was the longest reception this season by a Commanders player.
Chig Okonkwo had only a 17.4 percent chance of catching his 21-yard reception in the third quarter against the Eagles, according to @ZebraTechnology . pic.twitter.com/2hik9kmqRO
Here's what we do know: the Commanders scored 27 unanswered points after that moment and took a 27-10 victory over the Eagles. No one said it publicly after the game, but Daniels' address to the offense served as an unofficial turning point during a night in which the Commanders needed a win. To the players, it was everything they expected from Daniels, who took another step in his development as a leader.

The penalties and miscues Washington’s coaching staff had vowed to clean up during the bye week continued to plague the team early as Washington’s offense had 4 penalties, 1 dropped pass, 1 fumble, and 1 missed field goal during the first three drives of Sunday night’s game. The Commanders would finish with 7 penalties for 50 yards in the first half, after simplifying their offense in an attempt to clean up the pre-snap mistakes. The NFL average for an entire game this season is right around eight per team.

title: Commanders Power Rankings Rise After Eagles Win, but One Writer Makes Bold NFC East Call
full_text:
Each week during the regular season, we'll look at what the national media is saying about the Washington Commanders via various publications' NFL Power Polls. With it being Week 9, seasons are starting to slip away around the league. The Washington Commanders finally gave the national media another win to work with, scoring 27 unanswered points Sunday night to beat the Philadelphia Eagles 27-10. That victory moved Washington to 2-4-1 and gave the team its first win since Week 3 against Seattle. Eight of the nine publications we track each week moved the Commanders up in their latest power rankings. Oddly enough, one actually dropped them two spots. * Side note: Many have asked whether these polls are helpful, which is a fair question. One way to look at them is as a way to broaden your perspective on what others believe. Not to mention, sometimes it's fun to see the national media guys bump around in the dark, chasing their tails, clueless.
Commanders Power Rankings - Week 9 (Average of 24)
Sports Illustrated - No. 22
Note : The table above links each poll to the corresponding publication name. Here's where things get interesting. Washington beat Philadelphia by 17 points, scored 27 unanswered, and somehow managed to drop two spots in NFL.com's rankings. Meanwhile, Pro Football Talk moved the Commanders up six spots, and Sports Illustrated jumped them five. Same game, three very different opinions. If you're wondering why I enjoy looking at these polls each week, there's a pretty good example. Then there's Sports Illustrated's Conor Orr, who has Washington at No. 22 and is already calling the Commanders his favorite to win the NFC East. That's quite a statement for a team sitting at 2-4-1, although beating Philadelphia the way Washington did certainly gives him something to work with. I'm not ready to go that far just yet. One good game doesn't erase everything we've watched over the first half of the season, but another win against the Rams on Sunday would make things a little more interesting. Orr also pointed to the connection between Daniels and Antonio Williams, and the rookie's snap counts against Philadelphia certainly back up the idea that his role is growing. Last week’s Power Ranking Index : No. 26 HIGHEST Ranking: No. 17 LOWEST Ranking: No. 27 Last week’s result : beat the Philadelphia Eagles 27-10 This week : vs. Los Angeles Rams ESPN had this to say (25th): Instead of a normal ranking blurb, ESPN inserted best in-season trades: This really is based on one season, as Muhammad played only two years for Washington. The franchise needed help after Art Monk was injured and traded a fourth-round pick to Oakland for the speedy Muhammad. In his 10 games with Washington in 1984, Muhammad caught 42 passes for 729 yards and four touchdowns. He was a key reason why, even without Monk, Washington's offense remained among the best in the NFL, ranking third in points and ninth in yards. A year later, with a healthy receiving group, Muhammad caught only nine passes and was released before the 1986 season. -- John Keim
CBS Sports had this to say (27th) Jayden Daniels won for the first time in a long time. They rallied to beat the Eagles as the offense showed life and the defense was better. Now here come the Rams. — Pete Prisco NFL.com had this to say (26th) Washington recorded a much-needed win over the lowly Eagles on Sunday night in a display that wasn’t pretty but counted the same as any other victory. It’s nice to see Treylon Burks find a role in this offense, and it’s good to watch Jayden Daniels pilot the unit effectively. It also didn’t tell me all that much about where this team stands at 2-4-1. — Nick Shook
Fox Sports had this to say (25th): The Commanders scored 27 unanswered points to beat a division rival on Sunday night, and ordinarily that would be cause for celebration. But the team they beat is the ghost of the Philadelphia Eagles, and it’s not like the Commanders needed much of an effort to do it. It certainly was a much-needed win for Dan Quinn , who miraculously managed to survive the bye week. He’ll need a lot more of those and a lot more from star QB Jayden Daniels , however, to keep his job after the season. And there are too many injuries and holes in the Commanders’ lineup to expect that. — Ralph Vacchiano Sports Illustrated had this to say (22nd): At this point in the race, Washington is my favorite to wind up winning the NFC East. Last night, the breadcrumbs shown between Jayden Daniels and Antonio Williams leads me to believe there’s just enough of a spark left in this offense to generate a run.   — Conor Orr
Yahoo Sports had this to say (23rd): Like everyone else in the NFC South and NFC East, other than the Eagles, the Commanders should feel like they have a shot to be division champions. The Commanders are flawed, without question, but sit just two games behind the Giants in the division. It's not like New York is a lock to run away with it. The biggest problem for the Commanders is the loss of receiver Terry McLaurin for the season. It leaves them thin at receiver, and the good news is there are a lot of veterans available at the deadline at various price points. The Commanders should be interested. They also should be interested in improving a secondary that ranks 27th in passing yards allowed.  — Frank Schwab Pro Football Talk had this to say (24th) Backward Hat Energy. — Mike Florio The Athletic had this to say (25th) The Commanders quarterback took a big hit from Nolan Smith on Sunday night that just added to what already has been a black-and-blue season. Daniels has only rushed for 33 yards (all on scrambles) in the last two weeks. If he’s not dynamic on the ground, he’s not the player Washington thought he was as a rookie, but that style of play is taking a toll. — Chad Graff and Josh Kendall Walter Football had this to say (17th) It's hard to believe that Jayden Daniels just won his first game of the year. I know he was out for a while, but it still feels like he probably should have won a game by now. However, that apparently hadn't happened. The win over Philadelphia was Washington's first victory since Week 3 against Seattle, which feels like a million years ago.
Put all nine together, and the Commanders land at an average ranking of No. 23.8, an improvement from last week's 26.2 . That's a decent jump for a team with only two wins, and Conor Orr at Sports Illustrated is already calling Washington his favorite to win the NFC East. Not everyone is convinced, though. Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams should give the national media another opportunity to decide how much that Eagles win was worth. title: Commanders Lose Three More Players to Injured Reserve Ahead of Rams Game
full_text:
NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Tuesday that the Washington Commanders are putting Jeremy McNichols, Daron Payne , and Javon Kinlaw on injured reserve, meaning all three will miss at least four games. Payne and Kinlaw missed Sunday night's game against Philadelphia, and McNichols hurt his foot during the game. Payne reportedly suffered a season-ending Jones fracture during Friday's practice, while McNichols is expected to miss significant time with a midfoot injury. Tim Settle Jr. and Shy Tuttle remain available at defensive tackle, although Washington could still look for additional help . Byron Cowart was elevated from the practice squad before the Philly game; he isn't automatically part of the active roster for the Rams game. Jer'Zhan Newton is still in his 21-day practice window and must be activated before he can play. What's really bad for McNichols here is that he just came back from IR after missing the first five weeks with a quadriceps injury; he can't seem to catch a break. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt also on IR with a groin injury, Washington had been down to Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler on its active roster. According to The Athletic, the Commanders claimed Robert Henry Jr. off waivers from Seattle on Tuesday, bringing back a player who was on their practice squad earlier this season. Devin Neal and Craig Reynolds remain practice-squad options. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn was worried that McNichols ' injury was serious, and was already looking ahead on Monday during his press conference: "It's definitely something that, once we go through the scans to see where we're at, we have some [backs] on practice squad as well." UPDATE : According to a report from Adam Schefter , Javon Kinlaw underwent season-ending surgery Tuesday on his MCL. title: 3 Players the Commanders Could Trade to Fill Bigger Roster Holes
full_text:
Mike Sainristil didn't play a defensive snap in the Washington Commanders ' 27-10 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night. Commanders General Manager Adam Peters should be finding out what another team would give up for him. Washington has needs elsewhere, and using a player outside the defensive rotation to address one would make sense. At 2-4-1, the Commanders have reasons to examine the interior offensive line, defensive tackle, and possibly running back before the November 10 trade deadline at 4 p.m. Eastern. Daron Payne's foot injury and the availability questions around Javon Kinlaw and Jer'Zhan Newton leave the defensive front short. Jeremy McNichols' midfoot injury could create another need, pending additional scans. The three pairings below are my proposals for how Peters could improve the roster this season.
Washington's cornerback rotation against Philadelphia tells us where to start. Amik Robertson played 68 defensive snaps, Trey Amos played 60, and Rasul Douglas played 32. Dan Quinn also praised Nick Cross' work at nickel Monday. Mike Sainristil needs a path back into that group , but Peters has something another team might value: an experienced defensive back under contract through 2027, with a scheduled base salary of about $1.85 million next season. That gives Washington a reason to ask for a useful player in return. Jackson Powers-Johnson is one name I'd bring up. The Raiders have rotated him with Caleb Rogers at right guard, and he has starting experience at center and left guard. His rookie deal runs through 2027, giving Washington time to benefit if he earns a job inside. Las Vegas already has Taron Johnson, though, so Saintristil must have a role that interests the Raiders. I'd explore using him in an offer for Powers-Johnson, with compensation depending on how each team values the players. If the return is someone Washington would struggle to get on the field, I'd keep the affordable secondary depth.
Raiders iOL Jackson Powers-Johnson is playing out of position at OG with the Raiders. As a rookie, he played 6 games at C (288 pass block snaps) and allowed only 7 pressures while having a 67.2 pass block grade and a 66.5 run block grade per PFF. pic.twitter.com/3q9dZdw2Wd
Dyami Brown played 15 offensive snaps against the Eagles, or 25%, behind Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks, and Stefon Diggs . His contract ends after this season, making him a possible short-term addition for a team looking for speed at receiver. Washington still has to be careful here. Terry McLaurin is out for the year, and Burks spent last week dealing with a foot injury. Brown has a smaller role, but another injury could make those available snaps much more important. Kendre Miller is one name to examine. The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported that New Orleans could move him. He has 159 rushing yards on 57 carries, a 2.8-yard average, and his contract also expires after this season. Brown would give the Saints another receiving option, but I don't see any benefit for Washington to make this move. Based on Miller's production, I'd keep the receiver depth unless the staff identifies a specific role Miller can fill better than the backs it already has.
Kendre Miller ain't going down. TD for 25 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/4ILIHREgYE
Dorfance Armstrong should require the most convincing offer. He played 40 defensive snaps, or 58%, against Philadelphia and finished with seven tackles, a sack, a forced fumble, and a tackle for loss. Washington would be removing production from a front that finally put together a strong game . His contract is scheduled to void in 2027, which gives Peters a reason to listen, but it doesn't make Armstrong expendable. I'd need an immediate improvement elsewhere to justify taking him out of this rotation. Christian Barmore is where that conversation could start. Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer reported that the Patriots defensive tackle could be available after playing 41.9% of New England's defensive snaps behind Milton Williams and Cory Durden. The Patriots list Dre'Mont Jones and Elijah Ponder as their edge starters, giving Peters a reason to ask whether Armstrong could be part of an offer. Barmore's cost matters, too. He's under contract through 2028, with scheduled base salaries of $18 million in 2027 and $19 million in 2028, before other payments. I'd pursue that discussion only if Washington sees a significant interior upgrade worth the future expense. New England would still have to value Armstrong enough to make the rest of the deal workable.
Christian Barmore sack drives em back. 📺 Prime Video pic.twitter.com/xblB61RmST
Peters should be able to identify the incoming player's job before agreeing to a trade. Washington needs someone who can contribute immediately, and any return should justify the depth or production the Commanders would lose. title: Commanders Daily: How Washington Set Up Treylon Burks’ 53-Yard Catch Against the Eagles
full_text:
While the Washington Commanders have struggled to stop opponents from getting explosive plays, they haven't been very successful at getting them either. That changed Sunday night. With 2:51 left in the third quarter, Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels found receiver Treylon Burks for 53 yards, moving Washington from its own 40 to Philadelphia’s 7. It came exactly one play after Dorance Armstrong forced Tanner McKee’s fumble, which Charles Omenihu recovered, and it was the longest reception this season by a Commanders player.
Former Arkansas Razorback Treylon Burks with a nice move on Quinyon Mitchell #NFL #SNF pic.twitter.com/0sKPUugAfF
Commanders head coach Dan Quinn pointed to Burks’ earlier second-quarter comeback route when discussing how one route can create an opportunity for a double-move later. "There was a deep comeback by Trey Burks. He ran it at about 24, 25 yards," Quinn said. "And it was a good throw, good rip on the comeback. And that is kind of the setup for a double move later that can go for a big pass. And so that’s kind of the back-and-forth that you work with in the passing game."
#Commanders Jayden Daniels was lethally accurate pushing the ball downfield, going 3/3 for 104 yards on passes that traveled 20+ yards in the air Treylon Burks came down with two and Antonio Williams had the other. Check it out #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/t8xphqD1SM
The play Quinn is referencing was a 21-yard pass from Daniels to Burks on second-and-6 that moved Washington from its own 15 to its 36. The comeback route (first play above) shows Burks pushing upfield before breaking back toward the sideline. A defender expecting that comeback can get caught moving forward when the receiver sells the same break and takes off downfield. That catch helped Washington’s 89-yard touchdown drive , which ended with Stefon Diggs’ eight-yard reception to tie the game at 10. Quinn also made it clear that Washington has to pick its spots. “If you get the specific looks that say, hey, here’s the chance to go put the ball up. Oftentimes, if you chase too much, you can get yourself into trouble. But when the moments are there, are you able to go nail them?” Quinn said. Burks finished with three catches for a team-high 81 yards, which Washington certainly needs with Terry McLaurin out for the season . The Commanders could have gotten more out of his biggest catch, though. After reaching Philadelphia’s 7, they gained nothing on their next three plays and settled for Drew Stevens’ 25-yard field goal to stretch the lead to 16-10. Getting Burks open downfield gave Washington a chance to put that game further out of reach. Against the Rams, the offense needs to finish more of those chances in the end zone.
A BIG connection between Jayden Daniels and Treylon Burks. 🚀 📺 Sunday Night Football: Eagles at Commanders on NBC and Peacock pic.twitter.com/6a7YrKkBX0

title: Commanders News: Five Sacks Without Three DTs; Myles Garrett Set to Practice for Rams | Burgundy Roundup
full_text:
The Commanders got the win they needed Sunday night, even if they took a while to look like the team Dan Quinn wanted to see coming out of the bye. Washington fell behind Philadelphia 10-0 before scoring 27 unanswered points, and Jayden Daniels took charge of an offense that had struggled through the opening quarter. Quinn praised his quarterback Monday for bringing the group together. The 27-10 win moved Washington to 2-4-1 and gave Daniels his first victory as a starter since October 2025 . Washington’s defensive front supplied the answer it needed most. Daron Payne, Javon Kinlaw and Jer’Zhan Newton were all unavailable, but the Commanders sacked Tanner McKee five times and held Saquon Barkley to 30 yards on 13 carries. Charles Omenihu returned with a sack, three quarterback hits and a fumble recovery. Quinn said Monday the rush looked more coordinated and connected after the staff made it a focus during the bye. With Payne’s foot injury reportedly ending his season, Washington will need that work to hold up beyond one game. The win didn’t solve the penalty problem. Back-to-back false starts turned a third-and-1 into third-and-11 on Washington’s opening possession, and the Commanders finished with nine penalties for 70 yards. David Blough said last week the staff had simplified parts of the offense to help it get out of the huddle faster, but the pre-snap mistakes followed Washington into the Eagles game. Quinn said there isn’t one simple fix. The Rams game gives his staff another week to find one. Los Angeles arrives Sunday with a possible addition to its pass rush. Rams coach Sean McVay said Monday that Myles Garrett will return to practice this week, opening his 21-day window to come off injured reserve. McVay did not commit to Garrett playing against Washington; the Rams would have to activate him first. Los Angeles improved to 4-4 with a 24-9 win over the Chargers, and Wednesday’s practice reports should give the Commanders a clearer idea of which Rams defenders they’ll face.
Stefon Diggs caught the touchdown, and Treylon Burks supplied the biggest gain. But neither veteran was the receiver the Washington Commanders used most in Sunday night's 27-10 win over the Philadelphia Eagles . That was Antonio Williams. The rookie led Washington with seven targets and five catches for 54 yards, and his snap count showed how much work he's getting with Terry McLaurin out for the season. Now the question is whether Washington keeps putting that much of its passing game in his hands.

"I'll give you an update as it goes to Wednesday, but it's something that the team for sure is concerned with," Quinn said.

They made plenty of mistakes on their first few drives, but look no further than their very first series for a who's-who of classic errors that have regularly peppered Commanders games all season. Jayden Daniels missing on makeable throws, back-to-back false starts, surrendered once-friendly field position on third-and-one, and a blown kick by increasingly inconvenienced kicker Drew Stevens ruled the drive moot, all while backup Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee moved the ball upfield on the defense.

title: Dan Quinn Fears Serious Injury as Commanders Weigh Running Back Options
full_text:
The Washington Commanders are still sorting through injuries following Sunday's win over the Philadelphia Eagles , and one name could throw a monkey wrench into their running back rotation. Jeremy McNichols suffered a foot injury during the third quarter of Washington's 27-10 win over the visiting Eagles and did not return. Head coach Dan Quinn identified the issue today: "He does have a midfoot injury, JP. I'm concerned it's serious." Quinn's acknowledgment that Washington may need to examine additional running back options speaks volumes. For now, the team has no confirmed recovery timetable or diagnosis as they brace for additional scans on McNichols' injured foot. "I'll give you an update as it goes to Wednesday, but it's something that the team for sure is concerned with," Quinn said. McNichols recently returned from injured reserve after missing the first five games with a quadriceps injury. He had five carries for 21 yards and one catch for seven as he was starting to settle back into his role in Washington's three-man rotation.
Here are #Commanders RB Jeremy McNichols’ final two plays before he left the game with a mid foot injury The team is concerned that it is a significant injury pic.twitter.com/sbFGN0u9hQ
As we hit the midpoint of the season in Week 9, the running back rotation has taken some hits along the way. Jacory Croskey-Merritt is currently on injured reserve with a groin injury for at least two more games. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler are the remaining healthy backs on the active roster. White did well against Philly with 55 yards on 11 carries and a touchdown; Ekeler added 36 yards on eight carries and scored on a two-point conversion. Devin Neal and Craig Reynolds are the team's current practice-squad options. Washington hosts the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. Quinn expects to provide another update Wednesday, when the Commanders should have a better idea whether they need to bring in another running back. title: Commanders Snap Judgment: WR Battle Brewing and There's One Clear Winner
full_text:
Stefon Diggs caught the touchdown, and Treylon Burks supplied the biggest gain. But neither veteran was the receiver the Washington Commanders used most in Sunday night's 27-10 win over the Philadelphia Eagles . That was Antonio Williams. The rookie led Washington with seven targets and five catches for 54 yards, and his snap count showed how much work he's getting with Terry McLaurin out for the season. Now the question is whether Washington keeps putting that much of its passing game in his hands. Snap Judgment : Williams ( 50 snaps - 83% ) led the receivers in playing time, ahead of Burks (40 snaps - 67%) and Diggs (39 snaps - 65%). I'd keep him at the front of this rotation. Williams caught three passes for 20 yards on Washington’s 89-yard touchdown drive. His five-yard catch on third-and-4 kept the possession alive, and a 10-yard reception on second-and-10 moved the chains again. In the fourth quarter, his 30-yard catch was the biggest gain on the drive that pushed Washington’s lead to 19-10.
Antonio Williams was sensational Sunday night. Unguardable pic.twitter.com/uh06r9UegT
Tone's got hands 🫴 @a_williams2022 | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/PFB5qF2kQQ
Charles Omenihu returned with Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw inactive , finishing with a sack, three quarterback hits, and a fumble recovery. Snap Judgment : Omenihu played 46 defensive snaps (67%), compared with 49 for K’Lavon Chaisson, 45 for Odafe Oweh and 40 for Dorance Armstrong. I'd keep him involved when the front gets healthier. Omenihu was also credited with a quarterback hit on the fourth-down pass Rasul Douglas intercepted late in the fourth quarter. Douglas returned it to Philadelphia’s 37, and Washington scored on its next possession.
Austin Ekeler finished with eight carries for 36 yards and scored on the two-point conversion. Snap Judgment : Rachaad White (28 snaps - 47%) led the backfield, followed by Ekeler (20 snaps - 33%) and Jeremy McNichols (12 snaps - 20%). Ekeler played seven snaps against San Francisco, so Quinn followed through on giving him more work . Ekeler’s 18-yard run took Washington to Philadelphia’s 8-yard line in the second quarter. Diggs caught the tying touchdown on the next snap. The backfield split could change again against the Rams. Quinn said Monday that Jeremy McNichols has a midfoot injury and added, “I'm concerned it's serious.” More scans are planned for Tuesday. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt still on injured reserve, Washington could need Ekeler to handle more work if McNichols can’t play.
One of the most interesting takeaways from glancing at the snap counts for Sunday night's Commanders vs. Eagles game was seeing Mike Sainristil's jersey number next to his total number of defensive snaps. That's right: Sainristil played 16 special teams snaps, but zero on defense, as Washington beat Philadelphia 27-10. Now the question becomes: where does he fit in the defensive rotation after a game in which Washington never used him there? Snap Judgment : Amik Robertson (68 snaps - 99%), Trey Amos (60 snaps - 87%), and Rasul Douglas (32 snaps - 46%) handled Washington’s cornerback snaps against Philadelphia. Quinn said Monday that Amos no longer needs the workload restriction he had against San Francisco. He also praised Nick Cross’ work at nickel, where Washington used him near the line of scrimmage and as a blitzer. One question for Daronte Jones at his next press conference is why Sainristil never entered on defense. The next game will tell us whether he gets back into the rotation, Williams continues to lead the receivers in opportunities, and Omenihu stays this involved up front. title: Commanders Report Card: Who Delivered in Eagles Win — and Who Still Fell Short?
full_text:
The first few minutes of the Washington Commanders' attempt at revenge over the rival Philadelphia Eagles seemed to hit every last beat of what Washington fans didn't want to see in the squad's humiliating return to the primetime slate.
They made plenty of mistakes on their first few drives, but look no further than their very first series for a who's-who of classic errors that have regularly peppered Commanders games all season. Jayden Daniels missing on makeable throws, back-to-back false starts, surrendered once-friendly field position on third-and-one, and a blown kick by increasingly inconvenienced kicker Drew Stevens ruled the drive moot, all while backup Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee moved the ball upfield on the defense.
But the second the Commanders, down multiple scores, heard the boos from inside their own house at Northwest Stadium, they erased yet another slow start. Unlike in their previous loss to the San Francisco 49ers, they never took their foot off the gas, scoring 27 straight and somehow climbing right back into the divisional standings at 2-4-1 behind a complicated, well-rounded win.
Daniels looked generally lethargic at first, specifically during one of the false-start calls he initiated with a strange pre-snap pump-fake , but he mostly made the right plays from then on once he exorcised that gaffe from his system. Fans can't quibble with a stat line of 217 yards on 16/29 passing with a touchdown thrown in if he can perform as surgically as he did past the first quarter.
Jayden Daniels ➡️ Stefon Diggs for the TD! PHIvsWAS on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Okl6kfEkFL
That pass to Stefon Diggs was just the tip of the iceberg in Daniels' unflappable passing aggression. He stuck with Treylon Burks for a 53-yard gain after an early drop and kept finding Chig Okonkwo for bailout opportunities, using his receivers' varying strengths to interchange big plays with short-range reads.
This wasn't the cleanest overall outing he's completed in Washington, but Commanders fans have to feel relieved that one of the more subtly frustrating statistics surrounding the team can finally vanish; despite his best (if inconsistent) efforts, he'd yet to secure a win since Week 5 in 2025 , having had to watch backup Marcus Mariota secure this roster's lone previous victory over the Seattle Seahawks on the sidelines while the usual starter recovered from a dislocated elbow. This division win, the first of the Commanders' campaign in four tries, belongs to him as much as anyone.
Even if Jacory Croskey-Merritt were active enough to take his regular spot in the depth chart ahead of spot-starting back Rachaad White, the consensus around the Commanders' less-than-inspiring run game still likely wouldn't be very optimistic given their infrastructure. Whether it's a lack of high-end rushing talent, blockers struggling to create the necessary holes, or both excuses working in tandem, this element of the offense has yet to jump off the screen.
White ended the night with a team-high 55 yards on the ground, but just about all of that chunk yardage and the touchdown it resulted in arrived on Washington’s late, game-clinching drive. Older reserves Austin Ekeler and Jeremy McNichols added 57 more rushing yards, barely enough to punch the spiraling Eagles defense where it hurt.
The new top-three receiving trio post-Terry McLaurin did not disappoint. Following Burks' early flubbed attempt at a simple catch-and-run, a blunder that once looked like an omen for another tough showing out on the field, he, Diggs, and Antonio Williams did well to convert on the chances that Daniels passed their way.
They settled into zones, caught in stride with their passes and held their own against a usually feared Philadelphia secondary. The Eagles, who have often held up against big plays over their contending years, still had 2025 Pro Bowler and All-Pro cornerback Quinyon Mitchell to disrupt the Commanders' wideouts, but even he arguably got the worst of it when Burks burnt him on a deep route.
Quinyon Mitchell is a decent CB at best and Eagles fans will act like he’s playing like 09’ Darrelle Revis pic.twitter.com/V7HlEB7hVP
The receiving room may yet survive and enjoy some thrills without McLaurin, who's slated to miss the remainder of the season following a torn patellar tendon against the 49ers, meaning that Washington will take whatever they can get out of its prospects and supplementary veterans. As it turns out, their scheme heading forward heavily involves Okonkwo, and he's ready for Daniels' heaves.
32 yards on two completions on four targets doesn't look like much, but the tight end always seemed to be available whenever Daniels needed a savior out deep. That's where Okonkwo's size came in handy, with few individual defenders able to deter someone with his agility and hands. Had he not coughed up a tough fumble on one of his receptions, this could have easily gone down as the big receiver's most impactful outing of the 2026 slate.
CHIG OKONKWO ALMOST HAD ONE pic.twitter.com/hp1UGVPaQr
His double-catch to help Washington escape its own end zone already seemed like a special grab in the moment, and that was before he came within a foot of collecting a play-of-the-year contender with a goal-line fade attempt for the ages. The tight end rotation has desperately needed anyone to aid Daniels' pass-catching corps, and Okonkwo finally seems at home in Washington's offense.
At the very least, Washington's offensive linemen allowed the quarterback to sit back and watch routes develop a few times, a luxury that fans have come to appreciate given his slight frame and their lack of reliable blocking.
Even if Philadelphia's pass-rushers still made life tough for the tackles, this grade is a procedural, pre-snap-related indictment of the position group's composure. This unit is far too handsy in drawing holding calls and much too jumpy with Daniels calling the shots, with the false starts repeatedly hurting the offense's chances of converting on their promising drives.
Still, only two sacks in Daniels' game recap have to be mentioned when discussing a blocking line that's not completely untalented- just undisciplined.
Everyone enjoyed moments to shine against an Eagles offense that seemed to disintegrate as the game trudged on. McKee went down five times to sacks from Commanders tacklers, largely because Washington emphasized rushing the quarterback's distribution process.
There were the usual suspects, like regular edge presences like Odafe Oweh and K'Lavon Chaisson, but then there were breakouts like Charles Omenihu in his best Commanders appearance yet and Shy Tuttle, the impressive veteran who continues shining since barely sneaking onto the roster . The strength in numbers, particularly from versatile middle linebackers Sonny Styles and Frankie Luvu, empowered plenty of niche defenders to get in on the action within the deceptive scheme and keep the Eagles' own stoppers guessing.
This unit didn't have as much to do as in Week 1, when Eagles receiver DeVonta Smith was active in Philadelphia, but they still made their collective presence known within the blitzing attack. Nick Cross was everywhere as the much-appreciated safety who can split defenders at scrimmage, as was Amik Robertson in his typically loud breakups on screen pass attempts.
Trey Amos , now that his return game against San Francisco is finally in the past, looked comfortable breaking up his rare targets in isolation, and fans will remember the pick he collected off of Dallas Goedert's hands that was wiped out following a roughing-the-passer penalty. No matter: Rasul Douglas stepped up a few minutes later with an interception that triggered no flags, thereby setting up the final, game-clinching scoring drive in the matchup's closing minutes.
Rasul Douglas with the INT for the Commanders! PHIvsWAS on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/UYdodH2LDO
The one blooper that went down on the special…
